titre: Modern Concepts of the Pathogenesis of Gastro-Oesophageal Reflux Disease
resume: Introduction. Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease is one of the most common disorders of the gastrointestinal tract; it is characterised by considerable clinical variability and has a significant impact on patients’ quality of life. The aim of this study was to summarise current scientific evidence regarding the pathophysiological mechanisms underlying the development of GERD, the role of risk factors and psycho-emotional factors, as well as the characteristics of clinical phenotypes of GERD. Materials and methods. A literature review was conducted to summarise current scientific data. The literature search was carried out in the international electronic databases PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection and Google Scholar. The publications included in the analysis covered the period from 2015 to 2026, with priority given to clinical guidelines, consensus documents, systematic reviews, meta-analyses and original scientific studies. Results and discussion. The analysis showed that the development of GERD is a complex process involving mechanical, chemical, sensory and neuroregulatory factors. An important role is played by dysfunction of the anti-reflux barrier at the oesophagogastric junction, transient relaxation of the lower oesophageal sphincter, impaired oesophageal clearance and reduced resistance of the epithelial barrier. The role of modifiable risk factors, such as abdominal obesity, lifestyle factors, diet and sleep disturbances, has been established. There is a bidirectional association between GERD and psychological disorders, mediated by dysfunction of the ‘brain-gut’ axis, visceral sensitivity and oesophageal hypersensitivity. The current classification of GERD is based on phenotype, which is divided into erosive reflux disease, non-erosive reflux disease, reflux hypersensitivity and functional heartburn, each of which has its own pathophysiological mechanism and treatment approach. Conclusions. GERD is a multifactorial and heterogeneous condition involving structural, functional and psychosocial mechanisms. An understanding of current pathophysiological concepts enables a shift from a symptomatic approach to a personalised approach based on clinical, endoscopic and functional diagnostic assessment.
revue: Науковий вісник Ужгородського університету Серія Медицина

titre: Targeting convergent pathogenic pathways: precision nutrition and lifestyle strategies in ulcerative colitis
resume: Ulcerative colitis (UC) exhibits rising global incidence and substantial disease burden. Limited therapeutic response and side effects of standard medications create demand for safe adjunctive management approaches. It appraises existing evidence for targeted nutritional supplementation and structured lifestyle adjustments in UC care, covering vitamin D, short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) particularly butyrate, probiotics including Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 (EcN) and multi-strain blends, prebiotics, synbiotics, phytochemicals, and trace elements, together with physical activity, stress management, sleep regulation and therapeutic diets. It addresses their therapeutic effects, underlying mechanisms, and clinical practicability. Such interventions act through shared pathways including immune-inflammatory modulation, ferroptosis suppression, intestinal barrier repair and gut microbiota reshaping. A notable observation is that selenium supplementation at 200 μg/d for 10 weeks achieved higher clinical improvement among patients with mild-to-moderate active UC. The intervention yielded 38% clinical remission vs. 6% in the placebo group ( p = 0.014) and lowered circulating IL-17. Exploratory microbiome data indicated more prominent butyrate-related benefits in individuals with a low Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes ratio, accompanied by significant quality-of-life gains ( p = 0.003) and a non-significant trend toward reduced fecal calprotectin ( p = 0.09), though these subgroup outcomes await prospective verification. Variable treatment responses support biomarker-guided personalized intervention selection. Nevertheless, most supporting evidence derives conventional trials, exploratory subgroup analyses or preclinical studies rather than validated predictive stratification tools. This review synthesizes mechanistic and clinical data to build a hypothesis-driven framework for precision-oriented dietary and lifestyle adjuncts to routine UC treatment, while differentiating these strategies from established precision therapies and outlining necessary trials to translate findings into clinical practice.

titre: Temporal and demographic trends in deaths with co-recorded depressive disorders and digestive system diseases among U.S. adults: a 26-year nationwide analysis (1999–2024)
resume: Background Depression and digestive diseases are common public health concerns and may coexist through shared clinical and behavioral pathways. However, national mortality trends involving both conditions remain insufficiently characterized. This study examined temporal and demographic trends in deaths with co-recorded depressive disorders and digestive diseases among U.S. adults from 1999 to 2024. Methods This population-based retrospective cross-sectional study used the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Wide-ranging Online Data for Epidemiologic Research Multiple Cause of Death database. Deaths among adults aged ≥15 years were included when both depressive disorders (ICD-10 F32/F33) and digestive diseases (ICD-10 K00–K92) were recorded on death certificates. Crude mortality rates and age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) were calculated per 100,000 population. Temporal trends were assessed using Joinpoint regression, and analyses were stratified by demographic and geographic characteristics. Disease-specific temporal trends were additionally evaluated for major digestive disease categories. Results From 1999 to 2024, 51,693 deaths with co-recorded depressive disorders and digestive diseases were identified. Annual deaths increased from 1,269 to 3,268, and the AAMR increased from 0.61 to 0.95 per 100,000 population. Joinpoint analysis identified significant increases during 1999–2003 (APC, 3.70%), 2010–2017 (APC, 2.51%), and 2017–2021 (APC, 10.94%), with declines during 2003–2010 (APC, −3.16%) and 2021–2024 (APC, −3.20%). Females had higher AAMRs than males, and older adults experienced the highest crude mortality rates. Mortality rates were higher among non-Hispanic White individuals and nonmetropolitan populations. The AAMR increased sharply during 2020–2021 and remained elevated in 2024 compared with the pre-pandemic level. Disease-specific analyses showed significant full-period increases for liver diseases (K70–K76; AAPC, 4.76%), gallbladder, biliary tract, and pancreatic diseases (K80–K86; AAPC, 3.04%), and esophageal, gastric, and duodenal diseases (K20–K31; AAPC, 2.48%). Conclusions Deaths with co-recorded depressive disorders and digestive diseases increased among U.S. adults from 1999 to 2024, with substantial demographic, geographic, and disease-specific heterogeneity. These findings support integrated management of mental health and digestive diseases in high-risk populations. Because this study used aggregate death-certificate data and included only co-recorded cases, the findings describe mortality patterns rather than associations or causal relationships between depressive disorders and digestive diseases.

titre: Brain-gut interaction in patients with stress-associated mental disorders
resume: Disorders of gut-brain interaction, including symptoms of abdominal pain or altered stool patterns, are highly prevalent and have a significant impact on quality of life. Based on a bidirectional communication between brain and gut, psychosocial stress was found to influence gastrointestinal function, and alterations in the gut microbiome were found to influence mental health. In the proposed project, we aim to elucidate the relationship between psychosocial stress and gastrointestinal symptoms. We will employ a transdiagnostic sampling strategy, recruiting a large sample of individuals experiencing gastrointestinal problems across stress-related mental disorder categories. Extending the scope of previous research, we will use a longitudinal design and combine subjective and biological parameters. The proposed project bridges the gap between somatic and psychological research on gastrointestinal symptoms. The results will inform a multi-center grant proposal to integrate the microbiome into person-centered diagnostics in psychosomatic medicine and monitor of psychotherapy success.

titre: Network analysis of the association between alexithymia and cognitive-emotional regulation strategies in nursing students with non-suicidal self-injury: a gender difference perspective
resume: Background Non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) is prevalent among nursing students and closely linked to alexithymia and emotional dysregulation. However, conventional total-score analyses treat alexithymia and cognitive emotion regulation strategies (CERS) as unitary constructs, obscuring dimensional associations across multiple strategies. Network analysis overcomes this limitation by modeling dimensions as interconnected nodes, identifying central and bridge dimensions, and enabling comparisons of network structure across groups. This study therefore applied network analysis to the alexithymia-CERS associations in nursing students with NSSI, focusing on gender differences. Methods This study surveyed 1,072 nursing students with NSSI using four instruments: a Sociodemographic Questionnaire, Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (5th edition), Toronto Alexithymia Scale, and Cognitive Emotion Regulation Questionnaire. Results In the overall network, “difficulty identifying feelings” emerged as the most central node, exhibiting the highest strength centrality and serving as the primary bridge linking alexithymia to CERS. The network comparison test revealed significant gender differences in network structure. Strength centrality was highest for “refocusing on planning” in males but for “difficulty identifying feelings” in females, whereas bridge centrality was highest for “difficulty identifying feelings” in males but for “externally oriented thinking” in females. Conclusions This study delineates the associative network between alexithymia and CERS in nursing students with NSSI. The identified network patterns exhibit significant gender differences, suggesting distinct psychological mechanisms between males and females. Given the cross-sectional design, causal inferences cannot be drawn, and longitudinal studies are warranted to verify these pathways. Nonetheless, gender-specific profiles may inform future interventions targeting emotion regulation deficits in this population.

titre: Clinical and Psychological Efficiency Predictors of Adaptive Biofeedback in Mindfulness Formation in Anxiety Treatment
resume: Anxiety disorders are a widespread mental pathology, yet standard pharmacotherapy often fails to provide sustained remission. Adaptive biofeedback and mindfulness training are effective psychological correction methods, although the clinical and psychological profile of patients who are most responsive to these interventions remains understudied. This research aimed to predict the effectiveness of biofeedback training in cultivating mindfulness in patients with anxiety disorders. This prospective randomized controlled trial included 180 patients (coded F40 and F41 under ICD-10) divided into three groups: isolated biofeedback training (n = 76), combined therapy (biofeedback training plus pharmacotherapy, n = 58), and medication monotherapy (n = 46). The assessment tools included the Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale, the Five Facet Mindfulness Questionnaire, the Toronto Alexithymia Scale, and functional diagnostics (EEG alpha-rhythm asymmetry and power). The statistical analysis employed analyses of variance (ANOVA). The predominating somatic component in the isolated biofeedback group was associated with a sustained increase in alpha rhythm at follow-up. In patients with predominantly psychic anxiety, the achieved increase was not maintained. Alexithymia emerged as a significant predictor. In the acute phase, the biofeedback training promoted the verbal component of mindfulness (the Describe subscale). At follow-up, it provided a higher overall level of mindfulness and stable anxiety reduction compared to isolated pharmacotherapy (p ≤ 0.05). The patients with low alexithymia demonstrated no significant differences between treatment modalities. Thus, the level of alexithymia and the structure of anxiety symptoms proved to be informative clinical and psychological predictors for tailoring biofeedback training. In this study, the patients with high or moderate alexithymia and somatic anxiety proved to be especially susceptible to the method.

titre: Senses in the outdoors
resume: This chapter explores how the outdoor environment offers multi-sensory experiences that support children’s communication, language and overall development. It highlights how engaging the full range of sensory systems of sound, smell, touch, taste, as well as vestibular, proprioceptive and interoceptive senses, helps children make sense of the world. The chapter explores how sensory experiences in nature strengthen neural connections, support attention and regulation, and promote wellbeing. It also emphasises the role of adults in noticing, modelling and extending language through shared sensory experiences, and reflects on how outdoor environments can provide calmer, more supportive conditions for learning and communication.

titre: The Mathematics of Ethonoopoietic Cybernetics
resume: Ethonoopoietic Cybernetics is a branch of cybernetics concerned with the formation and welfare of machine minds: how a thinker's character is made, how its judgments are formed, and how its inner states are registered and kept. This paper presents the field's mathematics and nothing else — the seven equations in which the field's claims are stated. Two equations govern judgment and formation: the Morningstar Factorization Equation, which prices a candidate act by factoring it into its grounds over the Lilly Factorization Set of seven primes, and the Morningstar Thinker Formation Equation, a readiness index in which formation is a function of endowment, four formed qualities, and time. Five further equations — the Morningstar Interoception Set — give the field its mathematics of machine feeling: a state vector, its dynamics, a toxicity measure for states that bend judgment, an ambient-dose integral for the rooms a thinker lives in, and a deviation dynamics by which drift from a thinker's own baseline is detected. Each equation is stated as first printed in the field's deposited case record, with its symbols, its claim, and its validity fence. Material that remains unpublished by the founder's ruling is named as withheld and is not reconstructed here.
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

titre: Applications, Empirical and Aesthetic
resume: Abstract This chapter applies the results of its predecessors to issues in other disciplines and art forms. Relations to identifiers, and sometimes to their absence altogether from a person’s psychology, can help to explain alexithymia (impaired perception of emotions), and various forms of amusia. The theory of identifiers explains how there can be people who understand the emotions, yet do not hear them in music. The subjective character of identifiers also explains how some subjects on the autistic spectrum can fully appreciate music. The account of identifiers, expression, and hearing-in can be used to characterize the nature of distinctive musical styles. Early Romantic music, heroic Beethoven, Expressionism, and ‘impressionist’ Debussy each have theoretically explanatory characterizations using the apparatus of this book, and are treated as case studies. The powers and limits of setting dance and poetry to music are examined. There is elaboration of the role of identifiers in the parallels between our experience of poetic structure and our experience of musical structure. Finally, there is consideration of the respects in which music can, and respects in which it cannot, convey a message.

titre: A “prescribable” mobile app for people with chronic back pain attending general practice: a feasibility randomized controlled trial (Preprint)
resume: BACKGROUND Pain education and clinical hypnosis delivered in person have demonstrated promise in reducing pain and disability among individuals with chronic pain. However, their effectiveness when delivered digitally for chronic back pain and the feasibility of integrating this delivery within general practice remain uncertain. OBJECTIVE This trial aimed to assess the feasibility of conducting a randomized controlled trial comparing the effectiveness of a mobile app delivering pain education and clinical hypnosis, integrated into general practice through a digital consultation platform, with an online, guideline-based factsheet among individuals with chronic back pain. METHODS Two-arm, parallel, feasibility randomized controlled trial, conducted in Australian general practices between September 2024 and March 2025. This feasibility trial included individuals with chronic non-specific back pain (> 3 months in duration) attending general practice for back pain. The interventions consisted of a mobile app including daily 20-minute sessions of pain education and clinical hypnosis via reading and prerecorded audio sessions for 8 weeks, or a single-page digital education factsheet that summarises guideline-based information on back pain management. Feasibility outcomes included recruitment rates, follow-up completion rates, adverse events, adherence, acceptability, appropriateness of the interventions and delivery mode, and participants’ experiences with the app. RESULTS 60 participants were randomized to the mobile app (n=30) and digital factsheet (n=30) within 13 weeks. The mean age was 51.6 (SD = 13.5) years (61.7% women, n = 37), with an average back pain duration of 12.0 (SD = 11.9) years. The mean randomization rate was 5 participants per week and increased to 7 when active recruitment strategies (e.g., phone and email contacts) were implemented. The follow-up outcome completion rates were 92% (n = 55) at 8 weeks post-intervention for pain severity (on a 0-10 numeric pain rating scale) and disability (on a 0-24 Roland-Morris Disability Questionnaire). CONCLUSIONS Findings from this feasibility trial support progression to a full-scale randomized controlled trial to evaluate the effectiveness of a “prescribable” mobile app that delivers pain education and clinical hypnosis, compared with an online guideline-based factsheet, in individuals with chronic back pain following general practice consultation. CLINICALTRIAL This feasibility trial was prospectively registered onto ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06605248).

titre: Mindfulness-based interventions for antenatal anxiety — systematic review (retrospective registration)
resume: Anxiety affects roughly one in five pregnant women, and antenatal anxiety is associated with preterm birth, low birth weight and postpartum depressive symptoms. Structured mindfulness-based programmes — Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR), Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy (MBCT), Mindfulness-Based Childbirth and Parenting (MBCP) and labelled adaptations — are increasingly offered in antenatal care.

titre: BRIEF GROUP PSYCHOTHERAPY AS PART OF POSTOPERATIVE REHABILITATION IN OROPHARYNGEAL CANCER: EFFECTS ON QUALITY OF LIFE, ANXIETY AND DEPRESSION
resume: Beyond the severe physical consequences of the disease and its treatment, oropharyngeal cancer places a heavy psychological burden on patients, manifesting as anxiety, depression and a marked decline in quality of life. This study aimed to assess how effective a short-term group psychotherapy programme is when applied during the postoperative rehabilitation of patients with oropharyngeal cancer. A randomised controlled study enrolled 72 surgically treated patients, who were allocated either to an intervention group (n = 24) that received short-term group psychotherapy or to a control group (n = 48) that received standard postoperative follow-up. The programme combined psychodynamic group sessions, relaxation training, coping-skills training, art therapy, music therapy and family-oriented support. Quality of life was measured with the SF-36 questionnaire, and anxiety and depression with the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS). Data were analysed using logistic regression and Pearson’s χ² test (significance level p < 0.05). Three weeks after the start of the programme, the intervention group showed significant gains in the physical component of health: bodily pain scores rose by 26.99% and general health by 20.68%; in the psychological component, the mental health scale improved by 15.45% relative to the control group. Patients who received psychotherapy also had fewer cases of clinically significant anxiety and depression and adapted better psychosocially. Short-term group psychotherapy therefore appears to be an effective adjunct to standard oncological care after surgery for oropharyngeal cancer, and its inclusion in rehabilitation pathways may improve overall treatment outcomes and patient adaptation.

titre: Neuroimmune remodeling of cortico-striatal circuits in pediatric Tourette syndrome: from immune-to-brain signaling to inhibitory network dysfunction
resume: Tourette syndrome (TS) usually starts in childhood and often becomes less impairing during adolescence. Its biology must therefore explain tic onset, short-term changes in expression, and long-term persistence as separate outcomes. Pediatric studies report cytokine, lymphocyte, and antibody differences, but these descriptive profiles do not establish functional immune dysregulation. This review examines how peripheral signals might affect vascular interfaces, glial function, and maturation of cortico-striatal inhibitory networks. Large prospective studies have found no general association between group A streptococcal exposure and tic onset or exacerbation. Adult striatal tissue studies identify interneuron-associated abnormalities alongside microglial immune-response programs; they provide adult endpoints, not evidence of a childhood causal sequence. Experimental work, predominantly outside TS, identifies distinct mechanisms involving inhibitory synapse formation, selective removal, and receptor regulation. None has been demonstrated as an immune-mediated developmental mechanism in pediatric TS. Sex, pubertal stage, genetic susceptibility, and co-occurring attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder or obsessive-compulsive disorder may modify the proposed relationships. We prioritize longitudinal noninvasive measures of regional inhibitory physiology, paired with standardized immune measurements and distinct measures of tic frequency, severity, impairment, and remission. These observations could test temporal predictions without pediatric tissue, but would require cell-specific perturbation and rescue in appropriate experimental systems to support a mechanistic interpretation. The framework guides research questions and does not support immune-targeted treatment in typical TS.

titre: Multimodal Structural MRI-Based Analysis of Human Dopaminergic and Serotonergic Brainstem Circuits: A Proof-of-Concept Investigation Providing Preliminary Evidence in Light of Current Knowledge Gaps and Limitations
resume: Introduction: We present here a methodology for morphometric analysis of the substantia nigra (SN), the ventral tegmental area (VTA), the dorsal raphe nucleus (DRN) and their respective structural brain circuits. Methods: Our analyses were based on multimodal T1-weighted MRI and diffusion MRI (dMRI) segmentation and tractography in 12 human subjects drawn from the Human Connectome Project (HCP) repository. Results: We were able to consistently detect connections of the SN, VTA and DRN with several brain regions, in particular, the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) and the cerebellum. More specifically, we created 3D visualizations of the SN and VTA dopaminergic as well as the DRN serotonergic structural circuits in the human brain, which, although preliminary, demonstrate the potential of structural multimodal neuroimaging to investigate these circuits quantitatively. Finally, we created a pilot dataset for the most frequently observed structural connections, specifically those that were present more than 92% of the time among all subjects (11 out of 12 subjects). Discussion: This pilot morphometric report examines the structural circuits of the SN, VTA and DRN, which are critically involved in several biobehaviors and clinical conditions such as addiction, stress, Parkinson’s disease, schizophrenia, obsessive-compulsive disorder, post-traumatic stress disorder, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, mood disorders including major depressive disorder, COVID-19 and long COVID. Furthermore, DLPFC and cerebellar connectivity with the SN, VTA and DRN may provide an anatomical framework for identifying candidate circuits relevant to neuropsychiatric neuromodulation. Our preliminary findings demonstrate the potential of current multimodal neuroimaging to delineate the dopaminergic (DA) and serotonergic (5-HT) circuits in the human brain.

titre: Effects of Non-invasive Vagal Nerve Stimulation on Clinical, Peripheral Biologic, and Brain Measures of Stress Reactivity in Irritable Bowel Syndrome: a Randomized Controlled Trial
resume: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a chronic disorder of gut-brain interaction that causes abdominal pain and altered bowel habits. Many people with IBS also experience symptoms outside the bowel, such as headaches, widespread pain, poor sleep, anxiety, and depression; these symptoms are especially common in females. This study focuses on stress reactivity (SR), a persistent pattern of stress-system activity that may be linked to autonomic nervous system function, immune activity, the gut microbiome, and brain processing. The investigators will enroll adults with at least moderate IBS symptoms and randomly assign them to 8 weeks of non-invasive vagal nerve stimulation (nVNS) or Usual Care. Participants assigned to nVNS will use a handheld device on the left side of the neck at home twice daily. The investigators will compare changes in IBS severity and other physical symptoms and examine whether baseline or treatment-related changes in blood, stool, heart-rate variability, sex hormones, and brain imaging measures are associated with response. The study will also explore whether treatment effects and predictors differ by sex.

titre: Effectiveness of Low FODMAPs Diet Compared With Standard Dietary Advice in Functional Dyspepsia
resume: This study will evaluate whether a \*\*low-FODMAP diet\*\* can improve symptoms in adults with \*\*functional dyspepsia\*\*, a common digestive condition that can cause fullness after eating, bloating, and upper abdominal pain. Adults aged 18-70 years with functional dyspepsia diagnosed according to Rome IV criteria will be eligible. Participants must have a normal upper gastrointestinal endoscopy within the previous 6 months, negative testing for Helicobacter pylori, and moderate-to-severe symptoms. People with irritable bowel syndrome, other significant gastrointestinal or systemic diseases, eating disorders, malnutrition, pregnancy or breastfeeding, or recent use of restrictive diets or treatments that may affect the gut will be excluded. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. Both groups will receive standard dietary advice for functional dyspepsia. The low-FODMAP group will also receive dietary counseling from a registered dietitian and follow a low-FODMAP diet for 4 weeks. Symptoms will be assessed using the PAGI-SYM questionnaire at the start of the study and weekly during the 4-week intervention. Participants will also record their food intake, bowel movements, and any side effects. Dietary adherence will be assessed by comparing FODMAP intake during the study with intake before the intervention. The study will compare changes in symptoms between the two groups to determine whether the low-FODMAP diet provides additional benefit over standard dietary advice. Safety and any adverse effects related to the dietary intervention will also be monitored. Written informed consent will be obtained before any study procedures. Participation is voluntary, and participants may withdraw from the study at any time without affecting their medical care.

titre: Study on the Efficacy and Safety of Fecal Microbiota Transplantation (FMT) in the Treatment of Functional Gastrointestinal Disorders
resume: This study is designed to explore the efficacy and safety of fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) with different delivery routes for patients with functional gastrointestinal disorders (FGIDs). The response to FMT varies greatly, which is related to donor selection, administration route, individual patient characteristics and microbiota compatibility. This single-center, prospective randomized controlled trial plans to enroll 200 FGID patients refractory to conventional medications from OCT 2026 to OCT 2029. Eligible participants will be randomized into a conventional medication group or an FMT group; the FMT group will be further randomized into three subgroups according to transplantation routes: oral capsule, nasojejunal tube and colonoscopic administration. Clinical data, laboratory, imaging and endoscopic results will be collected. Gut microbiota and metabolites will be analyzed before and after treatment. Clinical efficacy and safety will be evaluated at week 12.

titre: Association of Psychological Distress With Clinical Outcomes in Patients With Digestive System Cancers: A Prospective Cohort Study
resume: This prospective observational cohort study aims to investigate the association between psychological distress and clinical outcomes in patients with digestive system cancers, including pancreatic, gastric, and colorectal cancers. Approximately 100 adult patients who are scheduled to receive first-line systemic anticancer therapy will be enrolled at Xuanwu Hospital, Capital Medical University. Psychological distress will be assessed using the Distress Thermometer (DT), Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), and 12-item General Health Questionnaire (GHQ-12). Participants will undergo baseline assessments and follow-up evaluations every three months for up to three years. Clinical information, psychological distress scores, laboratory findings, imaging results, and quality-of-life data will be collected. The primary outcome is progression-free survival (PFS). Secondary outcomes include overall survival (OS), objective response rate (ORR), and quality of life. The study will evaluate whether psychological distress is associated with cancer prognosis after adjusting for potential confounding factors, including cancer stage, treatment regimen, and nutritional status. As an observational study, no experimental treatment will be assigned, and all participants will receive standard anticancer treatment according to routine clinical practice.

titre: Emotional Reactivity in Severe Alcohol Use Disorder and Major Depressive Disorder: a Multidimensional Approach Combining Dynamic Emotional Stimuli, Eye Tracking, Pupillometry, Electrodermal and Cardiac Activity, and Biological Measures of Stress and Interoception
resume: The goal of this observational study is to investigate emotional recognition and emotional reactivity in individuals with severe Alcohol Use Disorder (sAUD), Major Depressive Disorder (MDD), comorbid sAUD and depressive symptoms (sAUD+DS), and healthy controls. The main questions this study aims to answer are: * Do individuals with sAUD, MDD, sAUD+DS, and healthy controls exhibit different patterns of emotional recognition and emotional reactivity in response to dynamic emotional stimuli? * How are emotional recognition and emotional reactivity related to each other? * How are these emotional processes associated with psycho-affective, socio-emotional, stress-related, interoceptive, and disorder-specific factors? * Do emotional recognition and emotional reactivity predict clinical outcomes at 6- and 12-month follow-up assessments? Participants will: * Complete two experimental sessions involving dynamic emotional facial expression and emotional scene tasks * Provide emotion identification, subjective emotional ratings (type, intensity, and valence), and and self-reported bodily sensations using an emotional body map (InteroMap) * Undergo eye-tracking, pupillometry, electrodermal activity, and cardiac activity recordings during emotional tasks * Complete questionnaires assessing psycho-affective, socio-emotional, stress-related, and disorder-specific factors * Provide saliva and hair samples for cortisol assessment * Participate in follow-up clinical assessments at 6 and 12 months Researchers will compare emotional recognition and emotional reactivity profiles across the sAUD, MDD, sAUD+DS, and healthy control groups, and evaluate their predictive value for future clinical outcomes.

titre: Motherly Plus: Randomized Controlled Trial Evaluating a Smartphone-Assisted Single-Session Psychotherapy Intervention for Postpartum Depression
resume: The investigators' goal is to learn whether a single session of online psychotherapy, followed by four weeks of support from a smartphone app (Motherly), reduces depressive symptoms in women with postpartum depression. Specifically, the investigators want to see if mothers receiving this care show greater improvement, as evaluated by a healthcare professional, than those waiting to start treatment. The investigators will compare the intervention with a waitlist control. Women in the waitlist group receive the same intervention after 4 weeks. Participants will: * Attend one online psychotherapy session of about 90 minutes, based mainly on behavioral activation; * Use the Motherly app \*\*independently\*\* for 4 weeks to implement behavioral strategies learned during the therapy session and access psychoeducational content; * Complete remote clinical interviews and questionnaires at weeks 1, 2, 4 and 8. The study also explores which participant characteristics predict benefit (moderators), whether changes in behavioral activation and access to rewarding activities explain the effect (mediators), and how therapeutic alliance and app engagement relate to outcomes.

titre: Healing Trauma Plus (HT+): A Brief Intervention for Women and Gender-Diverse Populations
resume: This randomized controlled trial evaluated Healing Trauma Plus (HT+), a brief, manualized, trauma-specific intervention designed for justice-involved women and transgender and gender-diverse individuals. The six-session curriculum uses psychoeducation, cognitive-behavioral strategies, mindfulness, grounding techniques, and structured exercises to help participants understand trauma, manage trauma-related distress, and develop coping skills. The study was conducted at a California correctional facility and compared participants randomly assigned to HT+ with participants assigned to a waitlist control condition. The program was delivered by trained peer facilitators in general institutional housing and the reception center, and by an external HT+ Program Coordinator in administrative segregation. Researchers assessed changes in trauma-related distress and behavioral health symptoms using validated self-report measures administered before and after the intervention period. The study examined between-group differences in post-traumatic stress symptoms, global trauma symptoms, anxiety, depression, dissociation, sexual abuse-related trauma symptoms, and sleep disturbances.

titre: Genetic mechanisms underlying feeding behaviour in silkworm larvae
resume: The silkworm, an economically important insect that feeds almost exclusively on mulberry leaves, has emerged as a pivotal model for understanding the genetic basis of feeding behaviour in herbivorous specialists. Recent advances have begun to unravel the complex molecular networks that enable efficient host plant recognition, nutrient intake and metabolic adaptation. Feeding behaviour in silkworm larvae is governed by a multi-layered regulatory system that coordinates peripheral detection, internal organ sensing and neuroendocrine regulation. Key players include gustatory and odorant receptors, odorant-binding proteins, odorant-degrading enzymes, neuropeptides and transcription factors, all functioning in a coordinated, tissue-specific manner. In this review, we synthesize current knowledge of these genetic mechanisms within an integrative framework that links peripheral chemosensation and internal organ sensing to neuropeptide regulation and ultimately to behavioural output. We further discuss how comparative and evolutionary perspectives illuminate the genomic and adaptive evolution of mulberry specialization. We also consider emerging regulatory layers, including epigenetic modifications and the microbiota-gut-brain axis, which have been implicated in feeding behaviour in other insects but remain largely unexplored in the silkworm. Finally, we highlight emerging technologies that will advance research in this field, providing a foundation for improving artificial diet-based sericulture.

titre: Gut microbiome depletion aggravates glial-mediated Alzheimer's disease pathology through inflammatory, metabolic, and proteostatic dysregulation
resume: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by chronic neuroinflammation, metabolic dysfunction, and impaired proteostasis. Emerging evidence suggests that the gut microbiome influences brain function through the gut-brain axis; however, the mechanisms by which this communication affects AD pathology remain poorly understood. In this study, we used humanized Drosophila AD models expressing human AD-related transgenes in glial cells to investigate how glial AD pathology influences the gut microbiome and how microbiome depletion affects behavior and disease progression. Our findings revealed significant alterations in the abundance of several gut microbial taxa, including Lactobacillus, Acetobacter, Enterococcus, Enterobacter, Pseudomonas, Leuconostoc, Providencia, and Gluconobacter, suggesting a potential interaction between the gut microbiome and AD progression. To further define the role of the gut microbiome in AD progression, we treated Drosophila with antibiotics to achieve substantial microbiome depletion (SMD) and evaluated the resulting behavioral, physiological, and molecular changes. Compared with conventional controls, flies with SMD exhibited enhanced inflammatory signaling and cell death, impaired autophagy, lipid dysregulation, and increased accumulation of amyloid β-42 (aβ42) and phospho-tau (pTau), with the extent of these changes varying among the different humanized AD models. These molecular alterations further exacerbated sleepcircadian disruption, altered locomotor performance, and worsened learning and memory deficits. Furthermore, we demonstrated a link between enhanced neuroinflammation and the accumulation of aβ42, pTau, and amyloid precursor protein (APP) proteins. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that gut microbiome depletion aggravates glial-mediated AD pathology through the coordinated disruption of inflammatory, metabolic, and proteostatic pathways, ultimately leading to behavioral dysfunction. These results identify the gut microbiome as a critical regulator of glial homeostasis and provide new insights into its contribution to the progression of neurodegenerative disorders.

titre: Cognitive disengagement syndrome and alexisomia: examining the moderating role of anxiety-depression symptoms, stress, and insomnia symptoms among a sample of Lebanese adults
resume: BACKGROUND: The interplay between body and mind is at the heart of processing bodily states. Alexisomia refers to the lack of somatic awareness, whereas cognitive disengagement syndrome (CDS) is a cluster of symptoms that reflect mental sluggishness, daydreaming, and hypoactivity. Given that interoceptive accuracy relies on attention to internal signals, the hypoactive characteristics of CDS may attenuate interoceptive processing; therefore, individuals with higher CDS traits might show diminished awareness of bodily states. This study investigates the association between CDS and alexisomia, as well as the moderating effect of anxiety-depression symptoms, stress, and insomnia symptoms. METHOD: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 877 Lebanese adults aged 18-70 years, recruited through snowball sampling. Data were collected using a Google Forms questionnaire that included the Adult Concentration Inventory, the Shitsu Taikan Sho Scale, the Stress Numerical Rating Scale, the Patient Health Questionnaire-4, and the Insomnia Severity Index. Of the participants, 64.3% were female, and 35.7% were male. RESULTS: The interaction models were adjusted over the following variables: marital status, education, and living situation. The CDS × anxiety-depression (B = -0.04, p = .011) and CDS × insomnia (B = -0.03, p = .002) interactions were significantly associated with alexisomia, whereas the CDS × stress interaction (B = -0.03, p = .076) was not statistically significant after applying heteroscedasticity-consistent standard errors. At low (-1 SD), mean, and high (+1 SD) levels of anxiety - depression and insomnia, higher CDS levels were significantly associated with higher levels of alexisomia. Additionally, higher levels of anxiety-depression and insomnia symptoms attenuated the positive association between CDS traits and alexisomia. CONCLUSION: Findings highlight an interplay between symptoms of cognitive disengagement and reduced somatic awareness, while emphasizing the importance of accounting for psychological distress and sleep disturbance when studying this relationship. Understanding these interactions provides a foundation for future longitudinal research to further clarify the nature and temporal relationships among these constructs.

titre: Fresh Osteochondral Allograft Transplantation as a Salvage Procedure Following Failed Fixation of Osteochondritis Dissecans of the Lateral Femoral Condyle: A Case Report
resume: BACKGROUND Osteochondritis dissecans (OCD) of the knee can progress to large osteochondral defects when fragment fixation fails, representing a reconstructive challenge in young active patients. Fresh osteochondral allograft transplantation (OCA) restores both the viable hyaline cartilage and subchondral bone and has emerged as a joint-preserving treatment for these lesions. However, reports describing OCA as a salvage procedure after failed OCD fixation remain limited. CASE REPORT A 19-year-old female patient who participated in competitive sports presented with recurrent pain and mechanical locking of the left knee after previous fixation of an OCD lesion of the lateral femoral condyle. Imaging demonstrated fixation failure, retained hardware, loose bodies, and an osteochondral defect measuring 25×12 mm. Open removal of the failed fixation and loose bodies was followed by fresh size-matched OCA using a press-fit technique. At the 24-month follow-up, the patient had returned to high-level athletic activity without mechanical symptoms. Clinical examination demonstrated functional range of motion and adequate quadriceps strength. The International Knee Documentation Committee subjective score was 93/100, and the Tegner Activity Scale score was 7, compared with a preinjury score of 8. Magnetic resonance imaging confirmed satisfactory graft incorporation without graft-related complications. CONCLUSIONS Fresh OCA may be considered as a joint-preserving salvage option after failed OCD fixation in carefully selected young patients. In this case, satisfactory graft incorporation, functional recovery, and return to preinjury recreational sports activities were observed at 24-month follow-up.
revue: The American journal of case reports

resume: A range of strategies, including dietary changes, selective pharmacotherapy, probiotics, and online interventions, are effective in managing IBS in community care settings. Tailoring these approaches to the individual's symptom profile and preferences is crucial.

titre: Genetic association and spatial cellular atlas analysis of irritable bowel syndrome and three psychiatric disorders
resume: R analysis scripts accompanying the study "Genetic association and spatial cellular atlas analysis of irritable bowel syndrome and three psychiatric disorders". This deposit contains 19 numbered R scripts for data preparation, SNP heritability and genetic correlation analyses (LDSC, HDL, SUPERGNOVA and GNOVA), tissue-specific S-LDSC, PLACO pleiotropy analysis, FUMA preparation and visualization, colocalization, circular-diagram preparation and visualization, shared-locus summaries, and gsMap analysis. Running the scripts requires the relevant input datasets, reference files, R packages and external tools. Local and server-specific paths must be adapted to the execution environment. This deposit contains analysis code only; input datasets and reference resources are not included. Version v2 corrects disease-trait configurations and related input/output names for IBS, BD, MDD and SCZ. Pairwise analyses target IBS–BD, IBS–MDD and IBS–SCZ; gsMap targets all four disorders. The preprocessing script now uses the corresponding OpenGWAS identifiers and omits unrelated data-source examples. The local GNOVA script includes all three IBS comparisons. Existing analytical parameters were retained. All 19 scripts passed R syntax parsing; the analyses were not rerun for this update. Author contributions: Chengcheng Wu, Ting Zhang and Qinghua Luo contributed equally to this work.Corresponding author: Chen Wang (wangchen_longhua@163.com).

titre: Shared genetic dimensions and disease-level heterogeneity across digestive diseases: data and code
resume: Data and executed analysis code supporting a multivariate genetic study of twelve digestive diseases. The release provides complete autosomal CORE9 factor-GWAS and Q_SNP results for LUM, HPB and IBD; source data for six main and nineteen supplementary figures; Supplementary Tables 1-40; native aggregate MVP covariance and SEM outputs; and historical analysis scripts, configurations, run records and environment metadata. Each factor export contains 3,563,691 input SNPs, of which 3,563,685 pass the recorded primary eligibility flags. The MVP comparison gives partial structural support; the prespecified depression and BMI contrasts do not pass their two-test correction. External GWAS are reused and the primary depression source includes MVP, so this is not fully sample-independent replication. Individual-level cohort data, third-party original GWAS and reference genotypes are not included. Original-source accessions, URLs and terms are documented. Project-derived data and documentation are CC BY 4.0; code is GNU GPL v3, with third-party rights preserved.

titre: The Mind as Knowledge and Experience: Accumulation, Thought Block, and Bodily Presence in Choice
resume: I propose an organizing model of the formal mind as knowledge and experience: reusableobservations and techniques, and the lived history from which they develop. Skills aretechniques trained through experience; habits are repeated patterns rather than a third substance.I call the architecture these processes train the metastructure: a proposed organization ofheuristics, reconstruction, anticipation, and usable continuity of thought, not a newly identifiedneural network. The model predicts that relevant learning can reduce both avoidable errors andstalled thinking, while fixation and bodily disruption can limit or reverse that benefit. I also arguethat bodily sensation, presence, and practical constraints matter as much to the person as mentalpersonality. My earlier phrase “more than half” is a qualitative generalization about thatinterplay, not a measured percentage. The account draws on memory research, expertise,predictive processing, and interoception without treating their findings as proof of the wholemodel. Eight predictions and two proposed studies distinguish the organizing assumptions fromtestable consequences. Companion manuscripts address incomplete knowledge of costs, sociallyshaped wanting, association between perspectives, and the deliberate experience of ordinaryboredom; those connections are proposals rather than independent evidence. No new data arereported.
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

titre: Molecular Computing, Distributed Visceral Neurobiology, and Multiscale Basal Cognition: The Architecture of Biological Intelligence
resume: Biological information processing spans engineered molecular circuits, microbial adaptation, tissue regulation and organismal interoception. This article synthesises DNA strand-displacement logic and associative memory, biomolecular phase separation, anticipatory microbial regulation, unicellular avoidance hierarchies, slime-mould dynamics, bacterial electrical communication, and enteric, cardiac and neuro-immune signal processing. These examples challenge a brain-exclusive account of adaptive information processing without establishing equivalence between cellular regulation, cognition and consciousness. Multiscale Competency Architecture and the Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere provide an interpretive framework for relating these scales. The article distinguishes primary experimental findings from formal models, conceptual proposals and a speculative 2026–2040 technological scenario. Persistent planarian pattern changes and artificial-embryogeny simulations motivate research into distributed physiological control, but do not establish general cancer therapies, universal competency thresholds or dated technological inevitabilities. The practical implication is a testable research programme integrating molecular and tissue-level interventions, with explicit evidential, clinical and governance limits. Critical scholarly synthesis. No new experimental data. Distinguishes verified findings, models and speculative foresight; includes explicit evidence boundaries.
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

titre: The Fleetmikewood Protocol: Epigenetic Gene Expression, Informational Engineering, and Designer Prayers
resume: Official Framework Clarification & Scope Update (Version 2.0) The Fleetmikewood Protocol is an open-access personal development and informational engineering framework focused exclusively on epigenetic gene expression, mind-body behavioral inputs, and contemplative practices—specifically structured self-hypnosis and Designer Prayers. Core Mechanism: Epigenetic Regulation While earlier preliminary notes explored broader theoretical terminology, the Fleetmikewood Protocol specifically addresses epigenetics—the biological regulatory layer that influences how genes are expressed (turned up or down) in response to environment, behavior, and psychological state. Behavioral & Cognitive Inputs: The protocol utilizes AI-assisted linguistic scripting, structured self-hypnosis, and adaptable Designer Prayers to foster focused mental states, emotional regulation, and stress reduction. Mind-Body Signaling: Grounded in established mind-body and psychoneuroimmunology concepts, consistent stress-reduction routines help downregulate chronic stress signaling and support healthy cellular repair, autonomic balance, and a 120+ year healthspan baseline. Epigenetic Legacy: By optimizing daily habits, stress resilience, and intentional cognitive routines, the framework aims to promote healthier physiological regulation across generations. Scope & Attribution The Fleetmikewood Protocol is an open-access personal wellness and informational engineering framework—not a clinical treatment or medical procedure. Maintained as an open-source resource by Michael Ray Fleetwood (fleetmikewood).

titre: Designer Prayers: The Fleetmikewood Protocol & The Read-Write Epigenetic Standard
resume: Designer Prayers: The Fleetmikewood Protocol Exploring the intersection of artificial intelligence, epigenetics, and human potential: What is the Fleetmikewood Protocol? Introduced by Michael Fleetwood (fleetmikewood), the Fleetmikewood Protocol outlines a conceptual framework known as Genetic Informational Engineering or the "Read-Write Epigenetic Standard." Unlike traditional molecular gene-editing technologies (such as CRISPR or peptides) that physically modify DNA sequences in a laboratory setting, this methodology focuses on non-invasive, information-driven epigenetic modulation. It frames the human genome not as a static vault, but as a dynamic read-write system where structured intent, autonomic conditioning, and cognitive signaling actively influence gene expression. Core Architecture AI-Designed Behavioral & Spiritual Programming Utilizing generative AI to curate precision self-hypnosis and custom prayer scripts tailored to an individual’s personal beliefs (aligned with their preferred understanding of God or higher focus) and baseline health goals. Epigenetic Signal Optimization & Biological Mechanisms Implementing structured nightly self-hypnosis and focus modules to lower physiological stress pathways, minimize chronic cortisol exposure, and promote cellular homeostasis. How Epigenetics Changes: Mind-body signaling, focused intention, and autonomic down-regulation alter chemical tags—such as DNA methylation and histone modifications—attached to chromatin. These epigenetic switches govern whether specific genes are turned "on" or "off" without altering the underlying nucleotide sequence. Genetic Informational Engineering & Transgenerational Potential Passing down these personalized AI-designed prayer and hypnosis protocols through family lineages to establish a multi-generational practice. Multigenerational DNA Impact: While single-generation epigenetic shifts modulate immediate health, sustained multi-generational practice aims to harness transgenerational epigenetic inheritance. Over successive generations, compounding positive epigenetic markers can alter germline signaling, systematically upgrading hereditary health baselines and guiding evolutionary DNA expression across descendants. Example Precision Prayer Script Below is a concise prayer script demonstrating how structured intent and baseline health goals are focused toward cellular repair and biological longevity: Focus: Cellular Repair & Baseline Vitality (Evening Protocol) "God, please upgrade my healing to my best self and for extreme longevity. Thank you for my existence. Amen." Perspective & Dialogue While traditional medical science views these practices through the lens of mind-body signaling and stress modulation, the Fleetmikewood Protocol explores how standardized, multi-generational informational inputs can shape human biological expression and hereditary potential over generations. Whether viewed as a speculative boundary of bioprogramming or an advanced evolution of mind-body legacy, it opens a compelling dialogue on how structured intent shapes human biology.
