titre: A COMPREHENSIVE SYSTEMATIC REVIEW: DIALECTICAL BEHAVIOUR THERAPY (DBT) AS THE GOLD-STANDARD PSYCHOTHERAPY FOR BORDERLINE PERSONALITY DISORDER
resume: Introduction: Borderline personality disorder (BPD) is a severe psychiatric condition with lifetime prevalence of 0.7-2.7% and suicide rate approaching 8-10%. Dialectical behaviour therapy (DBT), the first manualised psychotherapy developed for chronically suicidal BPD patients, is widely designated the gold-standard psychosocial treatment. This review synthesised primary evidence across all outcome domains to determine whether the evidence supports this designation. Methods: The study strictly adhered to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines. Eligible designs comprised RCTs, controlled non-randomised trials, cohort, case-control, cross-sectional and observational studies evaluating DBT in BPD populations. Systematic reviews were excluded from primary tabulation but retained for contextualisation. Two reviewers independently screened, extracted data and appraised risk of bias using RoB 2, ROBINS-I and Newcastle-Ottawa Scale; certainty graded with GRADE. Synthesis was narrative with structured vote-counting across seventeen outcome domains. Results: Sixty primary studies (up to 2026) encompassing >3,400 participants across 13 countries were included: 34 RCTs, 4 controlled non-randomised trials, 12 prospective cohorts, 4 retrospective studies, 4 mediation analyses and 2 economic evaluations. Statistically significant DBT benefits were demonstrated for non-suicidal self-injury and total self-harm, suicide attempts (hazard ratio 2.66 favouring DBT versus expert therapy, p=0.005), treatment retention (hazard ratio 3.2, p<0.001), psychiatric hospitalisation (up to 89% reduction in hospital days), emotion dysregulation, depressive symptoms, anger, comorbid substance use and PTSD, quality of life, medication load and cost-effectiveness. In head-to-head comparisons against other structured psychotherapies—general psychiatric management, schema therapy, mentalisation-based treatment, conversational model, CAMS—DBT produced large within-group improvements statistically equivalent rather than superior. Durability extended to 12.4 years in adolescent trials. Risk of bias was low in 30%, moderate in 50%, high in 20%; GRADE certainty was moderate for self-harm and retention, low for most other domains. Discussion: DBT demonstrates coherent, reproducible benefit across behavioural, affective, functional, service-utilisation and economic domains, sustained over follow-up exceeding a decade. Mechanistic evidence converges on emotion regulation capacity, behavioural skills acquisition, hopelessness reduction and validating therapeutic relationship as operative pathways. The principal qualification is equivalence, not superiority, against other well-specified BPD-specific psychotherapies; DBT's gold-standard status rests on breadth, replication, transportability and unique replicated effect on suicidal behaviour, not on demonstrated superiority over all active specialist comparators. Conclusion: DBT is supported by the largest, longest and most methodologically diverse primary evidence base of any BPD psychotherapy, with significant benefits across seventeen outcome domains. The gold-standard designation is empirically defensible as reference-standard status against usual and non-specialist care, and as equal-first-line among structured disorder-specific psychotherapies. Priorities include adequately powered equivalence trials, trials in male and culturally diverse populations, evaluation of briefer and digitally delivered formats, and implementation research in low- and middle-income settings.
revue: The Indonesian Journal of General Medicine

titre: Effectiveness of the Coping with Depression Course in Reducing Depressive Symptoms and Suicidal Ideation among Pakistani Adolescents: A Randomized Control Trial
resume: Depression is a problem that affects adolescents worldwide, contributing to an array of complications such as interpersonal problems and associated negative behavioral and emotional outcomes. Early, school-based interventions are crucial to address these concerns and promote positive youth development. The objective of the study was to investigate the effectiveness of the Adolescents Coping with Depression Course (CWD-A), in reducing symptoms of depression along with suicidal ideation among adolescents in Pakistan. The present study utilized a randomized control trial pre-post-test design. The sample consisted of 60 participants of age range 15-18 who were enrolled and further divided into the experimental and control group respectively. Among them, 57 completed the intervention. The experimental group received 10 sessions of the CWD-A program in 5 weeks. Pre- and post-assessments were conducted to determine the efficacy of the program. Descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, independent samples t-test, and paired sample t-test were applied to analyze and interpret the data. Post-intervention, the experimental group demonstrated significantly lower scores than the control group for both depression (M = 14.37, SD = 6.06 vs. M = 29.17, SD = 9.36; 95% CI [-18.97, -10.62], p < .001) and suicidal ideation (M = 4.62, SD = 5.39 vs. M = 11.06, SD = 14.13; 95% CI [-12.62, -1.34], p = .016). The overall outcomes suggest that CBT-based prevention programs can reduce depressive symptomology and enhance the mental health outcomes of adolescents. This thus emphasizes the need for inculcating structural, evidence-based interventions in schools to reduce the burden of mental health difficulties, and foster psychological well-being.

titre: INVOLUNTARY GENITAL SENSATIONS IN OBSESSIVE-COMPULSIVE DISORDER: A SCOPING REVIEW
resume: This is a protocol for a scoping review aimed at mapping the existing literature on the phenomenon of groinal sensations (involuntary/intrusive genital sensations, often described as resembling sexual arousal) in individuals affected by OCD. The objective is to clarify how the phenomenon has been named, described, defined and measured, as well as to identify gaps in the literature, given that it is a common description in psychoeducational sources and support groups for people with the disorder. It follows the JBI methodology for scoping reviews and the PRISMA-ScR reporting guideline, with eligibility criteria structured by Population, Concept and Context (PCC).

titre: Mapping the translational maturity of biological markers in perinatal mental disorders: a systematic scoping review
resume: This systematic scoping review maps human studies of biological markers in six perinatal mental disorders (depression, anxiety, postpartum psychosis, bipolar disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder and childbirth-related post-traumatic stress disorder) and classifies each marker by translational maturity, from biological association to externally validated, clinically useful prediction. The registration is submitted retrospectively, after completion of the database search and title/abstract screening and before full-text screening and data extraction. It supersedes an earlier, jointly registered protocol ("From Multidomain Markers to Clinical Utility in Perinatal Mental Disorders: A Systematic Cross-Disorder Integrative Review", OSF Registries, registered 11 September 2026, currently under embargo) that was not continued after a change in the author team.

titre: Eating Disorders and Musculoskeletal Health Beyond Bone Density: A Scoping Review of Soft-Tissue Injury, Orthopaedic Surgery Utilization, and Surgical Outcomes
resume: A scoping review, following JBI methodology and reported per PRISMA-ScR, mapping the evidence on how eating disorders (anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa, binge-eating disorder, ARFID, OSFED, and relative energy deficiency in sport / female athlete triad) relate to musculoskeletal soft-tissue injury, orthopaedic surgery utilization, fracture healing, and perioperative and postoperative outcomes of orthopaedic surgery: musculoskeletal outcomes beyond bone mineral density and fracture incidence, which existing meta-analyses already cover.

titre: Association of Blastocystis with the gut bacteria abundance and serum levels of serotonin in patients with irritable bowel syndrome; a case-control study
resume: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a chronic disorder of gut-brain axis. Although Blastocystis colonization has been reported in patients with IBS, the role of this parasite in modulation of the gut microbiota composition and the serotonin levels remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate association of Blastocystis colonization with serotonin-pathway-associated bacteria and serotonin levels in patients with IBS and healthy individuals. Sixty participants (30 IBS patients and 30 healthy controls), were divided into four groups based on the presence of Blastocystis. The relative abundance of Klebsiella spp., Bacteroides fragilis, Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., and Lactobacillus spp. were investigated using target-specific primers by real-time PCR. Concentrations of serum serotonin were measured using an ELISA kit. Data were analyzed using appropriate statistical tests in SPSS and R software. The relative abundance of Klebsiella spp. (P = 0.009) and B. fragilis (P = 0.004) differed significantly among study groups. The PERMANOVA analysis confirmed a significant difference in the overall composition of the target bacteria across four groups (R² = 0.144, P = 0.002). Serum serotonin levels were significantly differed among the groups (P = 0.032), with the highest level in the Blastocystis-positive IBS (BPI) group. Pairwise comparisons revealed significant differences between the BPI and BNH groups (P = 0.006), as well as between the BPI and BPH groups (P = 0.018). Furthermore, a significant positive association was observed between the relative abundance of Klebsiella spp. and serum serotonin levels (r = 0.454, P = 0.045). The findings suggest that Blastocystis may be associated with alterations in serotonin levels by modifying gut microbiota composition and influencing tryptophan metabolism. However, the precise mechanism linking Blastocystis, gut microbiota, and serotonin metabolism has yet to be fully elucidated, highlighting the need for further research.

titre: Differences in resilience and coping styles in women with asthma, dyspepsia, and a control cohort: A regional cross-sectional study
resume: BackgroundIndividuals with asthma experience more psychiatric comorbidities than the general population, and psychological stress modulates their immunity. Altered emotions and coping mechanisms often coincide with functional gastrointestinal disorders, and the "gut-brain axis" explains the interactions between the nervous system and intestinal functions, including reduced microbiota diversity and mucosal immune activation. The "gut-lung axis" explains the frequency of functional gastrointestinal disorders in individuals with atopic conditions, particularly asthma. Female gender and premenopausal hormonal status are strongly associated with specific immunomediated and functional gastrointestinal pathways, leading to a higher prevalence of conditions such as asthma and functional dyspepsia (FD) in this population.ObjectivesThis study aimed to explore the differences in psychiatric disorders, lifestyle, resilience, and coping styles between premenopausal women with and without asthma or FD.DesignRegional, cross-sectional study.MethodsThe study included 110 women aged 19-46 years (mean 31.71, SD 7.40) recruited from health centers and outpatient clinics in one region of Croatia. Among the participants, 36% had asthma, 20% had dyspepsia, 15% had both, and 29% had no comorbidities. Data collection involved interviews and questionnaires assessing resilience and coping styles. Chi-square tests and Welch ANOVA were used to analyze group differences.ResultsNo statistically significant differences were found in sociodemographic characteristics or lifestyle habits between the groups. Among coping strategies, positive reframing showed significant differences, being more pronounced in individuals with asthma than in those with FD 7.2 (1.14) vs. 5.82 (1.94) (p = 0.009). Resilience was higher in individuals without comorbidities than in those with FD, 3.54 (0.8) vs. 2.83 (0.62) (p = 0.006). Individuals without asthma and FD diagnoses scored significantly lower on the PHQ-15 questionnaire than those with asthma and both asthma and FD 6.84 (4.26) vs. 8.82 (4.62) vs. 14.44 (5.30) (p < 0.001).ConclusionOur findings highlight the importance of psychological factors in treating FD and asthma, considering the "gut-brain" and "gut-lung" connections. They can also help healthcare providers develop targeted psychological support to improve disease management and well-being in patients with FD and asthma.

titre: Bidirectional Microbiota-Gut-Brain Communication in Anorexia Nervosa: Mechanistic Insights and Therapeutic Perspectives
resume: Abstract: The gut-brain axis (GBA), particularly communication between the gut microbiota (GM) and the brain, has become a major focus in neuropsychiatric research because of its role in appetite regulation, energy metabolism, immune function, and behavior. Anorexia nervosa (AN) is a severe eating disorder with high morbidity and mortality, but the contribution of GBA dysfunction to its pathogenesis remains incompletely defined. This review synthesizes evidence linking GM dysbiosis with AN and organizes the current literature around neural, endocrine, immune, and metabolic pathways. It also summarizes altered brain regions and circuits implicated in AN and discusses how peripheral microbial changes may interact with central regulatory systems. Current evidence supports a multidirectional model in which GM alterations, intestinal barrier function, vagal signaling, hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis activity, immune activation, microbial metabolites, and neurocircuit dysfunction may reinforce disordered appetite and weight regulation. Microbiota-targeted strategies, including probiotics, prebiotics, fermented foods, dietary modulation, and lifestyle interventions, may offer adjunctive therapeutic potential, but clinical evidence remains preliminary. Future studies should use longitudinal multi-omics designs, mechanistic animal models, and rigorously controlled clinical trials to determine whether microbiome changes are drivers, consequences, or modifiers of AN. Plain Language Summary: Anorexia nervosa is a serious eating disorder that affects both mental and physical health. Growing evidence suggests that microorganisms living in the intestine may communicate with the brain through nerves, hormones, immune signals, and microbial metabolites. This two-way communication is known as the microbiota–gut–brain axis. People with AN often show changes in gut microbial composition, but it remains unclear whether these changes contribute to the illness, result from severe dietary restriction and weight loss, or both. This review summarizes current human and animal evidence and explains how gut microorganisms may interact with appetite, stress responses, inflammation, and brain circuits. It also discusses emerging microbiota-targeted approaches, while emphasizing that current clinical evidence remains limited and these strategies should be considered experimental or adjunctive rather than established treatments. Keywords: anorexia nervosa, gut-brain axis, gut microbiota, eating disorders, public health

titre: Optimizing cognitive and behavioural recovery after stroke: clinical integration of dietary supplements with a focus on ω-3 fatty acids
resume: Stroke remains a leading cause of long-term disability worldwide, with many survivors experiencing persistent cognitive and behavioural impairments despite advancements in acute management. Post-stroke neurorecovery is often incomplete, contributing to dementia, depression, and reduced quality of life, particularly in low- and middle-income settings where access to advanced rehabilitation and therapeutics is limited. This highlights an urgent need for accessible, adjunctive strategies that can enhance functional recovery. Emerging preclinical evidence indicates that dietary supplements can modulate key biological processes underlying neurorecovery, including neuroplasticity, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial function, and synaptic remodeling. In this narrative review, we examine the role of major classes of nutraceuticals such as omega-3 fatty acids, vitamins, minerals, polyphenols, and amino acids in supporting cognitive and behavioural recovery after stroke with particular emphasis on omega-3 fatty acids, given their central role in neuronal membrane integrity, lipid-mediated signaling, and resolution of inflammation. We integrate mechanistic insights with preclinical and clinical data explicitly highlighting that theoretical models and basic research demonstrate significant promise, while current clinical evidence remains heterogeneous and frequently inconclusive. We discuss how dietary supplementation might be strategically incorporated alongside conventional rehabilitation paradigms including physiotherapy cognitive training, and pharmacotherapy. We further highlight emerging concepts such as the gut-brain axis, precision nutrition, and biomarker-guided interventions, which are shaping the future of personalized neurorehabilitation. Ultimately, while dietary supplements offer a promising, cost-effective and accessible adjunctive approach, their current clinical utility is constrained by mixed translational efficacy. Overcoming these limitations will require rigorous patient selection, optimized timing and shift towards evidence-based personalized multimodal strategies. This will be essential to fully harness their therapeutic potential in improving cognitive and behavioural outcomes in stroke recovery.

titre: Beyond the brain: curcumin as a multi-target neuropharmacological modulator of the gut-brain axis in major depressive disorder and Parkinson's disease
resume: Curcumin, the principal polyphenol of Curcuma longa, has been proposed as a multi-target neuropharmacological agent for neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders. We propose that major depressive disorder (MDD) and Parkinson's disease (PD) share a convergent gut-brain axis dysfunction, and that curcumin can serve as a pharmacological probe to test whether this convergent pathway is causally relevant. This narrative review evaluates that hypothesis. We conducted a structured literature search across PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and CNKI using predefined search terms. This is a narrative review with a structured search strategy rather than a systematic review; no formal risk-of-bias assessment or meta-analysis was performed. From 2256 identified records, 112 primary studies were selected for synthesis after dual screening and consensus resolution. Findings should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than as a quantitative synthesis. We propose a differential metabolite-sensitivity threshold model as a testable hypothesis: shared dysbiosis-related metabolic and inflammatory disturbances may affect serotonergic function earlier than dopaminergic function because depressed mood manifests at modest neurotransmitter deficits, whereas nigrostriatal dopaminergic neurons possess substantial compensatory reserve. Preclinical studies indicate that curcumin exerts prebiotic-like effects, promotes short-chain fatty acid-producing bacteria, suppresses NF-κB-dependent neuroinflammation, restores BDNF signaling, inhibits α-synuclein aggregation, and improves depressive- and PD-like behaviors. These actions map onto convergent gut-brain pathways involving short-chain fatty acid deficiency, tryptophan-kynurenine imbalance, monoaminergic precursor depletion, and neuroinflammation. This model generates four testable predictions: (P1: functional dysbiosis convergence; P2: temporal precedence of depressed mood; P3: curcumin's multi-node modulation; and P4: clinical benefit with adequate bioavailability). Preclinical evidence supports functional convergence (P1), temporal asymmetry (P2), and curcumin's multi-target actions (P3), but clinical benefit in MDD-PD comorbidity (P4) remains untested. However, curcumin's clinical translation remains limited by poor oral bioavailability (~ 1% for standard extracts) and the absence of randomized trials in MDD-PD comorbidity. We conclude that the convergent gut-brain hypothesis is plausible, partially supported, and directly testable, and we specify the minimal studies required to confirm or falsify it.

titre: β-glucan mitigates necrotizing enterocolitis-induced long-term cognitive impairment by remodeling gut microbiota and restoring tryptophan metabolite IAA-mediated gut-brain signaling
resume: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is a life-threatening gastrointestinal disorder prevalent in preterm infants, and most NEC survivors suffer from persistent cognitive deficits and neurodevelopmental disorders, with no targeted therapeutic approaches available to date. β-glucan has been documented to regulate gut microbiota, suppress inflammation, and exert neuroprotective effects, yet its efficacy and molecular mechanisms against NEC-associated cognitive dysfunction remain unclear. In this study, we established a mouse NEC model with β-glucan intervention to explore its gut-brain axis protective effects. Behavioral assessments verified that β-glucan significantly rescued NEC-induced cognitive impairments, with comparable therapeutic effects between low and high doses. Multi-omics analyses demonstrated that β-glucan effectively reversed NEC-triggered gut microbiota dysbiosis and restored disrupted tryptophan metabolism, notably elevating the level of indole-3-acetic acid (IAA). Fecal microbiota transplantation and exogenous IAA supplementation recapitulated the neuroprotective phenotypes of β-glucan, which inhibited excessive hippocampal microglial activation and neuroinflammation, and repaired impaired synaptic ultrastructure and plasticity. Further mechanistic validation confirmed that IAA mediated neuroprotection via activating the AHR/MAP2K3/p38 signaling cascade. Collectively, β-glucan alleviates NEC-related cognitive injury through modulating the gut microbiota-tryptophan metabolism-IAA axis and subsequent AHR/MAP2K3/p38 signaling activation. This study elucidates a novel gut‒brain axis regulatory mechanism of β-glucan, providing reliable preclinical evidence for the clinical prevention and treatment of long-term neurodevelopmental complications in NEC survivors.

titre: Ginkgolide B alleviates granulomatous mastitis with gut microbiota remodeling and altered macrophage responses
resume: Granulomatous mastitis (GM) is an inflammatory breast disease linked to Corynebacterium kroppenstedtii, causing pain, abscesses, and reduced quality of life. The gut-mammary axis suggests intestinal homeostasis modulates peripheral immunity. Ginkgolide B (GB), a bioactive diterpene lactone, has anti-inflammatory effects, but its role in GM is unclear. In GM mice, GB significantly alleviated mammary inflammation and fibrosis, reducing cytokines, collagen deposition, and pathological lesions, while also restoring colonic mucosal thickness, Alcian blue-positive mucosal area, and tight-junction proteins (occludin, zonula occludens-1, and claudin-3), consistent with improved barrier-associated features. 16S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) sequencing showed GB partially reversed gut dysbiosis, restoring microbial diversity, enriching taxa (Ligilactobacillus, Muribaculaceae), and reducing the disease-associated expansion of genera (Lactobacillus, Dubosiella, Faecalibaculum). Metabolomics identified α-linolenic acid (ALA) metabolism as a key pathway, with ALA and related metabolites recovered after GB treatment, and this shift correlated with microbial remodeling. Antibiotic pretreatment attenuated GB's protective effects, supporting the involvement of the gut microbiota. GB treatment was associated with lower CD80, CD86, and iNOS and higher CD206 expression in whole mammary tissue. Mammary IL-1β, IL-6, and TGF-β1 were reduced, whereas the decrease in TNF-α was not statistically significant. Direct GB treatment also modulated inflammatory responses in RAW264.7 cells, supporting a direct effect of GB on macrophage-related responses. Overall, GB alleviated experimental GM in association with intestinal, microbial, metabolic, and macrophage-related changes, supporting a potential link between gut microbiota-associated metabolic remodeling and macrophage responses.

titre: Changes in wellbeing, self-compassion and alexithymia in a proof of principle trial with MDMA-assisted therapy for major depressive disorder
resume: BACKGROUND: Transdiagnostic factors such as emotion regulation, self-compassion, and alexithymia influence the development and outcome of psychiatric conditions, including major depressive disorder (MDD) and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). 3,4-Methylenedioxymethamphetamine-assisted therapy (MDMA-AT) has shown efficacy in reducing PTSD and depressive symptoms. This study examined MDMA-AT effects on alexithymia, self-compassion, and well-being in MDD, assessing durability and links to long-term outcomes. METHODS: Data were drawn from an open-label MDMA-AT trial (EudraCT 2021-000805-26) including twelve participants with moderate to severe MDD (baseline MADRS M(SD) = 29.6(4.9)). Participants received two MDMA sessions with manualized psychotherapy (three preparatory, six integration). Outcomes were assessed at baseline, post-treatment (8 weeks), and long-term follow-up (≥3 months) using the Toronto Alexithymia Scale (TAS-20), Self-Compassion Scale (SCS), and Warwick-Edinburgh Mental Wellbeing Scale (WEMWBS). Changes were analyzed with linear mixed models; estimated marginal means and post-hoc comparisons explored time effects. RESULTS: MDMA-AT significantly improved alexithymia, self-compassion, and well-being. TAS-20 decreased by -11.75 post-treatment and -16.42 at follow-up (both p < 0.001). SCS increased by 0.73 post-treatment (p = 0.017) and 1.07 at follow-up (p = 0.001). WEMWBS improved by 17.30 at both timepoints (p < 0.001). All SCS subscales improved; common humanity and isolation reached significance only at follow-up. Improvements were driven by therapy responders (9/12). Eight participants had at least borderline alexithymia at baseline; none did at follow-up. Self-compassion shifted from seven low and one high at baseline to seven high and one low at follow-up. CONCLUSIONS: MDMA-AT for MDD produced lasting improvements in alexithymia, self-compassion, and well-being, supporting its potential for durable psychological recovery beyond symptom reduction.

titre: When defense becomes compulsion: An evolutionary and circuit framework for obsessive-compulsive disorder
resume: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is characterized by intrusive thoughts and repetitive behaviors that are frequently organized around preventing potential harm. Although existing neurobiological models have focused on abnormalities in cortico-striato-thalamo-cortical circuits, habit formation, and cognitive control, they provide a less complete explanation for why compulsions preferentially take the form of precautionary actions. Here, we propose an evolutionary and circuit-level framework in which compulsive behavior is understood as a pathological dysregulation of neural systems that normally support adaptive defense. Integrating evidence from human studies with circuit-level findings from rodent studies, we organize defensive control into three sequential but interacting stages: threat appraisal, defensive action selection and execution, and post-defense safety assessment. During threat appraisal, abnormalities in sensory salience, threat valuation, contextual gating, and interoceptive processing may increase the salience or threat value of ambiguous cues. During action selection and execution, intolerance of uncertainty, impaired behavioral flexibility, corticostriatal dysfunction, and negative reinforcement may bias behavior toward premature and repetitive threat-reducing actions that can become increasingly habitual. Following defensive action, impaired outcome evaluation and safety-state updating may prevent successful actions from generating stable signals of safety or completion, allowing defensive responding to persist despite objective threat reduction. By organizing OCD-related circuitry according to when it contributes to defensive processing rather than solely where abnormalities occur, this framework integrates threat-based, corticostriatal, habit, and safety-learning accounts into a process-based model of how adaptive defense may transition into persistent compulsive behavior. This framework may help map stage-specific dysfunction onto symptom heterogeneity and guide more targeted interventions.

titre: The efficacy of evidence-based psychotherapy on functional outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis
resume: Mental health conditions, including anxiety, depression, and adjustment disorders, are leading causes of disability. While psychotherapies reduce psychological symptoms, their specific impact on functional recovery remains less defined, as functioning is often treated as a secondary outcome. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to identify which interventions improve functioning in adults with common mental health conditions. We searched PubMed and PsycInfo (2014-2024) for randomized controlled trials comparing evidence-based psychological interventions against active or inactive comparators on functional outcome measures. Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) moderately improved global functioning compared to inactive comparators (7 studies; d = 0.41 [95% CI = 0.13, 0.70]; I2 = 81.29%). Statistical heterogeneity was explained by the study focus either solely on depression (2 studies; d = -0.02 [95% CI = -0.24, 0.20]; I2 = 0.00%) or on multiple mental health conditions (5 studies; d = 0.56 [95% CI = 0.44, 0.69]; I2 = 0.00%). Pooled estimates from three studies indicated a moderate improvement in mental functioning associated with CBT (d = 0.33 [95% CI = 0.15, 0.52]; I2 = 0.00) but no meaningful change in physical functioning (d = 0.10 [95% CI = -0.11, 0.32]; I2 = 21.37%). Evidence for other modalities or active-comparator superiority was inconclusive, and overall study quality was constrained by high risk of bias. CBT may be an effective in improving functional outcomes among adults with common mental health conditions, though superiority over other active therapies remains inconclusive. Future research should prioritize functioning outcomes to evaluate how psychotherapies facilitate functional recovery.

titre: Interventions for anxiety, burnout, and resilience in university students: a systematic review with implications for mental health nursing practice
resume: This systematic review examines anxiety and burnout among students in higher education, with a focus on mental health nursing interventions within multidisciplinary university mental health and student support services. A comprehensive search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, PsycINFO, and ERIC was conducted for studies published between January 2010 and March 2024, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261342279) on 17 March 2026. A total of 38 studies met inclusion criteria. Findings indicate that academic pressure, financial strain, social isolation, and digital stress are key contributors to student anxiety and burnout, while resilience and social support serve as important protective factors. Effective interventions include cognitive-behavioral therapy, mindfulness-based approaches, peer support programs, and digital mental health tools. However, barriers such as stigma, limited access to services, and cultural influences affect help-seeking behaviors. The findings highlight translational implications for mental health nursing practice within multidisciplinary teams, including opportunities for nurses to contribute to the delivery, coordination, or advocacy for these interventions according to their professional competencies and training. However, most included studies did not directly evaluate nurse-delivered interventions, and the findings may be relevant to a range of health and mental health professionals working in university support services. Thus, the evidence supports translational recommendations rather than direct evidence of nursing intervention efficacy. Integrated, multi-level strategies combining individual, peer, and institutional approaches are essential to promote student well-being and address mental health challenges in higher education.

titre: Microbial genetic variation drives host social traits via agmatine and NO-mediated cGMP-PKG pathways
resume: Abstract The gut microbiota plays a vital role in regulating host physiology and behavior through its influence on the microbiota-gut-brain axis. Despite extensive research linking gut microbiota diversity to host behaviors, the genetic and molecular mechanisms underlying microbial regulation of social behaviors remain poorly understood. In this study, a screening for E. coli single-gene knockout mutants that increased social behaviors of C. elegans identified speB and narG as key E. coli genes regulating C. elegans aggregation. speB mutant increased the production and secretion of agmatine, while narG mutant E. coli reduced NO levels in C. elegans . Mechanistically, this study found that agmatine and NO regulated C. elegans aggregation via cGMP-PKG pathway. These findings deepen our understanding of the molecular basis of host-microbe interactions and provide new insights into the regulation of social behaviors by gut microbiota.

titre: Hand-washing frequency, gastric histopathology, and depressive symptom burden in adults undergoing upper gastrointestinal endoscopy: a structural equation modeling study
resume: Abstract Depressive symptoms are common among patients referred for upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, but their relation to mucosal pathology is unclear. We examined whether gastric histopathological severity links lifestyle exposures to depressive symptom burden in 442 adults undergoing endoscopy at two tertiary care hospitals in Pakistan, 320 of whom had gastric biopsies. Depressive symptom burden (five DSM-5-derived items) and gastric severity (four Updated Sydney System markers) were modeled as latent variables using structural equation modeling. An abrupt shift in patient characteristics and histology grades during recruitment was identified and adjusted for. In the primary model (CFI = 0.971; RMSEA = 0.040), less frequent hand washing was associated with higher depressive symptom burden (β = 0.23, 95% CI 0.06–0.39) but not with gastric severity (β = −0.11, 95% CI − 0.25 to 0.03). Gastric severity was not associated with symptom burden (β = 0.14, 95% CI − 0.06 to 0.35), and the indirect effect through gastric severity was null. The hand-washing association persisted in all six sensitivity analyses, whereas an apparent hand-washing–pathology association appeared only without adjustment for recruitment period. Depressive symptom burden in these patients was unrelated to mucosal pathology but tracked reduced self-care, supporting symptom screening irrespective of endoscopic findings.

titre: Long-term health-related quality of life in a complete-case subgroup of disease-free survivors after pancreatic resection: A single-centre exploratory study
resume: Abstract Background Health-related quality of life (HRQoL) has become an important outcome measure following pancreatic resection, particularly because postoperative morbidity remains high despite improvements in perioperative mortality. Although short- and mid-term changes in HRQoL over time have been described, data on long-term outcomes in disease-free survivors remain limited. This study explored longitudinal HRQoL changes in a complete-case subgroup of disease-free survivors after pancreatic resection and contextualized long-term outcomes against general population reference values. Methods This single-centre exploratory longitudinal study assessed HRQoL preoperatively and during follow-up using the validated EORTC QLQ-C30 and QLQ-PAN26 questionnaires. Assessments were grouped into baseline, early postoperative follow-up (1–3 months), and long-term follow-up. Seventeen of 115 initially scheduled patients (14.8%), corresponding to 17 of 67 patients who entered longitudinal HRQoL follow-up (25.4%), were disease-free and had complete data across all three analytical periods. Changes over time were analyzed using Friedman’s test with Kendall’s W as the effect size measure, and the results were descriptively compared with Slovenian general population reference values. All analyses were exploratory and limited to these 17 complete-case disease-free survivors. Results Nominal unadjusted p-values below 0.05 were observed for role functioning ( p = 0.014), social functioning ( p = 0.004), financial difficulties ( p = 0.029), weight loss ( p = 0.002), future worries ( p < 0.001), and planning of activities ( p < 0.001). HRQoL deterioration was most pronounced in the early postoperative period, followed by improvement at long-term follow-up. In the descriptive unmatched comparison, selected functional domains at long-term follow-up approached general population reference values, while insomnia, fatigue, and digestive disturbances persisted. Conclusions In this exploratory analysis of 17 highly selected complete-case disease-free survivors, HRQoL declined in the early postoperative period and improved at long-term follow up in several domains. These findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating and should not be generalized beyond comparable complete-case survivor populations.

titre: Reframing Autistic Elopement and Drowning Fatalities as Involuntary Interoception Blackouts and Motor Planning Paralysis
resume: A PARENT’S OBSERVATION & RESEARCH HYPOTHESIS Title: Reframing Autistic Elopement and Drowning Fatalities as Involuntary Interoception Blackouts and Motor Planning Paralysis Author: Lauren Brown, Independent Parent Researcher Date: Friday, November 6, 2026 Status: Citizen-Science Open Letter and Theoretical Framework 1. Abstract This framework challenges the mainstream clinical and educational paradigm that classifies elopement (wandering) and subsequent drowning fatalities in autistic individuals as a behavioral choice, "work avoidance," “sensory seeking” and "lack of safety awareness." Utilizing a multi-system neuro-metabolic model, this paper proposes that elopement is an automated, high-speed autonomic survival loop triggered when acute environmental, sensory, or physiological stress breaches an individual's metabolic threshold. When the nervous system enters an absolute fight-or-flight adrenaline hijack, the prefrontal cortex goes dark, inducing a profound interoception blackout that leaves the individual physically unable to process internal physiological danger signals. Furthermore, we document how the sudden physical shock of entering water causes an immediate neurological lock—an acute motor planning paralysis (apraxia)—that prevents the brain from calculating and coordinating the limb movements required to surface. We advocate for a complete transition away from behavioral tracking toward universal environmental safety and biological sanctuary. 2. The Mechanics of the Autonomic Flight Reflex Mainstream behaviorists utilize Functional Behavior Assessments (FBAs) to attribute elopement to surface-level motivations, such as attention-seeking or escaping an academic task. This framework refutes that narrative, mapping elopement as a pure, automated biological reflex: The Threshold Breach: When an individual with an inherited sensitive mitochondrial baseline faces compounding stressors—such as severe muscle tightness (hypertonia), internal gastrointestinal pain (constipation), or overwhelming sensory environments—their primary cellular energy (ATP) hits absolute zero. The Amygdala Hijack: The brain senses a literal life-or-death energy emergency. The sympathetic nervous system instantly takes over, flooding the body with a massive surge of adrenaline. The Involuntary Flight: At the millisecond of the surge, the conscious, reasoning mind is completely decoupled. The body moves on absolute instinct to flee the source of stress. It is a physiological panic response to find safety, entirely unconstrained by learned rules or verbal commands. 3. The Interoception Blackout and Perceptual Blindness When an individual is thrust into this intense survival loop, their sensory processing grid undergoes a severe, temporary degradation: Perceptual Tunnel Vision: The massive adrenaline flood causes absolute blindness to external environmental variables. The individual cannot process moving vehicles, traffic patterns, or terrain hazards because the brain is entirely consumed by the internal physiological crisis. The Interoceptive Blind Spot: Interoception is the internal sensory network that maps what is happening inside the body (heart rate, breathing, pain, and suffocation signals). During a survival-mode hijack, this internal map goes completely dark. The Danger: Lack of Panic Awareness: Because their interoceptive awareness is offline, if the individual enters a hazardous environment, their brain physically fails to register the internal physiological warning signs of drowning or suffocating. The visceral alarm bells that would trigger panic in a neurotypical mind do not register through the biochemical static of the loop. 4. Water as a Somatic Heat-Sink Statistics show that 91% of fatal autism elopement incidents involve drowning. Mainstream literature claims this is due to an arbitrary "attraction to water." This framework identifies water as a primitive somatic tool: An individual running on a massive adrenaline redline is experiencing intense internal neurological and thermal over-stimulation. Water provides an immediate, uniform, and massive hydrostatic sensory input. Entering water is an automated, reflexive attempt by the primal brain stem to find an immediate "heat-sink" to cool the system down, shock the body out of the adrenaline loop, and force a state of deep sensory grounding. 5. Acute Motor Planning Paralysis (The Neurological Lock) The fatal breakdown occurs not because the individual wishes to remain submerged, but due to an acute neurological motor failure: Motor Planning Deficits (Apraxia): Autistic individuals frequently manage underlying motor planning barriers, where the brain struggles to map out and execute complex physical movements. The Sudden Physical Shock: When an overloaded, adrenaline-flooded nervous system hits the sudden temperature and gravity shift of water, its motor planning networks experience an immediate, absolute paralysis. The Physical Lock: Even if a fragment of the conscious mind realizes it needs to surface, the brain loses the ability to calculate and send the lightning-fast, synchronized signals to the limbs required to swim, tread water, or push upward. The physical muscle tone and coordination lock up entirely under the weight of the neurological shock. 6. Conclusion Autistic elopement and drowning are not behavioral failures; they are the tragic downstream consequences of an unaccommodating environment forcing a vulnerable neuro-metabolic grid into a profound physical and sensory blackout. Mitigating this risk cannot be achieved through strict behavioral compliance or checklist tracking. Safety can only be secured by establishing total environmental accommodations, respecting physical motor boundaries, and preserving the child's underlying cellular energy thresholds.

titre: An Active Inference Cognitive Architecture for Artificial Silicon Life: Long-term Empirical Validation from Interoceptive Self-Sustenance to Multi-Family Generalization
resume: ABSTRACTAutonomous survival in open, non-stationary thermodynamic worlds cannot be reduced to maximizing arbitrary scalar rewards. When conventional agents optimize external scores under ongoing metabolic dissipation, they routinely succumb to reward hacking, catastrophic representation loss, or energetic collapse once environmental dynamics drift. Here, we present an autonomous cognitive architecture for Artificial Silicon Life (ASL) derived strictly from first principles of the Free Energy Principle (FEP) and Active Inference, entirely dispensing with reinforcement learning, hand-tuned reward curves, and geometric search trees. The architecture coordinates three non-redundant computational layers: a dual-branch neural valuation engine that dynamically arbitrates macro-goals by balancing viability probability against metabolic yield; an episodic spatial memory coupled with boundary-reflecting momentum search that breaks the diffusive limits of Brownian exploration; and a single-step neural cross-attention motor decoder that accommodates nonlinear, asymmetric actuator distortions without forward tree search. titre: The heart brain axis
resume: This narrative review examines why patients with total artificial hearts (TAHs) and left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) retain their memories and sense of self, and argues that identity is stored in distributed brain networks, not in the heart. It reviews the evidence on heart-to-brain communication (vagal afferents, baroreceptor pulse-phase signalling, heartbeat-evoked potentials, humoral pathways) and critically evaluates popular claims about a "heart brain" and cardiac electromagnetic entrainment. It identifies the genuinely open question: whether reduced pulsatility under mechanical circulatory support alters the intensity of emotional experience, for which direct evidence is currently lacking. It proposes the Archive–Modulator framework, with five falsifiable predictions, in which the brain stores identity and cardiac signals modulate, but are not required for, emotion. Finally, it outlines a prospective study design, including a within-patient pump-setting sub-study, to confirm or refute a modulatory role of cardiac pulsatility.Keywords: neurocardiology; interoception; heart–brain axis; total artificial heart; left ventricular assist device; emotion; heartbeat-evoked potential; pulsatility

titre: IMMAGINA… La comunicazione ipnotica nella cura del bambino e dell'adolescente. Le lezioni del Dr. Rocco Iannini – Dispensa per i partecipanti
resume: Dispensa didattica che raccoglie, in forma di testo continuo, le cinque lezioni tenute dal Dr. Rocco Iannini nel corso «IMMAGINA… La comunicazione ipnotica nella cura del bambino e dell’adolescente» (AOU Meyer IRCCS, Firenze, dicembre 2026), rivolto a professionisti sanitari che si avvicinano per la prima volta all’ipnosi clinica. Le cinque parti trattano: le definizioni di ipnosi, ipnotismo, rapport, comunicazione ipnotica e monoideismo plastico; la struttura dell’induzione e le modalità induttive; le tecniche induttive adatte all’età (fissazione, respirazione, bolle di sapone, pupazzi, luogo sicuro, viaggio immaginario); il ruolo della mente nella guarigione (cervello predittivo, stress e asse ipotalamo-ipofisi-surrene, PNEI, placebo e nocebo, paura e dolore anticipati nel bambino); il meccanismo d’azione dell’ipnosi. Completano il testo le schede pratiche per il reparto, un glossario e la bibliografia. La cornice di riferimento è la scuola di Franco Granone (CIICS – Istituto Franco Granone), integrata con le neuroscienze e la psiconeuroendocrinoimmunologia. Sono presentati come contributi originali dell’autore il Cerchio di Iannini, l’ideoplasia patogena e la teoria delle emozioni come meccanismo d’azione dell’ipnosi; quest’ultima è proposta come ipotesi di lavoro. In ogni parte il testo richiama i limiti e la sicurezza clinica: consenso dei genitori e assenso del bambino, integrazione con analgesia e sedazione senza sostituirle, valutazione specialistica nei casi che la richiedono. La dispensa non sostituisce una formazione strutturata in ipnosi clinica. Additional description (English abstract) Teaching handout collecting the five lectures given by Dr. Rocco Iannini at the course “IMMAGINA… Hypnotic communication in the care of children and adolescents” (Meyer Children’s Hospital IRCCS, Florence, December 2026), for healthcare professionals new to clinical hypnosis. Topics: definitions (hypnosis, rapport, hypnotic communication, plastic monoideism); structure of hypnotic induction and induction modalities; age-appropriate induction techniques; the role of the mind in healing (predictive brain, stress and the HPA axis, psychoneuroendocrinoimmunology, placebo and nocebo, anticipatory fear and pain in children); the mechanism of action of hypnosis, with the author’s working hypothesis of emotions as its mechanism. Includes practical cards, a glossary and references. Framework: the school of Franco Granone (CIICS). In Italian. titre: From Frederic Myers's Subliminal Consciousness to the Ben-Yehudah Investigation of Intellectual Reception: Trauma, Inwardness, and Previously Unrecognized Abilities
resume: From Frederic Myers's Subliminal Consciousness to the Ben-Yehudah Investigation of Intellectual Reception: Trauma, Inwardness, and Previously Unrecognized Abilities This independent scientific, philosophical, theoretical, and comparative research manuscript examines Frederic W. H. Myers's historical theory of subliminal consciousness alongside Yeshayahu Ben-Yehudah's independent investigation of SOURCE CONSCIOUSNESS, intellectual RECEPTION, the interpretive MIND, and the emergence of previously unrecognized intellectual abilities. Frederic William Henry Myers (1843–1901), a British classical scholar and investigator associated with the Society for Psychical Research, developed an influential account of psychological activity occurring beyond ordinary waking awareness. His investigations explored the subliminal self, supraliminal consciousness, memory, genius, creativity, hypnosis, dissociation, and the possibility that capacities not immediately accessible to awareness may nevertheless participate in human experience. The manuscript examines Myers's foundational writings, including The Subliminal Consciousness (1892) and Human Personality and Its Survival of Bodily Death (1903), with particular attention to his investigation of genius and the relationship between conscious awareness and previously unrecognized intellectual capacities. These historical inquiries are compared with the Ben-Yehudah Transducer Model, which identifies SOURCE CONSCIOUSNESS as foundational, proposes that the biological brain functions principally as a receiver, and distinguishes intellectual RECEPTION from interpretation by the MIND. The investigation also examines trauma, adversity, inwardness, isolation, intellectual development, and the distinction between previously unrecognized abilities and newly acquired capacities. It considers the limitations of assuming that traumatic experiences cause intellectual transformation or that the emergence of unexpected intellectual expression necessarily demonstrates a nonbiological source of information. The author's continuous STILLNESS, RECEPTION, ZERO INTENT, and SUBJECT–WITNESS–OBSERVER experience provide the phenomenological context for examining intellectual material becoming available without its emergence being attributed to deliberate intention. The manuscript identifies conceptual relationships between Myers's investigation of psychological activity beyond ordinary conscious awareness and the Ben-Yehudah investigation of intellectual RECEPTION while preserving their independent theoretical foundations. Central Finding “I Acquire ALL In STILLNESS” ~ YBY The central finding is that Frederic Myers's investigation of subliminal consciousness and the Ben-Yehudah investigation of intellectual RECEPTION converge in questioning whether ordinary waking awareness reveals the complete range of human intellectual capacities. Myers proposed that memories, psychological processes, and intellectual abilities may exist beyond the immediate reach of ordinary conscious awareness. His investigation of genius considered whether exceptional intellectual expression might involve processes not fully recognized by the conscious personality. The Ben-Yehudah investigation approaches a related question through SOURCE CONSCIOUSNESS, continuous RECEPTION, and the interpretive MIND. The author's foundational philosophical position is expressed through the statements: “Consciousness is the source of ALL” ~ YBY “I AM Consciousness experiencing Human Form” ~ YBY Within this framework, SOURCE CONSCIOUSNESS is foundational, while the biological brain is proposed principally as a receiver and the MIND performs an interpretive function. A central distinction concerns the emergence of intellectual abilities that were not previously recognized, anticipated, or formally cultivated. The investigation identifies the difference between an ability's original development and the moment that ability becomes recognizable. The emergence of intellectual expression following adversity, trauma, or inwardness does not independently establish that those experiences created the ability. The author's experience of intellectual RECEPTION is preserved without reducing it to Myers's subliminal self, conventional memory retrieval, creative incubation, or unconscious information processing. The author's ZERO INTENT is further expressed through the statements: “All of my work does not come from intention” ~ YBY “If my work comes from intention, I will no longer do this work” ~ YBY These statements establish that the author's scholarly work is not understood by him as originating from deliberate intention. His continuous STILLNESS and RECEPTION are not described as temporary conditions deliberately entered to produce intellectual results. The manuscript therefore identifies conceptual convergence without establishing theoretical equivalence between Myers's subliminal consciousness and SOURCE CONSCIOUSNESS. The historical significance of Myers's investigations does not independently validate the Ben-Yehudah Transducer Model, and the author's phenomenological experience does not establish an experimentally verified mechanism of biological reception. The principal scholarly contribution is the preservation of these distinctions while examining previously unrecognized intellectual capacities as an unresolved question concerning consciousness, experience, and intellectual expression. Scope of the Investigation This manuscript is an independent historical, philosophical, theoretical, phenomenological, and comparative scientific investigation. It does not report original controlled experiments in psychology, neuroscience, or consciousness studies. The study examines Myers's historical research concerning subliminal consciousness, the supraliminal self, memory, genius, creativity, hypnosis, psychological suggestion, and the broader organization of human personality. Foundational sources include Myers's writings published in the Proceedings of the Society for Psychical Research during 1892 and his posthumous work Human Personality and Its Survival of Bodily Death (1903). The historical investigation is supplemented by contemporary psychological literature concerning conscious and unconscious processing, creative insight, memory, and the cognitive consequences associated with traumatic stress. These sources are examined alongside the author's previously published research, including the Ben-Yehudah Field Theory, the Ben-Yehudah Transducer Model, The Mind as an Active Engine, and his investigations concerning SOURCE CONSCIOUSNESS, biological reception, observational fidelity, and consciousness experiencing human form. The manuscript distinguishes psychological processes outside ordinary awareness from the author's independent understanding of SOURCE CONSCIOUSNESS. It also distinguishes trauma from intellectual causation, inwardness from continuous STILLNESS, previously unrecognized capacities from newly acquired abilities, and phenomenological RECEPTION from experimentally established biological mechanisms. The author's SUBJECT–WITNESS–OBSERVER relationship is preserved as part of his first-person experience within consciousness. The Ben-Yehudah Six-Pillar Discipline remains: STILLNESS → AWARENESS → OBSERVATION → DISCERNMENT → INTEGRATION → TRANSMISSION SOURCE CONSCIOUSNESS is foundational and is not designated as a seventh pillar. The investigation does not establish that Myers's subliminal self is equivalent to SOURCE CONSCIOUSNESS, that trauma necessarily produces exceptional intellectual abilities, or that the biological brain has been experimentally demonstrated to receive information from a nonbiological source. Its central unresolved questions concern the origin, recognition, development, and expression of intellectual capacities; the relationship between inward experience and intellectual awareness; and the distinction between reported reception and independently established psychological mechanisms. The manuscript contributes to interdisciplinary consciousness studies while preserving the original philosophical framework and lived observations of Yeshayahu Ben-Yehudah. The comparison between Frederic Myers's subliminal-consciousness framework and the Ben-Yehudah investigation of intellectual RECEPTION was developed through human–AI scholarly inquiry. titre: Effectiveness and Durability of Psychological Interventions for Depressive Symptoms in Patients With Depressive Disorders: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
resume: Background Psychological interventions (PIs) are effective for depressive disorders (DDs). However, comparative evidence regarding their effectiveness and durability in reducing depressive symptoms (DSs) remains limited. Objectives To compare the effectiveness and durability of PIs for DSs in patients with DDs. Methods Five databases were searched for RCTs comparing PIs for DDs, up to June 23, 2024. A random-effects NMA synthesized changes in DSs at post-treatment and follow-up. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2. Results Of 12,076 records identified, 71 RCTs were included. All PIs except dialectical behavior therapy (DBT) were more effective than TAU for managing DSs at post-treatment (SMDs: −0.58 to −1.59). Problem-solving therapy (PST) and behavioral activation (BA) showed the highest short-term efficacy, followed by mindfulness-based cognitive therapy (MBCT), although PST evidence was based on a single study. At follow-up, IPT (SMD = −0.91), BA (−0.81), and CBT (−0.68) showed durable treatment effects. Conclusions BA and MBCT were more effective PIs for DSs reduction in the short term. IPT, BA, and CBT demonstrated durable treatment effects in patients with DDs. However, these findings should be interpreted with caution due to the heterogeneous TAU comparators and the low-to-very-low certainty of evidence.

titre: Efficacy of Online Shame-Based Acceptance and Commitment Group Therapy on Marital Adjustment in Women Experiencing Infertility and Moderate-to-Severe Depression
resume: Background: Infertility poses a profound psychological and social challenge for Iranian women, significantly impairing their mental health and marital adjustment. This study aimed to investigate the efficacy of an online shame-based acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT) group intervention on marital adjustment and its components among women experiencing infertility and moderate-to-severe depression. Methods: A randomized controlled clinical trial with a pretest-posttest design, including a control group and follow-up phase, was conducted. The study population comprised infertile women attending infertility treatment centers in Tehran in 2023. A purposive sample of 40 infertile women was randomly allocated to intervention and control groups (20 participants each). Data were collected using a demographic questionnaire, the Dyadic Adjustment Scale (DAS), and the Beck Depression Inventory-II (BDI-II). The intervention consisted of 10 weekly online ACT sessions based on the 10-session shame-focused ACT protocol by McKay et al. (2020). Data were analyzed using repeated-measures analysis of variance in SPSS version 25. Results: The results demonstrated that online shame-based ACT group therapy significantly improved overall marital adjustment and its components—satisfaction, cohesion, consensus, and affection- in women experiencing infertility and moderate-to-severe depression. (P-value<0.05). These improvements were sustained at follow-up. Conclusion: Online shame-based ACT group therapy proved effective in enhancing marital adjustment among women experiencing infertility and moderate-to-severe depression. It is recommended as a complementary intervention alongside other mental health services to improve the quality of marital relationships in this population.

titre: GENEDIS 2026 – Paper 69 – Short-Term Psychotherapeutic Interventions for Psychological Distress in Cancer: A Systematic Review
resume: Psychological distress, including anxiety, depression, and existential concerns, is highly prevalent among patients with cancer and adversely affects quality of life, treatment adherence, and clinical outcomes. Short-term psychotherapeutic interventions have emerged as practical approaches for addressing these challenges within oncology settings. This systematic review evaluated the effectiveness of brief psychotherapeutic interventions in reducing psychological distress and improving psychosocial outcomes among patients with cancer. A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed and Scopus according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Studies published in English between 2014 and 2026 were eligible if they investigated structured short-term psychotherapeutic interventions in adolescent and/or adult patients with cancer and reported psychological outcomes. Randomized controlled trials and quasi-experimental studies were included. Six studies met the eligibility criteria, comprising five randomized controlled trials and one quasi-experimental study, with sample sizes ranging from 6 to 305 participants. Overall, most interventions demonstrated improvements in at least one psychological outcome. Managing Cancer and Living Meaningfully (CALM), Short-Term Psychodynamic Psychotherapy (STPP), Intensive Short-Term Dynamic Psychotherapy (ISTDP), and Solution-Focused Brief Therapy (SFBT) were associated with improvements in depression, emotional functioning, hope, or quality of life. However, studies comparing structured psychotherapeutic interventions with active supportive controls generally reported improvements in both groups, indicating limited evidence of consistent superiority of any single approach. Current evidence suggests that short-term psychotherapeutic interventions may improve psychological well-being in patients with cancer. Nevertheless, methodological heterogeneity, variability in intervention protocols, and limited sample sizes warrant larger, well-designed randomized controlled trials to establish the comparative effectiveness of these interventions across diverse oncology populations.

titre: Experiential training reduces negative beliefs about exposure therapy and improves guideline knowledge
resume: Exposure therapy is an effective first-line treatment for anxiety disorders, post-traumatic stress disorder, and obsessive–compulsive disorder; however, it remains underutilized in clinical practice. This study examined whether participation in an experiential semester-long course influenced psychology students’ beliefs about exposure therapy and their knowledge of its guideline-consistent implementation. We hypothesized that participation would promote more positive beliefs about exposure therapy and greater knowledge of its evidence-based implementation. We also examined whether these effects were moderated by students’ anxiety sensitivity, given evidence that higher therapist anxiety is associated with less frequent use of exposure therapy. Seventy-two students participated in a course combining theoretical instruction with experiential exercises, during which they conducted exposure exercises targeting their own subclinical fears. Questionnaires assessing negative beliefs about exposure therapy, knowledge of guideline-consistent exposure therapy, therapist safety behaviors, and reasons for excluding clients from exposure therapy, were administered at baseline, post-course, and at a 6-month follow-up. Participants reported significantly fewer negative beliefs about exposure therapy and increased adherence to guideline-consistent practices at both post-course and follow-up assessments. Anxiety sensitivity did not moderate these effects. These findings suggest that experiential training may promote more favorable beliefs about exposure therapy and facilitate adherence to evidence-based guidelines. Future research should examine the long-term persistence of these effects and whether they translate into therapists’ clinical practice.
revue: Journal of Behavioral and Cognitive Therapy

titre: Uro-gynecological disorders in women with non-celiac gluten/wheat sensitivity: a prospective study and response to a wheat-free diet
resume: BACKGROUND: Women with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS)-like symptoms frequently report uro-gynecological complaints without identifiable organic disease. A substantial proportion are diagnosed with non-celiac gluten/wheat sensitivity (NCGWS), a condition characterized by systemic manifestations. AIM: To prospectively assess the prevalence of uro-gynecological disorders in women with NCGWS and their evolution following a wheat-free diet (WFD). METHODS: We enrolled 186 newly diagnosed NCGWS female patients and 403 age-matched healthy controls. A structured questionnaire evaluating menstrual, gynecological and urological symptoms was administered at baseline and repeated in NCGWS patients after 12 (T1) and 24 (T2) months of WFD. In a subgroup, cervical cytology was assessed before and after a 7-day open wheat challenge. RESULTS: Uro-gynecological disorders were more prevalent in NCGWS patients than controls (54.3% vs 35.7%, P < 0.0001), across menstrual (41.9%vs 28.8%, P = 0.002), gynecological (46.8%vs 8.9%, P < 0.0001), and urological domains (39.2%vs 4.0%, P < 0.0001). Strict WFD adherence was associated with significant reduction in all symptom domains at 12 months (P < 0.0001), with further improvement at 24 months in adherent patients. Poor adherence was associated with symptom recurrence, particularly gynecological complaints (+88.9%, P = 0.008). Cytology showed mild-to-moderate inflammation with increased granulocytes, more evident after wheat reintroduction. CONCLUSIONS: Women with NCGWS reported more uro-gynecological complaints than controls. Long-term adherence to WFD was associated with clinical improvement, while wheat exposure might (re)trigger urogenital inflammation. Controlled studies are needed to establish the specificity of these associations and the therapeutic effect of wheat exclusion. Nevertheless, these findings highlight the relevance of dietary management and multidisciplinary approach in NCGWS patients.

titre: Inflammatory bowel disease: another disorder of gut-brain interaction?
Psychobiotics and Trace Elements in Neurodegenerative Diseases: From Independent Modulators to Potential Interactions Within the Microbiota-Gut-Brain Axis-Narrative Review
resume: The microbiota-gut-brain axis represents an important bidirectional communication network linking the gastrointestinal tract and the central nervous system and may contribute to processes involved in neurodegeneration. Increasing attention has been directed toward psychobiotics as potential modulators of the microbiota-gut-brain axis, while accumulating evidence also indicates that disturbed trace-element homeostasis may contribute to the pathogenesis of neurodegenerative diseases. This review summarizes current evidence on the roles of psychobiotics and trace elements and examines their potential interplay within the microbiota-gut-brain axis. The review discusses bidirectional interactions between the gut microbiota and trace elements, the potential effects of psychobiotic interventions on trace-element homeostasis, and the possible implications of these interactions for neurodegenerative processes. Taken together, current findings indicate that the gut microbiota, psychobiotics, and trace elements may constitute an interconnected system influencing intestinal and systemic homeostasis as well as biological processes relevant to nervous system function. However, direct evidence demonstrating the clinical relevance of interactions between these components remains limited. Moreover, available evidence is largely based on experimental studies, while clinical findings remain scarce and heterogeneous. Further characterization of this interplay may improve our understanding of mechanisms underlying neurodegeneration and provide a basis for the development of more targeted and personalized approaches to supporting neurological health.

titre: Vagus Nerve Stimulation as a Potential Therapeutic Strategy for Alcohol Use Disorder
resume: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) contributes to approximately 3 million deaths worldwide each year and leads to substantial emotional, financial, and social implications for individuals and their families. AUD leads to multi-system damage, including the immune system, gut microbiome, neuroendocrine pathways, and the brain. Current treatments for AUD, focused primarily on behavioral and pharmaceutical interventions, insufficiently address alcohol's extensive impact on multiple body systems. Vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) has shown therapeutic benefits across a spectrum of neurological conditions, including epilepsy, depression, and addictive disorders. More recently, VNS is being investigated as a potential promising adjunctive treatment for AUD, which may complement currently used treatments by targeting many of the body systems dysregulated in AUD. Preclinical and clinical models have evaluated different VNS paradigms, including invasive, noninvasive, and minimally invasive approaches targeting motor and cognitive rehabilitation, withdrawal symptoms, and relapse during abstinence. However, while VNS has many promising potential benefits for improving AUD outcomes, direct evidence that VNS reduces alcohol consumption, alcohol seeking, or craving in AUD remains limited, and there are several logistical and ethical considerations that researchers, clinicians, and policymakers should evaluate before VNS is considered standard of care. Additionally, optimization of VNS parameters, modality (implanted versus noninvasive or minimally invasive), and development of responder biomarkers could better inform patient selection for VNS. Although significant work remains before transitioning VNS into clinical practice, VNS offers an exciting opportunity for adjunctive treatment in AUD that could potentially target multi-system AUD dysfunction.

titre: Propionate, a short-chain fatty acid, is associated with disease activity in pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis
resume: Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), metabolites found in fermented foods and produced by colonic bacterial fermentation of dietary fibers, may mediate gut-brain axis crosstalk influencing the course of multiple sclerosis (MS). In this study, SCFAs are measured in plasma and paired stool samples by targeted mass spectrometry in a large cohort of deeply phenotyped individuals shortly after MS onset. Propionate is consistently associated with a protective effect on three clinical and imaging activity-related outcomes. Findings are reproduced in an equally large external cohort for plasma and stool measurements. Despite the correlation between plasma SCFAs and SCFA-producing gut microbial taxa, propionate levels are not correlated with dietary fiber, suggesting that intake may not be sufficient to modulate its levels and ensuing inflammation. In conclusion, propionate is consistently associated with lower disease activity, and exogenous administration may be more likely than fiber supplementation to confer protective effects on MS activity in proof-of-concept clinical trials.

titre: Glutamatergic dysfunction in major depressive disorder: From receptor and glial abnormalities to circuit pathology and mechanism-based therapeutic strategies
resume: Major depressive disorder is a heterogeneous psychiatric disorder that cannot be fully explained by classical monoamine-deficiency models. Increasing evidence indicates that glutamatergic dysfunction provides a central framework for linking molecular, glial, synaptic, and circuit-level abnormalities in depression. This narrative review focuses on glutamatergic dysregulation as the organizing mechanism of major depressive disorder. We summarize core abnormalities involving context-dependent N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor dysfunction, impaired α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid receptor-mediated synaptic plasticity, altered metabotropic glutamate receptor signaling, and disrupted astrocytic excitatory amino acid transporter 2-mediated glutamate clearance. These changes converge on excitation-inhibition imbalance, leading to unstable cortical-limbic activity and contributing to emotional dysregulation, anhedonia, cognitive impairment, and impaired stress adaptation. We further discuss upstream mechanisms that regulate glutamatergic dysfunction, including brain-derived neurotrophic factor/mammalian target of rapamycin signaling, neuroinflammation, epigenetic regulation, and microbiota-gut-brain axis-related peripheral crosstalk. At the circuit level, we emphasize abnormalities in the prefrontal cortex-amygdala, amygdala-nucleus accumbens, prefrontal cortex-hippocampus, and lateral habenula pathways. We also consider how monoaminergic and opioid systems modulate glutamate-dependent synaptic and reward-circuit plasticity. Finally, we review therapeutic implications, including ketamine and related N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor modulators, α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid receptor facilitation, astrocyte-targeted strategies, anti-inflammatory interventions, circuit-based neuromodulation, and biomarker-guided patient stratification. By centering diverse pathological findings around glutamatergic dysfunction, this review provides a focused mechanistic framework for understanding major depressive disorder and developing precision, mechanism-based treatments.

titre: From Established Care to Precision Menopause Medicine: A Clinical-Actionability Framework for Contemporary Menopause Management
resume: Menopause care now spans established hormone therapy, mechanism-based non-hormonal drugs, behavioural interventions, and emerging microbiome- and biomarker-guided approaches. This state-of-the-art narrative review evaluated which dimensions of personalisation are clinically actionable and which remain hypotheses of precision medicine. A structured PubMed/MEDLINE search (January 2020-July 2026), updated to August 2026 and supplemented by landmark studies, current guidelines, and regulatory sources, was synthesized using a four-tier clinical-actionability framework (A, established; B, evidence-supported off-label; C, emerging; D, experimental). Menopausal hormone therapy remains the most effective treatment for vasomotor symptoms and prevents bone loss during use; the 2025-2026 FDA labelling revisions altered risk communication rather than the underlying evidence, and professional responses diverged. Fezolinetant and elinzanetant provide mechanism-based non-hormonal options, while SSRIs/SNRIs, gabapentin, cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT), CBT for insomnia, and clinical hypnosis remain evidence-supported. Exercise, yoga, acupuncture, soy, and equol are not guideline-recommended for reducing vasomotor symptom frequency despite benefits in other domains. Gut and genitourinary microbiome findings should not be conflated: pooled evidence identifies no consistent postmenopausal gut signature, whereas vaginal Lactobacillus depletion is more reproducible but does not reliably predict symptom resolution. Evidence-based personalisation therefore remains principally clinical; microbiome sequencing, equol testing, and multi-omic treatment selection require prospective test-guided validation.

titre: A Multimodal Intervention Including Tirzepatide in Women with Lipedema and Excess Body Weight: A Pilot Case Series
resume: Background: Lipedema is a chronic adipose tissue disorder characterized by disproportionate lower-limb fat accumulation, pain, and resistance to conventional weight-loss strategies. Tirzepatide produces substantial weight loss, but evidence in lipedema is limited. Methods: This single-center ambispective pilot case series described a 22-25-week routine clinical course in 2025. During the first 8-9 weeks, all participants received only a low-carbohydrate Mediterranean diet and recommendations for aerobic and resistance exercise; no participant received tirzepatide during this phase. After completion of the 8-9-week non-pharmacological phase, four participants started tirzepatide (2.5-7.5 mg once weekly) and continued it for the remaining 14-16 weeks, whereas one participant declined pharmacotherapy. After approval by the Bioethics Committee (Resolution No. 12/2026, 4 February 2026), the 2025 data were analyzed retrospectively; participants gave verbal consent to further follow-up in March-April 2026 and were followed up prospectively, and all signed written consent for publication of their data and photographs in October 2026. Anthropometric, ultrasound, biochemical, pain, and quality-of-life outcomes were summarized descriptively for each case. Where available, changes are reported separately for the diet-and-exercise phase (T1-T2) and the tirzepatide phase (T2-T3). Results: Weight loss among the five completers ranged from 7.7 to 17.1 kg. Body fat percentage decreased in four of five participants, whereas skeletal muscle mass decreased numerically in all four tirzepatide-treated participants. Lower-limb circumferences and subcutaneous adipose tissue thickness generally decreased, although the magnitude and distribution of changes differed between participants. Fasting glucose and HOMA-IR decreased in most cases, whereas lipid changes were mixed. Patient-reported SF-36 scores (assessed only at T2 and T3) generally improved among the four participants receiving tirzepatide, particularly for bodily pain, while pressure pain threshold responses (T2 to T3) were heterogeneous. No adverse events, gastrointestinal symptoms, dose reductions, treatment interruptions, discontinuations, or serious adverse events were reported by the four tirzepatide-treated participants; the study was not designed to assess safety. Conclusions: This ambispective pilot case series provides preliminary, hypothesis-generating observations on a multimodal intervention that included tirzepatide in four of five women with lipedema and excess body weight. The observed changes cannot be attributed to tirzepatide or interpreted as a lipedema-specific effect because all participants received concurrent dietary, exercise, and supplementation interventions, and the participant who declined pharmacotherapy was not a comparator or control.
