titre: Mind–body exercise and mental health in college students: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
resume: Background College student populations show elevated psychological difficulties. Mind–body exercise, a non-pharmacological intervention, has attracted increasing attention, but direct comparisons of effectiveness across modalities remain limited. This systematic review and network meta-analysis evaluated the comparative efficacy of mindfulness-based exercise, Tai Chi, Baduanjin, yoga, and combined mind–body interventions on core mental health outcomes in college students. Methods Following PRISMA-NMA guidelines, eligible RCTs were searched in PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science. Risk of bias was assessed using the RoB 2 tool, and analyses were conducted in R with anxiety, depression, and stress as primary outcomes (SMD, 95% CrI). Results Twenty-four RCTs were included, covering five single interventions and one combined intervention (mindfulness-based exercise + Tai Chi). Network meta-analysis showed that for reducing anxiety, Baduanjin (SMD = −0.53, 95% CrI: −0.96 to −0.10), mindfulness-based exercise (SMD = −0.70, −0.98 to −0.44), Tai Chi (SMD = −0.61, −1.22 to −0.07), yoga (SMD = −0.47, −0.85 to −0.11), and the combined intervention (SMD = −0.99, −2.00 to −0.01) were significantly effective. For depression, Baduanjin (SMD = −0.75, −1.10 to −0.36) and mindfulness-based exercise (SMD = −0.55, −0.82 to −0.29) were superior. For stress, mindfulness-based exercise (SMD = −0.67, −0.91 to −0.47) and yoga (SMD = −0.32, −0.61 to −0.05) were effective, with mindfulness-based exercise outperforming yoga. No intervention significantly improved mental well-being or sleep quality compared with controls. However, this lack of statistically significant benefit does not rule out genuine intervention effects, and these findings remain inconclusive given the limited evidence. Conclusion Mind–body exercises exert differential effects. Baduanjin may relieve anxiety and depression, while mindfulness-based exercise is beneficial for reducing stress.

titre: Integration of children’s wellbeing practitioners into a specialist paediatric psychology service: a non-randomised effectiveness study
resume: Abstract Children and young people (CYP) living with long-term physical health conditions (LTCs) have a higher prevalence of mental health conditions but report barriers in accessing mental health interventions. One way to increase access to such interventions is through Children and Young Person Wellbeing Practitioners (CWPs) who deliver low-intensity cognitive behavioural therapy (LI CBT). This non-randomised study evaluates the effectiveness of LI CBT delivered by CWPs integrated in a specialist paediatric psychology service. Thirty-six CYP aged 3‒23 years receiving LI CBT interventions were included in the evaluation. Outcome measures included the Revised Children’s Anxiety and Depression Scale (RCADS) and goal based outcomes (GBOs), which were administered at the beginning and end of the intervention. Feedback from participants was also gathered to complement quantitative data. Analysis of pre- and post-intervention data highlighted a reduction in symptoms across all RCADS subscales with notably large effect sizes observed when comparing total RCADS scores ( d = 0.86) and low mood scores ( d = 0.99). GBO data similarly reflected progress towards personal goals with a large effect size reported ( d = 1.44). Participants provided positive feedback, emphasising improvements in symptom control and emotional understanding. The integration of CWPs into paediatric hospitals demonstrated preliminary effectiveness in reducing anxiety and depression symptoms among CYP with LTCs and significant progress towards their personal goals. These findings suggest that LI CBT delivered by CWPs could fill a critical gap within paediatric settings, although further research with a larger sample size is warranted. Key learning aims (1) To understand the mental health needs of children and young people with long-term physical health conditions. (2) To learn how low-intensity cognitive behavioural therapy (LI CBT) delivered by Children and Young People’s Wellbeing Practitioners (CWPs) can be integrated into paediatric healthcare settings to improve mental health outcomes. (3) To explore the preliminary effectiveness of CWP-delivered interventions through clinical outcome measures and participant feedback, and consider implications for future service development and research.

titre: Inflammatory Markers in Obsessive-compulsive Disorder: The Role of Childhood Trauma
resume: Objective: Childhood trauma and obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) have each been linked to inflammation, but its role in OCD-related inflammation remains unclear.We compared serum tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and C-reactive protein (CRP) levels among patients with OCD with and without childhood trauma and controls.Methods: Eighty-six patients with OCD (45 with and 41 without childhood trauma, classified using the Childhood Trauma Questionnaire) and 36 healthy controls were included.OCD severity was assessed with the Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale.Group comparisons used nonparametric tests with false discovery rate (FDR) correction and confounder-adjusted quantile regression; childhood trauma was also analyzed continuously.Results: IL-6 (median 67.78 vs. 153.89pg/ml; p = 0.036) and TNF- (129.70 vs. 222.51pg/ml; p = 0.002) were lower in patients than controls.After adjustment for confounders, the IL-6 difference remained significant (p = 0.013), whereas the TNF- difference did not.CRP did not differ between groups.In the categorical comparison, IL-6 was lower in patients with than without childhood trauma (p = 0.028); however, this was not corroborated when trauma was analyzed continuously or after FDR correction.OCD severity was not correlated with any marker.TNF- and IL-6 levels were strongly positively correlated ( = 0.752, p ＜ 0.01).Conclusion: IL-6 and TNF- levels were lower in patients with OCD than in controls, with the IL-6 difference robust to adjustment.The association between childhood trauma and inflammation appears complex and was not supported dimensionally, underscoring the need for larger longitudinal studies.

titre: Artificial Intelligence and OCD: Interactions in Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Ethical Considerations
resume: Abstract Purpose of Review Artificial intelligence (AI) and associated technologies, including machine learning, deep learning, and generative systems such as large language models, have rapidly expanded in capability, scale, and daily use in recent years. These systems are also being explored for applications in healthcare, including mental healthcare. For some mental health conditions, such as obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), aspects and features of AI technologies may have unintended and unexpected interactions and consequences. Herein, we review the current literature exploring how AI and OCD interact in daily life and treatment settings, and consider ethical concerns. Recent Findings We find literature on this topic to exist within several broad domains: (1) how AI is shaping OCD presentations and symptoms; (2) how AI is being used in diagnosis and prognosis; and, (3) how AI is being used in treatment. Legal and ethical implications of AI in mental healthcare span domains including: (1) Privacy, Confidentiality, and Autonomy; (2) Bias, Transparency, and Humanization; and, (3) Patient Safety and Clinical Oversight. Summary AI use in daily life and mental healthcare settings is accelerating and can impact lived experience with OCD. Clinicians are advised to assess for use of AI by patients, and invite a conversation about AI’s role in their patients’ lives. As AI systems are incorporated into treatment settings, we suggest maintaining a human-in-the-loop for oversight of these systems. Finally, ethical concerns should continue to be reviewed as systems advance and adapt, with particular attention to privacy, transparency, patient agency, legal and ethical responsibility, and provider accountability.

titre: Maintenance mechanisms in OCD: maladaptive obsessive beliefs and negative reinforcement
resume: Intrusive thoughts are a common psychological phenomenon and do not necessarily lead to obsessive-compulsive symptoms. The key difference between individuals with OCD and non-clinical individuals may lie more in how they interpret these thoughts and cope with the distress they cause. Research shows that maladaptive obsessive beliefs make individuals more likely to interpret intrusive thoughts as signals of danger, importance, or responsibility, which may lead to anxiety, guilt, and uncertainty. Compulsive behaviors such as checking, washing, reassurance seeking, and mental neutralizing can provide short-term relief. However, this relief may increase the likelihood of repetition through negative reinforcement while also preventing threat appraisals from being tested against reality. This paper uses a literature review and theoretical integration to examine the roles of maladaptive obsessive beliefs and negative reinforcement in the maintenance of compulsive behavior.

RAWATAN WASWAS MENERUSI PENDEKATAN BIOPSIKOSOSIAL SPIRITUAL MENURUT PERSPEKTIF SARJANA ISLAM: SATU KAJIAN AWAL
resume: Waswas atau kecelaruan obsesif kompulsif (OCD) merupakan antara sepuluh beban penyakit utama di seluruhdunia yang diklasifikasikan oleh World Health Organization (WHO) (Murray, 1996). Kupasan terhadap isu, rawatan danpenyelidikkan terhadap waswas atau OCD banyak dirujuk kepada psikiatri moden dan klinikal psikologi. Sehubungandengan itu, pendekatan rawatan yang bersifat biopsikososial spiritual telah dianggap sebagai rawatan holistik dalamrawatan mental dan fizikal. Walau bagaimanapun, pendekatan rawatan ini kurang diketengahkan kepada masyarakatkhususnya yang melibatkan rawatan waswas atau OCD. Justeru, objektif kajian adalah untuk mengumpul dan mengenalpasti fokus rawatan waswas oleh sarjana Islam yang terpilih berteraskan empat domain hidup iaitu biologi, psikologi,sosial dan spiritual. Manakala dari aspek metode, kajian mengaplikasi sepenuhnya kajian kualitatif berasaskan pendekatandokumentasi. Hasil kajian mendapati, terdapat 10 terapi berasaskan biologi, 6 pendekatan menerusi psikologi, 3 pendekatanbersifat sosial dan 2 amalan beserta 8 doa sebagai pendekatan rawatan yang bersifat spiritual. Kajian ini penting untukmasyarakat Islam bagi memberi kefahaman terhadap keseimbangan dan kesepaduan empat elemen ini untuk mengatasigangguan waswas dan tidak hanya tertumpu kepada pendekatan rawatan bersifat spiritual.

titre: Efficacy of Lactic Acid Bacteria in Managing Diarrhea-Associated Functional Gastrointestinal Disorders: A Randomized Controlled Trial
resume: The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether a probiotic supplement can improve symptoms and quality of life in adults with diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D) or functional diarrhea (FD). These conditions can cause frequent loose stools, abdominal discomfort, and a lower quality of life. The main questions this study aims to answer are: * Does the probiotic improve quality of life compared with a placebo (a look-alike capsule that contains no active bacteria)? * Does the probiotic help participants have more normal stool consistency and fewer bowel movements? * Is the probiotic safe and well tolerated in people with IBS-D or FD? Researchers will compare the probiotic supplement with a placebo to see whether the probiotic improves symptoms and quality of life. Participants will: * Take either the probiotic or placebo capsule once daily for 3 months. * Switch to the other study treatment for an additional 3 months. * Complete quality-of-life questionnaires at the start of the study, after 3 months, and after 6 months. * Record the number of bowel movements each day throughout the study. * Record stool consistency each day using the Bristol Stool Form Scale. * Record daily pain during bowel movements using a Visual Analog Scale (VAS). * Report any medications they take and any health problems that occur during the study. The study will follow each participant for 6 months. Researchers hope the results will help determine whether this probiotic is a useful treatment option for people living with IBS-D or functional diarrhea.

titre: EPEGUT: Effects of Epetôme Supplementation on Gastrointestinal Function, Inflammatory Biomarkers and Wellbeing in Adults With IBS-like Symptoms
resume: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a common functional gastrointestinal condition characterised by symptoms including abdominal pain or discomfort, bloating, altered bowel habits and changes in digestive comfort. These symptoms can substantially affect quality of life, dietary behaviour, social functioning, and overall wellbeing. Although the underlying mechanisms are complex and multifactorial, growing evidence indicates that the gut microbiota and its interactions with the intestinal environment, immune system, gastrointestinal function, and gut-brain axis may play an important role in gastrointestinal health and symptom development. Prebiotics and probiotics have received increasing attention as nutritional strategies for supporting gut health. Prebiotics are substrates selectively utilised by beneficial microorganisms in the gut and can promote microbial growth and metabolic activity, including the production of short-chain fatty acids that contribute to intestinal barrier function, immune regulation, and colonic health. Probiotics are live microorganisms that, when administered in adequate amounts, may provide health benefits to the host. Selected probiotic strains have been investigated for their potential to support microbial balance, intestinal function, digestive comfort, and immune and inflammatory responses. However, responses to individual prebiotic or probiotic interventions can vary considerably between individuals, highlighting the potential value of complementary or combined nutritional approaches.

titre: MEDITERRANEAN DIET, HIGHLY PROCESSED FOODS AND THEIR IMPACT ON GASTROINTESTINAL SYMPTOMS, NUTRITIONAL STATUS AND QUALITY OF LIFE IN ADULT COELIAC DISEASE PATIENTS ON A GLUTEN FREE DIET: A MULTICENTRE CROSS-SECTIONAL STUDY
resume: Coeliac disease is a lifelong autoimmune condition in which the immune system reacts to gluten, a protein found in wheat, barley and rye, affecting about 1% of the general population. The only currently approved treatment is a strict, lifelong gluten-free diet (GFD). Although strict adherence to a gluten-free diet leads to mucosal recovery in most patients, up to 20-30% of coeliac patients continue to experience persistent gastrointestinal symptoms (such as abdominal pain, bloating, diarrhoea or constipation). Furthermore, commercially prepared gluten-free products often contain higher amounts of fat, sugar and salt, and lower amounts of fibre, protein, folate and vitamins compared with gluten-containing equivalents. Conversely, the Mediterranean diet-rich in vegetables, fruits, legumes, fish, nuts and extra-virgin olive oil-is widely recognised for its benefits on cardiovascular, metabolic and gut health, as well as quality of life, in contrast to diets rich in highly or ultra-processed foods. This multicentre cross-sectional observational study aims to evaluate whether adult coeliac patients on a long-term strict gluten-free diet whose habitual diet more closely aligns with the Mediterranean dietary pattern are less likely to experience persistent gastrointestinal symptoms and have a better quality of life and nutritional status, and conversely whether higher consumption of highly processed foods is associated with worse symptoms, poorer quality of life and less adequate nutritional status. No dietary intervention is provided as part of the study; participants complete validated questionnaires and undergo routine anthropometric and blood assessments during a single regular outpatient follow-up visit.

titre: Effects of Different Physical Activity Strategies on Disease Activity of IBD Patients
resume: The goal of this randomized controlled trial is to evaluate the effects of two different exercise programs, Pilates and combined resistance and aerobic training, on physical activity, kinesiophobia, quality of life, and disease-related outcomes in adults with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), including Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis. The main questions it aims to answer are: * Do the two exercise programs improve physical activity levels, reduce kinesiophobia, and improve quality of life in adults with IBD? * Are there differences between Pilates and combined resistance and aerobic training in their effects on participants' health status and disease-related outcomes? Researchers will compare participants assigned to the Pilates group and the combined resistance and aerobic training group with participants in the control group to evaluate the effects of the exercise programs. Participants will be randomly allocated to one of three groups: a Pilates group, a combined resistance and aerobic training group, or a control group. Participants in the exercise groups will follow their assigned exercise program using online instructional videos twice a week for 12 weeks, with each session lasting 20-30 minutes. They will record completed exercise sessions in an exercise diary. All participants will complete questionnaires before and after the intervention to assess physical activity, kinesiophobia, quality of life, depressive symptoms, knowledge of physical activity, and attitudes towards physiotherapists. Relevant demographic and clinical data will also be collected from medical records.

titre: Comparison of High-Flow Nasal Oxygen and Conventional Nasal Oxygen During Combined Upper and Lower Gastrointestinal Endoscopy Sedation in Elderly Patients
resume: This study aims to compare high-flow nasal oxygen (HFNO) with conventional nasal cannula oxygen during sedation for combined upper and lower gastrointestinal endoscopy (gastroscopy and colonoscopy) in patients aged 75 years and older. Sedation is commonly used during gastrointestinal endoscopic procedures to improve patient comfort. However, sedative medications may cause respiratory depression and hypoxemia. Conventional nasal cannula oxygen is routinely used to provide supplemental oxygen, whereas high-flow nasal oxygen delivers heated and humidified oxygen at higher flow rates and may help maintain oxygenation during sedation. The effectiveness of high-flow nasal oxygen in older patients undergoing gastroscopy and colonoscopy during the same session requires further evaluation. In this randomized controlled study, eligible patients will be assigned to one of two groups. In the high-flow nasal oxygen group, preoxygenation will be administered for 3 minutes at a flow rate of 40 L/min with an inspired oxygen fraction (FiO₂) of 50%. Once the target sedation level is achieved, the flow rate will be increased to 60 L/min, with FiO₂ maintained at 50%, and oxygen support will continue until the end of the procedure. In the conventional nasal cannula group, oxygen will be administered at a flow rate of 6 L/min for 3 minutes before sedation and continued throughout the procedure. Patients in both groups will maintain spontaneous breathing. The primary outcome is the occurrence of hypoxemia, defined as peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO₂) below 90% for at least 10 seconds during sedation and endoscopy. SpO₂ will be continuously monitored throughout the procedure. Secondary outcomes include the minimum SpO₂, total duration of hypoxemia, apnea episodes, the need for airway or ventilation interventions, changes in hemodynamic parameters, sedative and analgesic medication requirements, procedure duration, and adverse events. Any rescue interventions performed in response to hypoxemia or respiratory compromise will be recorded. The study will evaluate whether high-flow nasal oxygen reduces the incidence of hypoxemia compared with conventional nasal cannula oxygen in patients aged 75 years and older undergoing combined upper and lower gastrointestinal endoscopy under sedation. The findings may help inform oxygen supplementation strategies for this older patient population.

titre: Association Between Problematic Media Use and Preprocedural Anxiety, Sedation, and Recovery Outcomes in Children Undergoing Elective Upper Gastrointestinal Endoscopy: A Prospective Observational Cohort Study
resume: This observational study will investigate whether problematic digital media use is associated with anxiety in children undergoing a planned upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, a camera examination of the upper digestive tract. The study hypothesis is that problematic media use is associated with the child's anxiety immediately before sedation. Associations with sedation medicine requirements and recovery after the procedure will also be explored. The study will include 60 children aged 6 to 11 years. Parents or legal guardians will complete a questionnaire about their child's media use and provide information on screen time and viewing habits. An independent observer will assess anxiety at three time points: on arrival in the preparation area, before transfer to the procedure room, and immediately before sedation. Researchers will record the medicines and doses used for sedation or anaesthesia, procedure duration, agitation during recovery, recovery time, readiness for discharge, and sedation-related adverse events. Endoscopy and sedation will be managed according to routine clinical practice.

titre: Measuring the Frame: Examining the Clinical and Neurophysiological Impact of Verbal Expectations and Practice Instructions in a Mindfulness Exercise for Chronic Pain
resume: This randomized 2×2 factorial study will examine how verbal expectancy framing and mindfulness-specific practice instructions influence acute pain and brain activity in adults with chronic pain. Sixty meditation-naïve adults will be assigned to one of four conditions combining positive or negative expectancy framing with either a guided mindfulness exercise or a sham-meditation comparison exercise. Pain intensity, pain unpleasantness, anxiety, desire for pain medication, and mindfulness-related psychological states will be assessed before and immediately after the intervention, while electroencephalography (EEG) will be used to measure changes in brain activity during the exercise. The study is designed to clarify the independent and combined contributions of expectancy and mindfulness-specific instructions to acute pain relief and neurophysiological responses.
