titre: A Woman With Multiple Neuropathic Symptoms, Hypersensitivity to Heat, Peppers, and Alcohol, With a Variant in the TRPV1 Capsaicin Receptor Gene: Possible Implications to ME/CFS
resume: Transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 (TRPV1) is a ligand and heat-gated ion channel expressed on nociceptors that plays a central role in thermal and chemical pain signaling. Loss-of-function variants in TRPV1 have been associated with reduced nociception. We report a 65-year-old woman with disabling polyneurofunctional/neuropathic symptomatology including migraine, functional gastrointestinal disorders, and myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS). Diagnostic evaluation revealed sensory polyneuropathy and autonomic instability. Whole genome sequencing reanalysis identified a heterozygous TRPV1 c.2174A > T (p.Lys725Met) Likely Pathogenic variant that is very rare and highly conserved. Our patient reports consistent, longstanding, marked hypersensitivity to heat, capsaicin, and alcohol, all of which are known TRPV1 agonists, supporting a gain-of-function mechanism for this variant. Furthermore, prior studies have implicated TRPV1 hyperactivity in migraine, nociceptive sensitization, and ME/CFS. Despite the excellent clinical correlation, causality of the variant cannot be definitively established without functional studies. This case expands the potential phenotypic spectrum associated with TRPV1, and highlights a possible role for TRPV1-mediated channelopathies in complex neurofunctional disorders including ME/CFS.

titre: Survival analysis of spontaneous speech for predicting mild cognitive impairment-to-dementia conversion
resume: BACKGROUND: Speech is emerging as a promising digital biomarker of brain health. However, most speech-based studies in MCI and dementia have focused on cross-sectional diagnostic classification rather than longitudinal prognosis. Although speech-derived features have recently been used to predict MCI-to-dementia progression within fixed follow-up windows, their value for estimating time-to-dementia conversion within a survival-analysis framework remains insufficiently characterized. OBJECTIVES: To assess whether spontaneous speech-derived features serve as prognostic digital biomarkers for time-to-dementia conversion in individuals with MCI, and to benchmark their performance against established cognitive composite measures. METHODS: We conducted a longitudinal prognostic study in patients with MCI evaluated at the Ace Alzheimer Center Barcelona Memory Clinic from 2022 onward. At baseline, participants completed a brief spontaneous speech protocol from which multi-domain linguistic and acoustic features were automatically extracted. Patients underwent standard annual clinical follow-up to determine conversion to dementia. Baseline speech features were used to train survival models estimating conversion risk for all participants, and performance was evaluated using the C-index, 2-year time-dependent AUC, and IBS. Predictive accuracy was benchmarked against models trained on cognitive composite scores. RESULTS: A total of 853 individuals diagnosed with MCI were included at baseline, of whom 187 converted to dementia during follow-up. Cognitive composite models showed the strongest prognostic performance, achieving a test-set C-index of 0.77, 2-year horizon AUC of 0.82, and IBS of 0.12. Among speech-derived feature sets, Semantic Verbal Fluency showed the best performance, with a test-set C-index of 0.74, 2-year AUC of 0.74, and IBS of 0.12. CONCLUSION: Semantic Verbal Fluency-derived speech features demonstrated good prognostic performance for MCI-to-dementia conversion, although cognitive composites remained the strongest predictors. These findings suggest that a brief, automatically processed verbal-fluency task may provide a scalable and low- burden complement to standard cognitive assessment for dementia risk stratification, particularly in settings where repeated or remote monitoring is desirable. External validation and longer follow-up are needed before clinical implementation.
revue: The journal of prevention of Alzheimer's disease

titre: Mechanistic roles and therapeutic potential of gut microbiota-neuroimmune crosstalk in the development and progression of Alzheimer's disease
resume: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by cognitive decline and distinct neuropathological and biological alterations, including amyloid-β (Aβ) deposition, tau pathology, synaptic dysfunction, and neuronal loss. Increasing evidence suggests that dysregulated neuroimmune responses are closely associated with AD progression and may provide an important interface through which the gut microbiota influences brain homeostasis. Gut microbial dysbiosis and alterations in microbial functional output have been reported in patients with AD and mild cognitive impairment, although current human evidence remains predominantly associative. Experimental and animal studies further suggest that microbial structural components, microbiota-derived metabolites, and long-distance communication signals, including bacterial extracellular vesicles and microbial nucleic acids, may modulate intestinal barrier integrity, peripheral immunity, cerebrovascular interfaces, and central glial responses, thereby potentially influencing Aβ clearance, tau pathology, and synaptic function. Conversely, AD-associated alterations in neuroimmune regulation, autonomic signaling, neuroendocrine function, and mucosal immunity may reshape the intestinal ecological niche and further modify microbial composition and function, supporting a bidirectional gut microbiota-neuroimmune regulatory network. In this review, we integrate these interactions within a stage-oriented conceptual framework encompassing disease susceptibility, pathological initiation, amplification, and chronic progression, while emphasizing that these stages represent overlapping biological processes rather than established clinical categories. We also evaluate microbiota-based interventions, including dietary strategies, prebiotics, probiotics, psychobiotics, postbiotics, fecal microbiota transplantation, next-generation probiotics, engineered microorganisms, and metabolite-targeted approaches, with explicit consideration of their distinct evidence bases, translational limitations, and safety concerns. Overall, gut microbiota-neuroimmune crosstalk provides an integrative framework for understanding systemic contributions to AD pathophysiology, but establishing causal relevance in humans will require longitudinal studies, mechanistic validation, and population-stratified clinical trials.

titre: Bidirectional mechanisms of brain-gut interaction in sepsis-associated encephalopathy and its clinical translation
resume: Sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) is the most common and deadly neurological issue linked to sepsis. While traditionally thought to result from brain-specific processes like blood-brain barrier disruption and microglial activation, the exact systemic infection pathways causing brain damage are not well understood. As the gut-brain axis (GBA) theory gains traction, research on SAE is shifting from a brain-focused to a systemic view. This article reviews the two-way interactions between the brain and gut in SAE. In the gut-to-brain pathway, sepsis-induced dysbiosis of the gut microbiota promotes neuroinflammation via immune, metabolic, neurological, and endocrine pathways. In the descending GBA pathway, brain injury further impairs intestinal barrier function and gut microbiota homeostasis via autonomic nervous system dysfunction, excessive hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis hyperactivation, and the migration of brain-derived immune cells into the intestine, thereby forming a vicious cycle of synergistic dual-barrier destruction. Building on the existing mechanism, diagnostic and therapeutic strategies targeting the GBA are quickly moving towards clinical use. Intestinal molecules like fecal miRNA show promise as early SAE biomarkers. Treatments such as fecal microbiota transplantation and probiotics could restore gut health and reduce neuroinflammation. Additionally, targeted interventions like SCFA supplementation, tryptophan pathway modulation, and γδ T17/STING axis inhibition have shown neuroprotective effects in animal studies. Future integration of multi-omics and mechanism-based trials will enhance precise SAE diagnosis and treatment.

titre: Dietary betaine supplementation modulates feed intake via the microbiota-gut-brain axis in finishing pigs fed low-energy diets
resume: Betaine (BET), a key metabolic intermediate, regulates energy metabolism and influences feed intake, yet its mechanism remains unclear. This study investigated whether BET modulates feed intake in finishing pigs via the microbiota-gut-brain axis under varying dietary net energy (NE) levels. Seventy-two pigs (82.63 ± 4.13 kg) were allotted to six treatments in a 2 × 3 factorial arrangement, including two BET levels (0 or 1,500 mg/kg) and three NE levels (2,555, 2,475, or 2,395 kcal/kg). Results showed that, in pigs fed low-NE diets, dietary BET significantly reduced average weekly feed intake (AWFI) during week 6 (p 0.05), whereas no such effect occurred in pigs fed normal- or high-NE diets (p > 0.05). The addition of BET to low-NE diets resulted in elevated serum levels of cholecystokinin (CCK) and peptide YY (PYY), as well as a decrease in orexigenic neuropeptides (AgRP) and an increase in anorexigenic neuropeptides (POMC) within the hypothalamus (p < 0.05), indicating appetite suppression. Furthermore, BET was found to upregulate hypothalamic G protein-coupled receptor 41 (GPR41) and GPR43 mRNA expression in pigs on low-NE diets (p < 0.01). This effect was accompanied by increased volatile fatty acid (VFA) levels in both serum and hindgut digesta (p < 0.05), driven by BET-induced alterations in gut microbial composition. Notably, these compositional changes consisted of a reduction in the abundance of Prevotella and an increase in the populations of NK4A214_group and Methanobrevibacter (p < 0.05). Collectively, these findings support the involvement of the microbiota-gut-brain axis in the feed-intake response to BET under low-NE conditions and provide a mechanistic basis for further evaluating BET as a nutritional strategy to improve feed-energy utilization.

titre: Ileal transcriptional signatures associated with post-weaning growth in piglets: an exploratory comparison with hypothalamic profiles
resume: INTRODUCTION: Weaning is a major source of stress and economic lossin pig production, yet the molecular basis of individual variation inpost-weaning average daily gain (ADG) remains poorly understood. METHODS: We re-analyzed a public RNA-seq dataset (GSE324226)comprising ileal and hypothalamic transcriptomes from 24 pigletsclassified as high or low ADG and slaughtered at day 7 (D7) or day 39(D39) post-weaning (n = 6 per group and time point). Group, time andtheir interaction were modeled within each tissue, with sex, inferredfrom Y-linked gene expression and unevenly distributed between ADGgroups, included as a covariate. RESULTS: Few genes were individually differentially expressed. In theileum, genes involved in ribosome biogenesis (NES = 2.73, padj <0.001), rRNA processing and translation, together with independentlycurated MYC target gene sets, were coordinately shifted towardhigher expression in high-ADG piglets. The ribosome-biogenesissignal was strongest at D39, whereas Reactome translation andHallmark MYC-target gene sets were already enriched at D7. Thisrank-based signal was robust to leave-one-animal-out resamplingand to alternative gene-set definitions, but reflected small per-geneeffects (median log2FC = 0.26; no leading-edge gene individuallysignificant), did not separate individual animals and was not detectedby single-sample GSVA scores, indicating a group-level transcriptionalsignature; it persisted after adjustment for estimated cell-typecomposition. Ileal cholesterol biosynthesis, tricarboxylic acid cycle andoxidative phosphorylation genes showed a group × time interaction,being higher in high-ADG piglets at D7 and converging by D39.Inferred MYC and ATF6 activities, hypothalamic endoplasmic reticulumstress signatures and cross-tissue ligand-receptor expressioncorrelations did not differ significantly between groups. DISCUSSION: In independent datasets, MYC-target and translation genesets were also higher in normal- than in low-birth-weight piglets,whereas acute fasting reduced energy-metabolism but not ribosome-biogenesis gene expression. These exploratory findings nominate ilealribosome-biogenesis gene expression as a candidate transcriptionalcorrelate of post-weaning growth that requires validation at theprotein and functional level.

titre: Critical advances and translational bottlenecks of gut microbiota-gut-brain axis targeted therapy for neurodegenerative and neurodevelopmental disorders
resume: Neurological diseases have become a major global public health burden. Existing central nervous system-targeted therapies can only alleviate clinical symptoms but fail to halt the progression of neurodegenerative diseases, presenting mechanistic limitations and therapeutic bottlenecks. The gut microbiota participates in the regulation of central nervous system (CNS) homeostasis and neuropathological processes via the microbiota-gut-brain axis (MGBA). Notably, dysbiosis may induce damage to the blood-brain barrier, neurotransmitter dysregulation, and immune imbalance, thereby mediating the onset and progression of various neurological diseases, including Parkinson's disease, Alzheimer's disease (AD), autism spectrum disorder (ASD), and multiple sclerosis (MS). This article provides a systematic review of the core mechanisms by which the gut microbiome regulates neurological diseases, including inflammation regulation, oxidative stress responses, and neuroendocrine remodeling mediated by microbial metabolites. It also comprehensively summarizes the research progress, application advantages, and existing limitations of novel gut-targeted interventions, such as probiotics, prebiotics, fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), dietary interventions, and live biological therapies. At the same time, the article critically examines key bottlenecks prevalent in the field: the causal relationship between the microbiota and disease remains unclear; there is a significant translational gap between animal and human studies; there is a lack of unified standards for multi-omics analysis systems; and interference from confounding factors such as age, diet, and medications is significant. Existing research indicates that gut microbiota interventions complement traditional symptomatic treatments and hold promising prospects for early disease intervention and adjunctive therapy for refractory patients. Future efforts should integrate multi-omics and artificial intelligence technologies to decipher the causal networks governing gut-central nervous system regulation, establish standardized research frameworks, advance the clinical translation of precision gut microbiota therapies, and provide new approaches for the comprehensive prevention, control, and personalized treatment of neurological disorders.

titre: Alzheimer's Disease: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Advances
resume: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a devastating neurodegenerative condition accompanied by widespread central nervous system damage and complex networked pathogenesis spanning molecular, cellular, and systemic dimensions. Existing studies tend to focus on individual pathological cascades or monotherapeutic approaches, while overlooking the intrinsic crosstalk among protein pathology, neuroinflammation, metabolic dysfunction, and gut-brain axis imbalance, with insufficient systematic integration of nonpharmacological strategies and multifunctional nanoplatforms. Driven by intertwined molecular aberrations, glial dysregulation and systemic metabolic disorders, AD presents profound pathological complexity. Correspondingly, multitarget pharmacotherapy integrated with hierarchical nonpharmacological and nanotherapeutic interventions has achieved substantial progress, exerting synergistic effects on alleviating AD pathological cascades and optimizing overall therapeutic regimens. We comprehensively review current evidence to delineate the mechanistic landscape of AD and update therapeutic advances, including pharmacological agents, multimodal nonpharmacological interventions, and brain-targeted nanosystems for blood-brain barrier penetration, protein modulation, microenvironment remodeling, and gene editing delivery. This study underscores major research limitations and translational obstacles in therapeutic efficacy, biosafety, and nanomedicine applications. This work emphasizes biomarker-based early stratification and staged combined interventions, providing novel integrated insights into AD pathogenesis and prospective targeted therapeutic development.

titre: Gut-Induced Synuclein Propagation: A New Mechanism in Neurodegenerative Disease
resume: Gut-induced synuclein propagation has emerged as a potential mechanism linking gastrointestinal disturbances with the development and progression of Parkinson disease and related synucleinopathies. These disorders are characterized by progressive accumulation and spreading of misfolded α-synuclein (α-Syn), leading to selective neuronal dysfunction and degeneration. Although traditionally considered brain-centered diseases, increasing evidence indicates that gastrointestinal abnormalities, peripheral α-Syn pathology, and gut-associated immune alterations may precede neurological manifestations, suggesting that peripheral processes can influence disease evolution. Here, we review clinical, pathological, and experimental evidence supporting the role of intestinal environmental stress, microbial dysregulation, barrier dysfunction, and immune activation in promoting α-Syn misfolding, aggregation, and transmission through interconnected pathways. However, peripheral α-Syn abnormalities alone are unlikely to be sufficient to initiate neurodegeneration, indicating the presence of additional biological constraints. We propose a cumulative-threshold and biological-gates framework in which α-Syn induction, seed formation, propagation efficiency, anatomical connectivity, and neuronal vulnerability collectively determine whether gut-associated pathology progresses into a self-sustaining neurodegenerative cascade. Understanding the determinants that enable gut-induced synuclein propagation may provide new insights into disease heterogeneity and guide biomarker development and mechanism-based therapeutic strategies for synucleinopathies.
revue: The Neuroscientist : a review journal bringing neurobiology, neurology and psychiatry

titre: Non-invasive oral magnetoelectric vagus nerve neuromodulation for Parkinson's disease therapy
resume: Vagus nerve stimulation has shown promising neuroprotective and anti-inflammatory effects in progressive neurodegenerative disorders such as Parkinson's disease. However, its invasive nature introduces procedural and device-related risks. Here we introduce a magnetoelectric particulate system for oral delivery and non-invasive vagus nerve stimulation through the gut. The system comprises a magneto-responsive nickel ferrite core and a piezoelectric barium titanate shell, conjugated with capsaicin to specifically target TRPV1 receptors, ensuring effective adherence to the stomach lining after oral administration. Upon magnetic field stimulation, the particles generate electrical pulses that activate vagal afferent fibres, engaging the nucleus tractus solitarius in the brainstem via the gut-brain axis. This activation enhances norepinephrine production in the locus coeruleus and dopamine synthesis in the substantia nigra. Vagal efferent activation triggers the cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway, mitigating both neuroinflammation and systemic inflammation. This non-invasive approach demonstrates potential for alleviating motor symptoms and non-motor anxiety in Parkinson's disease, offering valuable insights into its mechanisms and clinical applications.

titre: Glioblastoma-associated microglia/macrophages (GAMs): Advances in knowledge and implications for glioblastoma (GBM) therapy
resume: Glioblastoma (GBM) is an exceptionally aggressive, therapy-resistant central nervous system malignancy. Within the tumour microenvironment, glioblastoma-associated microglia and macrophages (GAMs) constitute a highly heterogeneous population whose functional states profoundly influence disease progression, tissue architecture, immune evasion, and treatment response. In this review, we propose a conceptual framework in which distinct GAM phenotypes emerge from the integrated influence of vascular, tumoural, metabolic, biomechanical, neural, and immune inputs, together with glyco-immune interactions, extracellular vesicles, and epigenetic regulation. As GAMs process these cues, they actively remodel their surrounding ecosystem, sustaining a protumourigenic niche. We critically evaluate emerging therapeutic interventions-including those targeting GAM abundance, immunometabolism, mechanotransduction, and intercellular communication-as well as advanced platforms such as engineered myeloid systems, phytomedicines, targeted delivery vehicles, and gut-brain axis-based strategies. Furthermore, we address key translational bottlenecks, including extreme GAM plasticity, spatial heterogeneity, limitations of preclinical models, barriers to central nervous system delivery, and a lack of predictive biomarkers. We argue that the therapeutically relevant target is not the GAM population in isolation, but rather the diverse niche-GAM functional units and the cumulative signalling networks that sustain them. Ultimately, achieving durable clinical efficacy will require biomarker-guided, spatially informed combination regimens that selectively disrupt maladaptive myeloid states while preserving physiological microglial homeostasis.
revue: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Reviews on cancer

titre: Pilot prospective crossover study assessing the role of bile acid malabsorption in the causation and treatment of major low anterior resection syndrome: randomized clinical trial
resume: BACKGROUND: Major low anterior resection syndrome (LARS) affects approximately 60% of rectal cancer survivors, causing urgency and decreased bowel control, reducing quality of life. Bile acid malabsorption (BAM) is an under-recognized contributor whose prevalence and treatment efficacy remain unclear. This proof-of-concept study evaluated the effectiveness of colesevelam for treating LARS and described the prevalence of BAM. METHODS: This double-blind randomized placebo-controlled crossover trial was conducted between 2021 and 2024 in New Zealand. Adults aged 18-85 years with major LARS received colesevelam (up to 1.25 g, three times daily) or placebo for 5 weeks, separated by a 6-week washout period. A subset of patients underwent 75-selenium homocholic acid taurine (SeHCAT) testing for BAM. The outcomes of interest included changes in the LARS score, Fecal Incontinence Quality of Life Scale (FIQL), and Short-Form 12 (SF-12) questionnaire, with a composite outcome reflecting clinically important improvements. RESULTS: Of 80 eligible patients, 49 were randomized. However, 36 patients completed the study after washout and were included in a per-protocol analysis (mean age 71 years; 69% male). In these 36 patients, colesevelam did not significantly improve LARS scores, but did significantly improve the SF-12 mental component summary (median +2.36; 95% confidence interval 0.00 to 10.25; P < 0.01) and FIQL depression/self-perception. Eight of 19 patients (42%) had BAM and exhibited significant improvements in SF-12 physical and mental item scores with colesevelam. Using composite criteria, colesevelam produced a 33% response rate, versus 8% for placebo, with higher rates in BAM-positive (50%) than BAM-negative (11%) patients. CONCLUSIONS: BAM is a treatable contributor to LARS, present in 40% of tested patients. Although treating all LARS patients with bile acid sequestrants provides limited benefit, SeHCAT testing identifies patients likely to respond. BAM assessment would be beneficial if incorporated into LARS management.

titre: Distinct drug and aversive cue-reactivity patterns are associated with opioid use disorder
resume: BACKGROUND: Although addiction models posit that drug and aversive cues contribute to relapse, few studies have investigated cue-elicited biomarkers of relapse in opioid use disorder (OUD). METHODS: Individuals with OUD (n=64, 20F) and healthy controls (CTL; n=35, 19F) completed a cue-reactivity task during functional magnetic resonance imaging at baseline. Participants viewed Negative, Neutral, and Drug cues and provided ratings of valence, arousal, stress, and urge to use drugs. OUD participants were followed up for a three-month period to determine abstinence (n=29) versus relapse (n=35). Blood oxygen-level-dependent (BOLD) signals were extracted from striatum, insula, anterior cingulate cortex [ACC], amygdala, and hippocampus regions of interest (ROI). Linear mixed effects models were computed for ratings and ROI BOLD signals with group (OUD versus CTL; Abstinent versus Relapsed OUD subgroups) and condition as fixed factors. Whole-brain analyses were computed to complement ROI analyses, and both were corrected for multiple comparisons. RESULTS: Compared to CTL, OUD reported greater arousal, stress, and urge ratings to Drug cues but exhibited lower nucleus accumbens, insula, and ACC ROI BOLD signal to Negative cues. Whole-brain results replicated this pattern in OUD and also revealed blunted (a) inferior frontal and precentral gyri responses to Negative cues; and (b) orbitofrontal cortex responses to Drug cues. In contrast, OUD subgroups did not differ on subjective or brain responses. CONCLUSIONS: Disengagement from aversive stimuli via interoceptive and reward circuitry may be a vulnerability marker for OUD. Replication is warranted across additional aversive paradigms and OUD samples powered to evaluate longitudinal outcomes.
revue: Biological psychiatry. Cognitive neuroscience and neuroimaging

titre: Alteration in functional-structural connectivities of insula is associated with hypoxic ventilation
resume: BACKGROUND: Hypoxia elicits ventilatory adaptation, and the anterior insula, a hub for interoceptive and exteroceptive integration, is highly vulnerable to hypoxic stress. We hypothesised that it mediates hypoxia-related ventilatory regulation. METHODS: Thirty-one college students completed 30 days of high altitude exposure. Respiratory function tests and multimodal MRI were conducted immediately at high altitude. Moreover, follow-up MRI scans were performed 7 days, 2 months, and 3 months after the students returned to sea level. RESULTS: Pulmonary function (peak expiratory flow (PEF), forced vital capacity (FVC), forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1), FEV1/FVC%, maximal mid-expiratory flow (MMF) and minute ventilation (MV)) significantly declined after high altitude exposure. The ALFF increased in the insular cortex, with enhanced FC with the thalamus, motor cortex and postcentral cortex. FC of the left anterior insula with the thalamus was negatively correlated with FEV1 predicted values, while right lateral prefrontal insula-thalamus connectivity was positively correlated with FEV1 and MMF. FC of the anterior insula with the motor cortex and postcentral cortex was negatively correlated with PEF%, FVC and FEV1, respectively. Moreover, fibre pathways linking the anterior insular cortex with the thalamus, motor cortex and postcentral cortex showed increased fibre numbers between these brain regions. Follow-up MRI studies showed that ALFF in the anterior insular cortex was significantly increased immediately after reoxygenation and then recovered to baseline level. CONCLUSION: The anterior insula may serve as a potential hub for integrating hypoxic signals from the thalamus and modulating motor cortex activity, which may contribute to hypoxic ventilation.

titre: A qualitative exploration of self-control, emotions, and interoception in anorexia nervosa
resume: Anorexia nervosa (AN) is a prevalent condition associated with significant impairment across multiple domains of life and limited effective treatments. There is a need to refine theoretical frameworks of AN. There is also growing recognition of the value of incorporating first-person perspectives to inform researcher-derived models of mental disorders. Among individuals with lived experience of AN, this study aimed to explore the components of a previously proposed model that integrates self-control, emotions, and interoception. Using virtual semi-structured interviews, we asked ten adults (nine women, one non-binary individual) to describe their experiences of self-control, emotions, and interoception across different stages of their eating disorder. Interviews were recorded, transcribed, and analyzed using codebook thematic analysis. Five themes were identified: negative emotions, control to cope, salience of interoception, tension, and changes over time. Together, the findings highlight the dynamic and evolving nature of AN, as well as the coexistence of opposing experiences. Clinically, these results underscore the importance of attending to multiple interacting mechanisms rather than isolated symptoms, and of tailoring interventions to the stage and dominant processes of illness. Approaches that explicitly acknowledge ambivalence and shifting experiences of control may be particularly valuable.

titre: Mapping three decades of consciousness research in neuroscience: a scientometric synthesis of intellectual evolution and emerging frontiers
resume: Over the past three decades, consciousness research in neuroscience has expanded into a broad and increasingly diverse field. Despite significant progress, a quantitative understanding of how these research areas have collectively evolved has remained limited. In this study, we conducted a large-scale scientometric analysis of consciousness research in neuroscience based on 22,836 publications and 639,975 cited references retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection spanning 1998-2025. We identified three major research paths: neural correlates of conscious contents and states, internal awareness and self-consciousness, and integrative approaches bridging these two paths. Emerging hotspots included neural mechanisms of consciousness, subjective experience, disorders of consciousness (DoC), and interoception. Despite increasing boundary-spanning research across different areas, bibliometric connections between DoC and other major topics, particularly subjective experience and interoception, remain comparatively sparse. These findings provide a field-level synthesis of consciousness research in neuroscience, offering a quantitative framework for understanding its development and emerging research directions.

titre: Non Pharmacological Pain Management in Sickle Cell Disease, a Narrative Review
resume: BACKGROUND: Pain is a major cause of morbidity, disability, and reduced quality of life among people living with sickle cell disease (SCD). Although pharmacological treatment remains essential, non pharmacological interventions may provide complementary strategies for pain coping and symptom management. However, the strength of evidence supporting individual interventions varies considerably. OBJECTIVE: This narrative review aimed to critically evaluate the evidence for non pharmacological interventions used to manage acute and chronic pain in SCD, distinguish disease-specific findings from indirect evidence, identify limitations in the literature, and discuss implications for clinical practice and resource-constrained settings. METHODS: The review examined randomized controlled trials, quasi-experimental studies, observational studies, systematic reviews, and clinical practice guidelines addressing non pharmacological pain management in SCD. The evidence covered psychological and behavioral interventions, physical and sensory approaches, technology-assisted interventions, and supportive coping practices. Original SCD-specific studies were prioritized when evaluating intervention effectiveness. Findings from other chronic pain populations were treated as contextual evidence rather than proof of effectiveness in SCD. RESULTS: The evidence was most developed for selected psychological and behavioral interventions, particularly cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) and biofeedback in pediatric populations. In a multicenter randomized controlled trial involving adolescents with SCD, a digital CBT intervention was associated with a greater reduction in average pain intensity and fewer pain days at six months than an education control. Pediatric systematic reviews also identified studies investigating massage, virtual reality, yoga, and biofeedback; however, the evidence was limited by intervention heterogeneity, small sample sizes, methodological limitations, and inconsistent outcome reporting. The American Society of Hematology conditionally recommended massage, yoga, transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS), virtual reality, and guided audiovisual relaxation as adjuncts for acute SCD pain, based on very-low-certainty evidence. The available evidence for TENS was insufficient to establish benefit or harm. SCD-specific evidence for acupuncture, mindfulness-based interventions, hypnosis, and spiritual interventions was insufficient to establish their comparative analgesic effectiveness. CONCLUSION: Non pharmacological interventions may complement pharmacological treatment and support pain coping in SCD, but their effectiveness should be evaluated individually rather than assumed across intervention categories. Clinical decisions should consider patient preferences, intervention-specific evidence, clinical circumstances, safety, and local resources. Larger controlled trials and implementation studies, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa and other low- and middle-income countries, are needed.

titre: Added value of mindfulness in a digital cannabis intervention: Three-arm randomized trial
resume: PURPOSE: Digital interventions for cannabis use typically produce small short-term effects that fade over time. This three-arm randomized controlled trial examined whether integrating mindfulness into an established digital cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) self-help intervention improves the durability of outcomes. METHODS: We randomized 301 frequent adult cannabis users to Mindfulness CANreduce (mindfulness-enhanced CBT), Standard CANreduce (CBT only), or a waitlist control group with continued access to care as usual. The primary outcome was self-reported cannabis use days in the past 30 days, assessed at 6 weeks, 3 months, and 6 months, and analysed on an intention-to-treat basis using zero-inflated negative binomial mixed models with multiple imputation. MAIN RESULTS: Retention was 51.8% at 6 weeks and 31.6% at 6 months, and 6-month attrition did not differ across groups. At 6 weeks, both active interventions reduced cannabis use days relative to the control group (IRR = 0.76, 95% CI [0.64, 0.90]; IRR = 0.80, 95% CI [0.67, 0.95]). At 6 months, the Mindfulness CANreduce group reported fewer use days than both the Standard CANreduce group (IRR = 0.52, 95% CI [0.43, 0.64]) and the control group (IRR = 0.46, 95% CI [0.38, 0.56]), with greater improvements in depressive and anxiety symptoms. Complete-case and tipping-point sensitivity analyses supported these findings, which remain conditional on assumptions about the missing data. CONCLUSION: Integrating mindfulness into a fully automated digital intervention was associated with more durable reductions in cannabis use. Given the low retention and engagement, these findings should be interpreted cautiously.

titre: Potential Applications of Brain-Computer Interface Technology in the Rehabilitation of Patients with Anxiety Disorders: A Narrative Review
resume: Anxiety disorders are among the most prevalent mental disorders worldwide and can cause persistent impairment in emotional regulation, cognition, and social functioning. Pharmacotherapy, psychotherapy, exercise, and non-invasive brain stimulation are widely used, yet their effectiveness may be constrained by dependence liability, interindividual variability, treatment engagement, incomplete response, and limited objective measures of treatment processes. Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) acquire, decode, and feed back neural signals-most commonly electroencephalography (EEG), functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), or real-time functional magnetic resonance imaging (rt-fMRI)-thereby converting anxiety-related brain activity into targets that can be monitored, trained, or used to trigger intervention. This narrative review examines the mechanistic rationale for BCI-assisted anxiety rehabilitation, technological approaches across levels of invasiveness, and integration with pharmacological, psychological, and exercise-based care. Current evidence indicates that EEG has been used for both anxiety-state recognition and neurofeedback; rt-fMRI enables targeted modulation of deep emotion-related networks and functional connectivity; and fNIRS offers promise for portable prefrontal monitoring and as an input signal for closed-loop systems. Invasive closed-loop systems can directly record from and stimulate local or deep circuits, but anxiety-related evidence is derived mainly from animal studies, patients undergoing intracranial monitoring, and neurological populations with comorbid anxiety, and therefore demonstrates technical feasibility rather than efficacy in primary anxiety disorders. Overall, BCIs are better positioned as potential adjuncts to established care than as replacements. The field remains limited by small, single-center studies, inadequate follow-up, heterogeneous acquisition and training protocols, and unresolved governance of neural data. Because this is a narrative review without a formal risk-of-bias assessment or meta-analysis, its conclusions should be regarded as exploratory. Multicenter randomized controlled trials, harmonized technical and reporting standards, cross-device external validation, and risk-proportionate ethical and regulatory frameworks are needed to determine whether BCIs can be translated from proof of concept into safe, effective, and implementable tools for anxiety rehabilitation.

titre: Self-Guided Beta-Responsive Visual Neurofeedback in a Public Exhibition: Feasibility and Usability Randomized Controlled rial
resume: BACKGROUND: Neurofeedback is studied for stress and anxiety regulation, but most systems require supervision or research-grade equipment. Consumer electroencephalography (EEG) could broaden access, yet autonomous first-contact feasibility, usability, and baseline neural-state effects remain unclear. OBJECTIVE: We assessed autonomous completion and usability, tested whether a fixed breathing pacer improved outcomes over visual neurofeedback alone, and explored whether pretask resting beta was associated with usability. METHODS: We conducted a single-session, 2-arm randomized feasibility and usability trial at a public science exhibition in Bern, Switzerland, between March and June 2025. Eligible adults were aged 18 years or older, could read German or French, and reported no epilepsy or implanted electronic device. A tablet app guided participants without experimenter assistance through consent, setup, a 30-second eyes-closed baseline, 1:1 randomization, a 120-second beta-responsive task, and questionnaires. The final analytic sample included participants assigned to visual neurofeedback only (VN; n=27) or visual neurofeedback plus a 6 breaths/minute breathing pacer (VN+BP; n=25). Outcomes were usability, relaxation, and state mindfulness. Data were collected prospectively; no secondary data were used. Analyses used Mann-Whitney U, chi-square, Spearman, and permutation tests (2-sided, α=.05); EEG outcome and item analyses were exploratory. RESULTS: Of 110 visitors initiating a session, 79 completed the task with a valid EEG recording (71.8%, 95% CI 62.8-79.4) and 52 met analytic criteria (47.3%, 95% CI 38.2%-56.5%). Participants (35 women) had a mean age of 39.0 (SD 11.3) years. Usability was good (System Usability Scale [SUS] mean 72.3, SD 14.7; 95% CI 68.3-76.2), and 31/52 participants scored at least 68 (59.6%, 95% CI 46.1%-71.8%). Usability did not differ between VN and VN+BP (median 75.0, IQR 62.5-81.3 vs median 72.5, IQR 65.0-90.0; Mann-Whitney U=362.5, P=.65; rank-biserial r=-0.07, 95% CI -0.39 to 0.25). Relaxation (median 63.0, IQR 50.0-80.0 vs median 61.0, IQR 50.0-67.0; Mann-Whitney U=276.5, P=.27; r=0.18, 95% CI -0.14 to 0.49) and mindfulness (median 2.4, IQR 2.1-2.8 vs median 2.5, IQR 2.0-3.2; Mann-Whitney U=346.5, P=.68; r=-0.07, 95% CI -0.39 to 0.26) did not differ. Higher resting beta was associated with lower SUS before correction (Spearman ρ=-0.31, 95% CI -0.54 to -0.04; raw P=.03), but not after Benjamini-Hochberg correction (adjusted P=.30). SUS item analyses showed a global pattern (permutation P=.02), strongest for functional integration (ρ=-0.43, 95% CI -0.63 to -0.18; Holm-adjusted P=.01). CONCLUSIONS: This trial evaluated an autonomous consumer-EEG neurofeedback system integrating self-fitting, signal-quality checking, baseline calibration, adaptive feedback, randomization, and self-report without operator support. Many first-time users completed the autonomous workflow with acceptable-to-good usability; a fixed, open-loop breathing pacer did not improve usability, relaxation, or state mindfulness; and higher resting beta showed a preliminary association with lower perceived usability. These findings support autonomous consumer-EEG neurofeedback and motivate work on adaptive onboarding, validated EEG pipelines, and objective self-regulation outcomes.

titre: Therapeutic alliance as a mediator of message-based and video-based psychotherapy for adults with depression: A secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial
resume: BACKGROUND: There is robust evidence that therapeutic alliance contributes to the effectiveness of face-to-face psychotherapy, but less knowledge of its role in video-based psychotherapy (VBP) and message-based psychotherapy (MBP). This secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial examined therapeutic alliance as a mediator of treatment effects on depression severity and explored age, gender identity, and prior psychotherapy experience as potential moderators. METHODS: Participants (N = 850; M [SD] age, 33.8 [10.5] years) were randomized to MBP or VBP on Talkspace. Therapeutic alliance was measured at week 4 post-baseline, and depression severity was measured at baseline and week 5. Mediation and moderated mediation models were examined using path analysis with cluster bootstrap CIs. RESULTS: Therapeutic alliance was statistically significantly stronger in VBP than MBP (b = -5.43, SE = 1.19, p < .001), and stronger alliance was associated with lower depression severity across conditions (b = -0.13, SE = 0.01, p < .001). The indirect effect was statistically significant (b = 0.68, 95% CI [0.36, 1.03]) and opposite in direction to the direct effect (b = -0.81, SE = 0.32, p = .01). Depression outcomes were not significantly different between conditions (p = .73). The mediation effect was moderated by gender identity and prior psychotherapy experience. CONCLUSIONS: Despite weaker alliance in MBP, depression outcomes were comparable between modalities, suggesting that other factors may offset MBP's alliance disadvantage. Future research may examine alliance longitudinally alongside other variables, such as frequency of contact, to better understand treatment processes in MBP and VBP.

titre: Clinical practice guideline recommendations for subthreshold depression in adults: A systematic review
resume: BACKGROUND: Subthreshold depression (SD) is highly prevalent and associated with increased risk of major depressive disorder (MDD) and other adverse outcomes. Despite substantial mental healthcare needs, treatment recommendations remain dispersed across clinical practice guidelines, hindering healthcare professionals from obtaining a cross-guideline overview. OBJECTIVES: To synthesize recommendations concerning SD and identify consistencies and inconsistencies across guidelines. METHODS: Guideline-related websites and electronic databases were systematically searched. Recommendations concerning SD formed the primary narrative synthesis. Recommendations for adjacent mild MDD were synthesized separately as contextual evidence to support interpretation of treatment-recommendation patterns surrounding SD. Guideline-level methodological quality was assessed using AGREE II. RESULTS: Thirteen guidelines were included. SD was rarely addressed separately and was usually grouped with mild MDD or mild-to-moderate MDD. Five guidelines described recommendation-formulation frameworks incorporating the stepped-care principle. For SD, no guideline providing recommendations on antidepressant use supported routine use or positioned antidepressants as initial treatment; when considered, their use was limited to specific circumstances. In turn, all guidelines with formal, intervention-specific management recommendations placed low-intensity psychosocial or psychological interventions or supportive care at the start of care. The contextual synthesis for mild MDD showed a predominant pattern aligned with the overall SD pattern, although minority patterns included antidepressants as standard options or more psychotherapy options requiring trained professionals. The SD and predominant mild-MDD patterns persisted in quality-restricted analyses, while the minority antidepressant pattern for mild MDD was no longer observed. CONCLUSION: For SD, the primary synthesis identified a coherent pattern of low-intensity initial management rather than routine antidepressant use.

titre: Parent Anxiety and Response to a Telehealth Intervention for Hypoglycemia Fear: Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Trial
resume: BACKGROUND: Parents of young children with type 1 diabetes (T1D) frequently report fear of hypoglycemia (FH), which can impact their diabetes management. REDCHiP (Reducing Emotional Distress for Childhood Hypoglycemia in Parents) is a telehealth-delivered cognitive behavioral intervention shown to reduce FH, but less is known about which parents benefit most. OBJECTIVE: This secondary analysis examined whether pretreatment parent anxiety moderated REDCHiP's effects and explored responder patterns by intervention arm and pretreatment anxiety. METHODS: This was a secondary analysis of a large, randomized clinical trial comparing REDCHiP to an attention control condition (ATTN). We assessed outcomes before treatment (time 1) and 3 months after treatment (time 3). Our primary outcome was parental FH at time 3, adjusted for time 1 FH. The original trial used validated measures of parent FH and general anxiety. We evaluated parent anxiety at time 1 as both a categorical variable (clinically elevated or not) and a continuous variable (centered). We defined responders as parents achieving a reduction of ≥0.5 SDs in FH from time 1 to time 3. An analysis of covariance tested the treatment arm by anxiety interaction, with sensitivity analyses modeling anxiety continuously. RESULTS: There was no significant treatment arm by anxiety interaction when modeling parent anxiety as either a categorical or continuous variable (P>.05). However, exploratory analyses found that the adjusted mean time 3 FH was numerically lower among REDCHiP parents than ATTN parents with clinically elevated anxiety. Among parents with elevated anxiety, 78.6% (22/28) of REDCHiP parents met our responder criterion compared with 47.4% (9/19) of ATTN parents. Among parents with elevated anxiety, the adjusted odds of meeting the responder criterion were higher for REDCHiP than ATTN parents (odds ratio 6.35, 95% CI 1.47-29.00). CONCLUSIONS: While time 1 parent anxiety did not significantly moderate treatment response, exploratory analyses suggested a potentially meaningful pattern among parents with clinically elevated anxiety. As telehealth-delivered behavioral interventions expand in pediatric type 1 diabetes care, secondary analyses of participant characteristics may help guide targeted implementation and enhance treatment benefit.

titre: Videoconference-based cognitive behavioral therapy for children and adolescents with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a pilot randomized controlled trial
resume: Access to evidence-based psychological treatments for children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) remains limited by therapist shortages and geographical barriers. Videoconference-based cognitive behavioral therapy (vCBT) may provide an alternative to face-to-face CBT, but evidence in young populations is limited. This pilot randomized controlled trial (RCT) examined the feasibility and preliminary treatment outcomes of vCBT for children and adolescents with ADHD in Japan. Twenty-four participants with ADHD aged 11-17 years were randomized to a 12-week vCBT program (n = 11) or treatment-as-usual waitlist (n = 13). The primary outcome was change in ADHD symptoms on the Parent-Rated ADHD Rating Scale-IV (ADHD-RS-IV) from baseline to week 13. Secondary outcomes included depression, anxiety, quality of life, and self-esteem. The trial was registered at the UMIN Clinical Trials Registry (UMIN000048064). Completion and assessment rates were 100%. The adjusted between-group difference in ADHD-RS-IV total scores was 4.43 (95% CI [-2.02, 10.89], p = .17), non-significant, but with a moderate-to-large effect size favoring vCBT. This pilot RCT demonstrated good delivery feasibility of vCBT, although recruitment feasibility posed challenges, and provided preliminary evidence of treatment effects on ADHD symptoms. A definitive RCT is warranted to confirm efficacy.

titre: An Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Umbrella Review of Eating Disorder Meta-Analyses (2020-2025): Mapping Treatment Efficacy, Comorbidity, and Persistent Gaps in Sample Diversity
resume: Background/Objectives: Eating disorders (EDs) are serious psychiatric illnesses that result in physical and mental-health impairments. A unifying summary of the broad collection of ED research findings is lacking. This umbrella review leveraged artificial intelligence (AI) to summarize ED-focused meta-analyses, to identify directions for future research and treatment. Methods: PubMed, PsycINFO, Web of Science, Embase, and ProQuest were searched for meta-analyses of human ED research published between 1 June 2020 and 31 May 2025 (inclusive). A large language model (LLM) conducted risk of bias assessment and data extraction for studies meeting all inclusion criteria. Neural topic modeling (BERTopic) identified the themes present across included meta-analyses, and an LLM summarized findings of articles in each category. Results: 220 meta-analyses were included. AI tools demonstrated good accuracy in quality appraisal, data extraction, and data synthesis (97%, 93%, and 96%, respectively). Most meta-analyses had at least one critical flaw (per AMSTAR 2 quality appraisal). Neural topic modeling identified 16 themes within the set of included articles: Neurocognition, Treatment Effectiveness, Intervention Efficacy, Biomarkers, Premorbid Conditions, Clinical Features, Epidemiology, Psychiatric Comorbidity, Behavioral Addictions, Long-Term Outcomes, Prevention, Psychological Factors, Treatment Gaps, COVID-19, Pharmacotherapy, and Avoidant Restrictive Food Intake Disorder. Article summaries collectively identified ED prevalence of 1.69% and associations of EDs with mortality and disability. Studies covered a range of illness mechanisms and treatments, though disproportionately included Western females. Conclusions: This review highlights the broad scope but limited generalizability of ED research, as well as the potential of AI to accelerate systematic review workflows.

titre: Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder: Comorbidity, Biomarkers, Circuits, and Treatment Strategies
resume: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), characterized by intrusive thoughts and repetitive behaviors, frequently co-occurs with anxiety disorders, contributing to greater diagnostic complexity, more severe symptoms, and poorer treatment outcomes. In this review, we consider OCD in the context of its comorbidity with anxiety and examine evidence that the two conditions may share genetic, neurochemical, and circuit-level vulnerabilities. Particular attention is given to the cortico-striato-thalamo-cortical, frontoparietal, and frontolimbic networks, which may interact to form a self-reinforcing cycle in which anxiety intensifies OCD symptoms, while compulsive behaviors provide transient relief but may ultimately maintain pathological patterns of brain activity. We also discuss how these shared mechanisms may shape current and emerging treatment strategies, including pharmacological approaches targeting serotonergic, glutamatergic, dopaminergic, and histaminergic systems, cognitive-behavioral interventions, and neuromodulation techniques such as deep brain stimulation, repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation, transcranial direct current stimulation, and focused ultrasound. We further consider major depressive disorder and posttraumatic stress disorder as additional examples of psychiatric comorbidity, with overlapping neural substrates and clinical features. Taken together, these findings suggest that considering comorbidity alongside core OCD symptoms may improve our understanding of its pathophysiology, help identify clinically relevant biomarkers, and support individualized treatment, while providing a broader transdiagnostic perspective on psychiatric disorders.

titre: Wernicke's encephalopathy in an adolescent with avoidant restrictive food intake disorder, juvenile dermatomyositis, attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder, generalised anxiety disorder and a complex psychosocial background
Association between obsessive-compulsive symptoms, clozapine, and other antipsychotic treatment in psychotic disorders: a systematic review and meta-analysis of epidemiological findings
resume: INTRODUCTION: Obsessive-compulsive symptoms (OCS) and obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) are common in schizophrenia spectrum disorders (SCZ), yet their aetiology remains unclear. Antipsychotics, particularly clozapine (CLZ), have been implicated, but the strength and consistency of this association remain uncertain. METHODS: A systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis was conducted to evaluate the incidence and prevalence of OCS and OCD in psychosis, comparing people treated with CLZ and other antipsychotics, including first and second generation. RESULTS: The search identified thirty two studies. The prevalence of OCS was similar between the CLZ-treated and the non-CLZ groups [41%, 95% CI: 28-54% vs. 30%, 95% CI: 22-38%; p = 0.183]. In contrast, OCD prevalence was significantly higher in the CLZ group [25%, 95% CI: 18-33% vs. 12%, 95% CI: 7-18%; p = 0.007]. De novo outcomes did not differ significantly between groups, de novo OCS was 26% [95% CI: 17-36%] with CLZ versus 14% [95% CI: 7-21%] with non-CLZ antipsychotics (p = 0.239), and de novo OCD was 22% [95% CI: 9-36%] versus 19% [95% CI: 17-21%] (p = 0.458). In the two studies that had measured the incidence of de novo OCS or OCD, the incidence rate was zero in all groups. CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest a potential association between CLZ and increased rates of OCS and OCD in cross-sectional studies, though longitudinal evidence is lacking. Methodological limitations, including detection bias, confounding by indication and limited prospective data, highlight the need for further longitudinal and pharmacoepidemiologic research to clarify causal pathways.

titre: Family Accommodation in Chinese Pediatric and Adolescent Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder: Phenomenology, Correlates and Impairment
resume: Family accommodation (FA) describes the behaviors in which family members of individuals with obsessive‒compulsive disorder (OCD) tend to modify their own routines and rituals in an attempt to help them avoid the distress caused by symptoms or prevent them from engaging in compulsive rituals. This study investigated the incidence and factors related to FA among parents of Chinese pediatric and adolescent patients with OCD. The participants included 88 young people with OCD and their parents who completed clinician- and self-reported measures. Multiple linear regression was employed to examine factors related to FA, and mediation analysis was conducted to examine the role of accommodation levels in the relationships among symptom severity, level of insight, and functional impairment. All parents reported at least one FA per week, with approximately 60% reporting some accommodations daily. Multiple linear regression indicated that functional impairment, symptom severity, and insight were associated with FA. FA mediated the relationship between symptom severity and functional impairment, as well as the relationship between insight and functional impairment. Accommodation behaviors among parents of pediatric and adolescent patients with OCD are highly prevalent and manifest in various forms. Early identification of FA, parental involvement in treatment, and direct reduction in accommodation practices during interventions help mitigate negative outcomes in youth with OCD.

titre: Neuropsychiatric Features of Individuals With LGI1-Antibody Encephalitis
resume: OBJECTIVE: Leucine-rich glioma-inactivated 1 antibody (LGI1-Ab) encephalitis is one of the most common forms of autoimmune encephalitis and is associated with prominent psychiatric features. Psychiatric phenotyping of this condition has relied on small studies and has lacked detail. METHODS: In this retrospective study, the authors reviewed the psychiatric symptomatology and clinical course among patients with a confirmed diagnosis of LGI1-Ab encephalitis. RESULTS: The mean±SD age of the study sample (N=31) was 60.7±14.2 years; 71% of patients were men. The time to diagnosis was 4.9±5.8 months, and the follow-up time was 55.8±36.7 months. Eighteen patients had documented hyponatremia, and 22 were treated as inpatients. Psychiatric (71%), cognitive (81%), and neurological (84%) symptoms were present at similar rates, despite 97% of the patients coming from neurology referrals. Patients had a diverse range of seizures, including faciobrachial dystonic seizures. Of 19 patients undergoing detailed psychometric analysis, impairments were noted in memory or orientation (100%), executive function (63%), naming (47%), processing speed (37%), attention (32%), verbal fluency (26%), language (11%), and visuospatial abilities (11%). Patients had psychotic symptoms (42%), agitation or aggression (39%), emotional lability (35%), anxiety (26%), and subjective experiential phenomena (16%). Many patients had psychiatric sequelae that resolved after treatment, but a modest proportion of patients experienced ongoing apathy (6%), behavioral disinhibition (13%), obsessive-compulsive disorder (10%), subjective experiential phenomena (13%), and sleep disorders (29%). CONCLUSIONS: These findings show that cognitive impairment and psychopathology are frequent in LGI1-Ab encephalitis. Future research could examine neuroimaging, psychiatric symptoms, and cognitive deficits in further detail.
revue: The Journal of neuropsychiatry and clinical neurosciences

titre: Enterocolitis: a diagnosis in the news that may become more common in the emergency room
resume: Foodborne illness affects an estimated 48 million people in the United States each year, and outbreaks peak in the summer. Recalls during the summer of 2026 involved eggs, jalapeños, and frozen blueberries, along with a Cyclospora outbreak traced to iceberg lettuce that caused more than 12,000 illnesses and over 550 hospitalizations. Furthermore, they caused nationwide public anxiety and dominated news headlines. Patients with enteric infection usually reach the emergency department with abdominal pain, and radiologists often read their CT before stool studies return or before anyone suspects infection. This review describes the CT findings of bacterial and parasitic enteritis and colitis. Common features include symmetric segmental or diffuse bowel wall thickening with submucosal edema, mucosal hyperenhancement producing a halo or target pattern, associated fat stranding, engorged mesenteric vessels, and lymphadenopathy. CT also shows complications including toxic megacolon, perforation, and abscess. Recognition of these findings supports timely diagnosis and appropriate management of infectious enterocolitis.

titre: Long-term (≥ 5 Years) Low Anterior Resection Syndrome and Health Related Quality of Life in Rectal Cancer Patients: A Systematic Review
resume: Background Up to 80% of patients who undergo rectal resection suffer from low anterior resection syndrome, with approximately half continuing to experience symptoms more than 10 years after surgery. While short-term outcomes are well documented, evidence on long-term functional and health-related quality of life trajectories remains fragmented. There is some improvement over time, but symptoms often persist. Objective To systematically review the prevalence, severity, and long-term trajectory of low anterior resection syndrome, and its association with health-related quality of life, in rectal cancer survivors followed for at least five years after sphincter-preserving surgery. Data sources A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library from inception through September 2025. Study selection Eligible studies reported low anterior resection syndrome scores in patients at ≥5 years following sphincter-preserving rectal cancer resection. Studies lacking long-term functional assessment or not reporting low anterior resection syndrome were excluded. Interventions None; all included studies comprised observational cohort data assessing long-term functional outcomes. Main outcome measures Prevalence of major and minor Low Anterior Resection Syndrome, distribution of long-term low anterior resection syndrome severity categories, and associations between low anterior resection syndrome severity and health-related quality of life measures. Results Six studies comprising 1,000 patients were included, with median follow-up ranging from 6.9 to 14.6 years. Across cohorts, major low anterior resection syndrome was reported in 20.5-53.0% of patients and minor low anterior resection syndrome in 14.6-27.0%. Overall, 39.3% of patients experienced major low anterior resection syndrome, 21.5% minor low anterior resection syndrome, and 39.2% reported no low anterior resection syndrome at long-term follow-up. Major low anterior resection syndrome was consistently associated with significant health-related quality of life impairment across multiple domains. Neoadjuvant radiotherapy emerged as the most consistent risk factor for persistent bowel dysfunction. Limitations Heterogeneity in neoadjuvant radiotherapy, tumor height, and exclusion of patients with permanent or secondary stomas; observational designs. Conclusion Nearly half of rectal cancer survivors experience major Low Anterior Resection Syndrome ≥5 years postoperatively, highlighting the persistence of bowel dysfunction and its lasting impact on health-related quality of life. These findings underscore the need for long-term survivorship care and functional outcome monitoring.
revue: Diseases of the colon and rectum

titre: Patient-Reported Outcomes after Robotic Resection of Deep Endometriosis of the Bowel
resume: BACKGROUND: While minimally invasive surgery is the current surgical standard of care for excision of deep endometriosis of the bowel, there is little literature evaluating patient-reported outcome measures following a multidisciplinary, robotic approach. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to assess the functional outcomes of robotic surgery for patients undergoing resection of deep endometriosis involving the bowel. DESIGN: Retrospective cohort review. SETTINGS: A single academic tertiary institution. PATIENTS: Patients with endometriosis of the bowel undergoing multidisciplinary resection between January 1, 2018, and October 1, 2023. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: A survey assessing functional outcomes on a Numeric Rating Scale preoperatively and at multiple points postoperatively. RESULTS: Of 92 eligible patients, 41 completed a preoperative survey and at least one postoperative survey. Among these 41 patients, overall pain improved postoperatively from 5.3 ± 2.7 (Numeric Rating Scale) to a nadir of 1.6 ± 1.9 at 6 months and 2.3 ± 3.0 at 12 months (p < 0.001). Preoperative pain at ovulation (mean 4.2 Numeric Rating Scale ± 3.7), pre-period pain (4.9 ± 3.5), period pain (5.7 ± 3.6) and post-period pain (3.3 ± 3.3) all decreased to a mean of 1 at 12 months postoperatively (p < 0.001). The proportion of patients reporting pain impacting work decreased from 88% preoperatively to <40% postoperatively (p < 0.001). The proportion of patients happy with their bowel function increased from 39% preoperatively to 63.2% at 1 month, 80.0% at 6 months, and 69.2% at 12 months postoperatively (p = 0.014). LIMITATIONS: Only 31.7% of patients responded to their 12-month survey, tertiary care center, low diversity in patient demographics, retrospective design. CONCLUSION: In this cohort of patients undergoing multi-disciplinary robotic excision for advanced endometriosis involving the bowel, patients reported significantly improved pain and quality of life measures. See Video Abstract.

titre: Offering prenatal CFTR modulators to prevent cystic fibrosis-related organ damage in utero
resume: Background CFTR modulator therapy has drastically improved the prognosis and quality of life for those with cystic fibrosis (CF). CF complications begin to manifest in utero, including meconium ileus, and current regulatory approvals for CFTR modulator therapy does not have a pregnancy indication. Despite this, there have been several documented cases of women taking CFTR modulator therapy during pregnancy with promising results of potential CFTR correction in utero. Objective To report one center's experience offering CFTR modulator therapy to pregnant women for prenatal CF treatment. Study design Eight pregnant women carrying a fetus at risk of having CF were presented with the option of CFTR modulator therapy during pregnancy with extensive counseling on the potential benefits and risks. Records from routine clinical care from prenatal, birth, and perinatal period were collected. Results Of the eight pregnant women, three intended to take the CFTR modulator, elexacaftor/ tezacaftor/ ivacaftor (ETI), however only two were able, as the third was unable to obtain insurance authorization. In one case, the infant was homozygous for F508del(p.Phe508del, c.1521_1523delCTT, 1653delCTT) variant with signs of worsening bowel obstruction on fetal imaging, however after ETI initiation at 27 weeks he was born without meconium ileus. In the other case of CFTR modulator therapy treatment, the infant carried a CFTR variant of varying clinical consequence, Y1032C (c.3095A>G, p.Tyr1032Cys), and one disease causing CFTR variant. After ETI initiation, ultrasound findings suggestive of bowel obstruction improved and there was no meconium ileus at birth. The family who desired prenatal ETI therapy but was unable to obtain insurance coverage, also had one disease causing variant and one of varying clinical consequence, G622D (c.1865G>A, p.Gly622Asp). Despite fetal imaging concerning for bowel obstruction this infant had no meconium ileus at birth and was classified as CFTR related metabolic syndrome/CF Screen Positive Inconclusive Diagnosis. Of the remaining pregnant women, 3 declined prenatal CFTR modulator therapy, one ultimately had negative prenatal diagnostics, and another terminated the pregnancy. Conclusion Decisions to treat with prenatal CFTR modulators are complex and influenced by multiple factors including phenotype variability, inconsistent insurance coverage, and uncertain potential risks and benefits. Outcomes of these cases ranged from pregnancy termination to successful reversal of ultrasound findings suggestive of developing meconium ileus.
revue: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM

titre: Standardized Preparation of Ruyi Jinhuang Paste from Herbal Powder and Its Topical Application for Knee Osteoarthritis
resume: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a common chronic degenerative disease with an extremely high incidence in middle-aged and elderly people, characterized by a long disease course and progressive aggravation. Knee pain, swelling, and dysfunction severely reduce patients' quality of life and constitute the major health problem in this population. Currently, western medical treatments (such as non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs [NSAIDs]) can relieve symptoms. However, long-term use is often accompanied by gastrointestinal and cardiovascular risks, which can hardly meet patients' needs for long-term safe management, and the recurrence rate is relatively high. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) has a long history and extensive experience in treating orthopedic diseases. As a characteristic TCM therapy, herbal topical application is a commonly used TCM nursing intervention that can be prepared and applied without complex equipment, making it potentially suitable for use outside the hospital after appropriate instruction. This paper aims to introduce a standardized method for preparing and applying herbal ointment for self-management among KOA patients, including site selection, procedural steps, treatment duration, and other key aspects.

titre: Embodied Dynamic Causal Modelling: Brain and Cardiac Effective Connectivity
resume: Brain-body interactions underpin embodied inference and interoception, and are central to both general health and the pathophysiology of mental health disorders. These interactions are orchestrated across a hierarchy extending from the cortex, through the brainstem, to peripheral autonomic effectors. Existing methods either reduce this communication to scalar summaries or lack an invertible biophysical model, and so cannot resolve where in this extended architecture an observed effect originates. To address this, we introduce Embodied Dynamic Causal Modelling, an extension of the generative causal modelling framework that formalises hierarchical message passing across the full brain-body axis. We instantiate the framework for brain-heart interactions with the Brainstem Cardiac Network, a closed-loop neural mass model of brainstem autonomic circuitry and sinoatrial node dynamics. By incorporating five brainstem nuclei, a viscerosensory thalamic relay and the cardiac pacemaker, the network enables estimation of directed effective connectivity across the cortical-brainstem-cardiac axis. As an illustrative case study, representative of the experiments and extended physiological systems that Embodied DCM and the BCN can now interrogate, we applied the framework to simultaneously recorded electroencephalography and electrocardiography during an auditory Go/No-Go paradigm. A multimodal observation model permits joint inversion of electrophysiological and cardiac responses, so that neural and bodily measurements together constrain an account of central and peripheral dynamics. The case study shows how the framework can arbitrate between competing hypotheses about functional cytoarchitecture, distinguishing granular from agranular microcircuits within the viscero-sensorimotor hierarchy. It also shows how time-varying estimates of synaptic efficacy can be recovered alongside continuous latent neuronal dynamics, over extended windows spanning anticipation, target processing and motor inhibition. By linking neural and cardiac signals to a single generative architecture, this work moves the study of brain-heart interactions beyond correlation, providing a framework for testing theories of embodied inference and for identifying circuit-level disruptions in disorders of interoceptive and autonomic regulation.

titre: GEST-A: A Hierarchical and Dynamic Framework of Conceptual Abstraction
resume: Abstraction is central to human cognition, yet the term covers at least three senses that are routinely conflated: abstractness (how far a concept is removed from perceptible experience), specificity (how general or inclusive a category is), and the process by which conceptual change. We propose GEST-A (Grounded, Embodied, Situated Trajectories of Abstraction), a hierarchical and dynamic framework that separates these senses. Being abstract is a concept’s position in a dimensional space of grounding (physical-world constraints), embodiment (body-specific sensorimotor and interoceptive experience), and situatedness (dependence on context of use), with specificity as an orthogonal descriptor. Becoming abstract, in this view, is a trajectory through this space, driven by generalization and re-weighting of grounded, embodied, and situated content, and linked to a shift in feature structure from complete overlap to family resemblance. Using number concepts to illustrate these dynamics, we position GEST-A against earlier hybrid accounts of grounding, clarify that linguistic labels are cues and binding devices rather than constituting concepts, and argue that abstract concepts constrain rather than refute embodied cognition. We also revisit concreteness ratings and the symbol grounding problem and derive testable predictions. Abstract concepts reveal language as a powerful scaffold for building conceptual knowledge that exceeds individual sensorimotor experience.

titre: GLP-1 Receptor agonist use and attempted access in individuals with and without lifetime eating disorders: The role of diagnostic history, BMI, and medication motivation
resume: Abstract Background Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist medications (GLP-1RAs) have revolutionized management of type-2 diabetes and obesity and are increasingly widespread. In eating disorders (ED), where dietary restriction is a triggering and maintaining factor, concerns have been raised regarding risks related to GLP-1RAs. Methods We studied self-reported prescribed, unprescribed, and attempted use in 5882 individuals with various lifetime EDs compared to 1322 controls, stratified by highest lifetime body mass index (BMI) following drug indication thresholds (above 30 or above 27 with complications, e.g. hypertension). Logistic regression models using single-diagnosis- and mutually adjusted models was used, and prescription for T2D was used as a covariate to control for purely medically motivated use. Results Lifetime atypical anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa, and binge eating disorder were generally associated with higher engagement compared to controls. Anorexia nervosa was associated with lower engagement in participants with lifetime BMI above 30, but higher engagement in BMI strata below 30 and below 27. Sex-separated analyses suggested higher engagement in males with lifetime anorexia nervosa also in higher-weight strata. Avoidant-restrictive food intake disorder did not differ from controls on any outcome. While weight loss was the primary motivation for engagement, a notable proportion cited management of binge eating even though that is not among the approved indications. Conclusions Findings suggest that lifetime ED is associated with heightened drug-seeking and inappropriate use in some individuals, and support recent calls for increased monitoring of ED history and symptoms in relation to GLP-1RA treatment.
