titre: Prevalence and characteristics of Avoidant/Restrictive Food Intake Disorder (ARFID) among Danish children and adolescents referred to paediatric outpatient assessment for gastrointestinal symptoms
resume: Background Avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder (ARFID) is a recently introduced diagnosis within the eleventh version of The International Classification of Diseases (ICD-11) [1, 2]. ARFID is categorized as an eating disorder but differs from other eating disorders as patients with ARFID are not preoccupied with body weight or shape. The restricted or avoidant eating behavior may be caused by 1) lack of interest in eating, 2) concern about perceived aversive consequences of eating such as choking, vomiting, or bloating, or 3) hypersensitivity regarding the smell, taste, texture, or temperature of the food [2]. The diagnostic criteria of ARFID further include either impaired psychosocial functioning or somatic consequences [2]. In Australia, ARFID symptoms are reported in approximately 2% of adolescents from the general population, whereas prevalence rates of ARFID between 5% and 22.5% have been found in American and Canadian specialized eating disorder clinics [3, 4]. Both somatic and psychiatric comorbidity is common among individuals with ARFID [4, 5]. Particularly gastrointestinal symptoms and disorders have been found highly prevalent [4, 6]. Within paediatric gastroenterology, prevalence estimates of ARFID range from 1.5% in a chart review of a broad clinical sample to 65.2% in a sample of patients with functional dyspepsia [7-9]. There is an increasing awareness of the intersection between ARFID and disorders of gut-brain-interaction (DGBI), also called functional abdominal syndromes [10-12]. Parental psychological factors have been shown to play an important role in paediatric DGBI. Specifically, parental pain catastrophizing and health anxiety by proxy have been associated with poorer child quality of life, greater gastrointestinal anxiety, and increased functional disability [13, 14]. Another relevant psychological construct is illness perceptions, defined as the beliefs and expectations individuals develop about an illness, which influence their coping [15, 16]. In adults with DGBI, including irritable bowel syndrome, negative illness perceptions have been associated with reduced health-related quality of life [17, 18]. To date, no studies have investigated whether parental illness perceptions, pain catastrophizing, or health anxiety by proxy are associated with the presentation of ARFID in children and adolescents with gastrointestinal symptoms. Beyond their potential influence on symptom presentation, parental beliefs and concerns may also shape how symptoms are perceived, interpreted, and reported. Parent–adolescent disagreement is common in the assessment of child and adolescent mental health symptoms [19], but little is known about agreement regarding ARFID and related symptoms. Examining parent–adolescent correspondence may therefore clarify whether parent report alone adequately captures possible ARFID in older adolescents. With the upcoming implementation of ICD-11 in Denmark, there is a need for knowledge regarding the occurrence and clinical presentation of ARFID in Danish healthcare settings [20]. Paediatric gastroenterology represents a particularly relevant clinical context, given the substantial overlap between ARFID and gastrointestinal symptoms, including DGBI, as well as the risk that ARFID may remain unrecognized when clinical attention is primarily directed towards somatic symptoms. Investigating ARFID in this setting, including the potential influence of parental psychological factors, may contribute to improved identification, diagnostic assessment, and clinical management of the affected children and adolescents. titre: THE ROLE OF GUT MICROBIOTA DYSBIOSIS IN GASTROINTESTINAL DISEASES
resume: The gastrointestinal (GI) microbiota comprises trillions of microorganisms, including bacteria, viruses, fungi, and archaea, that inhabit the human gastrointestinal tract and play essential roles in digestion, immune system development, and metabolic regulation [1, 2]. Estimates suggest that the number of bacterial cells in the human body is approximately comparable to the number of human cells [1]. In healthy individuals, the gut microbiota is commonly dominated by members of the phyla Firmicutes and Bacteroidetes, while Actinobacteria, Proteobacteria, and Verrucomicrobia are generally present in lower proportions [7]. Alterations in the composition, diversity, and functional activity of the gut microbiota, collectively referred to as dysbiosis, have been associated with the development and progression of numerous disorders, including inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), Clostridioides difficile infection, and other gastrointestinal pathologies [2, 3]. Consequently, investigating microbiota-related disturbances represents an important area of contemporary clinical gastroenterology.
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

titre: Expert Consensus on the Clinical Application of Probe-based Confocal Laser Endomicroscopy in Colorectal Cancer, Precancerous Lesions, and Inflammatory Bowel Disease
resume: Colorectal diseases pose a serious threat to human health, and conventional endoscopy has limitations in lesion characterization. This consensus aims to clarify the indications, operational specifications, image interpretation criteria, and quality control requirements for probe-based confocal laser endomicroscopy (pCLE) in lower gastrointestinal diseases, particularly colorectal cancer, precancerous lesions and polyps, and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). A systematic literature search covered PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, CNKI, and Wanfang Database through August 2026. Evidence was graded using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation system. Forty-eight experts participated in two rounds of discussion and online voting, with agreement ≥80% required for consensus. Eight recommendations were finalized: five strong and three weak. Strong recommendations address colorectal lesion differentiation, targeted biopsy, mucosal barrier assessment, ulcerative colitis mucosal healing and relapse prediction, and IBD-associated colorectal neoplasia surveillance. Weak recommendations address distal resection margin assessment during radical surgery for low rectal cancer, irritable bowel syndrome research, and adjunctive IBD diagnosis and differentiation. Evidence for endoscopic resection margin assessment remains insufficient, and pCLE is not recommended for routine diagnosis of irritable bowel syndrome. pCLE provides adjunctive microscopic information for colorectal lesion characterization, targeted biopsy, and IBD assessment and surveillance; in IBD diagnosis, it does not replace conventional endoscopic and histopathological evaluation. This consensus provides evidence-based guidance for standardized clinical application.

titre: THE GUT–BRAIN AXIS: AN AYURVEDIC INTERPRETATION OF GRAHANI, AGNI AND MANOVAHA SROTAS
resume: The gut–brain axis describes bidirectional communication between the gastrointestinal tract and the central nervous system through neural, endocrine, immune, and microbial pathways. Its clinical relevance is evident in disorders of gut–brain interaction, in which altered motility, visceral sensitivity, and central processing can contribute to symptoms. Ayurveda discusses digestive and mental function through concepts including Grahani, Agni, and Manovaha Srotas. This conceptual review examines how these frameworks may inform a dialogue about digestion, emotional experience, and patient care. Selected classical-text presentations, contemporary biomedical literature, clinical guidance, and intervention studies were reviewed narratively. Grahani provides a traditional account of digestive retention and processing, Agni describes transformative capacity, and Manovaha Srotas concerns mental function within an Ayurvedic framework. These concepts offer interpretive parallels, but they are not established equivalents of the intestinal microbiome, digestive enzymes, vagal pathways, or contemporary psychiatric diagnoses. Responsible integration combines culturally meaningful health education with appropriate diagnostic assessment and evidence-based dietary, medical, and psychological care. Specific Ayurvedic interventions require independent evaluation of their efficacy, quality, and safety.
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

titre: P039 | GUT-BRAIN AXIS ALTERATIONS IN A NITROGLYCERIN MODEL OF MIGRAINE: FROM MICROBIOTA DYSBIOSIS TO TRIGEMINAL SENSITIZATION
resume: Background. Growing evidence implicates the gut–brain axis in migraine pathophysiology; however, the mechanisms linking gut microbiota (GM) dysbiosis, microbial metabolites, intestinal inflammation, and trigeminal nociception remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated these mechanisms in a nitroglycerin (NTG)-induced chronic migraine model.Methods. Adult male rats received five injections of NTG (5 mg/kg, i.p.) or vehicle every other day over a 9-day period. Trigeminal nociceptive sensitization was assessed 4 hours after the last administration, using the orofacial formalin test. Gut microbiota composition was analyzed in fecal samples by 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Differential abundance analysis was assessed using DESeq2, while PICRUSt2 was used to predict microbial functional profiles. Fecal and serum short-, medium-, and long-chain fatty acids were quantified by GC–MS. Inflammatory markers were evaluated in ileum, colon, and cervical spinal cord by RT-qPCR.Results. Compared with controls, NTG-treated rats exhibited significant trigeminal hyperalgesia at the orofacial formalin test. Alpha diversity of the gut microbiota was unchanged, whereas beta diversity analysis revealed a distinct microbial community structure in NTG-treated rats. Differential abundance analysis showed a reduction in specific Firmicutes taxa and an enrichment of Bacteroidota-associated taxa, including members of the Rikenellaceae family and the Clostridia_vadinBB60_group genus. Functional prediction indicated an increased representation of microbial pathways involved in fatty acid biosynthesis. Among the measured metabolites, fecal propionic acid levels were significantly elevated in NTG-treated animals, while other fatty acids remained unchanged. Intestinal inflammation was characterized by increased expression of IL-1β and IL-6 in both the ileum and colon. At the central level, NTG induced an upregulation of IL-6 and downregulation of IL-4 expression in the cervical spinal cord.Conclusions. Chronic NTG exposure induces trigeminal nociceptive sensitization accompanied by gut microbial dysbiosis, selective elevation of fecal propionate, intestinal inflammation, and central neuroimmune activation. These findings support the involvement of gut–brain axis-related mechanisms, whereby microbiota-associated metabolic and immune alterations may contribute to migraine-related trigeminal sensitization.

titre: Artificial Neural Network-Based Predictive Revalidation of Microbial Alpha-Diversity Patterns in an Experimental Gut–Brain Axis Model of Alzheimer’s Disease
Improving ADHD core symptoms and individual quality of life with dietary approaches through microbiota-gut-brain signalling (the ADAPT study): a prospective, randomized controlled trial
resume: Diet influences the gut microbiota, which in turn affects gut–brain signalling and may contribute to attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) pathophysiology. A microbiota-targeted diet rich in fibre and fermented foods has the potential to support microbial function and improve ADHD symptoms, offering an alternative or adjunctive pharmacological treatment where efficacy is limited. The Improving ADHD core symptoms and individual quality of life with Dietary APproaches Through Microbiota-Gut-Brain Signalling (ADAPT) study is a prospective, participant-blind, observer-blind, parallel arm, randomized trial designed to evaluate the effects of microbiota-targeted dietary intervention on ADHD symptoms and related outcomes over a 12-week intervention period, with an optional follow-up at 3-months after the end of the intervention. Adults with and without ADHD ( n = 100/group) will be randomized to either a combination intervention diet high in fibre and fermented foods (minimum 25 g of fibre and minimum of 3 servings of fermented foods daily) or a control diet (standard Irish dietary guidelines). The primary outcome will be changes in ADHD symptoms assessed using Conner’s Adult ADHD Rating Scale (CAARS). Secondary outcomes include neurocognitive function, mood, evaluation of goals individually established by participants, sleep, eating behaviour, gut microbial profile, inflammatory and immune markers, and cortisol and a wide range of metabolites and protein in blood samples. Significant improvements in ADHD symptoms measured by CAARS, alongside enhanced neurocognitive function and mood, would support the effectiveness of the microbiota-targeted diet in adults with ADHD. Alterations in gut microbial composition and function, as well as correlations with symptom improvement, would provide insights into the role of diet in ADHD management. Findings related to sleep, eating behaviour, immunity and inflammation, cortisol regulation and protein and metabolite alterations would further elucidate the broader impact of diet on ADHD and overall well-being with the microbiome-gut-brain axis framework. (NCT07376746||https://www.clinicaltrials.gov/||Registered in 21-01-2026) with the Clinical Trial Registry [1].

titre: OC16 | GUT MICROBIOTA FUNCTIONAL REMODELING IN PEDIATRIC MIGRAINE: A MULTI-OMIC INSIGHT INTO NEUROACTIVE AND IMMUNOMETABOLIC PATHWAYS
resume: Background. Pediatric migraine is increasingly linked to alterations of the microbiota–gut–brain axis, but the functional activity of the gut microbiota remains poorly characterized. We integrated fecal metaproteomics and untargeted metabolomics to investigate gut microbiota-associated functional and metabolic signatures in children with migraine.Methods. Stool samples from 50 migraine patients and 24 healthy controls were analyzed by LC–MS/MS-based metaproteomics, while metabolomics was performed on 83 migraine patients and 41 controls. Microbial protein groups were functionally annotated using COG and KEGG-based approaches, and fecal metabolites were annotated from untargeted metabolomic profiles.Results. Metaproteomics revealed selective remodeling of microbial pathways related to nitrogen metabolism, arginine/citrulline and glutamate–glutamine turnover, aromatic amino acid metabolism, and short-chain fatty acid-associated functions. These changes converged with fecal metabolomic alterations involving arginine-related metabolites, glutamate/GABA-associated compounds, tryptophan- and tyrosine/phenylalanine-derived metabolites, purine intermediates, and lipid-related molecules. The nitrogen and arginine/citrulline signature suggested a potential link with nitric oxide-related pathways, whereas glutamate/GABA and aromatic amino acid alterations pointed to remodeling of neuroactive microbial functions. Changes in lipid/acyl-CoA, butanoate/propanoate, and purine-related pathways suggested an altered intestinal immunometabolic environment potentially relevant to barrier integrity, mucosal immune regulation, purinergic signaling, and microbiota–gut–brain communication.Conclusions. Integrated metaproteomic and metabolomic profiling identified selective remodeling of gut microbial functions and fecal metabolic outputs in pediatric migraine, supporting a functional microbiota signature potentially linked to nitric oxide-related metabolism, neuroactive amino acid pathways, purine signaling, and intestinal immunometabolic homeostasis.

titre: Targeting BDNF to Overcome Treatment Resistance in Depression: Research Progress from Mechanism to Clinic
resume: Depression ranks among the top causes of disability worldwide. About 40%-50% of the patients have insufficient response to conventional antidepressants, and treatment resistance has become a core clinical bottleneck. BDNF, as a key regulatory molecule of neuroplasticity, is regarded as the common final pathway of antidepressant action. This article systematically reviews the biological basis of the BDNF/TrkB signaling pathway and its differential mechanisms in treatment sensitivity and resistance. In the sensitive state, antidepressants up-regulate BDNF in the hippocampal dentate gyrus and TrkB signaling in the dorsal raphe nucleus through epigenetic modification, and promote neurogenesis and synaptic remodeling; in the resistant state, the high methylation of the BDNF promoter, the imbalance of pro-BDNF/mBDNF conversion, the disorder of TrkB conduction and the impairment of neurogenesis together constitute the molecular basis. In addition, this article sorts out the regulatory effects of genetic polymorphism, environmental stress, inflammation and the gut microbiota-gut-brain axis on the BDNF treatment response, and discusses the BDNF-based treatment stratification strategy, and holds that targeting the BDNF system is expected to provide a new strategy for the precise treatment of treatment-resistant depression.

titre: Functional food intervention alleviates cognitive impairment by reshaping the gut microbiota and restoring propionate levels: evidence from edible bird’s nest supplementation
resume: Introduction Aging-related cognitive decline is closely associated with synaptic dysfunction, neuroinflammation, and alterations in gut microbial homeostasis. Edible bird’s nest (EBN), a glycoprotein-rich functional food, has attracted attention for its potential neuroprotective effects. However, whether EBN has an ameliorative effect on aging-related cognitive impairment remains unclear. This study evaluated the effects of EBN supplementation on memory impairment in a D-galactose (D-gal) -induced aging model and explored the potential mechanisms. Methods Mice were subjected to chronic D-gal administration and treated with low or high-dose EBN or sialic acid (SA). Spatial learning and memory were assessed using the Morris water maze. Hippocampal neuronal morphology, dendritic spine density, synaptic marker expression, glial activation, and inflammatory cytokines were evaluated. Gut microbial composition was analyzed using 16S rRNA gene sequencing, while fecal short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) were quantified by gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS). Correlation analysis was performed to examine the association between gut microbial taxa and SCFA levels. Results D-gal treatment induced marked cognitive impairment in mice, as reflected by reduced spatial memory performance, decreased hippocampal dendritic spine density, and diminished expression of synaptic markers including Bdnf (brain-derived neurotrophic factor), Dlg4 (postsynaptic density protein 95), and Syp (synaptophysin). In contrast, EBN supplementation, particularly at the higher dose, significantly improved spatial learning and memory, preserved dendritic spine integrity, and upregulated the synaptic genes. Moreover, EBN effectively attenuated D-gal-induced glial activation and lowered the elevated pro-inflammatory cytokine levels in both serum and brain tissue. Analysis of the gut microbiota revealed that EBN supplementation was associated with a partial reversal of D-gal-induced shifts in microbial community structure, with a pronounced increase in the relative abundance of Lactobacillus . Concurrently, fecal propionate levels, which were reduced by D-gal treatment, were restored following EBN supplementation, and propionate abundance correlated positively with Lactobacillus . SA supplementation also showed beneficial changes in several measured outcomes, suggesting that SA may contribute to some of the responses observed following EBN supplementation. Conclusion In summary, EBN supplementation ameliorated cognitive impairment in D-gal-induced aging mice, and this effect may be associated with restoration of gut microbial homeostasis and increased fecal propionate levels. Given that aging is a major risk factor for metabolic syndrome and related cognitive decline, these findings highlight the potential of EBN as a functional food for combating age-associated metabolic and neurological disorders, possibly through modulation of the microbiota-gut-brain axis.

titre: Inflammatory Bowel Disease: Current Concepts, Therapeutic Advances and Challenges in Resource-Limited Settings
resume: Background: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), comprising mainly ulcerative colitis (UC) and Crohn’s disease (CD), is a chronic, relapsing inflammatory disorder of the gastrointestinal tract that requires long-term multidisciplinary management. IBD is increasingly recognized as an important global health problem, with its incidence and prevalence rising in many newly industrialized and developing regions. South Asia, including Bangladesh, has experienced a growing burden of IBD, reflecting changing environmental exposures, dietary patterns, urbanization, lifestyle factors, improved diagnostic capacity, and greater disease recognition. The increasing prevalence of IBD and its intestinal and extraintestinal complications highlights the need for updated approaches to diagnosis, monitoring, treatment, and prevention. Objectives: To review current concepts and recent advances in the epidemiology, pathogenesis, risk factors, clinical manifestations, biomarkers, therapeutic strategies, treat-to-target approaches, and emerging management options for IBD, with particular relevance to the growing burden in South Asia. Methods: A narrative review of relevant peer-reviewed literature was undertaken, focusing on major studies, systematic reviews, international guidelines, and clinical trials addressing the epidemiology, pathogenesis, diagnosis, monitoring, complications, and management of IBD. Particular attention was given to recent advances in biologic and small-molecule therapies, therapeutic drug monitoring, biomarkers, microbiome-directed interventions, dietary factors, and treat-to-target strategies. Results: IBD results from a complex interaction between genetic susceptibility, dysregulated immune responses, intestinal microbiota, and environmental factors. Its global epidemiological transition has been accompanied by increasing incidence and prevalence in regions where IBD was previously considered uncommon. South Asian populations are increasingly affected, although epidemiological data remain comparatively limited, particularly from Bangladesh. Advances in biomarkers, including fecal calprotectin and other inflammatory markers, have improved non-invasive disease assessment and monitoring. Contemporary management has shifted from symptom control toward objective disease modification using treat-to-target strategies. Conventional immunomodulators remain relevant, while biologic therapies targeting tumor necrosis factor, integrins, and interleukin pathways, as well as newer oral small molecules, have expanded therapeutic options. Emerging evidence also supports the potential roles of dietary modification, microbiome-directed therapies, and personalized treatment approaches. Early intervention and tight disease control may reduce inflammatory burden and the risk of long-term complications. Conclusion: IBD represents an expanding global health challenge with increasing importance in South Asia. Improved epidemiological surveillance, earlier recognition, objective monitoring, and access to evidence-based therapies are essential to address the growing disease burden. Future research in South Asian populations, particularly Bangladesh, should focus on population-based epidemiology, environmental and genetic determinants, cost-effective diagnostic strategies, and locally applicable treatment approaches. A personalized, treat-to-target model integrating clinical, biochemical, endoscopic, and patient-centered outcomes may improve long-term disease control and quality of life J Com Med Col Teachers’ Asso July 2026; 30(2): 134-141
revue: Journal of Comilla Medical College Teachers Association

titre: Symptomatology and General Principles of Treatment of Chronic Enteritis, Chronic Colitis and Ulcerative Colitis
resume: This clinical review article provides an overview of chronic enteritis, chronic colitis, and ulcerative colitis, focusing on their etiology, classification, pathophysiology, clinical manifestations, and diagnostic approaches. It discusses characteristic symptoms such as chronic diarrhea, abdominal pain, malabsorption, rectal bleeding, and nutritional deficiencies. The article also covers laboratory investigations, endoscopic evaluation, and histopathological diagnosis. Special attention is given to treatment principles, including dietary management, aminosalicylates, corticosteroids, immunomodulators, biological agents, supportive care, and surgical intervention in severe cases. It further highlights disease complications, maintenance of remission, and long-term follow-up to improve patient outcomes and quality of life.
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

titre: Long-Term Impact of Novel Microbiome Pill on Quality of Life and Gastrointestinal Symptom Relief in Recurrent C. Difficile Infections
resume: Recurrent Clostridioides difficile (rCDI) infection is associated with significant morbidity, mortality, and decreased quality of life in affected patients. Vowst is a novel oral microbiome therapeutic that demonstrated efficacy in reducing rCDI recurrence; however, limited evidence exists on the long-term impact of patient-reported gastrointestinal symptoms and quality of life beyond 12 months after treatment. This study evaluated long-term patient-reported gastrointestinal and quality of life outcomes in patients who were treated with Vowst for rCDI at least 12 months following treatment. An anonymous 18-question survey was distributed through Facebook patient support groups, Reddit and the Mayo Clinic Connect forums. Adults aged 18 years or older with a history of rCDI who had completed Vowst treatment at least 12 months earlier were eligible to participate. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics. Likert-type responses were numerically coded and paired t-tests were performed to compare pre-treatment and post-treatment responses. Eight participants met the inclusion criteria of the study and completed the survey. Improvements were observed across all assessed patient-reported outcomes. At least 75% of participants reported improvement in gastrointestinal symptoms, activity limitations, diarrhea frequency, antibiotic use, symptoms preventing leaving home, and concern about recurrence. Overall quality of life demonstrated the greatest improvement, with 100% participants reporting overall better quality of life following Vowst treatment. Given the small size and self-reported nature of the study, these findings are exploratory and do not establish a causal relationship between Vowst treatment and reported improvements. This study suggests that Vowst not only prevents recurrence but also may be associated with sustained improvements in daily functioning and overall well-being more than one year after treatment. These findings support the continued evaluation of quality of life and patient-reported outcomes in larger, prospective studies of microbiome-based therapies.

titre: Hypnosis in Surgery: A Modern Adjunct to Anesthesia or a Forgotten Art? A Narrative Review
resume: Hypnosis was used for surgical analgesia long before modern chemical anesthesia, yet its role in contemporary perioperative care remains contested. Interest has revived because of the need for opioid-sparing strategies. Still, the literature mixes robust trial evidence with overstated claims about physiological effects, recovery, and digital applications, and a balanced synthesis for anesthesiologists is lacking. This review aimed to clarify the neurophysiological basis, clinical applications, comparative position, and implementation barriers of clinical hypnosis in surgery. A narrative review was conducted of meta-analyses, systematic reviews, randomized controlled trials, neuroimaging studies, surveys, and methodological guidance published between 1996 and 2026, with each claim verified against its primary source. Hypnosis modulates distributed pain-processing networks. The most consistent clinical benefits are reductions in anxiety, pain, selected medication consumption, and postoperative nausea and vomiting, particularly when hypnosis is combined with local anesthesia and light sedation. In contrast, effects on stress biomarkers, wound healing, gastrointestinal recovery, and length of stay remain unproven. Effects are heterogeneous, and virtual reality-delivered hypnosis has yielded inconsistent results. The novelty of this review lies in its evidence-calibrated positioning of hypnosis as an optional, individualized adjunct within multimodal anesthesia that separates established benefits from unsupported claims.
revue: International Journal of Psycology and Health Science

titre: Clinical and pathogenetic heterogeneity of anxiety disorders in COVID-19 survivors
resume: OBJECTIVE: To analyze the clinical and pathogenetic heterogeneity of anxiety disorders in COVID-19 survivors to inform differentiated therapeutic approaches. MATERIAL AND METHODS: 27), patients with a history of anxiety or affective disorders (F32.0-F42.0) before SARS-CoV-2 infection. Clinical-psychopathological and psychometric assessments included the Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAM-A) and Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAM-D), the Generalized Anxiety Disorder questionnaire (GAD-7), and the A.M. Vein autonomic disorder questionnaire. RESULTS: Anxiety severity reached moderately severe levels (median scores on HAM-A: 24-25; GAD-7: 16). Asthenia was observed in 87.8% of patients, and cognitive impairment ('brain fog') occurred in 77.8%. Autonomic disorders (A.M. Vein average score 37.4-37.9) included cardiac (53.3%), gastrointestinal (17.8%), and pain syndromes. Three clinically relevant primary psychopathological syndromes were identified: anxiety-asthenic (61.2%), anxiety-hypochondriacal (31.1%), and anxiety-depressive (7.7%). The organic pathway (neuroinflammation) was predominant in the pathogenesis. The somatogenic pathway was associated with autonomic dysfunction and pain syndromes, while the psychogenic (nosogenic) pathway contributed to the development of anxiety-hypochondriacal and anxiety-depressive syndromes. CONCLUSIONS: Anxiety disorders in the post-COVID period are highly heterogeneous and require differentiated therapeutic approaches. Pharmacotherapy, including antidepressants and neurometabolic therapy, is indicated for the organic subtype, while psychotherapy should be prioritized for the psychogenic subtype.
revue: S S Korsakov Journal of Neurology and Psychiatry

titre: Cognitive Reserve, Interoceptive Accuracy, and Brain Electrical Activity in Middle-Aged and Older Adults From Quindío, Colombia
resume: We worked in a study with elders of Colombia, we analized interoceptions responses y cognitive flexibility of them, while we were measuring electrical activity by a portable electroencephalography (EEG) device. We uploaded here the scripts of the statistics and EEG analysis.

titre: P103 | ALEXITHYMIA INCREASES THE RISK OF MIGRAINE CHRONIFICATION IN WOMEN WITHOUT DEPRESSION
resume: Background. Alexithymia is a psychological construct, characterized by a deficit in identifying and communicating feelings. Emerging data suggest a role for alexithymia in migraine, within a complex interplay with psychiatric comorbidities. This study was aimed to investigate the relationship between alexithymia and migraine chronification in females.Methods. This was an observational, multicenter study, enrolling female patients with migraine. Each patient underwent a psychological assessment for alexithymia (TAS-20 scale), anxiety and mood comorbidities (STAI-Y1/STAI-Y2, BDI-II) and apathy (Starksteln’s Apathy scale, SAS-I). Data on headache frequency, intensity and medication use were recorded.A multivariable logistic regression model was fitted to evaluate the association between alexithymia (TAS-20 score) and the probability of chronic migraine. The model included BDI-II categories, the TAS-20 × BDI-II interaction term, STAI-Y2 and SAS-I score, age and education as covariates.Results. The study included 507 participants. In the overall sample, 384 (75.74%) had episodic migraine, 31 (6.11%) had chronic migraine (CM), 43 (8.48%) CM with medication overuse headache (MOH), and 48 (9.47%) could not be classified (missing data).Alexithymia was identified in 207 patients (40.83%), depression in 206 (40.63%). Both variables had 34 missing observations (6.7%).In the logistic regression analysis performed on complete cases (n= 366), the association between alexithymia and chronic migraine was modified by depression severity. In patients with no or minimal depression, higher TAS-20 scores were associated with a higher probability of chronic migraine. The average marginal effect of TAS-20 was 1.74 percentage points for each one-point increase in TAS-20 among patients with BDI-II score 0–4, and 0.70 percentage points among subjects with BDI-II score 5–9. Conversely, the marginal effect of TAS-20 was not statistically significant among patients with a BDI-II score >10.These findings indicate a significant interaction between alexithymia and depression, with the association between TAS-20 and chronic migraine progressively attenuating as depression severity increases. Multiple imputation analysis on the whole sample confirmed this finding, with a milder modifier effect of depression.Conclusions. These results indicate a role of alexithymia in increasing the risk of migraine chronification in women without clinically relevant depression. Moreover, a modifier effect for depression is suggested.

titre: Empathy and compassion are comparable between individuals with cervical spinal cord injury and controls, but their association with interoceptive sensibility differs
resume: Abstract The extent to which empathic and compassionate processes depend on bodily signaling remains a central and unresolved question in affective neuroscience. Although converging evidence suggests that empathy and compassion are shaped by bodily dynamics, it remains unclear how these processes are expressed when spinal body–brain signaling is extensively and chronically disrupted. We examined individuals with chronic cervical spinal cord injury (cSCI; n = 30) and healthy controls ( n = 27) to determine whether chronic disruption of spinal bodily signaling is associated with differences in self-reported empathic and compassionate dispositions and interoceptive sensibility, and whether the associations of interoceptive sensibility with empathy-related dimensions and compassion differ according to injury status. Participants completed the Interpersonal Reactivity Index (IRI), Compassion Scale, and MAIA-2, and Bayesian regression models adjusted for age, affective symptoms, alexithymia, and perceived social support. No credible group differences emerged in the total or subscale scores of the IRI, Compassion Scale, or MAIA-2. Bayes-factor comparisons for the total scores favored models without group effects for the IRI (BF₀₁ = 3.43), Compassion Scale (BF₀₁ = 2.42), and MAIA-2 (BF₀₁ = 2.66), although the evidence was weak to moderate. Despite these broadly comparable self-reported profiles, the association between interoceptive sensibility and compassion differed by injury status. Greater interoceptive sensibility was strongly associated with greater compassion in controls, whereas this association was credibly weaker in cSCI. Together, these findings indicate that chronic disruption of spinal bodily signaling is not necessarily accompanied by differences in self-reported empathic and compassionate dispositions, but may be associated with differences in how interoceptive sensibility relates to compassion.

titre: Individual differences in liking for sweetness: a follow-up study
resume: This study follows up two earlier registered studies: DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/ZRH6E, and 10.17605/OSF.IO/5AP7E) where we contrasted liking and intensity of five concentrations of sucralose with those for 1.0M sucrose. Both studies used two separate taste tests, an initial taste test using 1.0M sucrose to define participants into three distinct phenotypes (see Iatridi et al., 2019: doi:10.3390/nu11010129) and then a separate taste test using 5 concentrations of sucralose. The analysis of both those studies showed that the essential 3-phenotype model used for sucrose still separated rated liking for the higher sucralose concentrations. However, because the two taste tests were conducted separately, there is the possibility that the exposure to 1.0M sucrose in the first test influenced ratings at the sucralose taste test 20 minutes later. The present study therefore controls for that possibility by comparing responses to sucrose and sucralose in the same taste test. The second aim is to further investigate how participants defined into three sweet-liking phenotypes differ in interoceptive awareness, following evidence that extreme sweet likers showed greater interoceptive awareness than did sweet dislikers based on their behaviour on heart tracking measures of interoception (Iatridi et al., 2021: 10.1016/j.appet.2021.105290).

titre: P047 | ONABOTULINUMTOXIN-A EFFECTIVENESS EVALUATION IN CHRONIC MIGRAINE PATIENTS WITH SHORT OR LONG DISEASE HISTORY AND PSYCHIATRIC COMORBIDITIES: AN ITALIAN MULTICENTRIC STUDY (THE BACH STUDY)
resume: Background. Onabotulinumtoxin-A (OBT-A) is a worldwide approved preventive treatment for patients suffering from Chronic Migraine (CM). The aim of the study was to o investigate whether the disease duration for over or less than 10 years can predict OBT-A effectiveness in patients with CM and to evaluate if psychopathological profile may influence their outcome.Methods. We considered consecutive CM patients undergoing OBT-A treatment for the first time and collected Monthly Headache Days (MHDs), number of Monthly Acute Medications (MAMs), pain intensity by Numerical Rating Score (NRS), Head Impact Test (HIT-6) and Migraine Disability Assessment questionnaire (MIDAS) scores at baseline and after 3, 6, 9 and 12 months. The psychopathological profile was evaluated by Beck Depression Inventory (BDI-II), State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI-Y), Toronto Alexithymia Scale (TAS-20) at baseline, 6 and 12 months. Effectiveness of OBT-A was also evaluated by the 4D Migraine composite scale, including 4 parameters: MHD, MAMs, NRS and MIDAS scores.Results. We enrolled 183 patients (mean age 46.8 yrs, SD 15.7; 158 female); at baseline 67% had a CM history longer than 10 years, 37% were affected by depression, 36% by alexithymia and 9% by anxiety. The MHD, MAMs, MIDAS, HIT-6, NRS and 4D scores significantly decreased (p0.05). Also TAS, STAI and BDI scores decreased during the one-year follow-up, suggesting a positive effect of OBT-A treatment also on psychiatric comorbidities. Those three scores decreased more in alexithymic, anxious and depressed patients beyond what expected for the regression-to-the-mean effect. However, those patients who presented BDI higher scores at 12 months in our sample tended to have lower benefit from the OBT-A treatment in the long term.Conclusions. In our study OBT-A effectiveness was neither affected by disease history nor by psychiatric comorbidities. People with higher BDI scores at 12 months tended to have less benefit from the treatment.

titre: How to Leverage Automatic Item Generation (AIG) for Novel Psychological Constructs (Part 1)
resume: This research investigates the effectiveness of AIG for novel psychological constructs, defined as conceptually emergent constructs that lack validated measurement tools. In this research, we focus on two newly developed constructs from distinct literatures: interoceptive self-regulation (ISR) and OSAP anxiety, which refers to postsecondary students’ apprehension about the Ontario Student Assistance Program, including concerns about eligibility, repayment, and reliance on loans and grants. The broader research compares AI-generated items with human-generated items for both constructs. This pre-registration focuses specifically on the data collection of the human-generated items.

titre: Effectiveness of Eight-Session Clinical Hypnosis in Reducing Somatic Symptom Severity Among Psychosomatic Patients: A Quasi-Experimental Controlled Study From Godhra, Gujarat
resume: Background: Medically unexplained somatic complaints such as stomach pain, headache and chest tightness with normal investigation reports are very common in primary care in India, with an estimated 30–40% of primary care patients affected. Psychological services remain very limited in the Godhra region of Gujarat, and hypnosis may be useful as a primary or supportive treatment for such psychosomatic patients. Objective: To examine whether clinical hypnosis reduces somatic symptom severity among psychosomatic patients and whether it can work as a primary or supportive treatment. Methods: A quasi-experimental pre-test post-test control group study was conducted among 300 patients from Godhra city and nearby villages within 10 km, with data collected from January 2024 to January 2025. The experimental group (n = 150) received eight sessions of clinical hypnosis, twice a week for four weeks, along with routine medical treatment; the control group (n = 150) received routine treatment only. Somatic symptom severity was assessed with the PHQ-15 before and after the intervention. Paired and independent t-tests and Cohen’s d were used for analysis, with p < 0.05 considered statistically significant. Results: Internal consistency of the PHQ-15 was good (Cronbach’s α = 0.80–0.82). In the experimental group, the mean PHQ-15 score fell from 12.81 (SD 4.11) to 5.92 (SD 2.87), a reduction of 6.89 points (53.7%); t(149) = 32.49, p < 0.01; Cohen’s d = 2.65; 95% CI of the reduction: 6.47–7.31. In the control group, the mean score changed from 12.59 (SD 3.58) to 9.31 (SD 3.48), a reduction of 3.28 points (about 26%); t(149) = 20.79, p = 0.12. The improvement was significantly greater in the experimental group (6.89, SD 2.60) than in the control group (3.28, SD 1.93); t = 13.67, p < 0.01. At post-test, the experimental group scored significantly lower than the control group (5.92 vs. 9.31; mean difference −3.39; t(287.5) = −9.22, p = 0.01). Most participants were aged 36–45 years (32% in both groups), slightly more than half were female (54% and 54.7%) and most were married (84% and 86%). Conclusion: Hypnosis was associated with a significantly greater reduction in somatic complaints in this Godhra sample and worked well both as a primary and as a supportive method. Larger multi-centric trials are warranted.

titre: SMART Study of Medication and Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Treating Pediatric Anxiety Disorders, Los Angeles, California, 2021-2025
resume: In this study, researchers assessed the effectiveness of cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) and/or administering fluoxetine (Prozac) on improving anxiety symptoms for predominantly economically disadvantaged, racial- and ethnic-minority pediatric patients. Researchers were particularly interested in whether beginning with CBT or medication was more effective, if optimizing the initial treatment or adding the other treatment to the first was more effective, and whether one sequence of treatment (CBT-only, med-only, CBT-med, med-CBT) was better or worse at improving anxiety symptoms. To investigate the issue, the research team used a single-blind Sequential Multiple Assignment Randomized Trial (SMART) design of 24 weeks duration with two levels of randomization, one in each of two 12-week stages. The design used an adaptive intervention, where treatment was modified in the second trial stage based on the patient's individual response in the first stage. In Stage 1, patients were randomized to fluoxetine or CBT. In Stage 2, patients who met remission criteria continued maintenance-level therapy with the single treatment received in Stage 1. Those who did not meet remission thresholds during the first 12 weeks of treatment were further randomized to either (1) optimization of their Stage 1 treatment, or (2) optimization of Stage 1 treatment and addition of the other intervention. After the 24-week trial, the research team followed up with participants for up to 12 months post-trial to assess the durability of study treatment effects. Patients aged 8 to 17 years of age with a diagnosed anxiety disorder were recruited and treated within 9 large clinical sites throughout greater Los Angeles, California (USA) (n=272). Data were collected from child patients and caregivers at multiple timepoints throughout the trial: baseline, week 6, week 12, week 18, week 24, and 12 months post-trial. The trial initiated recruitment (first screening) in December 2020, and the final treatment (24-week assessment) occurred in November 2024. This collection contains medical and demographic data collected at baseline (DS1 through DS6), process data for randomization and stratification (DS7, DS8), adherence to medication throughout the trial (DS9), side effects experienced by patients throughout the trial (DS10, DS11), main outcomes at 24 weeks (DS12) and 1 year post-trial (DS13), and exploratory outcomes (DS14). While data from a process evaluation were collected during the study, these data are not available. Please see the Scales field for a list of measures used in the study.

titre: Cognitive-Behavioral Couple Therapy for Relationship Distress: How Maladaptive Beliefs Shape Relationship Functioning and Psychological Well-Being
resume: Relationship distress is associated with poorer psychological well-being, including heightened stress, anxiety, and depressive symptoms. Cognitive-Behavioral Couple Therapy (CBCT) focuses on couples' relationship cognitions and interaction patterns; however, few existing reviews have synthesized the effects of specific relationship beliefs and attribution processes on relationship functioning and individual psychological outcomes. This literature review examines how hostile attributions, mind-reading expectations, catastrophizing, aversion to disagreement, and rigid destiny beliefs contribute to relationship distress, and how CBCT may modify these processes. Recent meta-analyses, randomized controlled trials, longitudinal studies, and large-scale relationship research published primarily from 2020 onward are synthesized. The evidence indicates that CBCT-informed interventions can improve relationship satisfaction, communication, and selected indicators of individual well-being. Collaborative communication and reduced maladaptive attributional processing are plausible mechanisms, although causal evidence is still limited. CBCT appears most useful when cognitive restructuring is paired with behavioral practice and communication skills. Clinical interpretation should nevertheless account for cultural variation, contextual stress, unequal access, and the need for safety assessment when coercion or abuse is present.

titre: Psychological Predictors f Rehabilitation Success: The Role of Anxiety, Depression, And Self-Efficacy in Physiotherapy Outcomes After Orthopedic Injury
resume: Orthopedic injury and rehabilitation following orthopedic surgery are generally assessed through physical benchmarks; however, individuals with comparable tissue injuries who undergo comparable physical therapy regimes experience varying recovery times. The current paper assesses whether anxiety, depression, and self-efficacy account for such variations. A critical analysis of relevant research with quantitative data extraction was carried out using 24 peer-reviewed articles written between 2022 and 2026, including research focused on arthroplasty of the knee and hip, anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR), and fractures of the lower limb. Effect estimates presented in the reviewed articles were recorded verbatim and, where possible, converted into equivalent derived measures (shared variance, per 10-point odds ratios, risk ratios). Psychological morbidity was common: the prevalence varied from 17% to 43% in case of depressive symptoms/diagnoses and from 21% to 36% in case of anxiety. The state anxiety, depressive symptoms, and low self-efficacy were consistently linked to poorer outcomes in terms of self-reported pain, function, and acceptable symptom state, showing bivariate correlations in primary studies in small-to-moderate sample sizes (|r| ≈ 0.31-0.57; 10-32% shared variance). Scores taken shortly after surgery predicted chronic pain a year later following fracture fixation more strongly than baseline scores. Correlations were less strong, and frequently not significant after adjustments, for objectively measured performance variables and clinical diagnoses of mental disorders, in meta-analyses. Cognitive-behavioural and theory-based physiotherapy interventions led to improvements in psychological preparedness, self-efficacy and function, in randomised and quasi-experimental trials. There is support for systematic psychological screening and physiotherapy interventions that account for psychological issues, but the research base is limited to single-site observational cohorts with different measures.

titre: Developing and testing the effectiveness of mindfulness intervention for reducing loneliness in Hong Kong older adults: a hybrid sequential multiple assignment randomized trial, micro randomized trial experimental design study protocol
resume: Loneliness is a growing public health concern among older adults, likewise in Hong Kong. Mindfulness-based interventions have shown promise in addressing loneliness, but often yield modest and short-lived effects. Digital delivery makes such interventions scalable but sustaining user engagement remains challenging. Adaptive interventions that integrate human support, mobile technology, and machine learning show promise, yet rigorous evidence remains limited. This study aims to develop and evaluate a machine learning-enabled mindfulness intervention to reduce loneliness and enhance well-being among older adults in Hong Kong. Using hybrid Sequential Multiple Assignment Randomized Trial–Micro Randomized Trial (hybrid SMART–MRT), 275 lonely older adults will be recruited and randomized into one of the five first-line intervention conditions over 4 weeks; single session mindfulness intervention (SSI of Tele-MF) with no coaching, app-based coaching, human coaching, a combination of app-based and human coaching, or an active control. Nonresponders, defined as those who do not exhibit a decrease of at least 2.86 points on the Revised UCLA Loneliness Scale from baseline (T0) to the post-first-line assessment (T1) will be re-randomized to either intensified human coaching or booster session. Concurrently, a single daily micro-randomized notification will be used to jointly evaluate the proximal effects of (i) receiving versus not receiving a push notification (MRT 1), (ii) receiving versus not receiving a brief mindfulness exercise within a push notification (MRT 2), and (iii) receiving personalized versus standardized motivational message within a push notification (MRT 3) on subsequent app engagement. Data will be collected at baseline (T0), within 1-week after each stage of intervention (T1 & T2), and three-month (T3) and six-month (T4) after completion of second-line intervention. The primary outcome is assessed by the Revised UCLA Loneliness Scale. Secondary outcomes include De Jong Gierveld Loneliness Scale, symptoms of anxiety and depression, perceived stress, and sleep quality. Potential mediators include mindfulness, perceived social support, and social network. Linear mixed models and weighted least squares regression will be used for analysis. The finalization of intervention materials, mobile application development and personnel training was completed in May 2026. Recruitment started in June 2026, with data collection expected to be completed by March 2027. This study will be among the first to apply a hybrid SMART–MRT design to a mindfulness-based loneliness intervention for older adults. Findings will inform the development of scalable, adaptive, and personalized interventions by identifying optimal combinations of human support and machine learning–driven digital strategies to enhance engagement and reduce loneliness. ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT07308613.

titre: Beyond motor improvement: The potential role of Mindfulness across the Deep Brain Stimulation pathway in Parkinson’s Disease
resume: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) provides substantial and durable relief of levodopa-responsive motor symptoms and motor complications in people with advanced Parkinson's disease (PD), yet motor improvement does not invariably translate into satisfactory psychological, social, and quality-of-life outcomes. Anxiety, depression, apathy, cognitive vulnerability, unrealistic expectations, altered illness roles, and concerns about identity or authenticity may persist or emerge during the DBS pathway. Mindfulness-based interventions (MBIs), including mindfulness-based stress reduction and mindfulness-based cognitive therapy, have been investigated as adjunctive treatments in PD, whereas acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT) provides a related framework focused on psychological flexibility and values-guided action. This narrative review integrates the literature on MBIs in PD with evidence concerning cognition, expectations, placebo/nocebo responses, psychosocial adjustment, and identity after DBS. Small trials and meta-analyses suggest that MBIs are feasible and may improve anxiety, depressive symptoms, mindfulness skills, and some aspects of quality of life, while evidence for motor, cognitive, apathy, sleep, and caregiver outcomes remains inconsistent or preliminary. Direct trials of mindfulness in patients with PD undergoing DBS are essentially lacking. We propose that mindfulness is unlikely to enhance the neurostimulatory effect itself but may target modifiable mediators between motor capacity and lived outcome: stress reactivity, attentional control, symptom appraisal, expectation rigidity, experiential avoidance, and dyadic adjustment. A phase-specific framework is outlined for preoperative preparation, early postoperative programming, and long-term adaptation. Dedicated co-designed feasibility studies and adequately controlled trials are required before mindfulness can be recommended as a routine component of DBS care.

titre: Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (rTMS): Efficacy and Safety in Treating Adolescent Depression
resume: Adolescent major depressive disorder (MDD) may not respond to current standards of care - pharmacotherapy and psychotherapy - creating a need for alternative evidence-based treatment options. Although repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) is FDA-approved for adult MDD and is increasingly available to adolescents through FDA-cleared devices, uncertainty remains about whether its benefits and risks support adolescent-specific guidance. This study asked whether current evidence on rTMS efficacy and safety supports developing adolescent-specific guidelines for MDD. This question remains unanswered because device availability and favorable preliminary findings have outpaced consistent guideline recommendations and definitive controlled evidence in adolescents. To address this gap, clinical guidance, randomized controlled trials (RCTs), and meta-analytic evidence were analyzed to characterize treatment-versus-control outcomes, safety findings, and remaining evidence needs. A comprehensive literature review searched PubMed and OpenEvidence for English-written publications from March 2018 through June 2026 on rTMS for adolescent MDD, including guidance documents, RCTS, and meta-analyses, and excluding electroconvulsive therapy and deep rTMS studies. Evidence was analyzed by participant population, treatment and control groups, efficacy outcomes, and reported safety outcomes. Across 15 documents reviewed, rTMS generally produced greater improvement in depressive symptoms, response, and remission than control groups in three RCTs and four meta-analyses; however, one sham-controlled treatment-resistant depression trial and one RCT-limited meta-analysis were inconclusive, while adverse events occurred more frequently with rTMS treatment but were primarily mild and well-tolerated. Analysis was limited by heterogeneous patient populations, rTMS protocols, controls, outcome measures, and insufficient follow-up. This study concludes that, despite expanding availability and favorable preliminary findings, the inconsistency of controlled efficacy evidence and limited long-term safety evidence do not support the development of adolescent-specific rTMS guidelines for treating MDD at this time, and rTMS should be limited to adolescent use within approved research protocols while larger sham-controlled trials with extended follow-up are conducted.

titre: OBSESSIVE-COMPULSIVE DISORDER IN FIVE SELECTED POEMS
resume: This study investigates the literary representation of obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) and the dialectical relationship between obsessive-compulsive psychological mechanisms and poetic form across five selected poems. The corpus comprises "O.C.D." and "Static Electricity" by Neil Hilborn, "You Can Take Off Your Sweater, I’ve Made Today Warm" by Paige Lewis, and "I’m Not Crazy" and "I Can…I Will…Replace Those Weeds with Beautiful Flowers!" by Cherry Pedrick. Utilizing a descriptive qualitative design, the analysis conducts heuristic-hermeneutic close readings grounded in Sigmund Freud’s psychoanalytic defence mechanisms alongside cognitive models of intrusive thoughts and compulsive neutralisation. The comparative findings reveal that OCD does not merely operate as topical content; rather, it functions as a generative principle that governs the structural and aesthetic architecture of the poems. Obsessive-compulsive traits are formally encoded through phonological-syntactic repetition, typographical fragmentation via white space, hyperfocused surreal imagery, and conceptual metaphors of agricultural management. This research demonstrates how poetic discourse translates psychological dissonance into literary form, establishing a medium for destabilising social stigma, navigating relational intimacy, and articulating cognitive resilience. ABSTRAK Penelitian ini mengkaji representasi obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) serta relasi dialektis antara karakteristik psikologis obsesif-kompulsif dan pengorganisasian bentuk puitik dalam lima puisi terpilih. Objek material penelitian meliputi "O.C.D." dan "Static Electricity" karya Neil Hilborn, "You Can Take Off Your Sweater, I’ve Made Today Warm" karya Paige Lewis, serta "I’m Not Crazy" dan "I Can…I Will…Replace Those Weeds with Beautiful Flowers!" karya Cherry Pedrick. Pendekatan deskriptif kualitatif diterapkan melalui pembacaan heuristik-hermeneutik serta analisis mikrostilistika baris demi baris. Kerangka teoretis memadukan psikoanalisis Sigmund Freud mengenai mekanisme pertahanan ego dengan model kognitif siklus netralisasi intrusi. Temuan komparatif menunjukkan bahwa karakteristik OCD tidak sekadar beroperasi sebagai muatan tematik, melainkan bertindak sebagai prinsip generatif pembentuk konvensi estetika teks. Manifestasi obsesi dan kompulsi ditransformasikan secara struktural menjadi repetisi fonologis-sintaksis, fragmentasi tipografi ruang putih (white space), hiperfokus citraan hiperbolik-surealis, serta rekonseptualisasi metafora agrikultural. Penelitian ini membuktikan bahwa artikulasi puitik mampu mengonversi disonansi kognitif dan penderitaan psikis menjadi sarana resistensi terhadap stigma, renegosiasi keintiman, serta trajektori pemulihan berbasis agensi diri.

titre: Episodic Paramenstrual Psychosis in an Adolescent with Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder: A Case Report
P065 | ANTI-CGRP MONOCLONAL ANTIBODY RESPONSE IN CHRONIC MIGRAINE WITH SEVERE NEUROPSYCHIATRIC COMORBIDITY: A CASE REPORT AND PATHOPHYSIOLOGICAL INSIGHTS
resume: Background. Chronic migraine is frequently associated with psychiatric disorders and central sensitization, both of which may influence the response to preventive treatments. Anti-calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) monoclonal antibodies represent an effective preventive strategy; however, the determinants of treatment response in patients with high clinical complexity remain poorly understood. We describe the case of a patient with chronic migraine and severe neuropsychiatric comorbidity, proposing an integrated model of symptom amplification.Methods. We analyzed the case of a 49-year-old woman with chronic migraine, bipolar disorder, and obsessive-compulsive disorder, treated with galcanezumab while receiving stable psychiatric therapy with olanzapine, aripiprazole, lamotrigine, paroxetine, and alprazolam. The assessment included neurological, psychiatric, neuropsychological, and psychometric evaluations using the Beck Depression Inventory-II (BDI-II), State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI), Central Sensitization Inventory (CSI), Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), Brief Cognitive Status Exam (BCSE), Minnesota Multiphasic Personality Inventory-3 (MMPI-3), Morisky Medication Adherence Scale (MMAS), and Patient Health Engagement Scale (PHE-S). Clinical follow-up was performed after treatment discontinuation and subsequent reintroduction.Results. The patient exhibited a clear "on-off-on" pattern. Treatment with galcanezumab reduced migraine attacks from more than seven episodes per month to 1–2 episodes/month. Treatment discontinuation was followed by headache recurrence, whereas reintroduction of the drug restored the clinical benefit. The multidimensional assessment revealed severe depression (BDI-II = 59), marked anxiety (STAI = 77/80), pronounced central sensitization (CSI = 100), multidomain cognitive impairment (MoCA = 19; BCSE = 18), and an MMPI-3 profile characterized by high negative emotionality, social withdrawal, and thought dysfunction. Overall, the findings suggest that treatment response is modulated by the interaction among peripheral mechanisms, central sensitization, psychiatric comorbidity, and brain networks involved in pain processing.Conclusions. This case supports a biopsychosocial model of chronic migraine in which the effectiveness of anti-CGRP monoclonal antibodies is also influenced by the functional state of central pain modulation systems. A multidisciplinary approach integrating neurological, psychiatric, and neuropsychological perspectives may facilitate a more personalized treatment strategy for patients with high clinical complexity.

titre: Role of Vitamin D Supplementation in Children With Irritable Bowel Syndrome: A Randomized Controlled Trial
resume: This study was designed to determine whether vitamin D supplementation improved symptoms in children with irritable bowel syndrome, a condition associated with repeated abdominal pain and changes in bowel habits. It was hypothesized that vitamin D supplementation would reduce symptom severity and increase blood vitamin D levels compared with placebo. The study was a randomized, placebo-controlled trial at the Department of Pediatrics, Aziz Bhatti Shaheed Teaching Hospital, Gujrat, Pakistan. It included 60 children aged 6-14 years who met established diagnostic criteria for irritable bowel syndrome and had low blood vitamin D levels of 10-29 ng/mL. Children were randomly assigned to two groups of 30 participants each. One group received oral vitamin D3 drops containing 2,000 international units once daily for 12 weeks. The other group received matching placebo drops without vitamin D for the same period. Both groups received routine supportive care, including advice on hydration, regular meals, diet, and symptom management. Follow-up visits were scheduled at 4, 8, and 12 weeks to assess symptoms, treatment adherence, and possible side effects. The main outcome was the change in symptom severity from the start of treatment to 12 weeks, measured using a standardized symptom score. The secondary outcome was the change in blood vitamin D levels over the same period. Changes in both outcomes were compared between the two groups.

titre: A Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled Research Study Evaluating the Efficacy and Safety of Multi-dose Fecal Microbiota Transplantation (FMT) in Capsule Form as an Intervention to Slow Down the Rate of Biological Aging
resume: The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate if multi-dose fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) capsules can safely and effectively slow down biological aging and reduce chronic low-grade inflammation in adults aged 45 to 80 with metabolic neglect. The main questions it aims to answer are: * Can oral FMT capsules significantly slow the biological pace of aging as measured by the DunedinPACE epigenetic clock? * Can FMT successfully reduce chronic systemic inflammation (measured by markers such as suPAR, IL-6, and hs-CRP)? Researchers will compare participants receiving the active product to those receiving a matching placebo to see if the microbiome intervention improves metabolic health and cognitive function via the gut-brain axis. Participants will: * Undergo a short-term preparation phase involving targeted antibiotics and standard bowel cleansing. * Receive an 2 initial induction doses of active product (or placebo) followed by 5 regular booster cycles administered approximately every 4 weeks. * Attend periodic clinical visits for physical examinations, blood draws, stool sample collection (at home), and cognitive testing using the CANTAB platform and MoCA scale. * Maintain a participant diary to record adverse events (AE), product administration, stool sample collection, and dietary habits.

titre: My Symptoms Young - a New Internet-based Programme for Young People With Persistent Physical Symptoms in Primary Care: Exploration of Effect and Health Literacy Characteristics Among Users
resume: The research programme is an ambitious effort aiming to improve overall functioning and quality of life for young people with bodily distress. Bodily distress is a condition characterized by persistent physical symptoms (PPS), such as headache, nausea or abdominal pain, not explained by a well-defined disease. Over time, PPS can develop into a functional disorder, with detrimental impact on the young person's everyday life and opportunities. Thus, early intervention is crucial, but at present, access to specialized treatment of PPS to young people in primary care is very limited. The investigators have developed the internet-based self-help programme My Symptoms Young as a new digital solution for early intervention of PPS. The intervention was developed using a high degree of user involvement (young people with PPS) and are now ready to be tested. The goal of this clinical trial is to learn and preliminary test the possible effects of the internet-based self-help intervention program My Symptoms Young in young people aged 15-25 who experience PPS (physical symptoms presenting for \>3 months). The main question the investigators aim to answer is: * What are the potential effects of My Symptoms Young In addition, the investigators aim to investigate if participation in the program can reduce overall symptom intensity and interference with daily activity in young people's lives. Finally, the investigators aim to examine if individual levels of health literacy (HL) and eHealth literacy (eHL) will modify the potential effects. * The primary outcomes will be symptom intensity and symptom interference with daily activities * The primary hypothesis will be: Symptom intensity and interference with daily activities will improve after the treatment with My Symptoms Young. The effect will be modified by levels of HL and aspects of eHL. The investigators will include a total of 62 participants. The are no comparison group. Participants will be recruited from a health care professional in primary care (either general practitioner or practising pediatrician; from now on referred to as HCP). The HCP will determine whether referral to the My Symptoms Young programme is relevant. To guide this evaluation, the HCP will use pre-defined inclusion and exclusion criteria for participation. When a young person has been referred to the project group, a research assistent from the investigator group will contact the young person to provide more detailed information on the research project and the programme. If written consent is obtained, the young person will receive access to the programme. Throughout the intervention, the referring HCP is fully responsible for the health care of the young person. Referral and participation will be documented in the participants' primary care medical journal. If participants experience physical or psychological challenges during the project, they are advised to contact the referring HCP, i.e. the responsible healthcare provider. The programme is accessed through a website, using either tablet, mobile or computer. It consists of seven modules, a closing module on relapse prevention, and a module targeting close relatives plus four tools: don't break the chain, goal setting staircase, symptom registration and notebook for reflections. The seven modules target symptom understanding, physical energy, resources and strains, thoughts, feelings, values, and self-care. Participants will gradually gain access to the modules. The programme encourages young persons to work with various exercises throughout the different modules but with freedom to choose what to work with. Besides text and exercises, the programme also includes explanatory animations, audio files on case stories, audio files on brief meditations and videos on physical exercises. At first login (baseline), the participant will need to complete a set of questionnaires to access the programme. When completed the participant receives access to the programme. The researcher will follow up with participants by phone after one week if they have not logged into the programme and after three weeks if they have logged in but remained inactive. Participants can decide individually how long they wish to use the programme, but they are encouraged and recommended to engage actively at least twice a week for a minimum of 30 minutes. Participants will have access to the program for a total of 8 weeks. They will fill in questionnaires at three time points: Baseline (first login to the programme), End of Treatment (8 weeks after baseline) and 3 months after End of Treatment.

titre: Phase Ib/II Clinical Trial of Serine/Glycine-Restricted Diet Combined With Chemoradiotherapy for Neoadjuvant Treatment of Rectal Cancer
resume: This is a Phase Ib/II seamless, open-label, clinical trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of a serine/glycine-restricted diet combined with neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC). The study consists of two phases. Phase Ib is a non-randomized, single-arm safety run-in phase enrolling 6 patients, all of whom will receive the experimental regimen (a serine/glycine-restricted diet plus CAPOX chemotherapy and long-course radiotherapy). The primary objective of Phase Ib is to assess the safety, tolerability, and dietary compliance. If the safety criteria are met in Phase Ib (≥3 grade diet-related adverse event rate ≤20% and compliance rate ≥70%), the study will proceed to Phase II. Phase II is a randomized, open-label, parallel-controlled phase in which 120 additional patients will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio to either the experimental group (serine/glycine-restricted diet plus standard neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy) or the control group (standard neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy alone). The total enrollment is 126 patients (6 in Phase Ib + 120 in Phase II). The primary endpoint is the complete response rate (pCR + cCR). Secondary endpoints include major pathological response (MPR) rate, R0 resection rate, mrTRG regression grade, event-free survival (EFS), progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), adverse event profile, changes in serum amino acid levels, quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30), and nutritional status. Exploratory endpoints include gut microbiome diversity and tumor immune microenvironment changes.

titre: Targeting Sleep and Slow-Wave Activity to Enhance Cognition in MCI
resume: Study Description As most clinical trials in Alzheimer's disease (AD) have been unsuccessful to date, it has become increasingly crucial to focus on treating earlier stages of the disease. Compelling evidence indicates that sleep disruption is associated with accumulation of Alzheimer's biomarkers, including amyloid-beta (Aβ) and tau pathology. Slow-wave activity (SWA) during sleep is particularly important for the clearance of Aβ and sleep-dependent memory consolidation, and sleep disturbance could reduce the amount of time spent in slow-wave sleep. Together, these findings suggest that treating sleep disruption in older adults may help reduce the level of adverse brain aging. The goal of this study is to better understand the effect of sleep interventions on improving sleep and building cognitive resilience in older adults with amnestic mild cognitive impairment (aMCI), and to assess the feasibility of relevant study protocols. Fifty older adults (ages 60-85) with aMCI and sleep disturbance (Insomnia Severity Index score of 8 or greater) will be randomized 1:1 to one of two treatment arms: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia only (CBT-I + Sham), or CBT-I combined with acoustic slow-wave activity enhancement (CBT-I + SWAE). CBT-I is a psychotherapy intervention designed to address maladaptive cognitive and behavioral patterns associated with sleep and bedtime. SWAE is administered through non-invasive earbuds (Smartbuds, NextSense Inc.) that detect and amplify endogenous slow-wave activity using acoustic pulses during sleep. Each participant will complete 3 visits over approximately 6 months: a baseline visit, a post-treatment visit (approximately 12 weeks after baseline), and a 6-month follow-up visit. Group differences will be compared on changes in cognitive performance and plasma biomarkers of AD (phosphorylated tau \[pTau-217\]) across these time points. The study will also explore potential mechanisms behind the relationship between sleep and cognition/biomarkers by investigating a range of objectively measured sleep metrics (e.g., sleep architecture, sleep duration, arousals) along with depressive symptoms. Hypotheses: CBT-I will be associated with more favorable outcomes (i.e., less decline or greater improvement) in frontal network functioning (sustained attention/target detection, executive functions), while SWAE will be associated with better outcomes in measures of episodic memory (word-list learning and story recall). Improvements in total sleep time and insomnia symptoms at 8 weeks are hypothesized to mediate the relationship between CBT-I and performance on attention and executive functions over 6 months, while improvements in slow-wave non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep at 12 weeks are hypothesized to mediate the relationship between SWAE and episodic memory measures. Additionally, CBT-I is hypothesized to be associated with increased scores on the Visuospatial Abilities, Planning, Organization, and Divided Attention subscales of the Everyday Cognition (ECog) questionnaire after 6 months, while SWAE is hypothesized to be associated with a significant increase in the Everyday Memory subscale. Objectives: Aim 1: To determine if CBT-I and SWAE have different neuropsychological outcomes in aMCI. Aim 2: To examine the impact of sleep treatments on cognitively mediated everyday functioning. Exploratory Aim: To assess whether CBT-I and/or SWAE are associated with changes in plasma pTau and whether pTau moderates the association between sleep and cognition. Results from this study will determine whether sleep interventions can build brain and cognitive resilience in the context of aging, and will inform the design of a future, larger-scale R01 study rigorously examining the association between targeted sleep modifications and markers of AD pathophysiology as a potentially modifiable risk factor for dementia.
