This retrospective cohort study compared quality of life, immune parameters, exploratory serum biomarkers, performance status, and adverse events between patients receiving paclitaxel-carboplatin with or without adjunctive Astragalus Injection. A total of 136 patients treated between January 2022 and March 2023 were included in an observation group (chemotherapy plus Astragalus Injection, n = 68) or control group (chemotherapy alone, n = 68). Treatment consisted of six 21-day cycles. Outcomes included European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire-Core 30 (EORTC QLQ-C30) scores, CD4⁺ and CD8⁺ T-cell counts, CD4⁺/CD8⁺ ratio, squamous cell carcinoma antigen (SCC-Ag), cytokeratin 19 fragment (CYFRA21-1), adverse events, and Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) scores. Changes in all five EORTC QLQ-C30 functional domain scores were significantly greater in the observation group than in the control group (P < 0.001). The increase in CD4⁺/CD8⁺ ratio was also significantly greater in the observation group (P < 0.001). SCC-Ag and CYFRA21-1 decreased more substantially in the observation group (P = 0.003 and P < 0.001, respectively). The incidences of grade ≥ 2 gastrointestinal toxicity (14.71% vs. 32.35%, P = 0.015) and bone marrow suppression (11.76% vs. 27.94%, P = 0.019) were lower in the observation group. KPS improvement was greater in the observation group (P < 0.001). Adjunctive Astragalus Injection was associated with improvements in quality of life, immune parameters, performance status, selected chemotherapy-related adverse events, and exploratory serum biomarkers. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in prospective studies.

titre: Self-reported genitopelvic pain disorders and symptoms among individuals with confirmed or suspected slipping rib syndrome: An exploratory cross-sectional survey
resume: ObjectiveSlipping rib syndrome is an underrecognized condition characterized by hypermobility of the false ribs (ribs 8-10), resulting in pain throughout the abdominal and pelvic regions. This study aimed to describe genitopelvic pain disorders and related experiences among individuals with slipping rib syndrome.MethodsAn exploratory, descriptive, cross-sectional survey was distributed using convenience sampling from July 2024 to November 2024. Sociodemographic characteristics, diagnostic timelines, and the Patient Global Impression of Change were used to assess the self-reported efficacy of pelvic floor physical therapy for genitopelvic pain disorders among individuals with slipping rib syndrome.ResultsSeventy-nine individuals with slipping rib syndrome participated; most were women (92.2%) and White (96.9%), and the mean age was 33.4 years. The average diagnostic delay was 5.4 years, and frequent misdiagnoses included costochondritis, anxiety, and gastrointestinal conditions. More than half (54.4%) had Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, predominantly the hypermobile subtype (81.1%). More than 50% reported moderate to severe impacts of slipping rib syndrome on sexual activity, and 26.9% attributed their vulvar or pelvic pain directly to the condition. Common comorbidities included hypertonic pelvic floor, chronic pelvic pain syndrome, endometriosis, vaginismus, interstitial cystitis, and pudendal neuralgia. Among participants who received pelvic floor physical therapy for genitopelvic pain disorders and symptoms, the mean Patient Global Impression of Change score was 4.5, indicating no change to minimal improvement, and 18.2% reported worsening symptoms. Diaphragmatic breathing similarly resulted in no improvement or worsening of symptoms in many participants.ConclusionsThis study is the first to explore the potential impact of slipping rib syndrome on sexual activity and its possible contribution to genitopelvic pain disorders. Symptom overlap with gynecologic conditions complicates diagnosis and management. These findings underscore the importance of evaluating for slipping rib syndrome during pelvic health assessments, particularly in patients with persistent or unexplained pelvic and abdominal pain. Further research is needed to clarify the musculoskeletal mechanisms underlying pelvic pain and to guide interdisciplinary care for individuals with slipping rib syndrome.
revue: The Journal of international medical research

titre: Three-fraction preoperative stereotactic radiotherapy for resectable brain metastases: the phase 2 STEP trial
resume: Background Postoperative stereotactic radiotherapy (SRT) is the standard adjuvant treatment after resection of brain metastases. It nevertheless requires delineation of a dynamic postsurgical cavity, delays local treatment by 3 to 6 weeks (and thus resumption of systemic therapy) and carries substantial risks of radiation necrosis and leptomeningeal disease. Preoperative SRT targets an intact lesion and may address some of these limitations. Methods In this open-label, single-arm, multicenter phase 2 trial, eligible adults had a Karnofsky performance status ≥70 and up to four brain metastases, including one resectable lesion ≤5 cm, from breast, non-small cell lung, kidney, or digestive cancer or melanoma. Patients received preoperative SRT (three fractions of 7.7 Gy prescribed to the encompassing 70% isodose line, equivalent to 11Gy per fraction at the isocenter) followed by surgical resection within 3 days of the last fraction. The primary outcome was 6-month local control on centrally reviewed MRI. Secondary outcomes included index-lesion radiation necrosis, leptomeningeal disease, distant intracranial control, overall survival, toxicity, cognition, and quality of life. Results Of 73 patients assessed, 67 were eligible and 63 received both SRT and surgery. Median age was 62 years. At a median follow-up of 12.7 months, the 6-month local control rate was 100% (95% CI, 95%-100%), meeting the primary endpoint; the 12-month rate was 96.4% (95% CI, 87%-99%). No leptomeningeal disease occurred. The 1-year cumulative incidence of index-lesion radiation necrosis was 7% (95% CI, 2%-16%), meeting the key secondary endpoint. Distant intracranial failure occurred in 22 patients (35%); 12-month overall survival was 81.2% (95% CI, 70%-89%). Postoperative complications occurred in 4 patients (6.3%); cognition and quality of life remained stable over the 12 months of protocol follow-up. Conclusions Three-fraction preoperative SRT followed by resection was associated with high local control, low radiation necrosis, and no leptomeningeal disease, supporting evaluation in ongoing randomized trials.

titre: Network Analysis of Symptoms and Comorbidity in Patients With Early-Onset Colorectal Cancer: Comparison With Late-Onset Colorectal Cancer
resume: Purpose Patients with early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC) experience various symptoms and comorbidities throughout the treatment continuum. Identifying the intricate relationship between symptoms and comorbidities in EOCRC can provide a deeper understanding of the underlying mechanisms that shape the patient's entire experience. This study aimed to compare the association between symptoms and comorbidities in patients by age of onset to identify key relationships between symptoms and comorbid disease in EOCRC. Methods Data of 985 patients enrolled in a prospective colorectal cancer (CRC) cohort between 2013 and 2021 in the Republic of Korea were analyzed. At baseline, patients were assessed for 33 symptoms and functions, as well as 14 comorbidities, and were subsequently stratified into two age groups: Results In total, 13.5% of the participants had EOCRC. In the EOCRC group, 44 patients (33.1%) had existing comorbidities. The symptom and comorbidity networks were more complex in EOCRC than in LOCRC. Fatigue was a central symptom in both age groups. The EOCRC group exhibited positive correlations between musculoskeletal disease and psychiatric disorder, stool frequency, and multiple symptoms. The LOCRC group showed pronounced correlations between embarrassment by bowel movement and multiple symptoms and between health functioning parameters and fatigue. Conclusion Cancer-related fatigue was an important feature in both groups. These findings underscore the importance of considering these factors to enhance quality-of-life care outcomes during and after CRC treatment.

titre: Does gamification enhance adherence?: A randomized controlled trial of a digital self-esteem intervention
resume: Background: Mental health problems and low self-esteem are highly prevalent among college students and are associated with impaired academic functioning and poorer long-term well-being. Digital interventions are a promising and scalable approach to improve student mental health, but adherence is often limited. Gamification may improve engagement, though evidence remains scarce. Objective: This study examines whether adding gamification elements to a guided digital CBT-based self-esteem intervention for students improves adherence, satisfaction, and mental health outcomes. Methods: In a randomized controlled trial, 873 students were allocated to a gamified or non-gamified version of a guided self-esteem intervention. The primary outcome was adherence (number of modules completed), while secondary outcomes included satisfaction, self-esteem, depressive symptoms, anxiety, and quality of life. Assessments were conducted at baseline and at 4-week follow-up. Results: No significant differences were found between conditions on adherence, satisfaction or clinical outcomes in the full sample. Among intervention starters (i.e. completed ≥1 module), the gamified version showed a small increase in adherence (d = .17). Across conditions, participants showed significant improvements in self-esteem, depression, anxiety, and quality of life from pre- to post-test (d = .44–.76). Conclusions: Gamification may modestly increase adherence among intervention starters but does not improve satisfaction or clinical outcomes. Both intervention versions were associated with improvements over time; however, the lack of an untreated control condition limits causal interpretation. Future research should investigate mechanisms behind gamification components.

titre: Ayurveda Management of Grahani (Irritable Bowel Syndrome): A Case Report
resume: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a disorder of gut brain interaction with unknown etiology, symptoms include loose motion, constipation, or both along with repeated abdominal pain.Worldwide researches show prevalence rate of IBS around 10-20% and the incidence at 1-2% per year globally while in India, it is reported between 4.2 and 7.5%.Vataj Grahani (disorder related to gastro intestinal system) shows particular symptoms like pain, bloating, borborygmi, constipation, or diarrheas.A 37-year-old male patient came to Panchakarma (five body purification methods) outpatient department (OPD) of Ayurvedic Medical College and Research Institute with symptoms like increased frequency of motion, abdominal cramps, mucus discharge while defecation, and incomplete evacuation.The patient was already diagnosed case of IBS D by Gastroenterologist and its was managed with Agnideepana, (carmenative medicines) Yoga Basti krama [8 days enema protocol with buttermilk] with Takra Basti, Shirodhara (procedure where medicated oil is poured in continues stream on fore head) and Shaman drugs (disease pacifying drugs) like Grahanikapat Rasa, Mustakarishta, and Panchamruta Parpati, Manas Mitra vatakam along with dietary and life style modifications.The treatment aims balancing the Agni, (digestive fire) removal of vitiated Doshas, (basic principles of body as per Ayurveda) removal of causative factors and pacification of residual Doshas.The IBS severity scoring system (IBS-SSS) score decreased to 65 from 340, Bristol stool scale, improved to type 4 from type 6-7 (loose/watery), visual analogue scale (VAS) score for spasmodic abdominal pain reduced to 1/10 from 8/10, quality of life (QoL) score improved from 40 at baseline to 88 after 1 month of treatment respectively.So, we can say that personalized Ayurvedic treatment plan depending on causative factors shows clinical improvement in case of IBS.
revue: Journal of Indian System of Medicine

titre: Irritable bowel syndrome, sleep quality, and mediterranean diet: A cross-sectional study
resume: Background and aim: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) represents a significant public health problem, particularly among university students. This study investigated the relationship between IBS symptoms, sleep quality, and adherence to the Mediterranean diet (MD) among university students in the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 270 students aged 17–25 years using self-administered questionnaires. Data included socio-demographic characteristics, the Birmingham IBS Symptom Questionnaire, a sleep quality questionnaire, and the 14-item Mediterranean Diet Adherence Screener (MEDAS). Body composition was assessed using a Tanita analyzer. Results: Among the 270 participants (57.8% female), the prevalence of IBS symptoms was 51.5%, with most cases classified as mild. IBS symptoms were more common in females (69.1% of those with IBS symptoms) and in students enrolled in health-related majors (54.7%). Approximately 80% of participants reported good sleep quality, and 41.1% had moderate adherence to the MD. In multivariable logistic regression, the presence of IBS symptoms was significantly associated with lower sleep scores (B = −0.10, OR = 0.91, 95% CI: 0.84–0.98, p = 0.01) and being female (B = −0.85, OR = 0.43, 95% CI: 0.24–0.76, p = 0.004), whereas adherence to the MD was not significantly associated with IBS symptoms. Conclusions: IBS symptoms were common in this sample of UAE university students and were strongly associated with female sex and poorer sleep quality, but not with MD adherence. These findings highlight the need for targeted interventions to promote healthy sleep and lifestyle behaviors to reduce IBS symptoms and improve well-being among university students.

titre: Ultra-Processed Foods in Inflammatory Bowel Disease and Irritable Bowel Syndrome: Epidemiology, the Intestinal Microenvironment and Implications for Dietary Management
resume: Ultra-processed foods (UPFs) provide more than half of daily energy intake in several high-income countries, and their consumption is increasing worldwide. Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) are chronic gastrointestinal conditions whose burden has grown alongside industrialized dietary patterns. Here, we summarize the epidemiological, mechanistic and clinical evidence linking UPF consumption to both conditions. Most prospective cohorts and meta-analyses associate higher UPF intake with incident Crohn’s disease, whereas associations with ulcerative colitis are weaker and inconsistent. In IBS, observational studies, including a large prospective cohort, suggest a modest, dose-dependent association with risk, although data are limited and the diagnostic criteria have recently changed with Rome V. Mechanistically, both disorders may converge on the intestinal microenvironment: in experimental models, emulsifiers alter microbial composition and metabolism, the mucus layer, epithelial barrier integrity and mucosal immune activation, and non-nutritive sweeteners alter microbial composition and epithelial barrier function, although human data are limited and causality has not been established. We also discuss IBS-like symptoms in quiescent IBD, dietary management in both conditions, and the main knowledge gaps, including exposure assessment, residual confounding and the need for adequately powered intervention trials.

titre: Grahani Roga: A Critical Review of Nidana Panchaka and Samprapti Vighatana with Correlation to Irritable Bowel Syndrome and Malabsorption Syndromes
resume: Grahani (the functional/anatomical site situated between Amashaya and Pakvashaya that retains ingested food until digestion is complete) is considered so clinically significant in Ayurveda that Acharya Charaka devoted an entire independent chapter — Grahani Chikitsa Adhyaya (Chikitsa Sthana, Chapter 15) — to its disorder, Grahani Roga. This review applies Nidana Panchaka, Ayurveda's five-fold diagnostic framework (Nidana, Purvarupa, Rupa, Samprapti and Upashaya–Anupashaya), specifically to Grahani Roga, presents the original Charaka Samhita shlokas from the Grahani Chikitsa chapter itself that embody this framework, and elaborates the Samprapti (pathogenesis) of Grahani Roga stage-by-stage to identify points of Samprapti Vighatana (interruption of the pathogenic chain) relevant to diagnosis and treatment planning. The pathogenesis centres on Agnimandya (diminished digestive fire), which leads to Ama formation; this Ama afflicts the Grahani, impairing its capacity to retain food for the normal duration of digestion and producing the hallmark presentation of alternating loose and hard stools, undigested or mucus-laden faecal matter, abdominal distension, and progressive loss of strength and complexion. Four Doshika types — Vataja, Pittaja, Kaphaja and Sannipataja Grahani — are described, each with a distinct Nidana and Rupa. This review systematically correlates these four types with the Rome IV diagnostic subtypes of Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS-D, IBS-C, IBS-M and IBS-U) and with the clinical presentation of malabsorption syndrome, highlighting the shared functional (non-structural), chronic, and multifactorial nature of both the classical and contemporary constructs. Grahani Roga is proposed as an early, physiologically framed Ayurvedic parallel to modern functional bowel disease, and its Nidana Panchaka-based diagnostic model — which uniquely incorporates a therapeutic diagnostic dimension — is suggested as a useful complementary tool alongside Rome-criteria-based diagnosis in integrative gastroenterology practice.
auteurs: Nikita K. Raskar Dr. Anand V. Kalaskar
Shivani B. Thakare Dr. Umesh B. Pawar
revue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology

titre: Single-Cell eQTL Mendelian Randomization and Colocalization Analysis Reveals Immune Cell-Specific Genetic Insights into Functional Dyspepsia
resume: Background Functional dyspepsia (FD) is a common gastrointestinal disorder characterized by multiple clinical symptoms, complex pathophysiology, and limited therapeutic agents. Emerging evidence indicates a role for immune dysregulation in the pathogenesis of FD; however, immune cell-specific gene regulatory mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated the genetic factors specific to different immune cell types in FD to explore promising therapeutic targets. Methods We performed Mendelian randomization (MR) and Bayesian colocalization analyses integrating single-cell expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) data from 14 immune cell types with genome-wide association study summary statistics for FD. Functional enrichment and protein–protein interaction (PPI) network analyses were utilized to identify key genes. Phenome-wide association studies (PheWASs) and drug signature enrichment prediction assessed the therapeutic potential and pleiotropic effects of the identified genes. Results Thirty-six immune cell type/eGene combinations strictly satisfied both MR and Bayesian colocalization thresholds, revealing cell-specific genes with putative causal links to FD. The PPI network identified nine key genes (HLA-B, HLA-DQA2, HLA-DQB1, HLA-DRB5, HLA-DOA, HLA-DOB, LTA, GTF2H4, and C6orf136) as critical potential genetic drivers across multiple immune cell types. The majority of these eGenes exhibited no significant pleiotropic associations in PheWAS analysis, indicating a lower risk that might affect suitability for therapeutic targeting. Drug repurposing predicted several approved drugs and natural bioactive molecules (e.g., rifaximin, cinnamaldehyde, and ellagic acid) as hypothesis-generating candidates used for FD therapies and dietary supplements. Conclusions This study identified putative immune cell-specific genetic factors with causal associations with FD and predicted several potential therapeutic candidates using computational integration analyses. Validation in future experiments and clinical studies is required to corroborate our findings.

titre: Efficacy of Polyethylene Glycol Electrolyte Powder Combined with Linaclotide for Bowel Preparation for Colonoscopy in Children with Functional Constipation
resume: Constipation is an independent risk factor for failing to prepare the bowel before colonoscopy. This study used a pediatric population aged 10-17 with functional constipation to evaluate Polyethylene Glycol Electrolyte Powder (PGEP), alone or in combination with linaclotide, for bowel cleansing efficacy and safety. This retrospective study enrolled 75 children aged 10-17 years who underwent Bowel Preparation for Colonoscopy, with 43 of them receiving PGEP and 32 taking PGEP/linaclotide combination. The primary outcome was Boston Bowel Preparation Scale (BBPS) scores. A total BBPS score of at least 6 and a score of at least 2 for each bowel segment were defined as adequate bowel preparation. Adverse events and sleep quality were secondary outcomes. Compared with the PGEP group, the BBPS scores in each intestinal segment and the total BBPS score of the PGEP+linaclotide group were higher (P < 0.05). The rate of adequate bowel preparation showed no significant difference between the two groups. Compared with the PGEP group, the total examination time was lower in the PGEP+linaclotide group (P < 0.05). The first time of defecation was lower in the PGEP+linaclotide group when compared to that in PGEP group (P = 0.002). No statistically significant difference in adverse events and sleep quality was observed between the two groups. Therefore, PGEP in combination with linaclotide can be an effective option for bowel preparation prior to colonoscopy in children aged 10-17 years with functional constipation.
revue: The Tohoku Journal of Experimental Medicine

titre: Occupational and psychological characteristics across IBS status trajectories: a two-wave study of Japanese workers
resume: Abstract Background Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is common among working-age adults and is associated with impaired work productivity. Although IBS symptoms fluctuate over time, little is known about how changes in status are related to occupational and psychological functioning. This study aimed to characterize occupational and psychological differences across IBS status trajectories over 1 year. Main body A two-wave online survey was conducted in Japan: Time 1in 2023 and Time 2 in 2024. Workers aged 20–49 years ( N = 442) completed measures assessing IBS severity (IBSSI), IBS-related cognitive (CS‑FBD) and behavioral (IBS‑BRQ) factors, depressive (PHQ-9) and anxiety (GAD‑7) symptoms, somatic burden (SSS‑8), occupational stress factors, and work productivity (WPAI-GH). IBS status was assessed using the Rome IV Diagnostic Questionnaire, and participants were classified as Consistent Non-IBS, Incident IBS, Resolved IBS, and Consistent IBS. Two-way repeated-measures ANOVA (group × time) was conducted ( p < 0.05). Significant group-by-time interactions were observed for the IBSSI and SSS‑8. The Consistent Non-IBS group showed the lowest symptom severity at both time points, and only the Resolved IBS group showed significant improvement. For occupational stress, supervisor support declined across all groups, whereas coworker support declined in all groups except for the Resolved IBS group. Significant main effects of group were observed for the CS-FBD, IBS-BRQ, PHQ-9, GAD-7, and the WPAI-GH subscales but not for work time missed, with the Consistent Non-IBS group generally showing the lowest levels of impairment. Conclusions IBS status trajectories did not uniformly correspond to broad psychosocial changes across measures. Significant group-by-time interactions were observed for supervisor support and co-worker support, although the observed effects were small. Given the descriptive nature of this study and the small effect sizes, these findings should be considered descriptive, hypothesis-generating observations that remain to be confirmed through larger longitudinal studies. Moreover, future studies that incorporate the recently introduced Rome V criteria may help improve our understanding of IBS transitions and provide a foundation for exploring potential workplace support strategies.

titre: Investigating the Therapeutic Mechanisms of Weiling Decoction in Alleviating IBS-D: Modulation of Gut Microbiota, Tryptophan Metabolism, and AhR Signaling Pathways
resume: Abstract Weiling Decoction (WLD) has been used clinically to treat diarrhea of complex-etiology; however, its therapeutic mechanisms in diarrhea-irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D) remains unclear. In this study, an IBS-D rat model was used to evaluate the efficacy of WLD and explore its underlying mechanisms. Systemic inflammation, oxidative stress, and intestinal barrier function were assessed. To investigate the gut microbiota-host metabolic axis, 16S rRNA sequencing, fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), and fecal metabolomics, and pharmacological modulation of the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) were performed. WLD significantly attenuated visceral hypersensitivity and diarrhea-like symptoms, reduced pro-inflammatory cytokines and oxidative stress, and enhances antioxidant capacity. It also restored intestinal barrier integrity, as evidenced by histological improvement and increased expression of Zonula occludens-1 (ZO-1) and Claudin-1. FMT and multi-omics analyses further showed that the therapeutic effects of WLD were associated with enrichment of Lactobacillus and increased levels of L-tryptophan and indoleacrylic acid, leading to activation of AhR signaling. These findings indicate that WLD alleviates IBS-D pathology by strengthening the intestinal barrier through Lactobacillus-mediated tryptophan metabolism and subsequent AhR activation.

titre: Psychometric performance of the Chinese version of Experimental EQ-TIPS-5L against PedsQL in young children with functional constipation: response distributions and construct validity
resume: Health-related quality of life (HRQoL) measurement in early childhood is challenging, and evidence for preference-based instruments in infants and toddlers remains limited. The EuroQol Toddler and Infant Populations instrument (EQ-TIPS) was recently expanded to a five-level version (Experimental EQ-TIPS-5L) with seven dimensions, but its psychometric performance has not yet been evaluated in Chinese clinical populations. This study aimed to assess the response distribution, known-group validity, and convergent validity of Experimental EQ-TIPS-5 Lin children with functional constipation (FC). A total of 228 caregiver–child pairs were enrolled from a tertiary children’s hospital in China, with children aged 0–4 years diagnosed with FC. Caregivers completed the ExperimentalEQ-TIPS-5L and age-appropriate PedsQL versions (Infant Scales for 0–2 years, Generic Core Module for 2–4 years). Analyses were stratified by age group due to clinical and instrument differences. Known-group validity was evaluated by comparing Experimental EQ-TIPS-5L LSS, EQ VAS, and PedsQL total scores across subgroups defined by FC clinical characteristics using independent-samples t-tests and one-way ANOVA, with effect sizes estimated by Cohen’s d. Convergent validity was assessed using Spearman’s rank correlations at scales and item levels. The proportion of children in the best health state (1111111) was 28.95%. The Experimental EQ-TIPS-5L Level Sum Score (LSS) discriminated between subgroups defined by FC characteristics, with the largest effects differing between age groups: bowel movement frequency predominated among children aged 0–2 years (d = 0.95), whereas comorbidity was the strongest discriminator in children aged 2–4 years (d = 0.69). Behavioral or emotional problems showed consistent moderate effects across both age groups. PedsQL total scores largely mirrored these patterns. Experimental EQ-TIPS-5L LSS correlated with PedsQL total scores at r = − 0.43 (0–2 years) and r = − 0.63 (2–4 years). Item-level analyses revealed strong correlations between theoretically linked pairs (e.g., Pain and “hurts or aches”). This study provides the first evaluation of psychometric performance of the Experimental EQ-TIPS-5L in a Chinese clinical pediatric population. Among children with FC, Experimental EQ-TIPS-5L shows promising initial evidence of construct validity, with support for known-group and convergent validity. However, reliability, responsiveness, feasibility, a healthy control comparison, and a head-to-head three-level comparator were not assessed and remain priorities for future work.
revue: Health and Quality of Life Outcomes

titre: IBS × ISS – Reforma Tributária: impactos, desafios e soluções para o Município de Olinda/PE
resume: Obra técnica sobre a Reforma Tributária do Consumo sob a perspectiva dos Municípios. Compara o Imposto sobre Serviços de Qualquer Natureza (ISS) e a parcela municipal do Imposto sobre Bens e Serviços (IBS) a partir dos critérios da regra-matriz de incidência tributária, com base na Emenda Constitucional nº 132/2023, na Lei Complementar nº 214/2025, na Lei Complementar nº 227/2026 e no Regulamento do IBS. Examina a transição dos tributos e a transição federativa entre 2026 e 2033, o Comitê Gestor do IBS, a arrecadação, a fiscalização e o contencioso, os cadastros e os documentos fiscais eletrônicos, a distribuição do produto da arrecadação aos Municípios e o cálculo dos coeficientes de participação. Toma o Município de Olinda/PE como caso de estudo, identifica os desafios da transição do ISS para o IBS e propõe soluções para uma adequação equilibrada, com ênfase na modernização da administração tributária municipal e na qualificação dos seus agentes. Reúne comparativos, casos práticos, roteiro de adequação da legislação municipal, calendário de obrigações, instrumentos de conferência dos dados do Siconfi e de memória de cálculo para contestação do coeficiente, glossário e índice remissivo. Destina-se a gestores, auditores fiscais e técnicos da administração tributária municipal. Legislação considerada até 27 de outubro de 2026; a obra receberá atualizações periódicas.
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

titre: VELHAS INCERTEZAS EM NOVOS TRIBUTOS: A RESTITUIÇÃO DO IBS E DA CBS À LUZ DAS DIMENSÕES DA SEGURANÇA JURÍDICA
resume: A reforma tributária instituída pela Emenda Constitucional nº 132/2023 prometeu um sistema de tributação do consumo mais simples, neutro e transparente. Este artigo investiga se essa promessa alcança a restituição do indébito do Imposto sobre Bens e Serviços (IBS) e da Contribuição Social sobre Bens e Serviços (CBS). O art. 38 da Lei Complementar nº 214/2025 condiciona a restituição a dois requisitos cumulativos: que a operação não tenha gerado crédito para o adquirente e que tenha sido observado o art. 166 do Código Tributário Nacional. Adota-se como parâmetro a teoria da segurança jurídica de Humberto Ávila, decomposta nas dimensões de cognoscibilidade, confiabilidade e calculabilidade. Com método dedutivo, pesquisa bibliográfica e documental e análise de precedentes do STF e do STJ, o novo dispositivo é testado em três cenários típicos de operação. Conclui-se que o art. 38 não supera os déficits de segurança jurídica do regime anterior. Ele os desloca, porque faz o direito do contribuinte depender de um fato de terceiro e importa para o novo sistema um ônus probatório historicamente insatisfazível. O trabalho propõe critérios interpretativos que separam o ajuste documental nas operações com crédito da restituição propriamente dita nas operações sem crédito. Nestas últimas, a legitimidade de quem suportou o encargo encontra no novo modelo fundamento mais sólido do que no anterior.

titre: Poria cocos polysaccharide ameliorates colitis-induced anxiety-like behavior by suppressing microglial mtDNA-cGAS-STING pathway through microbiota-gut-brain axis
resume: Abstract Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic, relapsing inflammatory bowel disease comorbid with psychiatric disorders. Poria cocos polysaccharide (PCP), a key bioactive component of Poria cocos, exhibits anti-inflammatory properties. Here, we investigated the therapeutic efficacy of PCP against colitis and anxiety-like behavior in a dextran sodium sulfate (DSS)-induced mouse model, and its underlying mechanisms. PCP mitigated gross symptoms and anxiety-like behavior. PCP preserved intestinal barrier integrity and mitigated colonic inflammation by reducing COX-2/iNOS activation. Simultaneously, PCP alleviated hippocampal neuroinflammation and neuronal impairment via modulating microglial activation and M1-to-M2 polarization. RNA-seq showed that PCP inhibited the cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) pathway in the hippocampus. 16S rRNA sequencing showed that PCP corrected gut microbiota disorders. Subsequently, fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) verified that PCP’s benefits were mediated by the gut microbiota. Further analysis revealed that PCP, via the gut microbiota, not only alleviated microglial mitochondrial damage by reducing oxidative stress but also promoted hippocampal mitophagy induction, thereby blocking mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA)-triggered cGAS-STING pathway. Intriguingly, serum metabonomics suggested that PCP augmented the production of microbial-derived metabolite, taurine. ELISA and HPLC analyses further verified that taurine levels in colonic contents, serum, and the hippocampus were significantly elevated following PCP or FMT from PCP-treated donors intervention. Taurine supplementation mimicked the benefits of PCP and activated the cGAS-STING pathway, whereas the taurine transport inhibitor GES reversed PCP’s protective effects. In vitro assays verified the role of taurine in decreasing inflammation and inhibiting the mtDNA-cGAS-STING pathway in LPS-induced BV-2 cells. These findings demonstrate that PCP relies on the gut microbiota and derived taurine to ameliorate colitis and anxiety-like behavior. Through the microbiota-gut-brain axis, PCP dampens the mtDNA-cGAS-STING pathway via mitochondrial protection and mitophagy, thereby exhibiting anti-neuroinflammatory and anxiolytic effects. This study provides new insights into PCP’s therapeutic effect on UC and associated anxiety disorders.

titre: THE IMPACT OF CHRONIC STRESS ON THE GUT-BRAIN AXIS: A REVIEW
resume: Aim of the study: The aim of this article is to review the literature on the relationship between the gut–brain axis and chronic stress, with particular emphasis on the key components and mechanisms of this system. Materials and methods: This study is a narrative review based on current literature retrieved primarily from the PubMed database. Original research articles and review papers published in English were included. Studies were selected according to their relevance to chronic stress and its impact on gut–brain axis functioning and associated mechanisms. Results: Chronic stress disrupts the gut–brain axis by altering gut microbiota composition, increasing intestinal permeability, and promoting systemic inflammation. These changes impair bidirectional communication between the gut and the brain, leading to neuroendocrine and immune dysregulation and increasing susceptibility to neuropsychiatric disorders such as depression. Microbial metabolites, particularly short-chain fatty acids, play an important role in these processes and may represent potential therapeutic targets. Conclusions: Gut–brain axis disorders result from complex interactions between the nervous, immune, and metabolic systems, with gut microbiota playing a key regulatory role. Although evidence supports its influence on stress responses and neuropsychiatric vulnerability, the underlying mechanisms are not yet fully understood. Further research is needed to clarify causal relationships and to develop targeted therapeutic strategies integrating microbiota modulation with stress regulation.
revue: International Journal of Innovative Technologies in Social Science

titre: The gut–brain axis: Immunometabolic crosstalk in neurodegenerative diseases
Gut–brain axis dysfunction in autism spectrum disorder: Exploring the potential of probiotics
Enteric glia and the gut-brain axis as a source of biomarkers in neurodevelopmental disorders: a scoping review protocol
resume: Protocol of a scoping review (JBI methodology, PRISMA-ScR) mapping the evidence on enteric glia, the enteric nervous system and the intestinal barrier in neurodevelopmental disorders, including autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, intellectual disability, communication, learning and motor disorders, tic disorders, genetic syndromes with a neurodevelopmental phenotype and fetal alcohol spectrum disorder, in humans and animal models. The review identifies which enteric glial, barrier and mucosal inflammation markers have been measured, in which matrix and with which method, the direction of change relative to controls, their associations with clinical features, and the gaps by disorder and marker. Planned as an invited Review Article for NeuroMarkers.

titre: Taxonomic Impact and Biomarker Identification on the Gut-Brain Axis Using L1-Regularized Selection and Ensemble Classification
resume: This production-grade machine learning pipeline is designed for the high-dimensional analysis of gut microbiome data. Implemented in Python, the pipeline automates the ingestion, transformation, feature selection, and classification of taxonomic relative abundance profiles to predict neurological states and biological phenotypes. Key Features & Architectural Workflow: • Tidy-to-Tabular Data Transformation: Implements robust pipelines utilizing pandas to reshape, melt, and pivot raw long-format OTU tables and public repository data (such as American Gut Project cohorts) into optimized wide-format feature matrices. • L1-Regularized Feature Selection: Integrates a built-in Lasso penalization layer using SelectFromModel and LogisticRegression to aggressively reduce dimensions, filter statistical noise, and isolate the most predictive microbial biomarkers. • Ensemble Classification Modeling: Employs a finely-tuned GradientBoostingClassifier optimized with custom learning rates and subsampling to accurately capture complex, non-linear multi-species interactions. • Stratified Cross-Validation: Evaluates pipeline generalizability and prevents data leakage across patient cohorts using stratified K-fold cross-validation. It assesses model performance via precise metrics including LogLoss, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, and area under the curve (AUROC). • Explainable AI (XAI) Attribution: Integrates SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) through TreeExplainer to calculate mathematical variable importance. It automatically exports publication-grade diagnostic beeswarm plots mapping exactly how specific neuroprotective or neurotoxic bacterial species drive the global model predictions.
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

titre: Comparative genomic and extracellular metabolomic profiling of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum LP140 and Bifidobacterium breve BB010 reveals distinct gut–brain-axis-associated metabolite profiles
resume: Abstract Background The microbiota-gut-brain axis provides multiple routes through which intestinal bacteria may influence host neurophysiology. Mechanistic evaluation of candidate probiotic strains therefore requires linking genomic metabolic potential with measurable extracellular output. We compared Lactiplantibacillus plantarum LP140 and Bifidobacterium breve BB010 to identify distinct metabolic traits potentially relevant to gut–brain-axis-associated functions. Results Genome-based pathway reconstruction predicted distinct metabolic capacities. LP140 showed stronger support for glutamate-to-γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) conversion and a broader succinate-associated fermentative framework, whereas BB010 showed stronger de novo B3/NAD-related capacity, PdxST-dependent PLP biosynthesis, and broader Gln/Glu interconversion support. Species-level pangenome analysis further showed that many of the canonical metabolic loci underlying these predictions were conserved across the respective species rather than unique to the focal strains. Replicated targeted LC–MS/MS confirmed major strain-resolved extracellular differences. LP140 showed pronounced accumulation of lactate (mean Δ ± SE = 127.0 ± 8.9 mM, q = 0.0089), succinate (999 ± 49 µM, q = 0.0147), and GABA (60.6 ± 4.2 µM, q = 0.0157). BB010 showed strong accumulation of nicotinic acid (22.8 ± 0.8 µM, q = 0.0009), glutamine (347 ± 38 µM, q = 0.0204), and glycine (5.55 ± 0.64 mM, q = 0.0204). Genome–metabolite relationships were not uniformly direct, indicating that extracellular metabolite pools cannot be predicted from pathway completeness alone. Polyamine-related findings were more consistent with turnover than broad de novo biosynthesis, while histamine and tyramine did not accumulate under the tested conditions. Conclusions LP140 and BB010 exhibit distinct, condition-specific extracellular metabolic profiles that are only partly predictable from genomic pathway content. These strain-resolved genome–metabolome relationships provide a functional basis for further testing in physiologically relevant host-interaction models but do not by themselves demonstrate psychobiotic efficacy.

titre: From Body to Brain and Back: Behavioral and Neural Perspectives on Interoceptive Alterations in Schizophrenia
resume: This project investigates interoception in individuals with Schizophrenia Spectrum Disorders (SSD). We assess interoception on a behavioral level using questionnaires, a Heartbeat Counting Task, as well as on the neural level using EEG. We expect the patients to show clinically relevant alterations in these interoceptive domains compared to healthy individuals. We aim to contribute to the understanding of the altered bodily self-consciousness in SSD and the clinical implications thereof. Thereby, aiding the development of individualized treatment strategies targeting a strengthening of the mind-body connection.

titre: Alexithymia and Difficulties in Emotion Regulation Among University Students
resume: This cross-sectional correlational study observed the relationship between alexithymia and difficulties in emotion regulation among undergraduate students. There were 400 students (164 men, 236 women; ages 20–24 years) in the fifth or seventh semester of Psychology (n = 200) or Business Administration (BBA; n = 200) programs at the University of Gujrat, recruited through convenient sampling. Alexithymia was measured through the Toronto Alexithymia Scale (TAS-20) and emotion regulation difficulties with the Difficulties in Emotion Regulation Scale–16 (DERS-16). The two measures were positively linked with r(396) = .44, p < .001. The demographic differences showed that BBA students scored slightly higher on externally oriented thinking, t(398) = −2.14, p = .033. In multiple regression, difficulty identifying feelings (β = .22), difficulty describing feelings (β = .10), and externally oriented thinking (β = .24) together explained 19.4% of the variance in emotion regulation difficulties, F(3, 394) = 31.66, p < .001. The findings are consistent with models that treat emotional awareness as a foundation for emotion regulation.

titre: Alexithymia, Empathy, Temperament, and Emotion Dysregulation in Boys with Conduct Disorder
resume: Abstract Background: Emotion-dysregulation frameworks emphasize impaired regulation of emotion in conduct disorder (CD). Alexithymia and empathy are theoretically linked to this framework but have rarely been examined together in youth with CD. Aim: The aim of this study was to examine alexithymia and empathy in boys with CD, aged 12 to <18 years, and their associations with temperament and emotion dysregulation, relative to matched typically developing controls. Materials and Methods: Seventeen boys with CD and 17 age- and education-matched controls completed child- and parent-rated alexithymia measures, an empathy questionnaire, the Difficulties in Emotion Regulation Scale, and a temperament questionnaire in a cross-sectional design. Group comparisons used Mann–Whitney U -tests; associations were examined using Kendall’s Tau (age) and Spearman’s correlations (within the CD group). Results: Self-reported alexithymia did not differ between groups, but parent-rated alexithymia and emotion-regulation difficulties were significantly higher in the CD group. The CD group also showed higher aggression and frustration. Depressive mood showed a nonsignificant upward trend. Within the CD group, self-and parent-rated alexithymia were positively correlated; parent-rated alexithymia correlated with aggression. Affiliation and attention were correlated positively with empathy. Attention and fear correlated negatively with emotion dysregulation. Age was unrelated to alexithymia or empathy. Conclusion: Parent-reported alexithymia and temperamental vulnerability – particularly Aggression and Frustration – appear central to the emotion-dysregulation profile of CD. Early identification of these factors, together with parental involvement in assessment, may inform prevention and intervention.

titre: Designing with AI, Teaching the Body: A Pilot Study on Pre-Service Teacher Training for Embodied Emotional Literacy
resume: Alexithymia, childhood obesity, and eating disorders converge in one educational emergency: children unable to read their own bodily signals. Somatic-marker theory (Damasio) and interoception research ground emotion in bodily sensation; embodied-cognition and body-oriented intervention (BOI) studies show teaching emotion through the body outperforms purely verbal approaches. SEN students (ADHD, SLD, disadvantage) are disproportionately affected, yet teacher training rarely builds operational body-based competences. Generative AI offers an unexplored opportunity: articulating embodied pedagogical intuitions to a bodyless system may externalize tacit knowledge (Polanyi, 1966; Nonaka & Takeuchi, 1995). This study introduces EEL, integrating embodiedemotion theory, BOI research, and interoception, asking: (RQ1) Does AI-assisted ADDIE co-design increase EEL design self-efficacy? (RQ2) What theoretical knowledge do participants demonstrate? (RQ3) How useful is AI perceived as a co-design partner for SEN-inclusive interventions? (RQ4) Is An exploratory mixed-methods pilot used a retrospective then-test (Howard et al., 1979) to avoid response-shift bias and preserve anonymity. Chapter in: Francesco Peluso Cassese (ed.), Algorithmic Heartbeats: Affective Education in the Age of the Fourth Revolution, REN Press – Cares srl, 2026, pp. 323-324. ISBN 979-12-82860-00-0. Volume DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23211262. Section: Teacher Education Between the "Frankenstein Complex" and the D-Generation.

titre: VIRTUAL REALITY (VR) ANALGESIA IN BURN AND TRAUMA CARE: A SCOPING REVIEW OF CLINICAL EFFICACY AND PSYCHO-SOCIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS OF PAIN DISTRACTION
resume: Pain management in trauma and burns poses a clinical challenge, often requiring high opioid doses that carry complication risks. Virtual reality (VR) is gaining prominence as a promising non-pharmacological analgesic tool. This scoping review evaluates the clinical efficacy, psychosocial, and neurobiological mechanisms of VR-based analgesia in burn and trauma patients. Based on a synthesis of 31 studies, immersive VR interventions during distressing procedures (e.g., dressing changes, debridement, physical therapy) were analyzed. Evidence clearly indicates VR significantly reduces pain intensity and unpleasantness while shortening cognitive focus on pain stimuli in adults and children. The underlying mechanisms include the limited attention span theory, achieving a 'flow' state, the embodiment illusion, and anxiety reduction. Furthermore, high immersion and interactivity enhance the analgesic effect, which can be amplified synergistically with hypnosis or targeted pharmacotherapy like ketamine. While VR is highly effective for acute procedural pain, it remains unclear whether this efficacy diminishes over time due to habituation or the novelty effect during prolonged hospitalizations. Addressing these limitations, alongside further technological optimization and integration into the biopsychosocial model, is essential for the full personalization of this digital therapy.
revue: International Journal of Innovative Technologies in Social Science

titre: Add-on efficacy of neurofeedback-augmented mindfulness training for stress reduction: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
resume: Stress is a psychophysiological response that occurs when environmental demands exceed an individual’s coping capacity, and it is closely linked to many psychosomatic disorders. Mindfulness training can effectively reduce stress, but conventional mindfulness training (CM) places high demands on self-monitoring ability, which limits its effect. Neurofeedback-augmented mindfulness training (NM) provides real-time feedback on brain activity signals and may help address this limitation. However, most existing studies are small-sample RCTs, and their conclusions remain inconsistent. This study used a systematic review and meta-analysis to compare the overall effects of NM and CM on stress reduction and related mental health outcomes, aiming to provide evidence-based guidance for intervention selection in non-clinical young and middle-aged populations with mental health needs. We searched MEDLINE, PubMed, Scopus, CNKI, the Cochrane Library, and the ClinicalTrials registry databases. Publication dates were limited to January 2016 to August 2026. Five randomized controlled trials with 358 participants in total were included, and outcomes included stress, anxiety, depression, sleep quality, phone addiction, no-phone phobia, fatigue, neuroticism, and psychological resilience. Extracted data were pooled using a random-effects model, and sensitivity analyses were performed based on heterogeneity. In terms of stress improvement, NM showed a trend toward superiority over CM (SMD 0.65, P = 0.0009), with robust conclusions. For anxiety, two studies comparing NM with CM consistently supported the superiority of NM (SMD 0.67–0.87, both P < 0.01); however, evidence comparing NM with mental health education was inconsistent. For depression, NM showed a trend toward superiority over mental health education (SMD 0.41, P = 0.04), though the robustness was limited; evidence comparing NM with CM was limited and inconsistent. For sleep quality, no advantage of NM was observed compared with either CM or mental health education (SMD 0.05, P = 0.74), and this negative conclusion was robust. For the remaining outcomes, evidence was insufficient or inconsistent, and no definitive conclusions could be drawn. The preliminary evidence from this study suggests that, among non-clinical young and middle-aged adults, NM demonstrated relatively consistent potential advantages in improving stress, with robust directional findings. For anxiety, NM may offer benefits over CM, although the certainty of evidence is limited; evidence comparing NM with mental health education remains inconsistent. For depression, NM may be superior to mental health education, but the robustness is insufficient, and evidence comparing NM with CM is limited and inconsistent. For sleep quality, no advantage of NM was observed, and this negative finding was robust. For the remaining outcomes, definitive conclusions could not be drawn due to the very small number of studies or inconsistent results. These findings are limited by the small number of included studies, the fact that some outcomes were derived from single studies, and the exclusively non-clinical nature of the samples. Further high-quality randomized controlled trials are warranted to verify these results.

titre: The role of the therapist in guided internet-delivered cognitive behavioural therapy (iCBT) for depression
resume: Guided internet-based cognitive behavioral therapy (iCBT) is an established treatment for depression, and guided formats generally show better adherence and larger effects than unguided ones. However, “guidance” is operationalised very differently across studies (who provides support, through which channels, how often, and with what content). This review aims to systematically describe how the therapist’s role is defined and delivered in guided iCBT for depression, and to explore how features of that role relate to depressive symptom outcomes, adherence/dropout and therapeutic alliance. We will perform a systematic review of studies retrieved from PsycInfo and Medline. Covidence will be used for double-blinded screening and data extraction. The systematic review will be written as our final thesis at the clinical psychology programme at the University of Oslo. As soon to be clinical psychologists we aim to gain a better understanding of the role of the therapist in a world in which digitalized therapeutic interventions are becoming more common due to its accessibility and cost-effectiveness. This is a primarily descriptive review, so we have no confirmatory hypotheses. We have the following exploratory expectations: (1) the therapist’s role will be reported inconsistently across studies and that studies therefore will yield non-conclusive findings, (2) more personalized guidance might lead to better outcomes. We expect this review to point to a need for more systematic research on the therapist’s role.

titre: The impact of timing of SSRI therapy initiation on efficacy of psychotherapy for depressive disorders
resume: Introduction. Depression is one of the leading causes of disability worldwide. The combination of selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) and psychotherapy is recognized as an effective treatment for moderate to severe depression. However, the optimal sequence and timing for initiating these interventions remain uncertain. Objective. To synthesize the theoretical rationale and empirical evidence regarding the impact of the timing of SSRI initiation on the efficacy of psychotherapy (primarily cognitive-behavioral therapy) in the treatment of depressive disorders. Materials and methods. A narrative literature review was conducted using the PubMed/MEDLINE, Cochrane Library, PsycINFO, Web of Science, and eLibrary databases. The analysis encompassed randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, cohort studies, neuroimaging research, and preclinical experiments. Results. Preclinical studies have given rise to two competing hypotheses. The "priming" hypothesis suggests that chronic administration of SSRIs enhances neuroplasticity (creating a "window of plasticity") which facilitates more effective psychotherapeutic learning. The "interference" hypothesis, by contrast, posits that an acute increase in serotonergic transmission may exacerbate anxiety and impair emotional learning. Clinical studies demonstrate the efficacy of various combination strategies (simultaneous initiation, sequential addition); however, there are no direct studies comparing different timing for the initiation of SSRIs relative to psychotherapy. Data from neuroimaging and biomarkers (such as BDNF) show potential for predicting treatment response, but they are not yet sufficient for clinical application in determining the sequence of interventions. Discussion and conclusion. The "plasticity window" hypothesis has a compelling preclinical rationale; however, its translation into clinical practice is limited by patient heterogeneity and a lack of studies designed to evaluate the timing of SSRI initiation. Testing these hypotheses requires randomized trials that incorporate repeated biomarker measurements and neuroimaging at critical time points. Such research would facilitate the development of personalized recommendations for determining the optimal sequence of treatment.

titre: A Guided Online Cognitive Behavioral Intervention to Prevent Persistent Pain After Breast Cancer Surgery: A Randomized Feasibility and Acceptability Study
resume: Persistent pain after breast cancer treatment (PPBCT) is highly prevalent. Psychological factors such as anxiety and pain worry are associated with increased prevalence of PPBCT. Perioperative psychological interventions may mitigate the risk for PPBCT. This study evaluates the feasibility and acceptability of a guided online cognitive behavioral intervention (eCBT) for women scheduled for breast cancer surgery. Additionally, the efficacy of the intervention to decrease anxiety and pain worry was compared to that of a guided online active control intervention. The current study is part of a larger RCT on the effectiveness of perioperative eCBT to decrease the prevalence of PPBCT. Patients were randomized to receive five sessions of eCBT or five sessions of health education, both accompanied by three video calls with a therapist. Feasibility was determined by participation and retention rate, attendance and treatment fidelity. Acceptability was assessed with evaluation forms completed by patients and therapists. Changes in anxiety and pain worry after the intervention were compared between the eCBT and control group. The intervention appeared feasible. Although only 40% of eligible patients participated, most of those randomized to eCBT followed the program and completed all sessions. Quantitative and qualitative data showed that participants appreciated the intervention and experienced benefits from it. Nevertheless, patients also indicated experiencing problems to fully engage in the intervention because of treatment and disease burden or private circumstances. Anxiety and pain worry significantly decreased after the intervention, but not more than after the control intervention. Effectiveness for reducing PPBCT remains to be determined.

titre: Mindfulness meditation plus transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation for alcohol use disorder: a randomized clinical trial
resume: Abstract Background Impaired inhibitory control under negative affect is a core mechanism sustaining alcohol use disorder (AUD), but receives limited attention in treatment development. Mindfulness meditation has shown efficacy in improving this function, but outcomes differ across individuals. Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) is a noninvasive neuromodulation approach that targets brain–heart interplay. It may enhance neurobiological pathways underlying emotion regulation and cognitive control and thus represents a promising augmentation strategy. This randomized controlled trial examined whether concurrent taVNS augments the efficacy of mindfulness meditation on inhibitory control under negative affect and whether brain–heart interplay represents a relevant physiological pathway. Methods Sixty-three patients with AUD were randomized to receive either sham ( n = 31) or active ( n = 32) taVNS during twice-daily mindfulness meditation sessions for 10 days. Inhibitory control under negative affect was measured by no-go accuracy when angry faces were presented as distractors in a color-based go/no-go task. Tonic brain–heart interplay was quantified by heart rate variability-electroencephalography coupling at rest. Secondary outcomes include latency to any post-discharge alcohol use, craving, negative affect, emotion regulation, mindfulness, and sleep quality. Primary analyses used ANCOVA to predict post-treatment angry-face no-go accuracy from group and baseline. Additional analyses examined changes in brain–heart interplay indices and self-reported outcomes across groups. Results Mindfulness meditation with active taVNS produced greater increases in angry-face no-go accuracy than mindfulness meditation with sham taVNS ( p < 0.001). Post-treatment accuracy remained baseline-dependent in the sham group (β = 0.406; 95% CI, 0.245–0.567; p < 0.001), whereas the active group achieved uniformly high accuracy regardless of baseline (β = -0.015; 95% CI, -0.205–0.175; p = 0.798). Enhanced BHI occurred only in the active group. Reductions in anxiety and craving were greater and earlier in the active group than in the sham group. Conclusions The combination of mindfulness meditation and taVNS provides an effective and safe treatment for men with AUD. The results support the promise of targeting brain–heart interplay to develop interventions for AUD. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07036055. Registered on June 16, 2025.

titre: The effect of psychological skills training on the sports performance and psychology of swimmers: a systematic review
resume: This program intends to systematically evaluate the impact of psychological skills and mindfulness interventions on the sports performance and psychological outcome of competitive swimming pool swimmers. The research subjects are competitive pool swimmers of unlimited age. Children, teenagers, adults and master groups are all included, and age is a layered variable. Interventions are divided into three categories: traditional psychological skills training, mindfulness/acceptation intervention, and mindfulness-related physical and mental intervention. They are analysed separately and not combined into a single intervention effect. The research design includes randomised controlled trials, whole population randomised trials, non-randomised controlled trials and single subject experimental design.The main outcome is objective swimming performance, and the secondary outcome includes competitive anxiety, psychological skills or mindfulness, happiness, sleep, compliance and adverse events. Two researchers screened and extracted independently, and the third person resolved the differences. Use RoB 2, ROBINS-I and RoBiNT for bias risk. Random effect meta-analysis is carried out only when there are at least three independent studies under the same intervention family, the same outcome and the same control type, and the clinical and methodological homogeneity; otherwise, SWiM narrative synthesis is used. This program does not presupote the effectiveness of psychological skills intervention, nor does it extrapote the results of all-age combination to a specific age group.

titre: FEAR OF SELF AND ITS RELATIONSHIP TO OBSESSIVE-COMPULSIVE DISORDER
resume: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is one of the most prevalent disorders among members of society. It is a chronic and complex psychological condition characterised by the presence of unwanted intrusive obsessions, thoughts, images, and doubts that provoke anxiety, along with compulsive acts represented by repetitive behaviours and mental rituals that the individual performs deliberately to relieve the distress associated with those obsessions. As for fear of self, it is the individual's deep anxiety about their true identity or about what they may become in the future, particularly regarding possessing undesirable traits. The present research aimed to identify the following: Fear of self among those with obsessive-compulsive disorder. The dimensions of OCD among those with the disorder. Statistically significant differences in fear of self according to the variables of sex (male/female) and age (15–20), (21–30), (31–40), (41–50). Statistically significant differences in OCD according to the variables of sex (male/female) and age (15–20), (21–30), (31–40), (41–50). The correlational relationship between fear of self and OCD. To achieve the foregoing, the researcher adopted the research scales, namely: the Fear of Self scale by Aardema et al. (2021), which consists of (27) items distributed across three domains: the corrupted self, the culpable self, and the malformed self; and, regarding OCD, the scale by Abramowitz et al. (2010), which consists of (20) items distributed across four dimensions: contamination, responsibility for harm, unacceptable thoughts, and order. The psychometric properties of the two scales were verified through face validity and construct validity, and reliability was also verified by two methods: test-retest and Cronbach's alpha. The present research has the following results: Individuals diagnosed with OCD have a fear of self. The sample has OCD. There are no differences in fear of self according to the sex variable (male – female), and no significant differences appeared with respect to age. There are no differences in OCD according to the sex variable (male – female), and no significant differences appeared with respect to age. There is a statistically significant positive correlational relationship between fear of self and OCD.

titre: Bergen four‐day treatment for OCD superior to internet‐based CBT
resume: Obsessive‐compulsive disorder (OCD) is an impairing condition that affects 1% to 3% of the population, but access to the recommended first‐line treatment, exposure and response prevention (ERP), is limited due to shortages of trained therapists, long waiting lists, and treatment dropout and refusal. Internet‐based cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) has been suggested as a replacement to ERP because of convenience, but another treatment, which is a concentrated four‐day ERP, was shown superior in reducing OCD severity in a study published this month.

titre: Developing a Questionnaire to Measure Behaviours in Response to Worries about Relapse in OCD
resume: Obsessive Compulsive Disorder (OCD) is a condition characterised by intrusive thoughts and repetitive behaviours (American Psychiatric Association, 2022). Although evidence based treatments exist, OCD is marked by long delays before treatment and high relapse rates (Perris et al., 2023; O’Neill & Feusner, 2015). Despite its clinical significance, the mechanisms contributing to relapse remain poorly understood. One underexplored factor is fear of illness recurrence (FOR)—the worry that symptoms will return after remission (Lee Jones et al., 1997). While examined in physical health conditions and psychosis (Khatibi et al., 2021; Jamalamadaka et al., 2020), its relevance to OCD has not been investigated. When in recovery, fear of intrusive thoughts re-emerging may prompt preventative compulsions, reinforce maladaptive cycles and increasing relapse vulnerability. Three constructs may explain this process. Intolerance of uncertainty reflects a tendency to perceive uncertainty as threatening (Reuther et al., 2013), heightening concerns about symptom return. Mental health anxiety involves excessive worry about one’s psychological state (Rachman, 2012), increasing vigilance towards intrusive thoughts. Mental defeat refers to losing autonomy during psychological distress (Ehlers & Clark, 2000); individuals with OCD often describe feeling overwhelmed and unable to control their thoughts, consistent with this construct (Moritz et al., 2021). These factors may create a cognitive vulnerability in which uncertainty becomes intolerable, self efficacy is reduced, and hypervigilance is amplified, thereby increasing FOR and promoting maladaptive coping. Although the Fears of Recurrence and Progression about Mental Health Questionnaire (FORP-MHQ; Coutts-Bain et al., 2025) exists, only a small subset of its validation sample had OCD, and all participants were in Australia. Moreover, the Reactions to Mental Health Worries Questionnaire (RMHWQ; Jamalamadaka et al., 2020), developed for psychosis, may not capture OCD-specific features. This research has two aims: (1) to validate the FORP-MHQ in a larger, more diverse sample of people with OCD, and (2) to develop and validate a new measure of the behaviours people with OCD engage in when worried about relapse or their OCD getting worse. Together, these will support future investigations into fear of relapse (FOR) within OCD and potential underlying mechanisms.

titre: Evaluation of the Effect of Acceptance and Commitment Therapy-Based Group Psychotherapy on Depression, Anxiety and Quality of Life in Patients Diagnosed With Chronic Headache
resume: The goal of this randomized clinical trial is to find out whether Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)-based group psychotherapy can improve depression, anxiety and quality of life in adults with chronic headache compared with psychoeducation. The main questions the study aims to answer are: * In adults diagnosed with chronic headache, can ACT-based group psychotherapy reduce depression and anxiety symptoms and improve quality of life and daily functioning? * In adults diagnosed with chronic headache, can ACT-based group psychotherapy improve psychological flexibility and reduce repetitive negative thinking? The study enrolled 72 adults aged 18 to 65 years who have been diagnosed with chronic headache and are receiving medication treatment for chronic headache. Participants were randomly assigned to one of two groups: ACT-based group psychotherapy or psychoeducation. Both interventions consist of four weekly group sessions, each lasting about 90 minutes. Study assessments are conducted before the first group session, after the fourth session and 1 month after the final session.

titre: Investigation of Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder in Patients With Medial and/or Lateral Elbow Epicondylitis
resume: This study will compare obsessive-compulsive symptoms in adults with medial and/or lateral elbow epicondylitis (pain and tenderness on the inner and/or outer side of the elbow). The study will include 90 participants in two groups of 45. One group will have no identifiable history of mechanical loading associated with their elbow condition. The other group will have a history of activities that place repeated strain on the elbow, such as manual work, sports, or caregiving. Group assignment will be based on medical history and clinical assessment, rather than random allocation. Each participant will complete the Turkish self-report Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale and the 37-item Turkish Maudsley Obsessional Compulsive Inventory once, at the study visit. The main outcome will be the Yale-Brown total score. The Maudsley total score will be a secondary outcome. The study will assess symptoms, not establish a diagnosis of obsessive-compulsive disorder. No treatment will be assigned as part of the study, and no follow-up visits are planned.

titre: Interbrain synchrony analysis for fNIRS: A signal processing primer
resume: Interbrain synchrony (IBS), also referred to as interpersonal neural synchrony (INS), has become a central construct in social neuroscience and beyond. It describes the temporal alignment of neural activity across individuals and has been studied in a range of paradigms, including sequential interactions, shared-stimulus settings, and hyperscanning, that is, the simultaneous neuroimaging of two or more individuals during real-time interaction. Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) is increasingly used for such studies because it supports portable, naturalistic, face-to-face paradigms. A central goal in these experiments is to quantify IBS between interacting individuals. Wavelet transform coherence (WTC) has become the most widely used method for estimating IBS in fNIRS studies. However, its application involves several non-trivial signal-processing assumptions and time-frequency trade-offs that are often not explicitly addressed, making it difficult to apply and interpret the method consistently. Reliable estimation of IBS is crucial not only for experimental design but also for the interpretation and comparison of results within and across studies. Here, we aim to support this endeavor by providing a principled overview of the relevant signal-processing foundations. To enable researchers to make informed methodological choices, the paper first introduces key concepts in time-frequency analysis and clarifies their relation to WTC. These principles are then connected to the analysis of IBS in fNIRS datasets, with particular emphasis on the time-frequency constraints inherent to wavelet-based methods. Building on these foundations, we provide practical recommendations for experiment design, preprocessing, and frequency targeting. By making resolution limits and analysis assumptions explicit, this primer aims to support improved study planning and more consistent interpretation of IBS in the rapidly growing field of fNIRS-based investigations and beyond. Establishing a shared methodological foundation for IBS analysis is essential for advancing toward more rigorous, transparent, and reproducible measurement of interpersonal brain dynamics in naturalistic neuroscience.

titre: Mendelian Randomization-Based Analysis of Causal Effects Between Statins and Common Upper Gastrointestinal Diseases
resume: BACKGROUND: Statins are widely used for cardiovascular disease prevention and exhibit multiple pleiotropic effects, including anti-inflammatory properties. However, conclusions from observational studies regarding the causal relationship between statin use and upper gastrointestinal diseases (such as gastric cancer, gastric ulcer, and functional dyspepsia) remain controversial. This study is aimed at systematically evaluating the causal association between statin-targeted gene (HMGCR)-mediated reductions in low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels and common upper gastrointestinal diseases using drug-targeted Mendelian randomization (MR). This approach seeks to uncover potential unintended effects. METHODS: We extracted genetic variants associated with the HMGCR gene region from genome-wide association studies (GWAS) as instrumental variables to simulate the lipid-lowering effects of statins. Outcome data were derived from large-scale GWAS meta-analyses covering gastric cancer (n = 202,308), gastroenteritis (n = 7651), gastric ulcer (n = 361,194), gastroesophageal reflux disease (n = 462,933), and functional dyspepsia (n = 84,572). The primary analysis employed inverse variance weighting (IVW), with sensitivity assessments for heterogeneity and pleiotropy conducted via MR-Egger, weighted median, and MR-PRESSO methods. RESULTS: Genetically predicted HMGCR-mediated LDL-C reduction was associated with reduced risk of gastric cancer (OR = 0.588, 95% CI: 0.423-0.816, p = 0.002), gastroenteritis (OR = 0.257, 95% CI: 0.086-0.766, p = 0.015), and gastric ulcer (OR = 0.996, 95% CI: 0.993-0.998, p = 0.003). However, analysis indicated a potential increased risk of functional dyspepsia (OR = 1.437, 95% CI: 1.014-2.036, p = 0.042). No significant causal association was found between statin use and gastroesophageal reflux disease (OR = 0.999, 95% CI: 0.992-1.006, p = 0.773). Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the results, with no evidence of significant level-specific multiplicity. CONCLUSION: This study provides genetic evidence supporting the potential protective effects of statins against gastric cancer, gastritis, and gastric ulcers, which may be associated with their anti-inflammatory properties. However, the potential increased risk of functional dyspepsia suggests the complexity of the drug's effects. These findings provide scientific basis for the repositioning of statins in gastrointestinal diseases and their safety assessment.

titre: Irritable bowel syndrome and related disorders of gut-brain interaction
resume: Irritable bowel syndrome, chronic constipation, and functional diarrhoea are disorders of gut-brain interaction, the symptoms of which include abnormal stool consistency or frequency accompanied by varying degrees of abdominal pain, discomfort, bloating, or distension. These conditions affect 20% of the global population with a relapsing and remitting course. Risk factors include female sex, younger age, a history of common mental disorders, and acute enteric infection. The pathophysiology of irritable bowel syndrome, chronic constipation, and functional diarrhoea remain incompletely understood, but are thought to be secondary to aberrant interactions throughout the gut-brain axis, resulting in disordered gut motility and visceral hypersensitivity. These conditions are diagnosed with a combination of clinical history, absence of alarm symptoms-such as weight loss or rectal bleeding-and targeted investigations. An empathetic management approach improves quality of life and symptoms, reduces health-care use, and enhances treatment adherence. Mainstays of treatment include education, dietary and lifestyle advice, modifying fibre intake, and drugs directed towards predominant symptoms. For severe symptoms, other treatments include specific medical devices, biofeedback, or psychological therapies. However, the effectiveness of most treatments is modest and there is an ongoing need to expand available treatments for bowel disorders, with several novel drugs currently in development.

titre: Wearable Technologies in Gastrointestinal Disorders: Current Evidence and Future Directions
resume: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Gastrointestinal disorders fluctuate between clinical encounters, creating a need for objective longitudinal monitoring. We review wearable technologies across gastrointestinal disorders, emphasizing clinical applications, current evidence, and barriers to implementation. RECENT FINDINGS: Wearables capture physiologic, biochemical, and acoustic signals relevant to gastrointestinal disease. In inflammatory bowel disease, wearable-derived physiologic changes may precede inflammatory and symptomatic flares and help distinguish inflammatory from non-inflammatory symptoms. Sweat biosensors can measure inflammatory analytes, including calprotectin. Beyond inflammatory bowel disease, autonomic measures characterize disorders of gut-brain interaction, electrogastrographic and acoustic devices assess gastrointestinal motility, and activity and sleep metrics may aid postoperative recovery assessment and risk stratification in chronic liver disease. Evidence remains predominantly observational, and validated clinical thresholds are lacking, limiting the current clinical applicability of wearable derived signals. Wearables enable continuous, noninvasive monitoring across gastrointestinal disorders, but prospective trials are needed to establish clinical utility, actionable thresholds, workflow integration, and patient-centered implementation, and demonstrate improvement in clinically meaningful outcomes.

titre: The potential role of dietary polyphenols in the management of gastrointestinal issues in autism spectrum disorder
resume: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a complex neurodevelopmental condition, frequently comorbid with heterogeneous gastrointestinal (GI) pathologies, including Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS), Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD), and functional motility disorders. Emerging evidence implicates the microbiota-gut-brain axis in the pathogenesis of these GI anomalies. Dietary polyphenols, characterized by potent antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and neuromodulatory properties, represent a promising candidate approach for exploring the management of these comorbid conditions. This review critically examines the proposed molecular mechanisms by which specific phenolic compounds (e.g., resveratrol, quercetin and curcumin) may mitigate GI symptoms in ASD.
