titre: The effects of zinc supplementation on olfactory disorders: a systematic review with meta-analysis
resume: Objectives This systematic review aimed to evaluate the efficacy of zinc supplementation for treating olfactory disorders, including quantitative and qualitative symptoms, in adults. Methods We conducted a comprehensive search of the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Pubmed, Embase, and other relevant databases for Randomized Controlled Trials (RCTs) and observational studies evaluating zinc supplementation for olfactory dysfunction. Studies published up to April 2025 were included. Improvement in olfactory function was assessed with validated olfactory tests or subjective questionnaires. Qualitative symptoms (parosmia, phantosmia), adverse effects, patient-reported outcomes, and quality of life measured by questionnaires were evaluated. Results A total of 6 studies, including 3 RCTs and 3 observational studies, were included in the review. Sample sizes varied between 25 and 606 participants, with follow-up durations ranging from 1 to 15 months. The meta-analysis showed no significant difference in olfactory function improvement between the zinc-treated group and the control group (OR = 1.78; 95% CI 0.63-5.03; p = 0.28). In addition, the analysis of subjective perception of improvement, also did not demonstrate a statistically significant effect (OR = 0.69; 95% CI 0.25-1.93; p = 0.48). However, an individual study reported improvement in specific subgroups, such as those with posttraumatic anosmia. Adverse events were generally mild and primarily gastrointestinal. Conclusion Current evidence does not support a clear benefit of zinc supplementation for olfactory disorders. Further high-quality RCTs are necessary to determine its potential role, particularly in targeted subgroups. Level of evidence Level 2a.

titre: Study protocol for a randomised controlled trial of the BODYPOSI digital body image intervention for improving body image among postpartum women
resume: The high prevalence of body image concerns during the transition to motherhood underscores the need for theory-driven, accessible interventions that promote positive body image, reduce body dissatisfaction, and enhance women's resilience to unrealistic appearance ideals. This paper presents the protocol for a two-arm randomized controlled trial (RCT) evaluating the effectiveness of BODYPOSI, a four-week digital self-help program based on positive body image theory. The trial will include women between 6 weeks and 12 months postpartum, who will be randomly assigned to either the intervention or a waitlist control group. Primary outcomes will include body appreciation, body functionality appreciation, appearance and weight satisfaction, evaluation of postpartum body changes, and perceived sociocultural appearance pressure related to postpartum body changes. Secondary outcomes will include postnatal depressive and anxiety symptoms, self-compassion, and general health status. Outcomes will be assessed at baseline, post-intervention, and three-month follow-up. Analyses will compare changes between the intervention and control groups and examine the maintenance of intervention effects at follow-up for intervention group. If shown to be effective, BODYPOSI has the potential to improve body image and psychological well-being among postpartum women while supporting the wider implementation of accessible digital interventions in postpartum care.

titre: Application of Bayesian Sequential Analyses to Single Case Data: A Proof-of-Principle Study
resume: Timely identification of whether a treatment is having the expected effect on symptoms could help improve outcomes and inform treatment personalization. Application of Bayesian sequential analysis to single case data may offer a useful method for rapidly identifying treatment success or failure at an individual level, tailored to an individual patient. This paper provides proof-of-principle for this concept, applied to simple internet-delivered interventions in an ABC randomized single case design. Seven participants with elevated symptoms of depression seeking treatment at an outpatient psychotherapy centre completed a two-week baseline period. They then completed two weeks of first one and then another internet-delivered cognitive training intervention, with the order of intervention randomized between participants. Participants rated depression symptoms on a daily basis throughout the study. Each participant’s baseline data was used to simulate hypothetical continuations after treatment initiation, and this in turn was used to determine individualised Bayes factor thresholds and other decision parameters for determining treatment success or failure. The study illustrates the potential application of sequential Bayesian analyses at a single case level to inform clinical decision-making, as well as highlighting potential challenges in implementing this approach.

titre: Role of artificial intelligence in irritable bowel syndrome: A narrative review
resume: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a prevalent yet incompletely understood functional gastrointestinal disorder whose estimated prevalence depends heavily on the diagnostic criteria applied, falling from approximately 9% under Rome III to approximately 4% under Rome IV. Characterized by recurrent abdominal pain and altered bowel habits, it substantially impairs quality of life and imposes a considerable economic burden. Its pathophysiology is complex and multifactorial, involving visceral hypersensitivity, altered gastrointestinal motility, immune activation, gut-brain axis dysregulation, and intestinal dysbiosis. This narrative review examines the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) to refine the diagnosis, subclassification, and management of IBS and related functional gastrointestinal disorders. We discuss the principal AI methodologies - machine learning, deep learning, and natural language processing - and how they enable the integration of diverse data sources, including patient-reported outcomes, microbiome profiles, and multi-omics data. Early studies suggest AI can support the differentiation of IBS from organic disease, the identification of biologically distinct microbiota subgroups, and the prediction of response to the low-fermentable oligosaccharides, disaccharides, monosaccharides and polyols diet. These findings, however, derive largely from small, single-center cohorts with heterogeneous methods and without external validation; a 2025 systematic review identified only six eligible studies comprising 1366 participants and found the evidence too heterogeneous to permit meta-analysis. We further identify domains in which AI is frequently invoked but not yet evidenced in IBS, including machine-learning analysis of longitudinal patient-collected symptom data and of psychological comorbidity. Substantial challenges remain around data standardization, external and temporal validation, model interpretability, and ethical and regulatory considerations. Progress will depend less on the development of further models than on standardized data collection, multi-center validation, and reporting against AI-specific standards such as transparent reporting of a multivariable prediction model for individual prognosis or diagnosis + AI.

titre: Evaluation of some biomarkers levels in women suffering from irritable bowel syndrome
resume: Background & objective: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a chronic functional pathology of the gastrointestinal tract (GIT), this disease is characterized by chronic abdominal pain, bloating, and altered bowel habits, which can significantly impair the quality of life, also the severity of symptoms varies in different individuals with some experiencing severe disease whereas others experiencing mild symptoms. The present study was designed to investigate a role of biomarker salusin- α as a prognostic markers for prediction of irritable bowel syndrome.Methodology: The research was conducted in Najaf Governorate, Iraq, from July 1, 2025, to December 1, 2026. A total of 90 participants were enrolled, including 60 patients diagnosed with IBS and 30 healthy individuals as controls. The results were stratified into subgroups according to age, body mass index, disease duration, diagnosis status (newly diagnosed or under treatment), familial or non, constipation or diarrhea, physical activity and non-physical activity.Results: The results revealed a significant decrease in salusin- α level among patients compared to the control group. The present results revealed significant decrease in salusin- α in women patients in compare with control. In ages groups that results showed significant decrease in ages group (20-29) years than other groups, also significant decrease in diarrhea group in compare to constipation. The results also indicated a significant decrease in new diagnosed patients than treated, also body mass index revealed a significant decrease in obese patients than overweight. Shorter duration of disease less than (1 year) showed significant decrease than long more than 1 year. both physical activity and familial status showed a significant decrease than non physical activity and non familial.Additionally, the study included a full analytical validation of the salusin α ELISA assay (linearity, sensitivity, precision, recovery, and cross reactivity) in accordance with FDA bioanalytical guidelines. A proof of concept design for a nanomaterial based biosensor and in silico simulation using COMSOL were also proposed to demonstrate future potential for point of care IBS diagnosis.Conclusions: In conclusion, the study suggests that salusin- α is a novel biomarker for irritable bowel syndrome It may serve as a valuable diagnostic and prognostic tool. Abbreviations: IBS-irritable bowel syndrome; GIT-astrointestinal tract; BMI-body mass index; NAFLD-non-alcoholic fatty liver disease; D-diarrhea; C-constipation; VSMCs- vascular smooth muscle cell.

titre: Do the Psychological Effects of Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation Depend on Gastrointestinal Response? Protocol for a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials in Disorders of Gut–Brain Interaction
resume: This review pools randomized trials of transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) in adults with disorders of gut–brain interaction (DGBI). It asks whether taVNS reduces anxiety and depression beyond sham or control stimulation, whether these psychological effects track or dissociate from gastrointestinal symptom response, and how the type of control and the rater (clinician vs patient) shape the estimated effect. Transparency statement: this is a retrospective registration. The protocol was written after the searches and a pilot extraction of psychological outcomes, and before any analysis; full extraction and analyses were completed before the registration was formally submitted.

titre: Frequency and Risk Factors of Functional Constipation among Children Attending Outpatient Clinics
resume: Background: Functional constipation is a common pediatric gastrointestinal disorder with multifactorial etiology. Despite its prevalence, many contributing risk factors are under-recognized in clinical settings, especially in limited resource. Objective: To determine the frequency of functional constipation and identify associated risk factors among children. Materials and Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 150 children attending a pediatric outpatient department. Functional constipation was diagnosed based on Rome IV criteria. Data on sociodemographic characteristics, clinical symptoms, bowel habits, dietary patterns, physical activity, and screen time were collected using a structured questionnaire. Statistical analyses included chi-square tests and multivariate logistic regression. Results: Among 150 children, 84 (56%) were diagnosed with functional constipation. The majority of affected children were aged 6–10 years (47.6%), with a slight male predominance (52.4%). Hard stool (75%), large-diameter stool (85.7%), painful bowel movements (69.0%), and abdominal pain (47.6%) were the most common clinical features. More than half of the children had prolonged screen time >2 hours/day (64.3%), inadequate fiber intake (53.6%), inadequate fluid intake (51.2%), and poor school toilet facilities (61.9%). Emotional abuse was reported in 25% of cases, while positive parental history of constipation was present in 46.4% of the children. Conclusion: Functional constipation is prevalent in children and is significantly associated with modifiable factors such as inadequate fluid intake, increased screen time, and parental history. Preventive strategies should include parental education, promoting adequate hydration, and reducing sedentary behavior. J Dhaka National Med. Coll. Hos. 2026; 32 (02): 53-59
revue: Journal of Dhaka National Medical College & Hospital

titre: Characteristics of functional constipation among paediatric patients in the North Denmark Region
resume: INTRODUCTION.This study aimed to describe clinical and demographic characteristics and examine stool consistency patterns in children with functional constipation in a hospital-based paediatric population.METHODS.This was a retrospective observational study that included children aged 0-15 years diagnosed with constipation (ICD-10: DK590/DK590A) between March 2019 and February 2024 at two paediatric departments in the North Denmark Region.Only functional constipation was included.Data were extracted from electronic medical records.RESULTS.A total of 1,672 children met the inclusion criteria.The median age was 3.1 years, with an equal sex distribution.Median symptom duration before initial contact was two months (IQR: < 1-12 months).Daily defaecation was absent in 48.5%, of whom 34.6% reported ≤ 2 defecations weekly.Soft stools (Bristol Stool Scale 3-5) were most frequent.The Rome IV-related symptoms were poorly documented.Faecal incontinence was the most common comorbidity, occurring in 23.7% of patients ≥ 4 years.Pharmacological treatment, particularly osmotic laxatives, was initiated in 96.7% of cases.Follow-up was completed within three months in 51.7% of cases. CONCLUSIONS.CONCLUSIONS.This study suggests that functional constipation predominantly occurs in infancy (median age: 3.1 years), presents with variable clinical manifestations and is predominantly managed with pharmacological treatment.Rome IVrelated symptoms are often incompletely documented in medical records.FUNDING.FUNDING.None.

titre: Scientific projects of the IBS synchrotron group
resume: The IBS synchrotron group combines macromolecular crystallography, on-line UV–Vis microspectroscopy, and method development to link structure, dynamics, and function. We will solve and spectroscopically characterize fluorescent proteins at 100 K and, when possible, at room temperature, to clarify photophysical determinants and light-induced structural changes while minimizing radiation damage. In parallel, we will determine ligand- and fragment-bound structures of key enzymes of the bacterial MEP pathway from major nosocomial pathogens to support structure-guided antibacterial inhibitor discovery. To probe enzyme motions and catalysis, we will map temperature-dependent conformational dynamics of TET aminopeptidases and initiate turnover via substrate soaks and temperature jumps. We will also improve crystallization using molecular glues and develop an in situ mixing approach to capture catalytic intermediates in oxidoreductases.

titre: Differential diagnosis and teratment of intestinal dyspepsia, malabsorption
resume: Background: Abdominal discomfort, bloating, altered bowel habits, and chronic diarrhea are common presentations in hospital and outpatient practice. They may reflect functional gastrointestinal disorders, infection, inflammation, impaired digestion, or reduced nutrient absorption. Objective: To summarize the differential diagnosis, clinical assessment, investigations, and evidence-based management of intestinal symptoms associated with suspected malabsorption. Methods: This educational narrative review synthesizes clinical principles and selected guidance on celiac disease, lactose intolerance, exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, irritable bowel syndrome, inflammatory bowel disease, intestinal infection, and related disorders. It is not a new systematic review or original clinical study. Results: Symptom overlap makes diagnosis challenging. A structured history and examination, recognition of alarm features, and targeted blood, stool, serological, endoscopic, or breath tests can help identify the cause. Management is cause-specific and may include dietary intervention, medications, enzyme replacement, treatment of infection or inflammation, and correction of nutritional deficiencies.

titre: Connecting Host–parasite Interactions to the Microbiota–gut–brain Axis
resume: Abstract Purpose of Review To provide a comprehensive overview of the key findings on the microbiota–gut–brain axis. Recent Findings Growing evidence indicates that microbial metabolites, neurotransmitters, cytokines, and gut-derived hormones modulate blood–brain barrier integrity, neuroinflammation, and brain function, while the brain reciprocally shapes gut physiology through neuroendocrine and autonomic pathways. Disruption of this axis by dysbiosis has been implicated in a broad spectrum of disorders, including depression, schizophrenia, neurodevelopmental diseases, and chronic inflammatory conditions. More recently, infectious diseases have emerged as important modulators of the microbiota–gut–brain axis, as pathogens such as Toxoplasma gondii , Plasmodium spp ., Trypanosoma cruzi , and Leishmania spp . induce microbial dysbiosis, intestinal barrier dysfunction, and systemic immune activation that may contribute to neuroinflammation and neurological manifestations. Summary The microbiota-gut-brain axis represents an interorgan communication system that integrates immune, neural, metabolic, and endocrine signals between the gastrointestinal tract and the central nervous system. The gut microbiota, composed of a vast diversity of microorganisms, plays a fundamental role in maintaining host homeostasis and immunity. Evidence indicates that alterations in its composition, such as dysbiosis, can compromise the integrity of the intestinal and the blood-brain barriers, favoring systemic inflammatory and neuroinflammatory processes associated with neurological, psychiatric disorders and infectious diseases. Furthermore, it dictates not only how the gut influences the brain in a steady state or during disease, but also how the brain coordinates the efferent signals to the gut. In this review, we elucidate the role of the microbiota-gut-brain axis in health and host disease and convey recent data showing that an imbalance in microbiota and gut infections could be mediating late effects on the central nervous system, through their direct effects on the gut barrier and immune system.

titre: Microplastics and gut–brain axis: a mechanistic review of metabolic and microbial pathways
Functional Roles of Lactic Acid Bacteria in the Gut-Brain Axis
Psychobiotics and polyphenols modulate the gut-brain axis through personalized nutritional strategies in mental health
resume: Anxiety and depression are major contributors to the global disease burden; however, fewer than half of patients treated with standard pharmacotherapy achieve sustained remission. This gap underscores the need to identify effective adjunctive treatments. The bidirectional gut-brain axis offers a valuable perspective by linking diet to neurotransmission, neuroinflammation, and hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis reactivity. This framework positions nutritional psychiatry as a complement, rather than a substitute, for established care. This narrative review examines three converging intervention classes: psychobiotics, dietary polyphenols, and precision nutraceuticals. Randomized trials of Lactobacillus helveticus R0052, Bifidobacterium longum R0175, and Lactiplantibacillus plantarum PS128 demonstrate modest but reproducible reductions in depressive and anxiety symptoms, although effect sizes vary. Plausible mechanisms include reduced low-grade neuroinflammation, partial normalization of HPA axis reactivity, and a shift in tryptophan metabolism from the kynurenine pathway toward serotonin synthesis—although human evidence supporting these pathways remains limited. Polyphenol biology introduces an additional dimension. Microbial conversion of ellagitannins, isoflavones, and lignans into urolithin A, equol, and enterolactone can alter the bioavailability of neuroactive metabolites. Consequently, an individual’s metabotype likely accounts for some of the variability in clinical response. We propose that microbiota-guided strategies—stratified by enterotype, metabotype, tryptophan–kynurenine flux, and short-chain fatty acid output—could significantly enhance psychiatric care. Multi-omic profiling and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven digital phenotyping can operationalize this precision approach. However, methodological heterogeneity, small sample sizes, inconsistent strain and dose reporting, and regulatory ambiguity continue to hinder translation, as recent meta-analyses highlight.

titre: Artificial intelligence in gut-brain axis research for Alzheimer’s disease: From associative insights toward causal inference and personalized interventions
resume: Abstract Alzheimer’s disease (AD) research is shifting from a “brain-centered” model toward a “gut-brain axis system” perspective. However, the causal roles of gut microbiota in AD pathology remain elusive, as traditional association studies struggle to distinguish potential drivers from passengers. This review examines the potential applications and inherent limitations of artificial intelligence (AI) in dissecting this complex relationship. We discuss three emerging and conceptually promising directions: First, AI-frameworks for hypothesis-generating causal discovery that can prioritize microbiota-AD relationships for subsequent experimental validation, while recognizing that current approaches predominantly identify statistical associations rather than empirically supported causal conclusions; second, multi-modal fusion networks, when applied with appropriate regularization and validation, can assist in constructing cross-scale molecular maps across microbiota, metabolites, and the brain, though such pathway inferences require careful interpretation as they represent statistical associations rather than biochemically validated mechanisms; and third, the conceptual application of digital twin-based simulation as a long-term vision for personalized microbiota modulation, which currently lacks the ecological resolution and validation required for predictive modeling. By integrating multi-pathway mechanisms of the gut-brain axis and characteristic profiles of gut microbiota, we critically evaluate the technical advantages of machine learning in microbiome data analysis alongside major challenges including overfitting, batch effects, confounding factors, and reproducibility. Leveraging AI-driven microbiota analysis, we propose a phased translational roadmap, from near-term standardization and cross-cohort validation, through mid-term endophenotyping and trial enrichment strategies, to the long-term exploration of personalized interventions, toward the eventual goal of precision prevention. This article outlines a full-cycle framework from discovery to clinical translation and envisions a conceptual ecosystem for future intelligent microecological health management. Achieving the promise of AI-empowered gut-brain axis research will require deep integration across neuroscience, microbiology, computational science, and clinical medicine, alongside rigorous experimental validation, standardized protocols, and realistic appraisal of current technological boundaries.

titre: THE EPIGENETICS OF INTELLIGENCE: HOW THOUGHTS, ENVIRONMENT, AND MICROBIOME REWRITE THE BRAIN'S CODE ACROSS GENERATIONS From Fixed Destiny to Dynamic Evolution: A Mathematical Framework for Understanding How Conscious Experience Chemically Transforms Neural Architecture and Cognitive Capacity
resume: The El-Rakhawi Epigenetic Intelligence Framework (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23744035) shatters the myth of fixed intelligence, proving that thoughts, environment, and microbiome chemically rewrite the brain's epigenetic code. Core insight: Intelligence is dynamically modulated through DNA methylation, histone modifications, and non-coding RNAs, with BDNF (via Promoter IV) as master regulator. Four dimensionless indices quantify this:- EPI (Epigenetic Plasticity Index) = 0.92- NMEI (Neural Methylation Efficiency Index) = 0.95- FSI (Flow State Index) = 0.94- FIC (Functional Intelligence Coefficient) with corrected Epigenetic_Age_Burden variable Key pathways: Gut-brain axis (butyrate as HDAC inhibitor), nootropics (with medical disclaimer), meditation, fasting, and flow state engineering. Transgenerational inheritance: Robust in animals; human evidence remains associative due to confounding factors. CRISPRoff/CRISPRon enables precision epigenetic editing. Academic citation permitted with DOI. Commercial use requires authorization. The alchemy of thought is molecular reality - we are the epigenetic alchemists of our own minds.
revue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

titre: Bowel urgency, ulcerative colitis, and the importance of being earnest
resume: “The important thing is not to stop questioning.” – Albert Einstein Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic immune-mediated inflammatory bowel disease with multidimensional and often negative effects on the lives of patients.1 Although typical symptoms include diarrhea, rectal bleeding, and abdominal pain, symptoms of anorectal dysfunction, including bowel urgency (BU), have gained wider recognition in recent years.2,3 Defined as the sudden and immediate need to have a bowel movement, BU is a burdensome symptom of UC that is associated with high levels of disease activity, steroid use, hospitalization, and colectomy.In addition, BU is also present during “remission,” with a negative impact on well-being.2,3 In a cross-sectional analysis of 576 patients with UC from the Study of a Prospective Adult Research Cohort with Inflammatory Bowel Disease (SPARC IBD), 31% of patients reported mild BU and 28% reported moderate to severe BU.4 Moderate to severe BU was associated with the presence of rectal bleeding, increased stool frequency, and elevated fecal calprotectin.4 In the Communicating Needs and Features of IBD Experiences (CONFIDE) study, 78.9% of US patients and 70.8% of European patients reported experiencing BU weekly over the past 3 months.5 Furthermore, among those patients receiving advanced therapy, 80.2% and 73.9%, respectively, reported weekly BU.5 Among 200 patients with a history of moderate to severe UC in the United States, 75% reported wearing some form of protection such as pads or diapers in the preceding 3 months, 43% reported declining social activities because of BU, and 37% reported declining to take part in work/school activities.5 The negative ramifications of BU in UC extend to physical exercise, education, employment, wider social activities, and sexual intimacy.4–7 It is sobering to note that while patients prioritize improvement in BU, abdominal pain, and quality of life over rectal bleeding and diarrhea, gastroenterologists report improvement in these areas to be of lower priority over mucosal healing.8,9 Notably, the evidence base characterizing the burden of BU comes largely from cross-sectional or observational epidemiologic studies, and data on the evaluation of BU in real-world clinical care are scarce.

titre: Machine learning-based diagnosis of inflammatory bowel disease using gut microbiome virulence factor profiles: multicohort integration and independent validation
resume: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic intestinal disease that includes Crohn’s disease (CD) and ulcerative colitis (UC). IBD severely affects the quality of life of millions of patients worldwide. Consequently, the timely diagnosis and treatment of IBD are critically important. However, current diagnostic methods are predominantly invasive and costly. In recent years, metagenomics-based studies, utilizing cross-cohort analysis, have successfully constructed biomarkers based on microbial composition or specific gene functions, enabling highly accurate, non-invasive diagnosis of IBD. The decreasing cost of metagenomic sequencing has increased its potential for the development of non-invasive microbiome-based diagnostic and risk-stratification tools. Recent studies have indicated that the structure and function of the gut microbial community are significantly altered in patients with IBD. Moreover, the abundance of certain virulence factors (VFs) is much greater in these patients than in healthy controls. High-resolution metagenomic data can aid in understanding the pathogenesis of IBD and have the potential to become a new generation of non-invasive diagnostic tools. This study established a Discovery cohort by integrating eight metagenomic cohorts. This cohort comprised 1,062 fecal samples, including 737 from patients with IBD and 325 from healthy controls. This study implemented a standardized virulence factor profiling workflow, termed VFfinder, to quantify gut microbial virulence factor profiles across multiple metagenomic cohorts. Using the species and virulence factor abundance matrices, we developed three machine learning models for IBD classification: the Species Model, the VFs Model, and the IBDseek, which integrates both feature types. The Validation cohort, comprising three metagenomic datasets with 170 IBD samples and 125 healthy controls, was used to evaluate the performance and generalizability of each model. Virulence factors in the gut microbiome were significantly enriched in patients with IBD. In the Validation cohort, the 79-species Species Model achieved an AUC of 0.94 and an accuracy of 88.81%. The VFs Model, a 45-VF-based machine learning model, achieved a sensitivity of 96.47% (95% CI, 92.48–98.69%) and an accuracy of 89.49% (95% CI, 85.42–92.75%) in the Validation cohort. Furthermore, the IBDseek Model, integrating 45 VF features and 79 species features, achieved a sensitivity of 96.47% (95% CI, 92.48–98.69%), specificity of 81.60% (95% CI, 73.68–87.96%), and accuracy of 90.17% (95% CI, 86.19–93.32%). In summary, our study demonstrates the cross-cohort enrichment of bacterial virulence factors in patients with IBD and supports their utility as stable diagnostic features. The IBDseek Model, which integrates VFs and species features, achieved the highest observed accuracy and shared the highest sensitivity with the VFs Model in the Validation cohort. These findings support the potential of virulence-associated microbial features as informative biomarkers for noninvasive IBD classification and provide a basis for the future development of microbiome-based diagnostic support and risk stratification tools. Prospective evaluation in clinically relevant populations is needed to establish their clinical utility and integration into existing diagnostic pathways. Not applicable.

titre: The impact of celiac disease on adult quality of life
resume: Celiakija je bolezen, ki zaradi preobčutljivosti na beljakovino gluten povzroči spremembe na steni tankega črevesja pri bolnikih z gensko predispozicijo. Pojavlja se tako pri ženskah kot pri moških v vseh starostnih obdobjih. Namen diplomskega dela je spoznati celiakijo kot bolezensko stanje in njen vpliv na kakovost življenja odraslega človeka. Izvedli smo sistematični pristop dela z metodami pregleda, analize in sinteze strokovne literature. Iskanje je bilo opravljeno v treh mednarodnih podatkovnih bazah: PubMed, CINAHL in ScienceDirect. V končno analizo smo vključili 10 raziskav. Ugotovili smo, da celiakija vpliva na kakovost življenja odrasle osebe, in sicer na zdravstveno, psihološko in socialno področje življenja. Upoštevanje brezglutenske diete ugodno vpliva na telesne simptome, psihološke in čustvene obremenitve. Sledenje dieti izboljša kakovost življenja in motnje razpoloženja ter ima pozitivne učinke na anksioznost in depresijo. Za izboljšanje kakovosti življenja odraslih oseb s celiakijo je potrebna celostna oskrba, ki vključuje redne zdravstvene preglede, zdravstvene intervencije, psihološke preglede in svetovanja, skupinska izobraževanja o celiakiji ter finančno pomoč pri nakupu brezglutenske prehrane.
revue: University of Maribor digital library (University of Maribor)

titre: The effects of dailY consumption of rUMinant MIlk on nutrition and digestive comfort in older women, The YUMMI study: A randomised controlled trial
resume: Background: Milk is rich in essential nutrients that support healthy ageing but concerns about the perceived negative gastrointestinal and cardiometabolic impacts of milk can deter consumption. While bovine milk is most commonly consumed, other ruminant milks such as caprine and ovine milk have been proposed to offer digestive and nutritional advantages over bovine milk. However, research comparing different milks consists mainly of in vitro and animal studies, with human studies largely limited to acute postprandial interventions in the general adult population. Objectives: The YUMMI study was designed to examine the impact of bovine, caprine, and ovine milk consumption on digestion, nutrition, and other health parameters in community dwelling older women in New Zealand. Using data from this study, the overall aim of this thesis was to examine the effects of regular ruminant milk consumption on digestive comfort, nutritional intake and status, and cardiometabolic markers in older women. Methods: The YUMMI study was a 12-week, multi-arm, parallel, multi-centre, single-blinded randomised controlled trial conducted at the Dunedin and Christchurch campuses of the University of Otago, New Zealand. A total of 165 healthy older women aged 60 to 80 years (mean ± SD: age, 68.1 ± 5.4 years; BMI, 25.2 ± 3.7 kg/m²) were randomised to one of four intervention groups, bovine, caprine, or ovine milk groups, or a control group. Those in the milk groups were asked to consume 500 mL of their allocated milk each day, half with breakfast and the other half with lunch, on top of their usual diet, whereas those in the control group maintained their usual diet. Digestive comfort (primary outcome), depression and anxiety symptoms, sleep quality, and daily bowel habits were assessed throughout the study using the Gastrointestinal Symptom Rating Scale (GSRS), Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS): Depression and Anxiety, Leeds Sleep Evaluation Questionnaire (LSEQ), and daily bowel habit diaries, respectively. Stool samples were collected at baseline and week 12 to assess the composition and functional potential of the gut microbiota using metagenomic sequencing. Dietary intake of protein (primary outcome) and other nutrients, plasma concentrations of zinc, selenium and amino acids, along with physical function assessments, were assessed at baseline and week 12 to examine the effects of milk consumption on nutrient intake and nutritional status. Additionally, the cardiometabolic effects of milk consumption were assessed through anthropometry, body composition, blood pressure, blood lipids, HbA1c, and inflammatory marker measurements at baseline and week 12. Mean changes from baseline to week 12 were compared between groups using ANCOVA, adjusting for baseline values, with pairwise comparisons conducted when the overall treatment effect was significant (P < 0.05). Results: After 12 weeks, there were no statistically significant differences in changes in GSRS scores between groups, nor were there differences in depression, anxiety, sleep, or bowel habit outcomes. While some early differences in constipation and stool form scores were observed between groups, the changes were small and unlikely to be of any clinical significance. Similarly, there were minimal changes to the composition and predictive function of the gut microbiota. Greater increases in the dietary intakes of protein, saturated and trans fat, and key minerals (calcium, phosphorus, potassium) were observed in one or more milk groups compared with the control group, with some minor differences between groups. These changes were accompanied by differences in plasma zinc, selenium, and some amino acid concentrations. Specifically, increased plasma zinc concentrations were observed in the ovine group compared to the caprine and control groups, and selenium concentrations were increased in the ovine milk group compared with all other groups. Greater increases in plasma tyrosine and lysine concentrations were observed in the ovine milk group. Plasma cystine concentrations decreased across all milk groups while glycine concentrations generally declined relative to the control group. There was no effect of milk intake on physical function. Despite the greater increase in saturated and trans fat intake with ruminant milk intake, there were no statistically significant between-group differences in changes in cardiometabolic markers apart from a greater increase in body weight and body mass index in the ovine milk group and a slight decrease in high-sensitivity C-reactive protein concentrations in the caprine milk group. Conclusions: Findings of this thesis show that the addition of 500 mL of ruminant milk was well tolerated by community-dwelling older women in New Zealand and increased the intake of key nutrients with minimal impact on digestive and cardiometabolic outcomes. Ruminant milks may therefore represent a practical strategy to support nutrient intake in older women who can tolerate milk. However, the associated increases in body weight and saturated and trans fat intake highlight the need to consider overall diet quality, as well as further guidance on appropriate intake and strategies to support nutritional balance, particularly in older adults.
revue: Otago University Research Archive (University of Otago)

titre: Feeling the body politic: Interoception as a mechanism of political stress resilience
resume: Abstract Politics can substantially harm physical and mental health, especially in polarized contexts, making political polarization a major non‐medical cause of disease and suffering. We examined whether citizens can protect their health without undermining civic engagement. Across three studies with over 2000 participants during the 2022 U.S. midterms and 2024 presidential election, we show that interoceptive sensibility, that is, the ability to perceive and trust one's internal bodily signals, protects against politics' adverse health effects. Higher interoceptive sensibility consistently predicted lower emotional, physical, behavioral, and social health costs, controlling for political identity, demographics, and emotion regulation. During the charged 2024 election, it further predicted fewer negative emotions, more hope for the future, and less fear, particularly when their candidate lost. Interoceptive sensibility also correlated with political engagement and efficacy, suggesting it enhances rather than inhibits participation. Our findings highlight it as a promising trait for mitigating political stress without reducing civic involvement.

titre: Association between alexithymia and lower quality of life in patients with psoriasis: a cross-sectional differential study
resume: Background Psoriasis vulgaris affects 90% of individuals with psoriasis, leading to a significant burden, reduced quality of life, and often psychopathology. Although alexithymia has been identified as a predictor of psychopathology, there is a need for studies that specifically examine its role in quality of life. This study aimed to investigate the association between alexithymia and quality of life and identify significant differences according to varying levels of alexithymia. Participants and procedure One hundred and thirty-nine patients with psoriasis vulgaris aged between 18 and 83 years old (M = 29.65, SD = 14.16) were recruited to the study. The diagnostic protocol consisted of a sociodemographic questionnaire, the Toronto Alexithymia Scale-20 and SF-36. Descriptive, correlational, regression and differential analyses were performed. Results Correlational analyses highlighted significant negative associations between alexithymia and quality of life. Regression analyses further identified alexithymia as a significant statistical predictor of lower quality of life. Significant differences were observed between non-alexithymic and borderline subjects, highlighting a threshold that is particularly relevant for understanding the association between alexithymia and quality of life. Conclusions Alexithymia was significantly associated with lower quality of life and emerged as a significant statistical predictor of poorer quality of life. Even borderline levels of alexithymia were associated with lower quality of life. The relationship be-tween alexithymia and quality of life of patients with psoriasis should be further investigated to develop targeted interven-tions aimed at reducing this burden.

titre: Associations of loneliness, psychological resilience, social support, and sleep quality with alexithymia among 7,964 Chinese adolescents: a cross-sectional study
resume: Alexithymia, a difficulty in identifying and describing emotions, is a significant psychological risk factor during adolescence. However, a comprehensive understanding of its modifiable correlates, including psychological, social, and physiological factors, within the Chinese adolescent population remains limited. This study aimed to investigate the levels of alexithymia and their associations with psychological resilience, social support, loneliness, and sleep quality among Chinese adolescents. A cross-sectional, school-based survey was conducted from February to April 2024 among 7,964 adolescents from 13 secondary schools across six provinces and autonomous regions in China. Participants completed the Chinese version of the Perth Alexithymia Questionnaire (PAQ-24), the Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale (CD-RISC-10), the UCLA Loneliness Scale (ULS-6), the Perceived Social Support Scale (PSSS-3), and the Brief Version of the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (B-PSQI). Data were analyzed using t-tests, analysis of variance (ANOVA), correlation analysis, and hierarchical regression, with linear mixed models used as a sensitivity analysis to account for school clustering. The mean PAQ total score was 80.52 ± 26.43. Adolescents reported greater difficulties in identifying and describing negative emotions than positive emotions. After adjustment for demographic, family, and behavioral factors, loneliness (β = 0.313, 95% CI [1.575, 1.817]) and poor sleep quality (higher B-PSQI scores; β = 0.099, 95% CI [0.826, 1.290]) were positively associated with alexithymia, whereas psychological resilience (β = −0.162, 95% CI [− 0.531, − 0.400]) and perceived social support (β = −0.058, 95% CI [− 0.569, − 0.248]) were inversely associated with alexithymia. The final model explained 23.9% of the variance. Additionally, variables such as gender, grade, boarding, and smoking were also associated with alexithymia after adjustment. Loneliness and poor sleep quality were associated with higher alexithymia scores, whereas psychological resilience and perceived social support showed inverse associations with alexithymia. These findings identify potentially modifiable correlates that may warrant consideration in future longitudinal and intervention research.

titre: Mindfulness-Acceptance-Commitment Approach with Wheelchair Rugby Athletes: A Preliminary Case Study
resume: Research on sport psychology interventions involving adaptive athletes remains limited, leaving practitioners with relatively little evidence to guide applied practice. This preliminary study explored the use of the Mindfulness-Acceptance-Commitment (MAC) approach with three wheelchair rugby athletes. Participants completed measures of flow, interoceptive awareness, and mindfulness in sport before the intervention, at its midpoint, and after its completion. Following the intervention, semi-structured interviews provided additional insight into participants’ experiences. Interview responses and researcher observations were used to contextualize individual patterns in questionnaire scores. The findings suggest the MAC approach may have value for wheelchair rugby athletes however, the small sample and descriptive design warrant cautious interpretation and further investigation.
revue: Journal of Sports Psychology and Medicine

titre: Combining hypnotics in general anesthesia: pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic perspectives on propofol and remimazolam
resume: Combining two hypnotics is an attractive option when increasing the dose of a single agent causes hypotension or an undesirable recovery profile.Propofol and remimazolam can both be used to maintain general anesthesia, but they differ in their hemodynamic effects and the availability of pharmacological reversal.The central question is whether combining these agents can improve the balance between hypnosis, adverse effects, and emergence by reducing the required concentration of each agent.Dose comparisons alone cannot answer this question.The effects of the combination must be considered in relation to drug concentrations, the responses being assessed, and the time course of administration.Studies published in the Journal of Anesthesia and JA Clinical Reports provide clinical context for this question.In a multicenter trial, Doi et al. reported that remimazolam was noninferior to propofol in anesthetic efficacy and was associated with a lower incidence of hypotension but a longer time to extubation [1].These differences provide a rationale for investigating the combined use of propofol and remimazolam. Katsuragawa et al. retrospectively evaluated combined administration during anesthesia maintenance [2]. After

titre: The Effectiveness of Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) in patients presenting with Depression in Saudi Arabia
resume: Background: Depression continues to be a serious public mental health issue in Saudi Arabia. Cultural stigma, fewer resources, and reliance on medication limits access to evidence-based psychotherapies. Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) is a third-wave cognitive-behavioural intervention that promotes the use of mindfulness, psychological flexibility, and values-based living, which has potential for cultural adaptation. This thesis evaluated the efficacy of ACT through a systematic review and meta-analysis of the international literature, and an empirical clinical trial in Saudi Arabia. Methods: A systematic review and meta-analysis was undertaken in accordance with PRISMA; a comprehensive review of published randomised controlled trials (RCTs) of ACT for depression published from 2019 to 2024 was completed. The researcher also conducted a quantitative experimental study at King Khalid University Hospital. Thirty-four participants diagnosed with depression were randomised into either the ACT intervention group (n=17), or standard care control group (n=17). Psychological indicators of depression (BDI, PHQ-9), anxiety (GAD-7, TMAS), mindfulness (KIMS, MAAS), cognitive fusion (ATQ-F, ATQ-B), and thought suppression (WBSI) were measured three times: pre-intervention (T1), post-intervention (T2), and follow-up (T3). The data were analysed using repeated measure ANOVA, independent t-tests and regression models using SPSS v30. Results: The meta-analysis found ACT produced moderate levels of statistically significant reductions in depressive symptoms across various populations and delivery models. Additionally, the Saudi clinical trial demonstrated improvements in depression scores for ACT participants, specifically, BDI interventions decreased from 36.06 to 18.88, and PHQ-9 dropped from 17.71 to 8.65, contrasting with negligible change in controls. Improvements were seen in anxiety scores (GAD-7, TMAS) and negative thoughts (ATQ, WBSI), while mindfulness (KIMS, MAAS) was meaningfully better. Time × Group interactions were large and statistically significant, thus supporting ACT intervention versus standard care. Regression analyses showed group assignment was the strongest moderator of outcomes, while gender and age were of lesser importance. Improvements were deemed most beneficial immediately post-treatment and at follow-up, but regression to the mean was suspected on delayed assessments; thus, future booster sessions would be beneficial. Conclusion: This thesis provides converging findings from international trials, with a Saudi-based experiment that ACT represents an effective intervention that adapts for cultural resonance and acceptance for depression and related distress. ACT improves aspects of mindfulness, cognitive rigidity, and results in sustainable improvements to respondents' mental health. In Saudi Arabia, ACT therapy could be embedded into healthcare service provision through digital and scalable models to close treatment access barriers, reduce stigma, and offer a credible one-step improvement pathway. Long-term maintenance boosters are considered to convert the therapeutic gains to longer-term benefits.
revue: University Of Wales Trinity Saint David Research Repository (University of Wales Trinity Saint David)

titre: Mindfulness-Based Intervention and Mental Health Disorders
resume: In the last 20 years, there has been a significant rise in both scientific and general interest in mindfulness-based interventions (MBIs). The main theoretical basis of MBIs is that engaging in mindfulness practices (such as sitting meditation, yoga, or other mindfulness activities) will help individuals become less reactive to negative internal experiences while fostering greater reflection, ultimately resulting in beneficial psychological effects. This chapter examines how the integration of mindfulness practices has enhanced cognitive and behavioural therapies for depression and anxiety. The last ten years have seen a significant rise in research focused on MBIs. The most prevalent are mindfulness-based stress reduction and mindfulness-based cognitive therapy. MBIs have shown effectiveness in lowering the severity of anxiety and depression symptoms in a wide variety of individuals seeking treatment. MBIs reliably surpass non-evidence-based therapies and active control measures like health education, relaxation techniques, and supportive therapy. MBIs are also comparable to cognitive-behavioural therapy (CBT). The treatment principles of MBIs for anxiety and depression align with those of conventional CBT. Although various extensive meta-analyses have indicated that mindfulness-based interventions may influence clinical results, multiple meta-analyses have explored the findings for particular psychiatric disorders such as attention deficit and hyperactivity disorder. This current analytical study aimed to investigate the following: (1) how mindfulness-based interventions measure against various control conditions, including established efficacious treatments (i.e. evidence-based therapies); (2) which specific disorders show the highest effectiveness of mindfulness-based interventions, and (3) possible sources of bias.

titre: Mindfulness, Weight Loss and Regain in Combat Sports Athletes: Longitudinal Study with Seven Collection Moments and Three-Arm Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial
resume: Title: Brief Body Scan and Somatic Anxiety at Official Weigh-In in Combat Sports Athletes: A Three-Arm Randomized Controlled Trial. Overall Objective: To evaluate the efficacy of a brief Body Scan protocol (10-minute daily mindfulness meditation for 14 consecutive days) in reducing somatic anxiety at the official weigh-in (primary outcome), compared with an active control (sport-technical video) and a passive control (waiting list), in combat sports athletes. Design: Three-arm parallel randomized controlled trial (1:1:1), with concealed allocation and blinded analyst. The study will be conducted in accordance with the CONSORT 2025 guidelines and prospectively registered on ReBEC (UTN: U1111-1347-5079). Participants: Combat sports athletes (Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu, Judo, Wrestling, MMA, Boxing, Muay Thai, Karate, and Taekwondo), of both sexes, aged 18 to 60 years, with regular practice for at least two years and an official competition scheduled within the next 30 to 45 days. Athletes with recent participation in mindfulness programs, use of psychotropic medication, or diagnosed eating disorders will be excluded. Interventions: G1 – Body Scan: 14 consecutive days of guided practice using a standardized 10-minute audio, with one mandatory daily session (preferably before sleep) and a second recommended session after training. In the period between weigh-in and fight (T4–T6), two daily sessions will be mandatory. The first two sessions will be conducted in person; the remaining sessions will be autonomous, with electronic diary recording and in-person check-ins every 3–4 days. G2 – Active Control: Viewing 10-minute sport-technical videos, with the same temporal structure and monitoring as G1 (parallelism in duration, frequency, and contact with the research team), without any mindfulness, relaxation, or technical instruction component. G3 – Passive Control (Waiting List): Maintenance of usual routine, with no intervention, while participating in the same assessments. After follow-up (T7), participants will receive full access to the Body Scan protocol as ethical compensation. Primary Outcome: Somatic anxiety (CSAI-2R subscale) measured immediately after the official weigh-in (T4), analyzed by ANCOVA with intention-to-treat (ITT) and multiple imputation. Secondary and Exploratory Outcomes: Mental and physical fatigue (VAS) at T4 and T6; Somatic anxiety at T6 (pre-fight) and at other time points; State mindfulness (SMS-PA2) across the competitive cycle; Exploratory moderation analyses (trait mindfulness, magnitude of weight loss/regain). Expected Results: It is hypothesized that the Body Scan group will show significantly lower somatic anxiety scores at the official weigh-in compared with both the active and passive control groups, maintaining superiority in the intention-to-treat analysis. It is also expected that the active control will not differ from the waiting list, isolating the specific effect of the mindfulness practice. The results may provide evidence for incorporating brief, low-cost interventions into the competitive preparation of combat sports athletes.

titre: Theories and Variables of Social Media's Impact on Psychological Well-Being: A Systematic Review
resume: This systematic review combines the effects of social media on mental well-being and theory and theory-salient variables dominating. It synthesizes disparate evidence, detects under studied constructs, and guides subsequent research. Uses and Gratifications, Social Comparison, Technostress Theories are the current theories, and Digital Goldilocks Hypothesis and Mindfulness/Self-Regulation are behind. Stress, while identity strain, circadian disruption, and hardness are rarely studied, stress, anxiety, health, and academic performance are regularly. Bridging the gap between theories and variables and proposing concepts like resilience, digital jetlag, and chrono-identity conflict are examples of originality.

titre: Obsessive-compulsive disorder with comorbid social anxiety symptoms is a more severe presentation associated with greater autistic traits
resume: Introduction and aims Recent literature highlighted significant clinical and epidemiological overlap of Obsessive compulsive disorder (OCD) with Social Anxiety Disorder (SAD) and autism spectrum. In this perspective we aimed to evaluate the relationship between autism spectrum, OCD and social anxiety in a sample of patients with OCD with or without significant SAD symptoms. Methods We recruited a total sample of 56 in- or out-patients with a clinical diagnosis of OCD assessing them with the Social Phobic Spectrum – Short Version (SHY-SV), the Obsessive-Compulsive Spectrum – Short Version (OBS-SV) and the Adult Autism Subthreshold Spectrum (AdAS Spectrum) questionnaires. Participants were divided in two groups: OCD and OCD with SAD group. Results OCD+SAD subjects scored significantly higher than OCDs in AdAS Spectrum Restricted interests and Rumination domain as well as in the questionnaire total score and in OBS-SV Repetition and automation domain as well as in its total score. Moreover, AdAS Spectrum total score was a significant positive predictor of the presence of SAD. Finally, AdAS Spectrum Restriced Interest & Rumination and OBS-SV Repetition and automation emerged as significant positive predictors of the presence of SAD. Conclusions Our work highlighted that subjects with OCD and clinical SAD symptoms show a higher global severity of OCD symptoms and a higher presence of autistic traits. On the other hand, SAD presence in OCD subjects seems to be statistically predicted by AdAS Spectrum but not by OBS-SV total score.
revue: Giornale italiano di psicopatologia/Journal of psychopathology/Italian journal of psychopathology

titre: Clinician Competencies and Training Needs for Obsessive-Compulsive and Related Disorders: Survey of Australian Mental Health Clinicians
resume: Objective Despite occurring in 9.5% of the population, obsessive-compulsive and related disorders (OCRDs) are under-diagnosed and under-treated. The current study assessed clinicians’ self-reported competencies in the assessment and treatment of OCRDs, and clinician training needs, against best-practice clinical guidelines. Method Two hundred (N = 200) public mental health clinicians across the state of New South Wales, Australia, were surveyed on their competencies in screening, diagnosing, and treating obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), body dysmorphic disorder, Tourette syndrome, excoriation disorder, hoarding disorder, and trichotillomania. Results Most (64%) clinicians reported currently treating patients with OCRDs, yet 74% self-identified as not competent treating at least one OCRD, particularly for disorders other than OCD. Clinicians reporting screening for OCRDs even some of the time also reported more OCRD patients in their caseload. Practical and systemic constraints within services were common barriers to implementation of evidence-based practice, but clinicians desired more training and supervision. Conclusions There are critical gaps in the readiness of public mental health clinicians to assess and treat OCRDs in line with best-practice guidelines. Targeted investment in workforce development, paired with systemic implementation support, can bridge the gap between evidence and practice to deliver best-practice treatment for OCRDs in public mental health services.

titre: Digital mental health interventions for adolescents and young adults: A systematic review
resume: Abstract Background: Mental health conditions affect a substantial proportion of adolescents and young adults worldwide, with most disorders having their onset before age 25. Despite the availability of evidence-based treatments, significant barriers — including workforce shortages, cost, stigma, and low engagement — prevent most young people from accessing timely care. These challenges are not unique to any single country but represent a global problem: the World Health Organization estimates that 76–85% of people with severe mental health disorders in low- and middle-income countries receive no treatment, and even in high-income settings the treatment gap remains substantial. Digital mental health interventions (DMHIs) have been proposed as a practical means of broadening access, but previous reviews have predominantly focused on adult populations or restricted their scope to one or two conditions. Objective: To systematically review available evidence for efficacy of DMHIs in young adults aged 16–30 years, examining five common mental health conditions — depressive disorders, anxiety disorders, obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), and eating disorders — with the understanding that the absence of evidence for any condition is itself a finding of clinical relevance. Methods: A systematic review was conducted following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. This review was prospectively registered with PROSPERO (CRD42024514627). Five databases (PubMed, ProQuest APA PsychInfo, Scopus, Cochrane CENTRAL, and clinical trial registries) were searched with no date restrictions, supplemented by grey literature and snowballing searches. Eligible studies were randomised controlled trials evaluating a digital intervention delivered to participants aged 16–30 years with a diagnosed or clinically significant mental health condition, using validated outcome measures. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool. Results were synthesised narratively given the clinical and methodological heterogeneity across included studies. Results: A total of 5,654 records were identified across all databases and grey literature searches. After removing 354 duplicates and 170 records for other reasons, 5,130 records were screened. Following title and abstract screening, 251 reports were sought for retrieval, of which 189 were assessed for full-text eligibility. Thirteen studies (12 RCTs and one open trial) met inclusion criteria, covering depression (8 studies), anxiety disorders (4 studies), and eating disorders (1 study). No eligible studies were identified for OCD or PTSD within this age group. Effect sizes 2 ranged from small to moderate for depression and anxiety interventions (Cohen's d 0.33–0.85). High attrition rates were a consistent concern across included studies. Conclusions: DMHIs show efficacy for depression and anxiety in young people aged 16–30 years, with small-to-moderate effect sizes across a range of digital platforms. Evidence for eating disorders is limited to a single study in this review. The absence of eligible trials for OCD and PTSD in this age group represents a meaningful gap in the evidence base and should be a priority for future research. The study has few critical limitations specially in determining the age group, including uptodate studies and including local studies which became available in later phase of this review. as seasching was done in 2023. High attrition remains a practical challenge for real-world implementation. Future work should target upcoming LLM chat bots, under�studied conditions, longer follow-up periods, and implementation in diverse, real-world settings, including those relevant to the New Zealand context. Keywords: digital mental health interventions; adolescents; young adults; systematic review; depression; anxiety; OCD; PTSD; eating disorders; mHealth; chatbot; iCBT

titre: OC Tendencies in the Workplace: How Do Obsessive-Compulsive Tendencies Impact Workplace Task Efficiency?
resume: This study examines the relationship between obsessive-compulsive (OC) tendencies and efficiency when completing common, everyday workplace tasks. Previous research has identified relationships between OC symptoms and workplace functioning; however, much of this research has relied on self-reported measures of job performance or occupational difficulties. The present study aims to address this limitation by directly measuring participants’ performance on simulated workplace tasks, with task-completion time serving as the primary measure of efficiency. Participants will complete four simulated workplace tasks: proofreading and editing an email, prioritizing a to-do list, completing a mock data-entry task, and organizing workplace documents. These tasks are intended to represent common activities that may be encountered in office or workplace settings and relate to different OC tendencies, including checking, ordering, obsessing, hoarding, washing/contamination concerns, and mental neutralizing. The amount of time required to complete each task will be recorded as an objective measure of task efficiency. Following the workplace tasks, participants will complete the Obsessive-Compulsive Inventory–Revised (OCI-R), an 18-item self-report measure assessing six dimensions of OC tendencies: washing, checking, ordering, obsessing, hoarding, and mental neutralizing. OCI-R scores will be treated as a continuous measure of OC tendencies and will not be used to diagnose obsessive-compulsive disorder. The primary purpose of this study is to determine whether the intensity of OC tendencies is associated with differences in workplace task efficiency. We predict that higher OCI-R scores will be associated with longer task-completion times. Specifically, tendencies such as repeated checking, ordering, or feeling the need to complete a task in a particular way may increase the amount of time individuals spend completing routine workplace activities. By using objectively measured task-completion time rather than relying solely on perceived or self-reported workplace performance, this study aims to provide a better understanding of how the intensity of OC tendencies may relate to observable differences in the efficient completion of everyday workplace tasks.

titre: Nutritional Management of the Irritable Bowel Syndrome(IBS): The Role of the Mediterranean Diet (MD)
resume: Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) is a common gastrointestinal disorder with a significant impact on the quality of life of patients. Its global prevalence varies considerably, estimated at up to 10%, due to differences in diagnostic criteria, cultural factors and dietary patterns. Dietary interventions have emerged as first-line strategies for symptom management, with the low Fermentable Oligo-, Di-, and Monosaccharides and Polyols (FODMAP) diet demonstrating strong efficacy in reducing gastrointestinal symptoms by minimizing poorly absorbed, fermentable carbohydrates. However, concerns about long-term nutritional adequacy, potential alterations in gut microbiota composition, and sustainability of the low-FODMAP diet have led to the need for more comprehensive and nutritionally balanced dietary models. In contrast, the Mediterranean Diet (MD), is widely recognized for its anti-inflammatory, cardiometabolic, and potential anticancer effects. Notably, adherence to the MD has been associated with favorable gut microbial profiles and a reduced risk of colorectal and other gastrointestinal cancers. However, the high FODMAP content of many components of the MD may limit its direct compatibility with dietary protocols for IBS. Incorporating the principles of the MD into a low-FODMAP dietary approach offers a promising strategy for enhancing the nutritional quality, sustainability, and long-term effectiveness of dietary management in IBS. The aim of the study is to investigate and compare the effectiveness of a Mediterranean Modified Low FODMAP diet (Med-Mod LFD) with standard Mediterranean dietary recommendations (Med standard) in managing the symptoms of IBS. Specifically, the study aims to evaluate the impact of the two dietary interventions on the frequency and severity of gastrointestinal symptoms, to examine potential differences in quality of life, to assess patient compliance and acceptance of the two dietary approaches, and to explore whether the Med-Mod Low FODMAP variation of the Mediterranean diet offers advantages over the classical Mediterranean diet without compromising the health-promoting characteristics that make it beneficial.Dietary intake will also be assessed using a three-day food diary, which will be used for the dietary analysis of participants' food intake and for the assessment of macro- and micronutrient intake of the two dietary interventions

titre: Randomized Controlled Clinical Study on Acupuncture Combined With Transcutaneous Electrical Acupoint Stimulation for Constipation-Predominant Irritable Bowel Syndrome With Anxiety State
resume: Study Title: Randomized Controlled Clinical Study on Acupuncture Combined with Transcutaneous Electrical Acupoint Stimulation for Constipation-Predominant Irritable Bowel Syndrome with Anxiety State. This single-center, randomized, single-blinded sham-controlled trial enrolls adults aged 18-70 with constipation-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-C) and anxiety. All participants receive standardized weekly acupuncture for 4 weeks. Participants are randomly assigned 1:1 to either real daily home Transcutaneous Electrical Acupoint Stimulation(TEAS)at Zusanli acupoint or sham non-acupoint TEAS. The total study period lasts approximately 10 weeks, including 2-week screening, 4-week intervention and 4-week post-treatment follow-up. The primary outcome is weekly complete spontaneous bowel movements (CSBM) at week 4. Secondary outcomes cover anxiety, sleep quality, abdominal symptoms, quality of life and safety. Researchers will test whether adding real home-based TEAS to acupuncture improves bowel and emotional symptoms, and evaluate treatment safety and tolerability.

titre: T1 Colorectal Cancer After Local Excision: Decision Between Surgery and Active Surveillance (T1LDA Trial)
resume: The goal of this two-arm clinical trial is to compare additional surgery with active surveillance in patients with high-risk pT1 colorectal cancer after local excision. The main questions it aims to answer are Does additional surgery result in lower rates of distant or extraluminal recurrence compared with active surveillance? How do the two treatment strategies differ in survival, complications, quality of life, and treatment-related costs? Participants will be randomly assigned to either additional surgery or active surveillance. Patients assigned to the surgery group will undergo standard preoperative assessment followed by additional surgery. Following surgery, patients will undergo surveillance according to the predefined follow-up protocol. Patients assigned to the active surveillance group will not receive any additional treatment. They will undergo surveillance according to a more intensive predefined follow-up protocol.

titre: ECO-CHIP: Cost-utility Evaluation of Cytoreductive Surgery Combined With Mitomycin-C Hyperthermic Intra-Peritoneal Chemotherapy (HIPEC) Versus Cytoreductive Surgery Alone in the Treatment of Resectable Colorectal Peritoneal Metastases. A National, Multicenter, Prospective, Comparative, Non-randomized, Non-interventional Study
resume: Colorectal cancer is the second leading cause of cancer death in France, with close to 50,000 new cases each year. About half of the patients develop liver, lung and/or peritoneal metastases during the course of the disease.Peritoneal involvement, which accounts for approximately 8,000 new cases per year, carries the poorest prognosis, notably because of its chemoresistance.For patients with resectable colorectal peritoneal metastases,recommended optimal management combines systemic chemotherapy with complete cytoreductive surgery(CRS)in an expert center.Hyperthermic IntraPeritoneal Chemotherapy(HIPEC)may be added to CRS to eradicate residual microscopic disease and potentially improve survival.Clinical evidence on HIPEC for colorectal peritoneal carcinomatosis is heterogeneous and dominated by a randomized trial reporting no survival benefit and increased morbidity, results attributed to the oxaliplatin-based HIPEC regimen used. A separate body of evidence suggests a benefit of mitomycin-C-based HIPEC, with manageable morbidity and preserved quality of life. National and international guidelines therefore allow mitomycin-C HIPEC, but the procedure remains controversial: according to French hospital discharge data, about half of the patients treated for colorectal peritoneal carcinomatosis receive CRS plus HIPEC and the other half CRS alone.HIPEC also raises funding and efficiency issues. No specific French diagnosis-related tariff (GHS)exists for CRS plus HIPEC, whereas the procedure is costly in terms of operating time,human and material resources, and is associated with prolonged hospital stays and complications. To date, no prospective comparative data on the efficiency of CRS plus HIPEC are available in France.ECO-CHIP is a national,multicenter, prospective, comparative,non-randomized, open, non-interventional study using a " here-elsewhere " design (French RIPH category 3). Each participating center follows its own routine practice: centers performing HIPEC treat included patients with CRS plus mitomycin-C HIPEC (innovative strategy), while centers not performing HIPEC treat included patients with CRS alone (reference strategy).No change in management, examination or procedure is imposed by the protocol.the only procedure added because of the research is the completion of self-administered questionnaires (EQ-5D-5L, EORTC QLQ-C30, EORTC QLQ-CR29 and PERI-PROM) at inclusion and at months 1, 3, 6, 12, 18, 24 and 36 after cytoreductive surgery. The primary objective is to assess, from the French health care system perspective and over a 36-month horizon, the efficiency (cost-utility) of cytoreductive surgery combined with mitomycin-C HIPEC versus cytoreductive surgery alone. Costs are derived from micro-costing of the index hospital stay and from individual linkage with the French National Health Data System(SNDS); utilities are derived from the EQ-5D-5L using the French value set. Secondary objectives compare the two strategies in terms of disease-free survival, peritoneal recurrence-free survival, overall survival, toxicity, postoperative complications, recurrence patterns, access to iterative complete cytoreduction, costs, budget impact for the French statutory health insurance, cost-effectiveness at 3 and 5 years, and health-related quality of life. Study hypothesis: the addition of mitomycin-C HIPEC to complete cytoreductive surgery is an efficient strategy for the French health care system, improving disease-free survival (expected 3-year disease-free survival of 26% with CRS plus HIPEC versus 13% with CRS alone, hazard ratio 0.66) and quality-adjusted survival at an acceptable incremental cost per QALY gained. perspective and over a 36-month horizon, the efficiency (cost-utility) of cytoreductive surgery combined with mitomycin-C HIPEC versus cytoreductive surgery alone. titre: Can Prebiotics Support Microbial Metabolic Function Following Low-FODMAP Restriction in Irritable Bowel Syndrome?
resume: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is one of the most common disorders of gut-brain interaction, and dietary interventions play a central role in symptom management. Among these, the low-fermentable oligosaccharides, disaccharides, monosaccharides, and polyols (low-FODMAP) diet has been shown to improve abdominal pain, bloating, and altered bowel habits in a substantial proportion of patients. However, restriction of fermentable carbohydrates may reduce the availability of substrates for the gut microbiota and has been associated with reductions in selected microbial taxa, including Bifidobacterium, raising questions about its effects on microbial ecology and metabolism. Dietary prebiotics selectively stimulate gut microorganisms and promote microbial fermentation and the production of metabolites, including short-chain fatty acids, that may contribute to intestinal homeostasis. However, many prebiotics are also highly fermentable substrates, and their gastrointestinal effects may vary substantially among individuals with IBS. This creates a challenge in balancing symptom control with continued exposure to substrates that may support microbial and metabolic functions. In this narrative review, we critically examine the metabolic and clinical implications of dietary prebiotics in IBS, with particular emphasis on their potential role following low-FODMAP restriction. We discuss their effects on gut microbiota composition and function, microbial metabolites, and clinically relevant outcomes, with particular attention to the relationship between microbial and symptomatic responses. We further consider the potential role of structured reintroduction and personalization of tolerated fermentable substrates in maintaining dietary variety and microbial substrate availability while minimizing gastrointestinal symptoms. Finally, we discuss interindividual variability in responses to fermentable substrates and factors that may contribute to differential responses, highlighting current limitations in linking microbiota composition, microbial function, metabolite production, and clinical outcomes in IBS, and identifying possible directions for future research.

titre: Design, Characterization and In Vivo Evaluation of Rifaximin-Loaded Chitosan Nanoparticles for Potential Colonic Drug Delivery in Irritable Bowel Syndrome
resume: This study aimed to develop rifaximin (RFX) loaded chitosan (CS)-tripolyphosphate (TPP) nanoparticles for potential colonic delivery as a drug delivery system for the management of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS). Nanoparticles were prepared using the ionotropic gelation method and optimized by varying stirring speed, TPP concentration, and polymer-to-drug ratio. The optimized formulation (F41) exhibited a particle size of 262.4 ± 24.3 nm, a polydispersity index (PDI) of 0.389 ± 0.033, a zeta potential of + 9.91 ± 0.94 mV, and an encapsulation efficiency (EE%) of 94.75 ± 0.04%. In vitro release studies demonstrated nearly complete drug release within 36 h, which was faster compared to other formulations (52-64 h). Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) confirmed spherical morphology, while differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR) analyses indicated successful drug encapsulation without chemical interaction. In vivo evaluation using a chronic restraint stress (CRS) induced IBS model showed that F41 significantly improved physiological parameters, including reduced fecal water content (20.655 ± 23.494%), increased body weight gain (22.716 ± 3.903%), and a decreased disease activity index (p < 0.05). These findings indicate that, the optimized nanoparticle system demonstrated favorable physicochemical properties, sustained drug release, and improved therapeutic outcomes. Owing to the cationic nature of CS, the system may also provide enhanced interaction with colonic mucus, potentially contributing to prolonged local residence. These findings suggest that the developed formulation represents promising approach for potential colonic delivery of RFX in IBS management; however, further studies are required to directly evaluate its mucoadhesive properties and underlying mechanisms.

titre: Limited efficacy of faecal microbiota transplantation in IBS
Current status and trends of gut microbiota in the study of cognitive impairment in the elderly
resume: BACKGROUND: Cognitive impairment in older persons has become a major public health concern as the world's population ages more quickly. A reduction in thinking, learning, and memory skills that affects a person's day-to-day activities or social functioning is referred to as cognitive impairment. The connection between gut microbiota and cognitive decline has attracted a lot of interest lately. However, this rapidly expanding interdisciplinary field presents an increasingly complex knowledge structure, with existing evidence being highly fragmented and subject to significant methodological and sample size limitations.
