After LASSO-based feature selection, four prespecified base learners-explainable boosting machine, calibrated support vector machine, random forest, and CatBoost-were combined using an L2-penalized logistic regression stacking meta-learner. Performance was assessed using discrimination, threshold-dependent metrics, calibration, decision curve analysis, learner diversity, and SHAP-based interpretability. RESULTS: Among 629 eligible patients, 210 (33.4%) had comorbid anxiety disorder. The training cohort included 440 patients, and the validation cohort included 189 patients, with similar anxiety prevalence in both cohorts. Clinically relevant correlates of anxiety included older age, longer symptom duration, higher pain frequency, night-time awakening, pain temporally associated with stressful events, higher SDSC and CSI-24 scores, higher parental GAD-7 score, and greater school absence. In out-of-fold training estimates, the stacking model achieved an AUC of 0.831 and a Brier score of 0.151. In the validation cohort, it showed the highest numerical performance among candidate models, with an AUC of 0.846 (95% CI, 0.789-0.894), accuracy of 0.788, sensitivity of 0.762, specificity of 0.802, F1 score of 0.706, and Brier score of 0.146. Decision curve analysis suggested potential clinical utility across selected threshold ranges. SHAP analysis identified school absence, parental GAD-7 score, CSI-24 score, pain-stress association, symptom duration, pain frequency, SDSC score, age, and night-time awakening as leading contributors to the final model output. CONCLUSION: A stacking machine learning model integrating clinical, psychosocial, school-related, and family-level variables showed acceptable internal-validation performance for identifying comorbid anxiety disorder in children and adolescents with functional abdominal pain disorders. External validation is needed before clinical implementation.

titre: Residue Gln370 of Newcastle disease virus nucleoprotein mediate viral inclusion body-like structure formation via interaction with residue Ser254 of viral phosphoprotein
resume: BACKGROUND: Newcastle disease virus (NDV) infects more than 250 avian species and mammals. Cytoplasmic inclusion bodies (IBs) are a hallmark of paramyxovirus infection; however, the molecular mechanisms underlying NDV IB formation remain poorly understood. METHODS: In this study, we investigated the interactive sites of viral protein driving IB-like structure formation via transmission electron microscopy, immunofluorescence assays (IFA), viral titration, co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP), structural modeling analysis. RESULTS: Both virulent and attenuated NDV strains induced IBs in chicken-, mouse-, and human-derived cells. And the virus replicated well in CEF and HeLa cells rather than MEF. Time-course analysis revealed that IBs emerged as small puncta early in infection, increased in size over time, and ultimately accumulated in the perinuclear region. Co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP) and IFA revealed that amino acid residues 367-375 of the nucleoprotein (NP) bound to the PMD of the phosphoprotein (P), and this interaction was required for IB-like structure assembly. Furthermore, structural modeling and experiments of the NP-P complex identified residues Gln370 of NP and residue Ser254 of P as the principal contact and interacting sites for IB-like structure assembly. DISCUSSION: These findings reveal a previously unrecognized NP-P binding interface that mediates NDV IB formation, providing new insights into the molecular basis of viral condensate biogenesis in paramyxoviruses and a potential target for antiviral intervention.
revue: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

titre: Irritable bowel syndrome in the community: a cross-sectional study looking at patient experiences and challenges with the low FODMAP diet
resume: While a diet low in fermentable oligosaccharides, disaccharides, monosaccharides and polyols (FODMAP) is the most evidence-based dietary therapy for irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), data on patient experiences with the low FODMAP diet (LFD) remains sparse. Even less information exists examining patients' experiences with the re-introduction and personalization phases of LFD, especially in the community setting. This cross-sectional study surveyed 387 participants from the mailing list of the International Foundation for Functional Gastrointestinal Disorders (IFFGD) about their experiences with LFD. Additionally, focus groups collected qualitative data about participants' experiences with the LFD diet. Despite 70% of participants reporting perceived improvement of symptoms with FODMAP restriction, 70% of participants reported that LFD was either somewhat or extremely difficult to follow and 59% of participants reported continuing the restriction phase beyond 8 weeks. 41% of participants found the re-introduction phase somewhat or extremely difficult and two-thirds took >1 month to complete it. Only 30% and 25% of participants worked with a dietitian for restriction and re-introduction phases, with many receiving their information online or via app. Finally, over 80% of participants reported they would be interested in a simplified version of the LFD. While the LFD led to perceived symptom improvement in most IBS patients, it is associated with limitations, including its complexity and restrictiveness. Furthermore, food-related fear and anxiety, particularly during restriction and reintroduction phases, pose significant challenges. These findings underscore the practical limitations LFD has, and participants expressed a strong interest in a simpler, more convenient alternative.

titre: Trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO) in heat stroke: molecular mechanisms from gut dysbiosis to multi-organ injury
resume: Heat stroke, a life-threatening condition characterized by core hyperthermia (≥40 °C), central nervous system dysfunction, and multi-organ failure with mortality rates of 20-70%, is increasingly recognized as a systemic inflammatory and hemodynamic disorder rather than a purely thermoregulatory collapse. Among the emerging mediators of its pathophysiology, trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO)-a gut microbiota-derived metabolite generated from dietary choline, L-carnitine, and betaine-has attracted growing attention as a molecular link between heat-induced gut dysbiosis and multi-organ injury. This review synthesizes current evidence on the physiological and molecular mechanisms whereby TMAO is proposed to aggravate heat stroke pathology, including: (1) NLRP3 inflammasome activation via ROS-TXNIP, SIRT3-SOD2-mtROS, and cathepsin B-mediated pathways; (2) endothelial dysfunction through tight junction disruption, eNOS/NO suppression, and ALDH2/ROS/GSDMD-dependent pyroptosis; (3) platelet hyperreactivity and thrombosis through enhanced Ca2+ mobilization and IP3 signaling; (4) mitochondrial oxidative stress and bioenergetic failure; and (5) neuroinflammation via the gut-brain axis. We further discuss the concentration-dependent duality of TMAO as a chemical chaperone versus a pathological mediator, and evaluate translational strategies targeting TMAO metabolism, including gut microbiota modulation, TMA lyase inhibition, and NLRP3 blockade. Importantly, the majority of the mechanistic evidence synthesized herein derives from disease models other than heat stroke (e.g., atherosclerosis, chronic kidney disease, obesity, aging, preeclampsia, and ischemic stroke); direct evidence obtained in heat-stroke settings remains limited, and several proposed pathways should be regarded as hypotheses awaiting heat-stroke-specific validation. Elucidating TMAO-dependent mechanisms may therefore inform future biomarker development and therapeutic investigation-both of which require clinical validation in heat-stroke patients-in this increasingly prevalent climate-sensitive disease.

titre: Microbial metabolites as modulators of gut-brain communication in neurodegeneration: from intestinal sensing to disease initiation and progression
resume: How heterogeneous gut metabolite alterations relate to Parkinson's disease (PD) and Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains unresolved. We propose a framework in which intestinal sensing of indole derivatives, short-chain fatty acids and bile acids links microbial function to barrier regulation and gut-brain communication. Integration denotes tissue-level convergence of aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR), pregnane X receptor (PXR) and metabolite-responsive G-protein-coupled receptor responses across epithelial and neighbouring immune cells, rather than an established same-cell receptor complex. Tryptophan metabolism provides an analytical focus connecting microbial indole production with host kynurenine and serotonin pathways; metabolite concentrations alone do not establish pathway flux or receptor activity. We hypothesise that suppressed indole-associated epithelial signalling, barrier hyperpermeability and peripheral immune activation could form a shared gut-derived vulnerability state in subsets of PD and AD. Its co-occurrence and temporal relationship to CNS pathology have not been prospectively demonstrated. Neural, immune and vascular processes may overlap in both diseases, with genotype and cellular context modifying relative susceptibility rather than determining exclusive pathways. Human observational findings are distinguished from experimental mechanisms and proposed interactions. Receptor-directed treatments and metabolite-based biomarkers remain candidates requiring mechanism-specific, safety and clinical validation. Whether a gut-derived intervention window exists, is reversible, or favours earlier treatment requires longitudinal and controlled studies. The framework accommodates bidirectional communication and CNS-intrinsic disease, and generates separate tests of composite gut phenotyping and genotype-metabolite interactions.

titre: Correction: Aging, the microbiota-gut-brain axis, and late-life epilepsy: a hypothesis-driven review

titre: Reprogramming the gut-brain axis in neurodegeneration: comparative microbiome, metabolite, immunometabolic, polyphenol, probiotic, and epigenetic mechanisms in Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases
resume: The gut-brain axis has emerged as a central mechanistic framework linking dietary bioactives, microbial ecology, and neurodegenerative disease progression. Similar microbiome-related mechanisms have also been implicated in colorectal cancer, suggesting potential shared links between microbial dysbiosis, inflammation, and disease progression. This study synthesizes preclinical evidence examining how polyphenols, polyphenol-derived compounds, and advanced delivery systems, including nanoparticles and synbiotics, modulate Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD) through microbiome-dependent mechanisms. Evidence from transgenic mice, toxin-induced rodent models, and Drosophila systems was compared across microbiome alterations, microbial metabolites, signaling pathways, epigenetic regulation, and functional outcomes. Across AD and PD models, dietary bioactives consistently promoted restoration of gut microbial homeostasis, characterized by enrichment of beneficial taxa and reduction of dysbiosis-associated microorganisms. These changes were accompanied by alterations in microbial metabolites, particularly short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), tryptophan-derived metabolites, and lipid-associated signaling molecules. These metabolites provide functional links between microbial ecology and CNS physiology and may regulate epigenetic processes, including histone acetylation, DNA methylation, chromatin remodeling, and non-coding RNA activity. Despite substantial upstream convergence, downstream effects showed disease-specific patterns. In AD models, microbiome modulation predominantly influenced metabolic, amyloidogenic, and neurotrophic pathways, including AKT/GSK3β, NRF2, NF-κB, and BDNF-associated signaling, contributing to reduced amyloid-β deposition, attenuated tau pathology, and improved cognitive outcomes. In PD models, greater emphasis was placed on inflammatory, oxidative, and mitochondrial pathways involving SIRT1/NRF2, TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB, inflammasome signaling, and neuronal survival mechanisms, resulting in reduced neuroinflammation and preservation of dopaminergic neurons and motor function. Epigenetic regulation represents an additional convergence layer through which microbial metabolites and polyphenols may influence inflammatory, metabolic, mitochondrial, and neuronal gene programs in both disorders. Nanoparticle-based delivery systems enhanced bioavailability, tissue targeting, and microbiome-related effects, whereas synbiotic strategies reinforced microbial and metabolic homeostasis. Collectively, these findings support a microbiome-metabolite-epigenome-brain framework in which dietary bioactives modulate neurodegeneration through interconnected microbial, metabolic, immune, redox, mitochondrial, and epigenetic pathways. This framework provides a mechanistic basis for developing disease-tailored and precision-oriented gut-brain interventions for AD and PD.

titre: Dietary fiber, gut microbiota, and host immunity: the immunomodulatory roles of short-chain fatty acids
resume: Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) are a class of key metabolites produced by the gut microbiota through the fermentation of indigestible components such as dietary fiber. They primarily include acetate, propionate, and butyrate. In recent years, a large body of research has revealed that SCFAs are not only an important energy source for colonic epithelial cells but also key signaling molecules linking the gut microbiota to the host immune system. SCFAs play a central role in immune regulation. This review summarizes the production and characteristics of SCFAs. It explores the multifaceted roles of SCFAs in regulating immune homeostasis and inflammatory responses. Through key mechanisms such as activation of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), inhibition of histone deacetylases (HDACs), and metabolic reprogramming, SCFAs broadly regulate the differentiation, function, and inflammatory responses of immune cells, maintain intestinal barrier integrity, and induce an anti-inflammatory state. At the same time, the manuscript analyzes the molecular mechanisms by which SCFAs contribute to inflammatory bowel disease, metabolic disorders, tumor immunity, and neuro-immune diseases through multi-organ pathways such as the "gut-liver axis" and the "gut-brain axis". In addition, this article summarizes treatment strategies targeting SCFAs, including dietary interventions, probiotics, prebiotics, and fecal microbiota transplantation. It also discusses the current challenges in this field and outlines future directions, with the aim of providing new insights for the prevention and treatment of immune-related diseases.

titre: Faecalibacterium prausnitzii in neurological disorders: mechanistic links and therapeutic potential along the microbiota-gut-brain axis
resume: Widespread dysbiosis in neurological disorders highlights the critical role of the microbiota-gut-brain axis (MGBA) and the therapeutic potential of probiotics in modulating the central nervous system (CNS). Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, a key butyrate-producing commensal bacterium in the human gut, has attracted broad attention as a candidate next-generation probiotic (NGP). This review aims to describe and discuss the mechanisms of action of F. prausnitzii and its potential in the prevention and management of neurological disorders. Multiple human observational cohort studies indicate that the relative abundance of F. prausnitzii-or the genus Faecalibacterium-is negatively correlated with disease severity in conditions such as Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), stroke, and multiple sclerosis (MS); however, the directionality of this association remains discordant in neurodevelopmental conditions such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD). To date, interventional evidence is predominantly derived from rodent models, in which oral gavage of specific F. prausnitzii strains or synbiotic formulations has been reported to alleviate cognitive deficits, motor dysfunction, anxiety-like behaviors, and pathological protein deposition. Mechanistically, these neuroprotective effects involve diverse F. prausnitzii-derived neuroactive metabolites-including the microbial anti-inflammatory molecule (MAM), extracellular vesicles (EVs), and phenolic derivatives-as well as indirect pathways mediated by butyrate through histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibition and intestinal barrier fortification. Given the current lack of clinical intervention trials directly administering live F. prausnitzii in human neurological populations, future research requires rigorously designed, strain-specific randomized controlled trials (RCTs) to establish its clinical safety, colonization efficiency, and therapeutic efficacy.

titre: Editorial: Decoding the gut-brain axis: implications for neurodegenerative disease therapies
Clinical characteristics and outcome of CLL/SLL patients with renal involvement in the era of targeted drugs
resume: BACKGROUND: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL)/small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL) is a clonal mature B-cell neoplasm with rare extranodal organ renal involvement. OBJECTIVES: To summarize the clinical and pathological characteristics of biopsy-confirmed CLL/SLL-associated renal lesions and evaluate the efficacy of targeted combination therapy. DESIGN: Retrospective multicenter observational study. METHODS: Eleven patients with CLL/SLL-associated nephropathy were enrolled from January 2017 to October 2024 across three Chinese centers. As of December 31, 2025, data were collected through electronic medical records and telephone follow-up. RESULTS: The median age was 58 (range 40-72) years. Among tested patients, 88.9% (8/9) exhibited IGHV mutation and 62.5% (5/8) were CLL-IPI low-risk, and no TP53 mutations were detected. The median time from CLL diagnosis to renal biopsy was 40.7 months (range: 0.2-58 months). Biopsy indictions included proteinuria (90.9%, 10/11), hematuria (54.5%, 6/11), renal dysfunction (54.5%, 6/11), and nephrotic syndrome (9.1%, 1/11). Main pathologies were tumor cell interstitial infiltration (45.5%, 5/11), membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis (27.3%, 3/11), membranous nephropathy (18.2%, 2/11), and C3 glomerulonephritis (9.1%, 1/11). Concomitant monoclonal gammopathy and cryoglobulinemia were observed in 27.3% and 18.2%, respectively. Nine patients received BTKi -based therapy. The best overall response rate (ORR) for CLL/SLL was 100%, with a CR rate of 72.7%. According to KDIGO 2021 guidelines, the renal best ORR was 100%, with a CR rate of 36.4%. Four patients achieved CR in both CLL and renal assessments. As of December 31, 2025, the median follow-up was 70.1 months and median PFS was not reached. Grade ≥3 hematologic toxicities included neutropenia (27.3%) and thrombocytopenia (18.2%). Common non-hematologic adverse events were COVID-19 (27.3%), bleeding (18.2%), and gastrointestinal symptoms (18.2%), all of grade 1-2. CONCLUSIONS: CLL/SLL with renal involvement is associated with a favorable IGHV-mutated profile. Interstitial infiltration and membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis are the predominant renal pathologies. BTKi-based regimens were associated with favorable hematologic and renal outcomes in this small cohort.

titre: Nutrition and Depression: A Narrative Review of Biological Mechanisms and Evidence from Observational Studies and Clinical Trials
resume: Depression is one of the most prevalent and disabling psychiatric disorders worldwide and has a heterogeneous pathophysiology involving interacting neurobiological, neuroimmune, and metabolic processes. Alterations in neurotransmission, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, gut-brain communication, hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis dysregulation, and immunometabolic homeostasis may provide biological links between nutrition and depression. This narrative review examines current evidence linking nutrition and depression across mechanistic, observational, and clinical levels. Regarding dietary patterns, observational evidence generally associates greater adherence to the Mediterranean diet with more favorable depression-related outcomes, while evidence for the DASH diet remains more limited. In contrast, Western dietary patterns and greater consumption of ultra-processed foods are associated with higher risks of depression-related outcomes. Individual nutrients, including omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids, vitamin D, vitamin C, folate, vitamin B12, vitamin B6, and essential minerals, have also been investigated in relation to depression, but findings from supplementation studies vary across nutrients, study populations, and baseline nutritional status. However, much of the evidence linking nutritional factors with depression is observational and does not establish causality. Clinical trials of nutrient supplementation and dietary interventions have reported potential benefits in some populations, but findings remain heterogeneous, and large prevention trials have also reported null results. Differences in baseline nutritional status, depression phenotype, and metabolic and inflammatory profiles may partly contribute to this heterogeneity. Future well-designed clinical trials, together with advances in multi-omics and precision approaches, may help identify individuals most likely to benefit from targeted nutritional strategies.

titre: Exercise Training in Patients with Established Cancer Cachexia: A Case Series
resume: Background/Objectives: Exercise is a supportive strategy for patients with cancer; however, evidence in individuals with established cancer cachexia remains limited. This study aimed to provide a preliminary description of feasibility and exploratory changes during a supervised exercise program in patients with cancer cachexia. Methods: Five women diagnosed with gastrointestinal or breast cancer and meeting the diagnostic criteria for cancer cachexia participated in a 12-week supervised exercise program, combining aerobic with resistance training, conducted twice weekly. Feasibility outcomes included completion, attendance, adherence, and adverse events. Muscle strength, flexibility, body composition, functional capacity, and patient-reported outcomes were assessed at baseline and post-intervention. Results: All participants completed the intervention and post-intervention assessments. Attendance ranged from 54% to 96%, with interruptions primarily related to treatment schedules and treatment-related side effects. No serious exercise-related adverse events occurred. Functional capacity improved in all participants (+ 33 to +73 m). Grip strength increased in all patients for the right hand (+0.5 to +5.5 kg) and in three patients for the left hand (+2.0 to +3.5 kg). Body composition responses were heterogeneous: fat-free mass increased in three patients (+1.3 to +2.8 kg), whereas two patients showed reductions. Fat mass decreased in three patients (-2.6 to -5.0 kg) and increased in two. Several domains of quality of life and symptom burden improved in most participants. Conclusions: In these five women with cancer cachexia, a supervised exercise program showed variable attendance and no serious exercise-related adverse events, whereas favorable changes for functional outcomes and heterogeneous response in body composition were observed.

titre: From single pathways to holistic networks: unraveling the multimechanistic actions of acupuncture in depression
resume: Depression is a globally prevalent mental disorder; however, current pharmacological treatments are limited by a delayed onset of action and significant adverse effects. As a safe and effective non-pharmacological therapy, acupuncture demonstrates unique advantages in treating mild to moderate depression. Its antidepressant mechanisms are multifaceted. Primarily, acupuncture mitigates neuroinflammation by inhibiting classical signaling pathways (e.g., nuclear factor kappa B/NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain containing 3), modulating microglial polarization, and restoring cytokine homeostasis. Furthermore, it enhances neuroplasticity by upregulating brain-derived neurotrophic factor expression, improving synaptic plasticity, and promoting adult neurogenesis. At the cellular level, acupuncture exerts neuroprotective effects by suppressing apoptotic cascades associated with mitochondrial dysfunction and endoplasmic reticulum stress, regulating autophagic balance, and restoring neuronal excitability. Systemically, it ameliorates metabolic dysregulation by optimizing cerebral energy metabolism, modulating gut microbiota composition, and reinforcing intestinal barrier integrity. Additionally, acupuncture effectively alleviates comorbid pain by modulating peripheral nociceptive signaling and central pain-emotion feedback loops. These synergistic effects across multiple systems and targets may together ameliorate the pathophysiological alterations associated with depression. Despite these advances, current research faces challenges, including the translational gap between animal models and clinical pathology, as well as an insufficient investigation of multi-mechanism interactions. Future efforts should focus on developing clinically relevant models, integrating multi-omics technologies, conducting high-quality clinical trials, and exploring biomarker-guided personalized treatments to advance the scientific and standardized application of acupuncture for depression.

titre: Perioperative individualized nursing for an adolescent with recurrent tracheoesophageal fistula after endoscopic repair: a case report
resume: BACKGROUND: Congenital esophageal atresia (CEA) type III is a common neonatal digestive malformation, and recurrent tracheoesophageal fistula (rTEF) is a refractory long-term postoperative complication. Combined suspension laryngoscopy and flexible bronchoscopy minimally invasive fistula repair is a novel therapeutic strategy, yet standardized perioperative nursing experience targeting adolescents with multiple failed transthoracic surgeries remains scarce. Conventional nursing cannot simultaneously manage compound risks including severe malnutrition, tracheomalacia, adolescent anxiety and airway edema. This case report aimed to summarize multidisciplinary team (MDT) individualized full-cycle nursing protocols for this rare patient population. CASE PRESENTATION: A 17.5-year-old male patient with rTEF, 17.5 years after neonatal primary congenital esophageal atresia repair, with two failed transthoracic fistula closures, presented persistent feeding choking, recurrent pneumonia and severe malnutrition (BMI=15.5 kg/m2). MDT refined airway management, quantitative staged nutrition, whole-course psychological intervention and predictive complication prevention were implemented before and after endoscopic fistula repair. No severe complications occurred during hospitalization. Esophagography and bronchoscopy on postoperative day 10 confirmed complete fistula healing. The patient was discharged on postoperative day 14 with a 0.8 kg weight gain, and one-month follow-up showed sustained fistula repair and continuous weight improvement. CONCLUSION: MDT-driven individualized perioperative nursing effectively reduces airway and nutritional complications and promotes fistula healing in adolescent rTEF patients receiving endoscopic minimally invasive surgery. This case provides replicable evidence-based nursing references for similar complex rare esophageal malformation cases.

titre: Neuroscience-informed psychoeducation for anorexia nervosa
resume: Anorexia nervosa (AN) is a debilitating and often chronic disorder associated with significant morbidity and mortality. In recent decades, research on AN has identified key neurobiological pathways and brain regions that likely contribute to risk for and maintenance of the disorder and its symptoms. These include alterations in neurocircuitry underlying fear, motivation and reward, interoception, habit formation, and cognitive control, in addition to the detrimental effects of malnutrition on brain structure and function. Neuroscience-informed psychoeducation (NIPE) for AN can be integrated with existing therapeutic approaches to improve patients' and families' understanding of the disorder and engagement in treatment. This chapter outlines content, strategies, and considerations for the effective implementation of NIPE in the treatment of AN.

titre: Associations of Self-Reported Temporomandibular Disorder Symptoms with Sleep Problems, Perceived Stress, and Alexithymia in Young Adults: A Cross-Sectional Study
resume: Background: Temporomandibular disorders (TMDs) are increasingly understood as chronic pain conditions in which biological susceptibility and psychosocial factors interact. Alexithymia, a personality trait characterized by difficulty identifying and describing feelings, has been linked to chronic pain; however, its relationship with self-reported TMD symptoms, perceived stress, and sleep problems in non-clinical young adults remains insufficiently explored. Objective: To examine the associations of self-reported TMD symptom severity with sleep problems, perceived stress, and alexithymia in young adults. Methods: In this cross-sectional online survey, 634 participants aged 18-40 years (74.3% female) completed the Fonseca Anamnestic Index (FAI), the 20-item Toronto Alexithymia Scale (TAS-20), the 14-item Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-14), and the Jenkins Sleep Scale (JSS). Group comparisons, Spearman correlations, and hierarchical multiple linear regression with FAI score as the dependent variable were performed. All analyses were re-run on the raw data during revision. Results: Self-reported TMD symptoms of any severity were present in 90.5% of participants. FAI scores correlated weakly to moderately with JSS (r = 0.40), PSS-14 (r = 0.37), and TAS-20 (r = 0.29) scores (all p < 0.001). After adjustment for sociodemographic variables (R2 = 0.147), sleep problems (β = 0.24), perceived stress (β = 0.16), and alexithymia (β = 0.14) explained an additional 14.6% of the variance in FAI scores (final R2 = 0.292; p < 0.001). Female sex, older age within the 18-40 range, and residence in an earthquake-affected province were also independently associated with higher FAI scores. Among the alexithymia dimensions, only difficulty identifying feelings was independently associated with FAI scores. Conclusions: In this young adult sample, self-reported TMD symptom severity was associated with sleep problems, perceived stress, and alexithymia, with weak-to-moderate effect sizes. Given the cross-sectional design and reliance on self-report, these findings reflect associations only-causal or temporal relationships cannot be inferred, and the findings support considering psychosocial factors when TMD-related symptoms are assessed.

titre: Medicinal plant-derived bioactive compounds modulate gut microbiota-host signaling in cancer-related fatigue: a phenotype-to-target framework
resume: Cancer-related fatigue (CRF) is a frequent and disabling symptom during cancer and anticancer therapy, and pathway-directed pharmacological treatment remains limited. This review examines CRF through the plant-microbiota-host axis, in which medicinal plant-derived bioactive compounds reshape gut microbial community structure and function and are in turn biotransformed by gut microbes into metabolites that host sensors detect. Tumor- and treatment-associated injury of the intestinal mucosa alters epithelial renewal, barrier selectivity, and microbial metabolism, reshaping host exposure to microbial products and metabolites. These changes generate molecular mediators, including short-chain fatty acids, tryptophan-derived metabolites, bile acids, and microbe-associated molecular patterns, which are detected by epithelial, immune, enteroendocrine, and neural sensors. We organize the evidence into mediator-sensor modules and discuss how vagal, humoral, and immune-metabolic routes may converge on brainstem and monoaminergic networks involved in activity, effort, and interoceptive malaise. Because direct causal evidence in CRF remains incomplete, we separate established biology from candidate mechanisms and define pharmacodynamic readouts that can test target engagement. Medicinal plant-derived compounds enter the framework upstream: their microbial conversion products engage the same mediator-sensor modules. We argue that future CRF studies should match the fatigue domain, biological subgroup, molecular target, and biomarker before efficacy is interpreted mechanistically; for plant-derived interventions, this matching must also include the administered compound and its microbially generated metabolites.

titre: First evidence of an association between alexithymia and reduced humoral immunity following COVID-19 vaccination, independent of insomnia and metabolic factors in healthcare workers
resume: INTRODUCTION: Psychological factors have been increasingly implicated in immune regulation; however, the role of emotional awareness in shaping vaccine responses remains unexplored. Alexithymia, characterized by the difficulty in identifying and describing emotions, represents a psychosomatic construct associated with chronic stress physiology and immune dysregulation. This study investigated for the first time whether alexithymia, alongside other psychological factors, is associated with vaccine-induced humoral immunity, especially serum SARS-CoV-2 anti-Spike (anti-S) IgG concentrations following vaccination. METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 198 healthcare workers who received the BNT162b2 mRNA vaccine were evaluated 4-6 months post-vaccination. Alexithymia was assessed using the Toronto Alexithymia Scale-20 (TAS-20), insomnia using the Athens Insomnia Scale, and anxiety/depression using Hamilton scales. Self-reported positive thinking was also assessed. Anti-S IgG concentrations against the receptor-binding domain (RBD) of the S1 subunit were quantified, and multivariable linear regression (stepwise method) analyses were performed adjusting for demographic, metabolic, inflammatory, and behavioral covariates. RESULTS: Higher alexithymia (p = 0.002) and insomnia scores (p < 0.001) were independently associated with lower anti-S IgG concentrations after adjustment for vaccination doses, prior COVID-19 infection, BMI, interleukin-6 (IL-6), smoking, and alcohol consumption. Among alexithymia subscales, difficulty identifying and difficulty describing feelings, but not externally oriented thinking, were inversely associated with anti-S IgG concentrations. Participants who reported post-vaccination fever exhibited higher anti-S IgG concentrations and lower alexithymia scores; this retrospective finding is exploratory and does not establish a difference in inflammatory activation. CONCLUSION: Alexithymia and insomnia are independently associated with lower anti-S IgG concentrations in healthcare workers. Although these concentrations correlate with neutralizing activity, neutralization and clinical protection were not directly assessed in this study. Nevertheless, these findings suggest that alexithymia may represent an underrecognized psychosomatic correlate of post-vaccination antibody responses, meriting further investigation as a potential marker of variation in vaccine responses and protection. Prospective studies should determine whether the observed association extends to neutralizing activity or clinical protection.

titre: IRF8 deficiency causes anxiety-like behavior with sex differences
resume: Anxiety disorder is a serious psychiatric disease that affects women more than men and disrupts patients' daily lives. It is often comorbid with major depression and other mental diseases. Various underlying mechanisms have been proposed, such as neurotransmitters and neuroanatomical disruptions, and more recently, oxidative stress; however, much remains unclear, including the role of glial cells. Here, we investigated the role of IRF8 in anxiety-like behavior using mouse models. IRF8 is a transcription factor expressed primarily in microglia in the brain. A battery of behavioral tests revealed that female IRF8 knockout (IRF8KO) mice show increased anxiety-like behavior relative to male IRF8KO and wild-type mice. Female IRF8KO mice also exhibited a higher tendency for obsessive-compulsive-like disorder. However, these behavioral abnormalities were not observed when IRF8 was deleted postnatally, indicating that it acts during the fetal stage to control anxiety-like behavior. Transcriptome analysis revealed that IRF8 deficiency leads to redox dysregulation. Further, 2',7'-dichlorofluorescin diacetate (DCFDA) staining for microglia demonstrated that female IRF8KO microglia produce higher levels of reactive oxygen species (ROS) compared to WT and male IRF8KO counterparts. Detailed RNA-seq analysis, however, did not reveal specific genes that cause high ROS production in female cells. In sum, this work demonstrates that IRF8 in microglia plays a major role in controlling anxiety and OCD-like behavior with potential sex-specific differences.

titre: Accelerated Multi-Target Theta-Burst Stimulation for Obsessive-Depressive-Anxious Symptoms: Real-World Outcomes of the aTTODA Protocol
resume: BACKGROUND: Obsessive-compulsive symptoms frequently co-occur with depression and anxiety, contributing to a complex and potentially treatment-resistant clinical phenotype. Although transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) is an established treatment option for obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), many patients continue to experience residual symptoms across multiple domains. Multi-target neuromodulation approaches may help address overlapping neural circuits. This study evaluated the real-world effectiveness and feasibility of an accelerated Triple-Target Obsessive-Depressive-Anxious (aTTODA) theta-burst stimulation protocol. METHODS: In this naturalistic cohort study, 25 patients with treatment-resistant depressive-anxious disorder and comorbid OCD were treated with TMS at a specialized neuropsychiatric center. All patients received the accelerated aTTODA protocol, consisting of 30 sessions delivered over 3 weeks. Obsessive-compulsive, depressive, and anxiety symptoms were assessed at baseline and post-treatment using the Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale (Y-BOCS), 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HDRS-17), and Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAM-A), respectively. RESULTS: Treatment with the aTTODA protocol was associated with significant improvements across all symptom domains (all p < 0.001), with large within-group effect sizes (Cohen's d ≥1.0). Mean symptom reductions were 32.7% for the Y-BOCS, 44.6% for the HDRS-17, and 42.1% for the HAM-A. For OCD symptoms, 40% of patients met response criteria and 20% achieved remission. A shift toward lower Y-BOCS severity categories was also observed following treatment, suggesting broad clinical improvement beyond changes in mean symptom scores. CONCLUSIONS: In this complex, treatment-resistant population, the accelerated multi-target aTTODA protocol was associated with clinically meaningful improvements across obsessive-compulsive, depressive, and anxiety symptom domains. These preliminary findings support the feasibility of time-efficient, circuit-based neuromodulation strategies. However, controlled randomized, blinded, sham-controlled trials are needed to establish efficacy, durability of treatment effects, and optimal patient selection.

titre: Efficacy of a Limosilactobacillus reuteri DSM 17938 and BG-R46® Formulation in Predominantly Breastfed Infants with Infant Distress Syndrome: A Randomized Double-Blind Placebo-Controlled Trial
resume: Background: Infant distress syndrome, previously termed Infantile colic, is a common disorder of gut-brain interaction characterized by excessive crying and impaired behavioral regulation. Although Limosilactobacillus reuteri DSM 17938 has shown efficacy in predominantly breastfed infants, treatment responses remain variable, highlighting the need to investigate alternative probiotic formulations. BG-R46™, a strain derived from DSM 17938, exhibits distinct properties in preclinical models, providing a rationale for evaluating the combined formulation. This study investigated the efficacy and tolerability of DSM 17938 plus BG-R46™ compared with placebo in infants with infantile colic. Methods: In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 50 infants were randomized to receive either the probiotic formulation or placebo for 21 days. Forty-eight infants (24 per group) were included in the intention-to-treat and per-protocol analyses. The primary endpoint was the change from baseline to Day 7 in total infant distress time, defined as the sum of awake fussing, crying, and inconsolable crying recorded using the Baby's Day Diary®. Secondary outcomes included crying time, infant behavioral regulation (sleep duration, awake and content behavior, awake fussing, and inconsolable crying), maternal emotional well-being assessed using the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS), and safety. Results: Baseline infant distress time was comparable between groups. At Day 7, infant distress time decreased by 43% in the probiotic group versus 13% in the placebo group (-236.0 ± 111.5 vs. -66.7 ± 100.1 min/day; p < 0.001). At Day 21, reductions reached 62% and 26%, respectively. The probiotic formulation was well tolerated throughout the study. Conclusions: Supplementation with L. reuteri DSM 17938 plus L. reuteri BG-R46™ significantly reduced infant distress compared with placebo.

titre: Metagenomic characterization of gut microbiota in patients with Disorders of Gut-Brain Interaction
resume: BACKGROUND: Patients with Disorders of Gut-Brain Interaction (DGBI) experience recurrent gastrointestinal symptoms without identifiable organic abnormalities. While earlier studies focused on neural and hormonal regulation, recent evidence suggests that gut microbiota dysbiosis and altered microbial metabolism may play key roles in DGBI. METHODS: A total of 86 DGBI patients meeting the Rome V criteria were enrolled. Demographic data, disease duration, and symptom scores (Wexner Constipation Score, Self-Rating Anxiety Scale, and Abdominal Bloating Score) were collected. Fecal samples were subjected to metagenomic sequencing, followed by diversity, taxonomic, and functional analyses to characterize the gut microbiota profile of DGBI patients. RESULTS: DGBI patients and healthy controls (HC) showed comparable α-diversity and no significant overall separation in β-diversity. At the genus level, Prevotella was more abundant in HC, whereas other dominant genera showed similar patterns between groups. Co-occurrence network analysis revealed altered microbial associations in DGBI. A species-level random forest model moderately discriminated DGBI from HC (AUC = 0.769). Among DGBI subtypes, FD showed lower species richness, while IBS-M exhibited higher microbial evenness and diversity. Subtype-specific microbial signatures were identified, including Ruminococcus gnavus in IBS-D, Prevotella stercorea and Asaccharobacter celatus in IBS-C, and Victivallis vadensis in FC. Moreover, exploratory analysis showed a negative correlation between Asaccharobacter celatus abundance and Wexner constipation scores in the IBS-C subtype. CONCLUSION: In conclusion, this study showed that patients with DGBI exhibited limited changes in overall gut microbial diversity compared with healthy individuals, but certain differences in microbial community patterns were observed across clinical subtypes, suggesting potential microbial ecological heterogeneity among different DGBI phenotypes.

titre: Potential Mechanisms of Chlorogenic Acid in Cognitive Impairment: A Comprehensive Review
resume: Cognitive impairment (CI) is a clinical syndrome primarily affecting cognitive functions such as learning, memory, perception, and problem-solving. Its causes are heterogeneous, including neurological, psychiatric, metabolic, vascular, toxicological, and age-related factors. Currently, no specific and effective pharmacological therapies are available for CI in clinical practice. As one of the most abundant dietary polyphenols, chlorogenic acid (CGA) displays diverse biological effects and has recently garnered growing interest within cognitive neuroscience. This review summarizes the mechanisms by which CGA ameliorates cognitive impairment, encompassing neuroprotection, modulation of the gut-brain axis, inhibition of neuroinflammation, inhibition of oxidative stress, promotion of autophagy, inhibition of apoptosis, and suppression of amyloid-β (Aβ) formation. The signaling pathways implicated include activation of the PKC, Nrf2/PPAR and Nrf2/ARE pathways, as well as inhibition of the TLR4/NF-κB, mTOR/TFEB, p38 MAPK, and JNK/c-Jun pathways. This article provides an overview of current advancements in CGA, addressing its chemical attributes, dietary origins, drug metabolism, and the mechanistic basis for its efficacy in neurodegenerative diseases.

titre: Altered gut microbiota and untargeted metabolomic features in patients with schizophrenia: a case-control study
resume: BACKGROUND: Mental disorders are among the leading causes of global disease burden, and their etiology spans genetic, environmental, and physiological factors. Emerging evidence suggests that the gut microbiota may contribute to the development of neuropsychiatric disorders through the microbiota-gut-brain axis. This study aimed to characterize differences in gut microbial composition and untargeted metabolomic profiles between patients with schizophrenia and healthy controls. METHODS: Fecal samples were collected from 30 patients with schizophrenia and 30 healthy controls; 59 samples (30 patients and 29 controls) yielded qualified 16S rRNA gene sequencing data. Untargeted metabolomic profiling was performed by ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UHPLC-MS/MS). RESULTS: Compared with healthy controls, patients with schizophrenia showed reduced microbial richness and diversity together with marked separation in β-diversity. In an exploratory random forest ranking, Pseudocitrobacter, Hafnia-Obesumbacterium, and Escherichia-Shigella contributed most strongly to between-group discrimination. Escherichia-Shigella was significantly enriched in patients (median relative abundance 2.377% in group S vs. 0.119% in group H; q = 0.00031; Cliff's δ = 0.646), whereas Faecalibacterium (2.630% vs. 7.275%) and Agathobacter (0.903% vs. 2.874%) were more abundant in healthy controls. Untargeted metabolomics likewise revealed between-group differences that predominantly involved metabolites and pathways of amino acid and lipid metabolism. CONCLUSION: Patients with schizophrenia show alterations in gut microbial composition and untargeted metabolomic features, supporting an association between schizophrenia and microbiota-metabolite alterations. Future confirmation requires larger longitudinal cohorts and independent validation datasets. Owing to the small sample size, cross-sectional study design, and antipsychotic drug exposure, we could not disentangle disease-specific effects from medication-related effects.

titre: Microbiota Dysbiosis and the Gut-Brain Axis in Psychiatric Disorders: Molecular Mechanisms, Clinical Evidence, and Therapeutic Perspectives
resume: The gut-brain axis provides a biologically plausible framework for understanding the bidirectional interactions among the intestinal microbiota, immune-inflammatory signaling, neuroendocrine regulation, neurotransmitter metabolism, and psychiatric symptoms. Although numerous recent reviews have examined individual psychiatric disorders, microbial composition, or microbiota-targeted therapies, the field still lacks a sufficiently integrated appraisal that clearly distinguishes associative findings from human studies, mechanistic evidence from preclinical research, and preliminary clinical interventions. This structured narrative review synthesizes clinical, translational, and preclinical studies across major depressive disorder, bipolar disorder, anxiety disorders, schizophrenia, and trauma-related conditions. The main literature search covered publications from January 2015 to January 2026; earlier foundational mechanistic studies of key relevance to gut-brain communication were also considered. Recurrent pathways include altered short-chain fatty acid production, tryptophan-kynurenine metabolism, immune-inflammatory activation, hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis dysregulation, neurotransmitter-related signaling, impaired intestinal and blood-brain barrier integrity, and vagus nerve-mediated communication. Human studies predominantly demonstrate associations between microbial signatures and psychiatric phenotypes, symptom severity, inflammatory status, or treatment response, whereas preclinical models provide stronger mechanistic evidence that microbiota manipulation can influence behavioral, neurochemical, immune, and neuroendocrine outcomes. Probiotics, prebiotics, dietary interventions, and fecal microbiota transplantation show therapeutic potential; however, the current evidence is limited by small sample sizes, methodological heterogeneity, insufficient standardization, and a lack of long-term validation. The distinctive contribution of this review is its structured comparison of three levels of evidence-human observational findings, experimental mechanistic studies, and emerging clinical interventions-thereby clarifying what has been consistently replicated, what remains mechanistically plausible, and what is not yet ready for routine application in psychiatric practice.

titre: Assessing the Use, Impact, and Perspectives of Generative Artificial Intelligence Among Health Consumers: A Cross-Sectional Survey in Saudi Arabia
resume: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Saudi Health consumers increasingly rely on generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) to access health information from a growing number of health-related resources. Little is known about the frequency and patterns of generative AI tool use for seeking health information among consumers, its reported impact, and health consumers' perceptions of these tools. This study aims to investigate the use of and perspectives on generative AI tools among health consumers in Saudi Arabia (SA). It also aims to assess the impact of their use on health-seeking behaviours. METHODS: An exploratory, cross-sectional, self-administered online survey was distributed to adults (≥18 years) residing in SA during two data collection rounds in 2026 (March-April and July-August). All adults who used generative AI tools to seek online health information in the past year were included. Bivariate and multivariate analyses were conducted to examine relationships among variables. RESULTS: A total of 403 eligible health consumers (58% male) participated. Among respondents who had used generative AI for health purposes, approximately 49% reported using it more than five times per month. Younger age, higher income, and more frequent pre-use were associated with higher odds of frequent seeking health information behaviour. Headache, abdominal pain, and musculoskeletal pain were the most common claims. ChatGPT was the main platform (84%) used for seeking information. Age was significantly negatively associated with frequency, whereas income and pre-visit use were positively associated. The primary reasons for seeking health information via generative AI were quick information retrieval (71%), time saving (34%), and curiosity (30.5%). CONCLUSIONS: The high frequency of use suggests that generative AI can serve as a source of health information and may lead users to withhold health information from healthcare providers. It may influence subsequent health-seeking behaviours, such as requesting urgent care or postponing physician visits. These self-reported findings do not establish diagnostic accuracy, clinical effectiveness, or patient safety, and the clinical risk and appropriateness of self-management actions were not assessed. Many respondents reported concerns about inaccurate information, missed serious illness, and increased health anxiety.

titre: Brain-heart coupling in Parkinson's disease: from autonomic dysfunction to network physiology
resume: Cardiovascular autonomic dysfunction is a well-established feature of Parkinson's disease (PD), yet the brain and cardiovascular system are still largely investigated as separate physiological domains. This separation may overlook an important dimension of PD pathophysiology: the dynamic communication between them. Here, we examine emerging evidence that brain-heart coupling itself is altered in PD. A focused PubMed search identified studies directly relating neural activity to cardiac dynamics, complemented by relevant physiological and autonomic literature. Despite a small and heterogeneous evidence base, electrophysiological, neuroimaging, and dynamic network studies suggest disrupted central-cardiac coordination. Alterations are detectable in early and de novo PD, relate to dysautonomia, and appear sensitive to dopaminergic state. Emerging evidence for impaired cardiac interoception further suggests that dysfunction may extend from descending autonomic control to ascending heart-to-brain processing. Importantly, cross-system measures can reveal abnormalities that remain not captured by neural or cardiovascular signals alone. Their clinical potential is promising but remains to be established through larger, standardized, and longitudinal studies. At present, brain-heart coupling is best viewed as a physiological framework with emerging translational relevance rather than as a validated biomarker. By revealing interactions that remain hidden when neural and cardiovascular systems are examined separately, brain-heart coupling may uncover a distinct dimension of PD pathophysiology and provide a bridge from integrative physiology to disease phenotyping and future clinical stratification.

titre: Primed for nocebo: Effects of negative treatment information on pain expectations and the role of psychological vulnerability
resume: INTRODUCTION: Negative treatment expectations are central to nocebo effects and shape symptom perception as a transdiagnostic mechanism relevant to persisting physical symptoms. Little is known about how such expectations form, how they respond to threatening treatment information across somatic and visceral pain domains, and which dispositional factors moderate this process. METHODS: Using data from the randomized NOVIS trial, 101 healthy participants (52 females; 18-36 years) completed a multiple-threat pain paradigm involving visceral (rectal distension) and somatic (cutaneous heat) stimuli. Participants received either negative information (nocebo: 50% probability of a pain-enhancing infusion) or neutral information (control) regarding an intravenous treatment that was always saline. Generalized expectations of symptom worsening and side effects, as well as symptom-specific pain expectations, were assessed prior to treatment. Bayesian cumulative probit and linear models estimated the effects of treatment information and moderation by pain catastrophizing, somatosensory amplification, and negative affect. RESULTS: Negative information induced expectations of symptom worsening and side effects. Effects on symptom-specific expectations were modality-dependent: anticipated unpleasantness increased for somatic but not visceral pain. Pain catastrophizing and somatosensory amplification were associated with elevated negative expectations independent of treatment information. Somatosensory amplification, pain catastrophizing, and trait negative affect each moderated the effect of negative information on somatic pain unpleasantness expectations. CONCLUSION: Nocebo-related expectations differed between generalized and symptom-specific expectations and depended on symptom modality and psychological vulnerability. Individuals with heightened bodily vigilance, catastrophizing, and negative affect, may be particularly vulnerable to nocebo effects as a psychological mechanism implicated in persisting physical symptoms. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS) - ID: 00024410.

titre: Remimazolam in older surgical patients: postoperative delirium, hemodynamic stability, and mechanistic considerations
resume: The growing number of older adults undergoing surgery has increased interest in anesthetic strategies that preserve physiological stability without worsening postoperative neurocognitive outcomes. Remimazolam is an ultra-short-acting benzodiazepine that produces hypnosis through positive allosteric modulation of the γ-aminobutyric acid type A (GABA-A) receptor and is rapidly hydrolyzed to the low-activity metabolite CNS7054. This focused narrative review examines remimazolam in older surgical patients, with particular emphasis on postoperative delirium (POD) and hemodynamic stability. Randomized trials and meta-analyses generally report fewer hypotensive events with remimazolam than with propofol, but neurocognitive findings are heterogeneous. Earlier trials in orthopedic, hip, gastrectomy, and abdominal surgery largely reported similar POD incidence, and one trial in frail patients undergoing hip surgery reported a lower POD incidence with remimazolam. In contrast, a 2026 randomized non-inferiority trial involving 455 patients aged ≥65 years undergoing lung resection found a higher overall incidence of delirium with remimazolam (48% vs. 31%), driven predominantly by emergence delirium in the post-anesthesia care unit (46% vs. 28%), whereas delirium after post-anesthesia care unit discharge through postoperative day 3 was similar (4% vs. 5%). This temporal distinction indicates that outcome definitions and assessment windows materially influence apparent treatment effects. PACU delirium is also associated with subsequent adverse outcomes in observational studies, underscoring the clinical importance of this early phenotype. The relatively consistent hemodynamic advantage of remimazolam should therefore be regarded separately from neurocognitive benefit; reduced hypotension has not yet been shown to translate into delirium prevention. Preclinical anti-inflammatory and organ-protective pathways are biologically plausible but remain unconfirmed at clinically relevant neurocognitive endpoints. Current evidence supports individualized use rather than routine selection of remimazolam for delirium prevention.

titre: Comparing treatment outcomes for younger and older adults with anxiety disorders, OCD, or PTSD in generalized mental healthcare
resume: The prevalence of anxiety disorders, obsessive compulsive disorder (OCD), and posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is comparable across younger and older adults, but older adults are under-referred, undertreated, and understudied. It is unclear whether existing psychological treatments are (equally) effective in older and younger adults, leaving a substantial treatment gap. This study examined whether treatment outcomes for anxiety, OCD, or PTSD differed between younger and older adults. RM ANOVA analyses were conducted in a sample of Dutch patients in generalized mental health care (N = 20,554). Age groups were categorized based on differences at which symptoms presentations emerge (i.e., 18-50 versus a group aged 51 years and older). Next, analyses were repeated based on the conventional retirement age (i.e., 18-64 versus a group aged 65 years and older). Findings showed statistically significant main effects of age group for PTSD and anxiety disorders, but not for OCD. However, the magnitude of the statistically significant effects did not reach the threshold for a small effect (ƞ2 =.007). Pre-treatment scores were lower in the older age groups. After controlling for pretreatment differences using propensity score matching, the main effects of age group were no longer statistically significant. The absence of age effects provides a first step in extending the evidence-base for the treatment of anxiety, OCD, and PTSD to older adults. We recommend clinicians working with older adults to adhere to the clinical guidelines established for younger adults with anxiety, OCD, and PTSD. This will remove treatment barriers for older adults.

titre: Understanding Psychological Health in Adults with Irritable Bowel Syndrome: A Cross-Sectional Study Using the All of Us Research Program
resume: BACKGROUND: Psychological health is an important aspect of health and well-being among adults with irritable bowel syndrome, yet the interrelationships among individual vulnerabilities, social experiences, perceived stress, and psychological health outcomes remain poorly understood. OBJECTIVE: To characterize psychological health and examine direct and indirect associations of childhood adversity and adult attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder-related symptoms within an adapted Stress Process Model. DESIGN: Cross-sectional secondary analysis. SETTING: The United States All of Us Research Program. PARTICIPANTS: 2,417 adults with electronic health record-documented irritable bowel syndrome and complete data on the primary analysis variables and covariates. METHODS: Separate structural equation models examined childhood adversity and adult attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder-related symptoms in relation to perceived stress, anxiety and depressive symptoms, and positive psychological well-being, with loneliness and perceived social support as psychosocial pathways. Models adjusted for sociodemographic and social-context factors. RESULTS: The median age was 54.39 years; 80.7% were female and 84.4% were White. Moderate-to-high perceived stress was reported by 56.2%, at least moderate anxiety symptoms by 21.0%, and at least moderate depressive symptoms by 24.3%. Higher ACE-8 scores were associated with greater perceived stress, anxiety symptoms, and depressive symptoms and lower psychological well-being (β = 0.063, 0.089, 0.116, and -0.100, respectively); corresponding associations for higher ASRS-6 scores were β = 0.299, 0.355, 0.390, and -0.260. Loneliness-specific indirect associations were positive for perceived stress, anxiety, and depressive symptoms (ACE-8: β = 0.023-0.034; ASRS-6: β = 0.043-0.075) and negative for psychological well-being (ACE-8: β = -0.039; ASRS-6: β = -0.089; all p < .001). Social support-specific indirect associations were not significant in the ACE-8 model and were small and significant only for anxiety and depression in the ASRS-6 model (β = 0.003-0.004). CONCLUSIONS: Psychological health among adults with irritable bowel syndrome was associated with interconnected individual and social factors within an adapted Stress Process Model. Childhood adversity and adult attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder-related symptoms showed direct and indirect associations with psychological health, with loneliness emerging as the most consistent social factor. These findings support prospective investigation of individual vulnerabilities and social experiences in psychological health. The cross-sectional design does not establish temporal ordering or causal mediation.
revue: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

titre: Interactions between physical activity, diet, and gut microbiota in gastrointestinal health: celiac disease as a model in children and athletes
resume: Physical activity, diet, and gut microbiota are key determinants of gastrointestinal physiology, immune regulation, and metabolic homeostasis, collectively influencing gastrointestinal health, physical performance, and long-term wellbeing. Although regular physical activity generally promotes intestinal function and systemic health, excessive exercise, nutritional imbalance, and underlying gastrointestinal (GI) disorders may adversely affect gastrointestinal integrity and athletic performance. Within this context, celiac disease (CeD) represents a unique clinical model for understanding the complex interactions among physical activity, dietary interventions, gut microbiota, and gastrointestinal health in both children and athletes. This clinical review provides a comprehensive overview of current evidence regarding these interactions, focusing on gastrointestinal physiology, exercise-related GI disorders, bone health, dietary strategies, and gut microbiota modulation. Current evidence indicates that appropriately prescribed physical activity improves gastrointestinal function, immune regulation, body composition, skeletal health, and quality of life, partly through favorable modulation of the gut microbiota, whereas prolonged or poorly individualized high-intensity exercise may impair gastrointestinal integrity through splanchnic hypoperfusion, increased intestinal permeability, oxidative stress, and transient dysbiosis. A Mediterranean-style gluten-free diet appears to improve nutritional adequacy and musculoskeletal health, while a short-term low-fermentable oligosaccharides, disaccharides, monosaccharides, and polyols (low-FODMAP) diet may relieve persistent irritable bowel syndrome-like symptoms in selected individuals despite strict gluten-free diet adherence. In children with celiac disease, integrating individualized physical activity with optimized dietary management supports growth, skeletal development, and long-term health while addressing the specific physiological demands of physically active children and young athletes. Overall, celiac disease provides a clinically relevant model for understanding how physical activity, diet, and gut microbiota interact to influence gastrointestinal health, highlighting the importance of individualized lifestyle strategies that integrate appropriate exercise with nutritional optimization to improve gastrointestinal function, musculoskeletal health, and quality of life.
revue: Frontiers in sports and active living

titre: Preventive effects of compound probiotics supplementation on migraine: Mendelian randomization analysis and experimental evidence
resume: INTRODUCTION: Migraine imposes a substantial economic and societal burden. The microbiota-gut-brain axis (MGBA) has emerged as a key potential mechanism, yet its causal relationships with migraine and the underlying pathways remain unclear. METHODS: We performed Mendelian randomization (MR) to assess the causal effects of gut microbiota on migraine, and further conducted mediation analysis to identify key mediating brain regions. In addition, we performed in vivo mouse experiments, in which we induced migraine-like pain via nitroglycerin (NTG) and investigated changes in gut microbiota, mechanical pain threshold, and regional brain activation following pretreatment with composite probiotics. RESULTS: MR analysis identified eight gut microbial taxa causally associated with migraine and its subtypes. Mediation analysis suggested that the association between genetically predicted Paraprevotella abundance and migraine risk was partially mediated by ICVF in the posterior insular cortex. In NTG-induced migraine mice, composite probiotics ameliorated gut dysbiosis and maintained Paraprevotella abundance, while elevating mechanical pain thresholds in both periorbital and hind paw region. Probiotics intervention also suppressed c-Fos expression in the pIC, Sp5c, PVT, and mPFC. Additionally, it specifically decreased CGRP immunoreactivity in the Sp5c. CONCLUSION: This study provides genetic and experimental evidence supporting a potential role of the gut microbiome in migraine and the potential of microbiome-based strategies for migraine prevention.

titre: Microbiome-mitochondria crosstalk in neuro-oncology: molecular mechanisms, immunometabolic reprogramming, and therapeutic opportunities
resume: Although the gut microbiome is increasingly recognized as an important regulator of metabolic, immune, and neurophysiological functions, and mitochondrial dysfunction is considered a hallmark of metabolic flexibility, oxidative stress, and resistance to therapy in cancers, the role of microbiome-derived cues and mitochondrial processes in brain tumors remains poorly understood. The Microbiome-Gut-Brain-Mitochondria Axis in Neuro-Oncology provides a framework for understanding metabolism and immunity in neuro-oncology by highlighting this axis and emphasizing its role in glioblastoma. Metabolites produced by the microbiome, including short-chain fatty acids, bile acid metabolites, tryptophan metabolites, and other microbial compounds, have been shown to affect the immune system, barrier function, cellular metabolism, and neural signaling. Mitochondria are capable of functioning as intracellular communication mechanisms that will help to decipher those signals in order to create energy, ROS, calcium communication, biogenesis of mitochondria, quality control, and apoptosis. These processes may contribute to metabolic plasticity in glioblastomas, including glycolytic, oxidative phosphorylation, and amino- and lipid-metabolic adaptations, mitochondrial transfer, adaptation to hypoxia, tumor cell stemness, and immune suppression in the tumor microenvironment. The article also discusses the relationships between microbiome-derived cues, mitochondria, and tumor-associated immune populations. Microbiome-derived and mitochondrial biomarkers, combined with multi-omics approaches, single-cell technologies, spatial biology, artificial intelligence, and new experimental models, may help to identify relevant microbiome-mitochondria signatures. Modulating the microbiome, mitochondria, and combination therapies appears promising for glioblastomas. However, the causative link between microbiome-derived mitochondrial mechanisms and human brain tumors remains unproven. The necessity of prospective and mechanistic studies of the microbiome, mitochondria, metabolism, immunity, and clinical aspects arises.

titre: Natural Bioactive Compound Combinations in Alzheimer's Disease: Gut-brain Axis and Quantitative Interaction Assessment
resume: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disorder for which singletarget therapies have repeatedly shown limited clinical efficacy. Natural bioactive compounds offer multi-target neuroprotective potential, yet contemporary research has predominantly focused on individual compounds rather than rationally defined combinations. This review examines natural bioactive compound combinations in AD through the gut-brain axis, with particular attention to distinguishing mechanistic complementarity from quantitatively demonstrated pharmacological synergy. The major pathways connecting gut microbiota dysbiosis to AD pathology were first summarized, and then discussed how compound combinations may produce enhanced effects through complementary microbiota modulation, metabolic regulation, and coordinated actions at intestinal and central nervous system targets. As an illustrative case, the combination of Icariin (ICA) and Panax Notoginseng Saponins (PNS), derived from the deconstruction of a traditional Chinese medicine formula, is critically evaluated. Available studies suggest combination-associated changes in gut microbiota, hippocampal protein expression, and AD-related outcomes, while evidence from the individual components supports biologically plausible complementary mechanisms. However, current evidence remains largely qualitative and does not establish that ICA-PNS produces supraadditive effects or that microbiota changes causally mediate its benefits. Improved combination efficacy should therefore not be equated with synergy. Future studies should use informative doseresponse matrices and pre-specified interaction models, including the Chou-Talalay combination index with complementary Loewe or Bliss analyses, together with multi-omics and microbiotacausality experiments, to enable more rigorous and reproducible evaluation and support mechanistic validation and future translational development of natural compound combinations.

titre: Triple-Positive Antiphospholipid Syndrome with Splenic Infarction Triggered by Tocilizumab Withdrawal in A High-Titer ACPA-Positive Rheumatoid Arthritis Patient: An Unmasking Storm of Polyautoimmunity
resume: INTRODUCTION: We describe the occurrence of an uncommon thrombotic event, namely splenic infarction, as the onset of antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) after temporary suspension of anti-IL-6 treatment in a patient with rheumatoid arthritis (RA). CASE DESCRIPTION: A 53-year-old patient with anti-citrullinated protein antibody (ACPA) and rheumatoid factor-positive RA, previously showing transient positivity for immunoglobulin (Ig)G anticardiolipin antibodies and lupus anticoagulant (LAC), refractory to multiple biological disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (DMARDs), anti-tumour necrosis factor (TNF)-α agents, and rituximab, had been treated with tocilizumab since 2013 with good clinical response. After temporary suspension of tocilizumab for minor orthopaedic surgery complicated by skin abscess, he developed acute abdominal pain and computed tomography evidence of splenic infarction. Laboratory evaluation revealed elevated inflammatory markers and triple positivity for LAC, aCL IgG, and aB2GPI IgG, leading to the diagnosis of APS. Treatment with warfarin, methotrexate, and baricitinib resulted in stable disease control without recurrent thrombotic events. CONCLUSION: Clinical stability in RA is a delicate balance between control of inflammation and avoidance of medication toxicity, especially in patients with high thrombotic risk and previous antiphospholipid positivity. Temporary withdrawal of biologic therapy may induce immunological rebound and thrombotic complications. This case highlights the importance of thrombotic risk stratification and multidisciplinary management when biologic therapies are suspended. LEARNING POINTS: Tocilizumab may act as a suppressor of autoreactive B-cell clones producing antiphospholipid antibodies.A high anti-citrullinated protein antibody (ACPA) titer may be associated with an increased risk of developing autoantibody storm with possible prothrombotic complications in rheumatoid arthritis, such as antiphospholipid syndrome.In case of surgical interventions in patients with rheumatoid arthritis treated with biological disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (bDMARDs) it is important to evaluate the stratification of thrombotic risk with multidisciplinary discussion before suspending therapy.
revue: European journal of case reports in internal medicine

titre: Comparing a body-oriented and a cognitive online intervention for adults with depressive symptoms: A three-arm randomized controlled trial
resume: Based on findings from basic and clinical research indicating that the motor system can causally influence emotional processes, Body, Breath and Mind (BBM) was developed as a minimally guided online intervention. BBM combines body-oriented Qi Gong practice with elements of behavioral activation and aims to target embodied aspects of depression. In a pre-registered three-arm randomized controlled trial, the effects of BBM were compared with MoodGym (MG), an established online intervention based on cognitive behavioral therapy, and with a waitlist control group (WL). A total of 303 participants with negative and depressive mood were randomized to BBM, MG, or WL. The primary outcome was depressive symptom severity, assessed with the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9). Quality of life, measured with the Short Form Health Survey (SF-36), served as a secondary outcome. Both BBM and MG showed greater reductions in somatic depressive symptoms of the PHQ-9 compared to WL. For the affective component of the PHQ-9, only MG demonstrated significantly greater reductions than WL. No significant differences between conditions were observed for changes in quality of life. The results do not provide evidence that adding body-oriented components yields specific benefits in the online treatment of depressive symptoms. However, overall, BBM showed largely comparable effects to those of MoodGym, although the findings were less consistent for affective depressive symptoms. BBM may therefore provide an additional minimally guided online intervention option for addressing negative and depressed mood, which may be of particular interest to individuals who prefer a body-oriented approach.

titre: Coronal Alignment in Pediatric Patients With Discoid Lateral Meniscus
resume: BACKGROUND: Despite the established clinical significance of discoid lateral meniscus (DLM) and the impact of coronal alignment on knee health, a comprehensive understanding regarding the specific characteristics and prevalence of coronal plane alignment among pediatric patients with symptomatic DLM remains limited. PURPOSE: To describe coronal alignment parameters in patients with DLM and analyze associations of high-grade valgus or varus with radiographic imaging, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and descriptive factors in pediatric patients treated for symptomatic DLM. STUDY DESIGN: Cross-sectional study; Level of evidence, 3. METHODS: This 2-institution, institutional review board-approved retrospective study included patients ≤18 years of age with an MRI diagnosis of DLM. Full-length standing hip-to-ankle alignment radiographs were obtained for 141 patients (156 knees) with DLM between 2017 and 2024. Radiographic coronal alignment was classified into mechanical zones (varus, valgus, or neutral) using the linear femoral head center to talar center assessment and categorized into 3 zones: zone 1 (±1), representing low-grade malalignment, and zones 2 and 3 (±2 and ±3), representing high-grade malalignment. The mechanical axis deviation (MAD), medial proximal tibial angle (MPTA), and lateral distal femoral angle (LDFA) were measured. MRI scans were assessed for Watanabe subtype and osteochondritis dissecans (OCD). Descriptive statistics were calculated for continuous variables, while categorical data are summarized using frequencies and percentages. Comparisons were performed using the chi-square test, Fisher exact test, and 1-way analysis of variance with application of post hoc Bonferroni correction for variable significance. RESULTS: The mean age was 12.91 ± 3.24 years (range, 4-18 years), with 52.48% male patients. DLM subtypes were complete (48.08%), incomplete (44.87%), and Wrisberg (3.85%). Coronal malalignment was found in 83.33% of patients: 55.13% valgus, 28.21% varus, and 16.67% neutral. High-grade malalignment (zones ±2 and ±3) occurred in 11.53% (n = 18): 4 varus (2.56%) and 14 valgus (8.97%). OCD of the lateral femoral condyle was found in 8.33% of patients, all with valgus alignment. No statistically significant associations were found between coronal malalignment (high-grade or low-grade) and descriptive factors, co-occurring conditions, sports participation, or DLM subtypes. There were significant differences in LDFA, MPTA, and MAD across malalignment severity. High-grade valgus and varus alignments showed no significant associations with age, sex, OCD, sports participation, or Watanabe type. CONCLUSION: Coronal malalignment is prevalent in pediatric DLM, with nearly 1 in 10 patients having high-grade valgus. Routine lower limb alignment assessment is key, as early detection and correction of coronal malalignment may improve the long-term success of meniscal rim-preserving surgery (MRPS). Further investigation is warranted to evaluate alignment changes over time after MRPS.
